ST01-01.name: The Two-Wave Lance
ST01-01.origin: The Hide-Knights of the Crown hold their Hides of crown land for one purpose: to ride in Aldmark's two-wave charge, two lines of knights 80 m apart so that the second rides through whatever the first has broken. It was the charge of the Horde Wars, at the Gashmar Fords in 1070 and along the Gordush, and the Crown teaches it every winter to the 5,000 Hide-Knights quartered at Kingsmere, Swanvale and Yewmarch.
ST01-01.philosophy: Never one blow: the first wave breaks the line, the second breaks the men behind it, and nobody stops to fight.
ST01-01.strengths: Shock on open ground; knee-to-knee discipline; a second blow arriving before the first is answered.
ST01-01.weakness: Stakes, set spears and mud stop both waves; a horse archer who will not close; on foot a Hide-Knight is a heavy man in mail.

techniques.name: Knee to Knee
techniques.desc: Ride stirrup to stirrup with the man beside you, so your point carries the weight of the whole rank.

techniques.name: Knight Afoot
techniques.desc: Unhorsed, you stand still behind your shield and get your breath back; a Hide-Knight afoot does not chase anyone.

techniques.name: Walk, Trot, Canter
techniques.desc: Walk, trot and canter, and only the last eighty metres at the gallop: the horse arrives with wind left, and so do you.

techniques.name: The First Wave
techniques.desc: The first line goes in knee to knee and does not try to kill, only to break: men go down, shields go sideways, the line opens.

techniques.name: Through the Gap
techniques.desc: The second wave arrives eighty metres behind the first and rides into the hole it tore, at men still getting up.

techniques.name: Two Waves
techniques.desc: The whole charge in one pass: you break him with the first shock and are already riding through him with the second.

maneuver.name: The Two-Wave Charge
maneuver.desc: Two lines of knights 80 m apart at a walk, trot and canter; the second rides through the gap the first has torn before the enemy can close it.

ST01-02.name: The Shire Set Spear
ST01-02.origin: The 10,000 Shire Spears of the Crown Lands and the Eagle March hold their Hides for a spear and a day's drill a month, and the drill is the set spear: kneel, butt in the earth, point at the horse's chest. Aldmark learned its worth at the Gordush fords, where Gunnar Harrow's 300 held the Bend for an hour in 1049, and its forest marches keep the cross-barred boar spear for riders and beasts that come singly.
ST01-02.philosophy: Let the charger kill himself on your point; your only work is to be there, kneeling, when he arrives.
ST01-02.strengths: Stops horses and beasts cold; cheap and quick to learn; holds a ford or a gap with plain men.
ST01-02.weakness: Rooted where it kneels: an enemy who stops short and shoots, or comes on foot and goes round, finds a man who cannot follow.

school.name: The Spear Yard of the Eagle March

techniques.name: Butt in the Earth
techniques.desc: Kneel, drive the butt into the ground behind your heel and let the point find the horse's chest.

techniques.name: The Cross-Bar
techniques.desc: The boar spear's bar stops the point a hand deep, so the spear is not lost in him and comes back out for the next.

techniques.name: Kneel and Receive
techniques.desc: Nerve more than skill: hold the point still while he comes on, and he spits himself on his own weight.

techniques.name: Ford Thrust
techniques.desc: A man wading waist-deep cannot step aside; thrust low into his legs as he comes up out of the water.

techniques.name: Gunnar's Hour
techniques.desc: What the 300 did at the Gordush Bend: hold the ford one hour more, and make every man who comes at you pay for the hour.

maneuver.name: Set Spear Line
maneuver.desc: Spearmen kneel and set the butts of their spears in the ground, points at a horse's chest; the charger spits itself on its own weight.

ST01-03.name: The Wall Crossbow
ST01-03.origin: Aldmark's crossbows are town and wall crossbows: the 6,000 Kingsmere Crossbows on the river walls and the 1,500 Wall Crossbows at Dunwatch and Thornstone, men who shoot from a parapet, a wagon bed or the far side of a stream. The Thornleys have kept the old Solen forts of the Crown Wall since Harald took them in 956, and their wall school teaches every crown crossbowman to shoot down a stair, across a ford and through a loophole.
ST01-03.philosophy: Never stand in the open: put stone, wood or water between you and him, and make him cross it under your bolt.
ST01-03.strengths: Kills a knight in mail at 60 m; deadly against men wading, climbing or crossing a ditch.
ST01-03.weakness: Two bolts a minute; caught in the open without a wall, a wagon or water it is a short sword and a slow reload, and rain slackens the string.

techniques.name: Belt-Hook Span
techniques.desc: Foot in the stirrup, hook on the string, stand up: two bolts a minute, and the first one before he is close.

techniques.name: Crenel Cut
techniques.desc: The short sword is for the man who reaches the parapet: one short chop at the hands on the stone.

techniques.name: Behind the Merlon
techniques.desc: Stay behind the stone until he shows himself to reach you, then shoot the part of him he showed.

techniques.name: At the Ford
techniques.desc: Shoot him in the water at forty metres, where he is slow, wet and cannot answer.

techniques.name: Down the Stair
techniques.desc: Above a man on a tower stair you have the height and he has the steps: catch his blow on the shield and kick him back down onto the men behind.

techniques.name: The Sixty-Metre Bolt
techniques.desc: From good cover, at sixty metres, the crossbow kills a knight in mail; you wait as long as it takes for exactly that shot.

maneuver.name: Crossbow Line behind a Stream
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen behind a stream, a flooded ditch or a wall: attackers slowed to a wade or a climb are shot at 30–60 m and cannot answer.

ST01-04.name: The Ring Warden's Sword
ST01-04.origin: The 1,000 Ring Wardens keep the Oath Hall and the treasury beneath it, and the 10,000 Crown Shield Foot of the shires are drilled in their image: kite shield, Kingsmere sword, mail. Their yard on Oath Hill teaches what mail does to a sword, that the cut skids off the rings, and so the Warden fights with the point at the gaps and the pommel at the face.
ST01-04.philosophy: Shield high, point low: against mail you do not cut, you find the armpit, the throat and the eye.
ST01-04.strengths: Steady in mail against mail; finds the gaps; a sound shield in a sound line.
ST01-04.weakness: Slow and heavy: against a fast unarmored fighter in the open the kite shield is a sail and the point arrives late.

school.name: The Wardens' Yard of Oath Hill

techniques.name: Shield High
techniques.desc: Kite shield up to the eyes, sword arm tucked: the first lesson on Oath Hill is to be hard to hit.

techniques.name: Point to the Gap
techniques.desc: Mail turns the cut, so you do not cut: the point goes to the armpit, the throat or the hole under the nasal.

techniques.name: Pommel to the Face
techniques.desc: Close in over the shields and hit him in the face with the pommel; a stunned man in mail is a man you can kill.

techniques.name: Half-Sword
techniques.desc: Left hand on the blade, right on the grip, and drive the point through the rings like a spike.

techniques.name: The Oath Hall Door
techniques.desc: The Wardens' last lesson, taught at the treasury door: watch his shoulder, take the blow on the kite, and put the point through the gap he opened to make it.

maneuver.name: Kite Wall
maneuver.desc: Crown foot lock their kite shields edge to edge and work their points through the gaps; the line gives ground a step at a time and never breaks.

ST01-05.name: The Split-Shield Lance
ST01-05.origin: The Lance Yard of Kingsmere claims a chain back to Brand Ironside's horse-breeders of Dunfield, who won the Millrun fords in 913. Sir Wymar Holt held it from 1049 to 1081 and taught Sir Roland Ashby, who has drilled the Iron Guard since 1075 and taught Garrick Harrow, Aldous Crane and Prince Harald.
ST01-05.philosophy: Read the shield while the horses close, lay the point three centimetres inside the rim along the grain, and let the wood split itself.
ST01-05.strengths: Splits linden shields seven passes in ten; exact, patient and deadly on the first pass.
ST01-05.weakness: It needs a canter and a steady point: a gallop spoils it, a steel-rimmed or hide-faced shield does not split, and a horse archer or a long fight undoes it.

techniques.name: Read the Board
techniques.desc: While the horses close, look at his shield, not his face: which way the grain runs and where the linden is thinnest.

techniques.name: Couch Late
techniques.desc: Keep the lance high until the last strides, so he sets his shield for a blow that comes from somewhere else.

techniques.name: Inside the Rim
techniques.desc: Lay the point three centimetres inside the rim along the grain, and the shield splits like kindling into the arm behind it.

techniques.name: For the Horse's Head
techniques.desc: If the lance breaks, draw and cut at his horse's head, not at him; a rearing horse ends the pass for you.

techniques.name: Seven in Ten
techniques.desc: Sir Roland's pass at a steady canter: the shield splits, the lance goes on into the forearm, and the man is down before he knows his shield failed.

maneuver.name: The Iron Guard's Pass
maneuver.desc: Knights couch late at a steady canter and aim at the shields, not the men; a line that trusted its linden finds it split.

ST01-06.name: The Moonless Way
ST01-06.origin: Maud Ravenscar the Owl rode 200 riders into the orc camp at Graknak on a moonless night in 988 and freed 400 captives; her web of foresters and pedlars became the empire's night patrols and her house the Wardens of the Oak Line. The Night School of Northmoor teaches what she did to anyone with quiet feet, and Corbin Ravenscar, who maps an enemy camp to the tent row in the dark of the moon, holds it now.
ST01-06.philosophy: Go out after dark, count everything, touch nothing, and be home before dawn; a fight means you were seen.
ST01-06.strengths: Silence, night movement, and reading a camp or a man before he knows anyone is there.
ST01-06.weakness: It is not a fighting art: caught by daylight or face to face with a formed enemy, the scout has a knife and a horse and should use the horse.

techniques.name: Dark of the Moon
techniques.desc: Wait for the moonless night and the downwind side; you see him long before he knows there is anything to see.

techniques.name: Soft Boots
techniques.desc: Step where the grass is wet and the twigs are rotten, and you are somewhere else by the time he swings.

techniques.name: The Sentry's Throat
techniques.desc: Hand over the mouth, knee in the back, knife under the ear: the sentry who would have shouted does not.

techniques.name: Home Before Dawn
techniques.desc: A scout who is found does not fight it out: break off, reach the horse and ride, and let the dark close behind you.

techniques.name: The Unseen Man
techniques.desc: Corbin Ravenscar's lesson: let him strike at where you were, and answer from where you are.

maneuver.name: Count the Fires
maneuver.desc: Night riders go out after dark, find the enemy's camp fires, count them and are home before dawn; the army that moves next morning moves knowing.

ST01-07.name: Stake-and-Bolt
ST01-07.origin: Aldmark's stake line was made on the Gordush: at Hartgate in May 1051 crossbows behind sharpened wood broke the Horde's relay waves, and the Stake Yard of Crossmarch has drilled the Gordush Stake-Men ever since. Captain Hilda Rook judges every newcomer by how fast he can set a stake and could build the Hartgate Box in her sleep.
ST01-07.philosophy: Ten minutes of mallet work buys an hour of killing: plant the stakes, shoot on the count, and never step in front of the wood.
ST01-07.strengths: Breaks charges of horse and orc relays; a drill that turns farmhands into a line in weeks.
ST01-07.weakness: Without ten minutes to plant it is a slow crossbow in the open; foot that walks through the stakes, or riders with ropes to pull them, unmake it.

techniques.name: Plant the Stake
techniques.desc: A stake sharpened at both ends, driven in at forty-five degrees with two blows of the mallet: he comes on and runs onto it.

techniques.name: Loose on the Count
techniques.desc: Hilda Rook's count: span, nock, aim, and loose together on the word, so the whole rank hits at once.

techniques.name: Behind the Wood
techniques.desc: Never step in front of your own stakes: let him tangle in them, and shoot or thrust while he is caught.

techniques.name: Bolt at the Horse
techniques.desc: Aim at the horse's chest, not the knight's shield; a knight on a dying horse is a man on the ground in front of your stakes.

techniques.name: The Second Rank Spans
techniques.desc: Three ranks loosing in turn, one shooting while two span: the bolt that kills him is the one he did not count on.

maneuver.name: The Hartgate Box
maneuver.desc: A wagon fort on three sides, a stake line on the fourth, crossbows on the wagons and behind the stakes, and heavy horse inside to sally through the gaps.

ST01-08.name: The Ironside Anvil
ST01-08.origin: Brand Ironside fell 9 m from a hayloft as a boy and walked away, and at the Millrun fords in 913 he took a Wind rider's mace on his ribs and got up. The iron bones have run in the imperial line since, and every Ironside is taught to take the blow that would break another man and answer through it, and taught as firmly never to wear mail near a river.
ST01-08.philosophy: Let him hit you: the blow that ends other men only bruises an Ironside, and he is open while it lands.
ST01-08.strengths: Trades blows no one else can afford; hard to knock down and hard to stop.
ST01-08.weakness: It invites the blow, so a thrust in the face or a giant's maul still kills; and an Ironside in mail near water sinks like an anvil.

techniques.name: Take It on the Ribs
techniques.desc: Let the mace land on your ribs instead of your shield, and strike under his arm while it is still coming down.

techniques.name: We Do Not Break
techniques.desc: The house's words, said through the teeth: what would have broken another man's bones has only bruised yours.

techniques.name: The Hayloft Fall
techniques.desc: Throw your whole weight on him and fall with him; you walked away from nine metres as a boy, and he will not.

techniques.name: The Millrun Ford
techniques.desc: Brand Ironside's way at the fords: walk into the blows and hit back harder than you were hit.

techniques.name: Oath on the Iron Ring
techniques.desc: Every Ironside swears on the ring and fights like a man who has sworn: take the worst he has, stand, and answer it.

maneuver.name: We Do Not Break
maneuver.desc: The Emperor's own banner stands in the line, and men who see an Ironside take a blow and stay up do not run.

ST01-09.name: The Harrow Bull
ST01-09.origin: Gunnar Harrow the Bull pulled an old orc war-chief from his horse bare-handed near Crossmarch in 1033 and held the Gordush ford with 300 house-men in 1049 until he died there. The Harrows marry their Harrowsett cousins to keep the bull-blood, and teach every son to win in the first minute with mace, lance and bare hands.
ST01-09.philosophy: Win in the first minute: close, seize and smash before the bull's breath runs out.
ST01-09.strengths: Terrible strength at the start; drags men from saddles; breaks shields and the arms behind them.
ST01-09.weakness: Blown in a long fight, hot-tempered, and the heart fails young; a patient man who backs away wins the second minute.

techniques.name: Bull's Rush
techniques.desc: Head down, shoulder first: the whole Harrow strength put into one step before he has his feet set.

techniques.name: Drag from the Saddle
techniques.desc: Gunnar the Bull pulled an orc war-chief off his horse bare-handed; his grandsons are taught to do it to anyone within reach of a fist.

techniques.name: Mace on the Rim
techniques.desc: A bull's swing with a flanged mace does not go round the shield; it goes through it, and through the arm behind it.

techniques.name: Red Bull
techniques.desc: The blood comes up and you stop feeling anything; it is the best minute any Harrow will have, so spend it.

techniques.name: Hold the Ford
techniques.desc: Gunnar's last hour at the Gordush: stand in the water with your house-men and kill whatever comes until your heart gives out.

maneuver.name: Bull Lances
maneuver.desc: Harrow's heavy lances go in first and hardest, led by men of the bull-blood while their first minute lasts.

ST01-10.name: Ravenscar Night Knife
ST01-10.origin: The Ravenscars were verderers of the Northmoor chase who tracked deer and poachers by starlight, and Maud the Owl made the owl-eyes a weapon at Graknak in 988. The Night School teaches anyone to move by night, but the knife-work of the blood is taught only to Ravenscar children, who ride at night before they ride by day and wear dark gauze at noon.
ST01-10.philosophy: Fight only where you can see and he cannot: put out his light, step in, and finish it with the short blade.
ST01-10.strengths: Sees a man at 200 m by starlight; ends fights in the dark before the other side has found its eyes.
ST01-10.weakness: Dazzled and in pain at noon: a fight by daylight, or a torch thrust in the face, leaves an owl-eyed fighter half blind.

techniques.name: Snuff the Lantern
techniques.desc: Put out the light first; in the dark an owl-eyed fighter sees the man, and the man sees nothing.

techniques.name: Under the Arm
techniques.desc: The short blade goes where the mail ends, up under the arm, and you are gone before he knows how badly he is cut.

techniques.name: Owl Eyes
techniques.desc: By starlight you see his weight shift before he swings, and you are already answering.

techniques.name: The Graknak Night
techniques.desc: Maud the Owl's ride of 988: come into the camp on a moonless night at a gallop and cut whatever stands up.

techniques.name: We See You
techniques.desc: The house's words: he cannot hide from you in the dark, and he learns it from a knife he never saw.

ST01-11.name: The Greymane Boarding Axe
ST01-11.origin: Grim Greymane beached his boats at the Glenwash mouth about 700, and his jarls have fought at the water's edge ever since: the salmon weirs, the amber beaches and the ford where Harald Ironside killed Jarl Ulf in 945. Jarl Sigurd carries an orc lance scar from the Gashmar fords, and his daughter Ingrid captains the 600 marines of the Cold Bay squadron with a boarding axe at her belt.
ST01-11.philosophy: Fight where land meets water: over the gunwale, on the shingle, waist-deep at the weir, where footing beats skill.
ST01-11.strengths: Boarding, wet footing and close axe work; hooks shields down and men over the side.
ST01-11.weakness: No reach and little armor, because men in mail drown; on dry open ground against horse it is a crew of sailors with hatchets.

techniques.name: Over the Gunwale
techniques.desc: Over the side with the axe first and the shield after: land on him, not beside him.

techniques.name: Beard on the Rim
techniques.desc: Hook his shield rim with the beard of the axe and pull it down, and his face is open for the second blow.

techniques.name: Axe at the Oars
techniques.desc: A hand-axe thrown across the closing water at the man who is still finding his feet.

techniques.name: The Tide Remembers
techniques.desc: Keep the water at your back and let him come to you over the wet stones; you know the footing of the weir, and he does not.

techniques.name: Waist-Deep
techniques.desc: In the river to the waist you are steady and he is not, and the axe falls on a man who is trying to keep his feet.

maneuver.name: Shingle Landing
maneuver.desc: Marines jump from the bows into knee-deep water and are among the enemy on the shingle before he has formed.

ST01-12.name: The Ringmere Banner
ST01-12.origin: Sir Ulf Ringmere carried the iron ring banner before Harald Ironside at his crowning in 951, and his line has carried it in every battle since. Sir Aldric Ringmere was cut down holding it in the river at the Gordush Bend in 1049, and Sir Edric carried it at the Gashmar Fords in 1070 with an orc spear through his thigh and never let it dip.
ST01-12.philosophy: One hand for the banner, one for the shield: you do not win the fight, you are still standing at the end of it.
ST01-12.strengths: Unshakable, hard to unseat, a rallying point that does not move.
ST01-12.weakness: One-handed and tied to the banner: it cannot chase or strike first, and every enemy on the field is looking for it.

techniques.name: Banner Up
techniques.desc: Shield on the left arm, pole socketed at the stirrup: first you learn to stay upright with one hand.

techniques.name: Pole Butt
techniques.desc: The iron-shod foot of the banner pole, driven into the face of the man reaching for the flag.

techniques.name: Spear Through the Thigh
techniques.desc: Sir Edric at the Gashmar Fords with an orc spear through his leg: the banner did not dip, and neither do you.

techniques.name: Rally to the Ring
techniques.desc: Men run to the banner when the line breaks; you stand still for them and cut down whoever followed them in.

maneuver.name: The Banner Does Not Fall
maneuver.desc: While the iron ring banner stands, the knights and foot around it rally to it instead of running.

ST02-01.name: The Lantern Ward
ST02-01.origin: Since Ash Night 759, when General Marcus Vell opened the Lantern Gate and the city was sacked for three days, the High Luminary's guard has been taught one thing first: a door does not open. The Lantern Guard in white and gold holds the Needle Court and the archive doors with tall lantern-painted shields and a straight sword held low, the way Captain Benedetto Sarno taught Leandro Fosca in a doorway from 1079.
ST02-01.philosophy: Stand in the gap, shield forward and point low, and let nothing hurry you out of it.
ST02-01.strengths: Doorways, stairs and gates; patience; turning a rush and wearing it out.
ST02-01.weakness: It never steps out: a man who goes round, a crossbow from the side, a feint that will not commit, or an open field leaves it standing behind a shield with nothing to hold.

school.name: The Lantern Yard of Needle Hill

techniques.name: Point Low
techniques.desc: A short thrust under the rim at the thigh, and the point comes straight back.

techniques.name: Shield Forward
techniques.desc: The tall shield takes it, and the low point answers from behind it.

techniques.name: Nothing Hurries Me
techniques.desc: You breathe, you watch, you do not move a hand's breadth out of the door.

techniques.name: The Door Does Not Open
techniques.desc: Ash Night's lesson: he spends himself on the shield and you cut him when he steps back.

techniques.name: Under the Lantern
techniques.desc: When he is spent, the thrust goes under the rim into the groin or the armpit.

maneuver.name: Gate Holding
maneuver.desc: Tall shields fill the gate or the door four deep, crossbows above, and nobody steps out after a beaten attacker.

ST02-02.name: The Forty-Day Spear
ST02-02.origin: When Tavian I ruled in 781 that Temple tenants owe forty days of service, he set knights over them to lead them, and the Sworn Tenant Spears have mustered on the Temple's farms ever since: 35,000 men in their villages, many of them in the Mirona hills where the Ashen are hunted. The Orvieni bannerets teach them at the muster yard of Mirona what forty days a year can teach: a spear, a shield, a hymn and the line.
ST02-02.philosophy: Forty days a year you are a wall: sing, keep the line, and let the knights do the killing.
ST02-02.strengths: Nerve and numbers in a line; holding ground; beating the hills for men in hiding.
ST02-02.weakness: Forty days of drill a year: slow, stiff and easily fooled alone, and the first man to break takes the hymn with him.

techniques.name: Spear and Hymn
techniques.desc: The pilgrim march sung under the breath keeps the feet and the spear steady.

techniques.name: Thrust Together
techniques.desc: Out on the word, back on the word, the way the whole file does it.

techniques.name: Wall of the Forty Days
techniques.desc: Shields locked, and the spear behind yours finds the man who hit you.

techniques.name: Beating the Hills
techniques.desc: Driving a man from hedge to hedge across the Mirona hills until his legs give.

techniques.name: Spears Forward, Sun Behind
techniques.desc: The rare day the line advances: slow, singing, and impossible to stop.

maneuver.name: Spear Wall
maneuver.desc: Tenant spears stand three deep behind locked shields and let the knights of the Noon ride round the flanks.

ST02-03.name: The Sun Road Ride
ST02-03.origin: After the Wind riders raided the Ostran coast in 893, Aurelius I wanted word of any danger on the Sun Road within a day, and in 896 he gave the posts to the Vialardi of Brunentia. Their riders change horses every fifteen kilometres on the Sun Road and the pilgrim roads, ride beside the pilgrim bands from one chapter house to the next, and learn at the Brunentia stables to fight only long enough to get the pilgrims, or the word, through.
ST02-03.philosophy: The word gets through: fight from the saddle only to open the road, then ride.
ST02-03.strengths: Endurance, speed, warning of ambush, a fighting retreat.
ST02-03.weakness: Light men on post horses with a light spear: they cannot hold ground or break foot, and a knight who catches them rides straight through.

techniques.name: Fresh Horse
techniques.desc: You change horses at the stage without stopping, and the new one carries you out of reach.

techniques.name: Spear in Passing
techniques.desc: A light spear under the arm at the gallop, never held long enough to lose it.

techniques.name: Ride Them Out
techniques.desc: Fifteen kilometres to a fresh horse is nothing to you and everything to the man chasing you.

techniques.name: Between the Stations
techniques.desc: You know where the road dips between chapter houses, and you were watching the ambush before it moved.

techniques.name: Through the Ambush
techniques.desc: Straight through the men in the road at a full gallop, and on to the next stage with the word.

maneuver.name: Pilgrim Road Escort
maneuver.desc: Riders ahead of and behind the column, chapter houses as stations, and a fast warning down the road at the first sign of ambush.

ST02-04.name: The Noon Mace
ST02-04.origin: High Luminary Clement I founded the Knights of the Sun on Return Day 626 to guard the Temple's granaries, estates and pilgrim roads, and their chapter house and riding yard on Needle Hill teaches mace and shield from the saddle with the sun behind you. Sir Ansaldo Verre taught Grand Master Bruno Castell from 1063 and Garin Solis from 1074; Solis, sober since 1094 and doing penance for the Mirona road, has held Noon Hall since 1100.
ST02-04.philosophy: Put the sun behind you, keep the shield up and the horse at the trot, and let the mace fall on the helmet in passing.
ST02-04.strengths: Breaking bones through mail from the saddle; choosing the light; vowed discipline in a line of sun-shields.
ST02-04.weakness: Afoot on a stair or a hill it is an old man with a club; the breath goes after two passes, and the sun does not always stand where you want it.

techniques.name: Mace on the Helm
techniques.desc: A flanged mace falling on the helmet in passing; mail does not stop what it does to the skull.

techniques.name: Sun at Your Back
techniques.desc: You chose the hour and the side; he is squinting, and you can see every move he makes.

techniques.name: Shield Up, Trot On
techniques.desc: The sun-painted shield takes the blow and the horse carries you past into the backswing.

techniques.name: Close Fast Afoot
techniques.desc: Unhorsed, you do not wait to be circled: you run in under his guard with the mace.

techniques.name: The Noon Charge
techniques.desc: The old drill the Knights keep from the desert clans: the charge at midday, the sun straight behind you.

maneuver.name: Noon Charge
maneuver.desc: The chapter waits for the hour and the side, then charges at a trot with the sun behind it into men who are dazzled and half spent in their mail.

ST02-05.name: The Dorata Count
ST02-05.origin: High Luminary Odo I founded the Crossbow Yard of Dorata on 1 April 811 so that paid crossbowmen, not tenants, would man the Valerian Wall in turns, and hired a Tessarian-trained sergeant, Bruno Quadrelli, to drill them; Quadrellis have drilled the Yard ever since. The Dorata Crossbows hold the Wall in war and the coast towers in peace, each master shooter with two or three loaders spanning and passing bows, and Captain Hugo Varr counts every bolt in the stores.
ST02-05.philosophy: Shoot by the count, in your turn, from behind stone, and let the loaders keep your hands full.
ST02-05.strengths: Steady aimed fire from walls and towers; bolts that go through mail; drill that does not break.
ST02-05.weakness: Rank and wall work: alone and in the open it is one slow shot and a short sword, and a fast man who closes before the span wins.

techniques.name: In Your Turn
techniques.desc: Loose on the count, step back, and the next rank looses behind you.

techniques.name: Bolt Through the Mail
techniques.desc: A square-headed bolt at a hundred and fifty kilograms of draw; rings do not stop it.

techniques.name: Stock and Short Sword
techniques.desc: The Yard's last lesson: when he is on you, the bow becomes a shield and the short sword comes out.

techniques.name: The Loader's Bow
techniques.desc: A spanned bow is passed into your hands the moment the first is empty.

techniques.name: The Count
techniques.desc: You have counted his steps and his breaths the way you count bolts, and you know what comes next.

techniques.name: From the Valerian Wall
techniques.desc: From a loophole of the wall that fell only to treachery: the best shot of a life, taken at leisure.

maneuver.name: Wall Crossbow Relay
maneuver.desc: Each master shooter on the wall has two or three loaders spanning and passing bows, so one loophole keeps up four to six shots a minute.

ST02-06.name: The Lorina Rail
ST02-06.origin: House Brennus walled Lorina four centuries before the Solen crown, lost its lord and 2,400 men at Lorina Hills in 2 BR, and has heard Solenne's children chant that Brennus burned the bread for eleven hundred years. It keeps Lorina Castle and the See's Lorina galleys, its children learn to row before they learn Old Solen, and Lady Petra fought off a Blackreef raider at the mouth of the bay in 1096 with the axe and shield the house teaches on its own decks and stairs.
ST02-06.philosophy: Keep what is yours: hold the stair, hold the rail, and make whoever comes for the bread pay at every step.
ST02-06.strengths: Stairs, rails and close quarters; a stubborn defence that hits back hard; rowers' strength.
ST02-06.weakness: A house that waits to be attacked: slow to carry the fight anywhere, and on open ground or against horse it is a short axe and a grudge.

techniques.name: Rower's Shoulders
techniques.desc: The pull you learned on a galley bench, put behind an axe.

techniques.name: Hold the Stair
techniques.desc: One step above him, shield on your knee, axe ready for the head that comes up.

techniques.name: Beard Over the Rim
techniques.desc: Hook his shield or his wrist with the axe's beard and pull him off his footing.

techniques.name: Brennus Burned the Bread
techniques.desc: Every Brennus has heard the chant; nobody who says it to one says it twice.

techniques.name: Over the Side
techniques.desc: Shield under his arm, shoulder in his chest, and he goes over the rail into the bay.

ST02-07.name: The Sea Gate Sword
ST02-07.origin: The Lantieri held the Sea Gate of Solenne for the emperors from 418. On Ash Night 759, when Marcus Vell opened the Lantern Gate, Captain Ottavio Lantieri held the Sea Gate until dawn and then fought his way up to the palace too late, and his widow kept the gilt spur he picked off the bedchamber floor. The poor, proud house still teaches its sons his old court way of sword and parrying dagger, and its son Valerio has twice been stopped from using it on a Vell.
ST02-07.philosophy: Old Solen manners with a blade: salute, measure, and keep the dagger ready for the moment the honourable part ends.
ST02-07.strengths: Parry with the left hand and strike with the right; stairs and gates; exact, formal duelling.
ST02-07.weakness: Punctilious to a fault: slow to begin, bound by honour, light in armor, and a shield wall or a crowd gives the parrying dagger nothing to do.

techniques.name: The Salute
techniques.desc: The old court salute, slow and correct, and you learn how he holds his blade while he waits for it to end.

techniques.name: The Left-Hand Parry
techniques.desc: The parrying dagger catches his blade and the sword is already moving.

techniques.name: Up the Palace Stair
techniques.desc: Ottavio's climb: step by step upward through men who hold the higher ground.

techniques.name: Until Dawn
techniques.desc: The Sea Gate held all night: no hurry, no step back, sword and dagger crossed in the gap.

techniques.name: The Gilt Spur
techniques.desc: Taught only to the heir, on the night the spur is shown to him: the sword high, the dagger low, both home.

ST03-01.name: The Muster-Stone Spear
ST03-01.origin: After the Black Cough killed one in five on the plain, Teodor the Patient let the free farmers of Valia keep their land rent-free for drill and war service, and since 918 the hundreds have gathered at the muster stone when the horn blows. They were caught in their blankets on the Brightwash in 1014, and they have taught the hidden spear line ever since: lie flat behind a crest or in a sunken road, let the horse come on, and rise with spears set thirty paces in front of it.
ST03-01.philosophy: Stand with your neighbours, let the enemy come onto the point, and never be the first man to run.
ST03-01.strengths: Holding a line, stopping horse, ambush from the grass; cheap and many.
ST03-01.weakness: Farmers, not swordsmen: slow, predictable, lost alone, and a man who gets inside the point has a free hand.

techniques.name: Set the Butt
techniques.desc: Butt to the ground, point at his chest; let him do the running.

techniques.name: Rise from the Grass
techniques.desc: You lay still and watched him come; now you stand up thirty paces in front of him.

techniques.name: Shoulder to Shoulder
techniques.desc: Shield against your neighbour's shield, and the spear comes out between them.

techniques.name: The Horse Stopper
techniques.desc: The point goes into the horse's chest and the rider comes over its head.

techniques.name: When the Horn Blows
techniques.desc: The whole hundred steps forward at once, and you are its front.

maneuver.name: Hidden Spear Line
maneuver.desc: The hundreds lie flat behind a crest or in a sunken road while horse draws the enemy on, then rise at the horn and set spears in front of the pursuers.

ST03-02.name: The Dawn Field Sword
ST03-02.origin: Duels have been banned inside Varenna's walls since 1071, the year Cesare Montaro laughed off a thrust under the ribs and died of it four days later, so the city's quarrels are settled at dawn on Crown Gate Field outside the walls. The fencing yards of Bluewater teach the heavy Varennan blade for those mornings: the falling cut to the hands, the dagger at the hilt and the habit of ending it in two passes.
ST03-02.philosophy: Commit early and hard: cut the hand, open a vein, and finish before the sun is up.
ST03-02.strengths: Fast, bloody endings; cuts to the hands; wounds that keep bleeding.
ST03-02.weakness: Everything is committed early, so a patient counter-fencer eats it alive; no shield, no armor, and no plan for a second man.

techniques.name: The Falling Cut
techniques.desc: The heavy Varennan blade dropped from above the head, all weight and no art.

techniques.name: To the Hands
techniques.desc: Cut the fingers on the hilt, and the sword is yours to worry about no longer.

techniques.name: Dagger at the Hilt
techniques.desc: Blades locked at the cross, the left hand finds the dagger and his side.

techniques.name: First Blood
techniques.desc: A cut he did not see to a place he cannot bind, and the grass goes dark.

techniques.name: Under the Ribs
techniques.desc: The thrust that killed Cesare Montaro, taught on the field where it was done.

ST03-03.name: The Lion Marine Axe
ST03-03.origin: Lothar I built the royal yards in 783 and the Lion Fleet has carried marines ever since, but their art was made in the Corsair War, when Blackreef's fire-rafts burned eleven galleys at Gull Isle in 1053 and the men who lived were the ones who could cut a burning boat free with an axe. Captain Marta Rema drills the 6,000 Lion Marines at Varenna, Tibata and the Isle of Bells: one bolt across the gap, then over the rail without mail, because mail drowns.
ST03-03.philosophy: Shoot once across the gap, then go over the rail with the axe before they have counted you.
ST03-03.strengths: Boarding, hooking shields, fighting in a crush on a wet deck.
ST03-03.weakness: Fights in shirts because mail drowns: ashore on open ground they are light foot with short weapons, and a horseman rides them down.

techniques.name: Bolt Across the Gap
techniques.desc: One bolt from the rail while the hulls grind together.

techniques.name: Hook the Rim
techniques.desc: The beard of the axe over the shield's edge, and a hard pull down.

techniques.name: Over the Rail
techniques.desc: Feet on the rail, shield first, and you land on top of whoever is there.

techniques.name: Cut Her Free
techniques.desc: The stroke that cut burning grapnels at Gull Isle, put into a man instead of a rope.

techniques.name: Lion of the Deck
techniques.desc: Down the gangway with the deck rolling under you, rim and axe together.

maneuver.name: Boarding Rush
maneuver.desc: A crossbow volley across the gap, grapnels over, and the marines go over the bow in shirts before the enemy can form on his own deck.

ST03-04.name: The Albano Hill Ride
ST03-04.origin: The Albano Hill Riders keep the dry western hills of the Ashland March on small hard ponies bred at the Torossa studs, against bandits and the Hael Hounds that tore apart the king's surveyors in April 1099. They retook Albano with Vittor Montaro after the granary rising of 1093, and their yard teaches what the March needs: ride light, throw from the saddle, cut a horse's hocks and be gone before a lance arrives.
ST03-04.philosophy: Never be where the lance arrives: throw, wheel, throw again, and let the hills tire him out.
ST03-04.strengths: Javelins from the saddle, hamstringing, wearing an enemy down, the chase.
ST03-04.weakness: Light men on light horses: a set spear or a knight who catches them is the end, and on foot in the mud they are hunters with a knife.

techniques.name: Javelin at the Canter
techniques.desc: Thrown overhand from a pony at the canter, then the pony turns away.

techniques.name: Turn Away
techniques.desc: The pony wheels on its hocks and his blow cuts air.

techniques.name: Cut the Hocks
techniques.desc: Low and from behind, at the leg of the horse or the man.

techniques.name: Three Javelins
techniques.desc: One, two, three before he has closed the distance, the March way.

techniques.name: Ride Him Into the Ground
techniques.desc: Hours of chasing end here, with the spear in the back of a blown man.

maneuver.name: Skirmish Screen
maneuver.desc: Hill riders spread loose ahead of the army, throw, hide the deployment and fall back through the gaps when the lines close, then run down the beaten.

ST03-05.name: The Lion Chain
ST03-05.origin: Roderic the Lionheart founded the Hall of the Lion at Varenna in 866 to give the crown knights who fought for it rather than for the barons, and his knights broke the Wind riders on the Coast Road in 896. Its masters are the Grasso and Montaro families: Bruno Montaro held it until the gangrened foot killed him in 1062, Sir Lucio Grasso after him, and since 1094 Matteo Grasso, who unhorses one rider and has the lance couched for the next.
ST03-05.philosophy: Ride straight at him on open ground, trust the first shock, and have the lance level again before he hits the ground.
ST03-05.strengths: The couched lance, the second rider in one charge, the long-armed Valdane thrust; the best heavy horse in the world.
ST03-05.weakness: Bad on foot in the mud; a set spear line, stakes, a terrace wall or a crossbow at sixty paces undo it, and it has little for a man who will not be charged.

techniques.name: Couch and Ride
techniques.desc: Walk, trot, canter, and the lance comes down under the arm in the last fifty paces.

techniques.name: The Rising Point
techniques.desc: A hand's breadth higher than the Hall teaches, rising over the rim to lift him out of the saddle.

techniques.name: Draw Back and Couch
techniques.desc: The lance rides the shock, comes back a forearm's length, and is level again three strides on.

techniques.name: The Valdane Thrust
techniques.desc: The long-armed thrust of the Lionheart's house, taught to every knight of the Hall.

techniques.name: The Second Rider
techniques.desc: The first man goes over the crupper and the same lance takes the man behind him.

maneuver.name: The Lion Charge
maneuver.desc: Knights knee to knee at the walk, trot and canter, lances couched only in the last hundred paces, into a line that has already begun to waver.

ST03-06.name: The Terrace Crossbow
ST03-06.origin: The Coast Road taught Varenna in 896 that dry-stone terrace walls every twenty or forty paces stop horsemen from wheeling, crossbows shoot from behind them, and knights wait for the moment. The Terrace School of Castella has taught that lesson to the realm's crossbowmen ever since, borrowing the Arcella pike drill for the men in front and the Dorata windlass drill for the bows; Ilario Monti, patient and methodical, teaches it now by endless repetition.
ST03-06.philosophy: Make the ground fight for you: wall, stake, ditch, then one aimed bolt at a time while he breaks himself on the stone.
ST03-06.strengths: Aimed bolts from cover, field works, stopping horse, patience.
ST03-06.weakness: It never learned the open field: take away the wall and the stakes and it is a slow shot and a short sword; rain slackens the strings, and a fast charge before the span wins.

techniques.name: Shot from the Wall
techniques.desc: Bow on the coping stone, head down, one bolt into the man who is coming.

techniques.name: Behind the Stone
techniques.desc: Crouch behind the wall or the pavise and let the blow hit stone.

techniques.name: Stake and Wait
techniques.desc: He comes onto the sharpened stake you drove at forty-five degrees, and you strike while he is caught.

techniques.name: Aimed at Sixty Paces
techniques.desc: The range at which a bolt goes through mail, and the bow held still until he reaches it.

techniques.name: The Knights Go Now
techniques.desc: You have watched him spend himself on the terraces; you know the moment before he does.

maneuver.name: Terrace Wall Defense
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen behind dry-stone terrace walls and stakes shoot riders who cannot wheel, while the knights wait behind for the moment to charge.

ST03-07.name: The Lionblood Reach
ST03-07.origin: Roderic the Lionheart, the first of his house with the long Lionblood arm, taught his children to use the reach that a weak heart pays for, and in 891 made the Rule of the Long Blood to keep it inside the house. The Valdanes of Castella kept the art alive through the long-lived kings who lacked the blood, and Ettore of Castella brought both the reach and the art back to the throne when he married Lucilla in 1044.
ST03-07.philosophy: Keep him at the end of your arm, where he cannot reach you, and finish it before your heart is asked for more.
ST03-07.strengths: Reach on foot and in the saddle; keeping a man out; short, clean endings.
ST03-07.weakness: The long fight: an art built around a heart that fails tires fast, and a man who gets inside the reach or drags it out has it beaten.

techniques.name: Arm's Length
techniques.desc: The point held out where his blade cannot follow it.

techniques.name: Reach and Hold
techniques.desc: The house's words: he stops on your point, and you answer before he can close.

techniques.name: The Coast Road Wait
techniques.desc: The Lionheart waited behind the terraces until the riders bunched; so do you, breathing slowly.

techniques.name: The Long Blood
techniques.desc: A thrust from a distance no other man's arm would cover.

techniques.name: Lionheart
techniques.desc: Everything at once, as the first Lionblood king did, and the heart pays for it after.

ST03-08.name: The Laughing Run
ST03-08.origin: Cesare Montaro, Who Bled Laughing, crushed the Serafin rising at Venina in May 1049 with three wounds he laughed off, and raised the Laughing Company the next year from his own cousins with the blood that feels little pain. The cousins are fostered at Vitia and drilled by Ottavia Montaro, who has every man stripped and searched by surgeons after each fight, because the art that will not feel a wound does not see one either.
ST03-08.philosophy: Run at the line laughing, hit it with the rim, and be inside the spears before they believe what they are seeing.
ST03-08.strengths: Shock, fear in the enemy, fighting on with wounds that stop other men.
ST03-08.weakness: It does not notice it is dying: a set spear line bleeds it, archers shoot for the legs, and every Montaro needs friends to pull him out.

techniques.name: Laugh at It
techniques.desc: The blow lands, and you laugh, and he does not know what to do next.

techniques.name: Rim First
techniques.desc: You hit his shield at a run with the edge of yours, not the face.

techniques.name: Over the Shield
techniques.desc: On the second step the sword goes over his shield into his face.

techniques.name: Inside the Spears
techniques.desc: Straight at the points without slowing, and inside them in the first three seconds, laughing.

techniques.name: Who Bled Laughing
techniques.desc: Cesare's way: three wounds, no pause, and the line broken before anyone counts them.

maneuver.name: Laughing Charge
maneuver.desc: A dense column of mailed foot runs at a shield wall with Montaro cousins laughing at its point, and does not stop when the arrows land.

ST03-09.name: The Lion Banner Ward
ST03-09.origin: On 14 April 896, among the olive terraces of the Coast Road, the crossbow sergeant Pello Sabrini picked the Lionheart's fallen banner out of the dust and held it on a terrace wall until the knights charged past him. His sons have carried it since, at the Brightwash in 1014, where the bearer died covering the retreat, and at Gull Isle in 1053, and every Sabrini boy is raised in the Lion Hall to stand where the king stands.
ST03-09.philosophy: Where it goes, we go: one hand for the banner, one for the shield, and nobody reaches the man beside you.
ST03-09.strengths: Holding a spot, covering another man, a long steady guard.
ST03-09.weakness: It will not chase and will not leave its post: an enemy who walks away, feints, or goes for the man it guards sets the terms.

techniques.name: Shield High
techniques.desc: The shield up where the banner and your face both need it.

techniques.name: The Banner Wall
techniques.desc: Pello's terrace wall: you take it on the shield and cut back past the rim.

techniques.name: Rim to the Face
techniques.desc: When he leans in for the banner, the iron rim meets his teeth.

techniques.name: Covering the Retreat
techniques.desc: The Brightwash bearer's last hour: step back, turn him, step back, and make him pay for every pace.

techniques.name: Where It Goes, We Go
techniques.desc: Nothing gets past you to the banner, and what tries does not get up.

ST03-10.name: Eighteen Feet of Answer
ST03-10.origin: After the Black Cough emptied the Northern Lakes of knights, Galen IV the Fair let the Castella towns raise long spears from the freed farmers, and the lake fisherman Nerio Arcella, who had served in Morhaven, drilled them in square blocks with eighteen-foot pikes. The post has been hereditary since 931, and the Castella Long Spears held the Brightwash crossing in 1014 while the camp fled, the one Varennan company that did not run.
ST03-10.philosophy: The point arrives first: make every man and horse come onto it, and never let the block break to chase.
ST03-10.strengths: Reach, stopping horse, holding a crossing or a bridge.
ST03-10.weakness: Alone a pike is a pole: once a man is inside the point, or broken ground, a barge or a wood breaks the block, it has nothing left.

techniques.name: Level Pikes
techniques.desc: Eighteen feet of ash between you and him, and he has to come down it.

techniques.name: Push of Pike
techniques.desc: Everyone leans at once, and the man in front goes backwards.

techniques.name: Ground the Butt
techniques.desc: Butt under the foot, point at the horse's breast, and his charge does the killing.

techniques.name: Hold the Crossing
techniques.desc: The Brightwash drill: the camp runs behind you and you do not look round.

maneuver.name: Pike Hedge
maneuver.desc: Square blocks of eighteen-foot pikes, crossbowmen behind, set across a crossing or a road; horses will not go onto it.

ST04-01.name: The Lucernan Answer
ST04-01.origin: Lucerna will not arm its poor and will not march, but its council sons walk the canal paths with a light sword, and the fencing halls of the Council Quarter teach the one thing a merchant needs: to answer a committed attack in a single movement and be home by dark. The master Enzo Faro taught the duel to Sir Rinaldo Vasco, now Captain of Varenna's Lion Guard, and his son Tullio keeps the hall and its boast.
ST04-01.philosophy: Let him commit, and be already answering: the parry and the thrust are one movement, inside his blade.
ST04-01.strengths: Counters, reading a committed attacker, short and decisive exchanges.
ST04-01.weakness: It waits to be attacked: a man who refuses to commit, a shield and patience, or a crowd gives it nothing to answer, and it is over in two passes or in trouble.

school.name: The Fencing Halls of the Council Quarter

techniques.name: Inside the Blade
techniques.desc: The parry slides along his blade and is a thrust before it stops.

techniques.name: The Quick Thrust
techniques.desc: A light blade straight to the face and back, from the canal-path guard.

techniques.name: Let Him Drink First
techniques.desc: As a Lucernan host does with the cup: you offer, he takes it, and you see what it does to him.

techniques.name: Bind and Take
techniques.desc: The left hand closes on his wrist in the bind, and his sword is suddenly a long way off.

techniques.name: Two Passes
techniques.desc: The first pass shows you his attack; the second is the answer, and it is over.

techniques.name: Faro's Answer
techniques.desc: The answer that begins on his breath, before the cut: the thrust that taught a Lion Guard captain the duel.

ST04-02.name: The Quarter Band Drill
ST04-02.origin: Lucerna will not arm its poor, but it arms its citizens: each of the six quarters keeps a band of crossbowmen and spears that drills once a month on its own quay, and every citizen drawn by lot for the galleys learns the same drill first. The lagoon is the wall, so the bands are taught to hold what a lagoon city has instead of gates: bridges, quays and water gates.
ST04-02.philosophy: Shoot from the quay, the bridge or the water gate, then hold it with the spear until the galleys come home.
ST04-02.strengths: Bridges, quays and water gates; a shot and then a spear; numbers who know their own streets.
ST04-02.weakness: A monthly drill: citizen soldiers who have never been tested, slow to span, and lost in the open or against professionals.

school.name: The Quay Musters of the Six Quarters

techniques.name: Shot from the Water Gate
techniques.desc: From behind the arch of a house's water gate, at the boat or the man on the quay.

techniques.name: Hold the Bridge
techniques.desc: A canal bridge is two men wide; the spear makes it one.

techniques.name: Into the Canal
techniques.desc: Shove with the shaft, and the canal does the rest of the work.

techniques.name: The Second Bow
techniques.desc: Your neighbour spanned while you shot, and passes you his bow.

techniques.name: The Six Quarters
techniques.desc: Every quay has its band, and every band knows where the next one stands: nobody gets far.

maneuver.name: Bridges and Quays
maneuver.desc: The quarter bands hold the bridges, quays and water gates of their own quarter, crossbows on the rooftops and spears at the crossings.

ST04-03.name: The Arsenal Deck
ST04-03.origin: Doge Enrico Bassan founded the Arsenal in 762, Doge Tomaso Salvi widened it, and it can build a galley in twenty days; in its yard the marines and rowers learn oar, sea legs and fighting on a pitching deck. Master Iacopo Rizzo, a thick-armed marine with an axe scar on his jaw and singed eyebrows, drills about 300 at a time in ramming, the crossbow over the gap and the axe on the gangway, and hints in taverns at a fire that water will not put out.
ST04-03.philosophy: The deck moves and you move with it: brace for the ram, strike as the ship rolls toward him, and never be the man in mail when she sinks.
ST04-03.strengths: Footing on a pitching deck, the shock of the ram, crossbow and axe at close quarters.
ST04-03.weakness: A sea art: on dry land, on horseback or in a long fight on open ground it is a sailor with an axe, and in a shirt it dies to one good cut.

techniques.name: Sea Legs
techniques.desc: Knees soft, weight low; the deck heaves and you are still standing.

techniques.name: Bolt over the Gap
techniques.desc: Across the closing water, at the man with the grapnel.

techniques.name: When the Ram Strikes
techniques.desc: You braced for the beak and he did not; everyone falls but you.

techniques.name: Roll With Her
techniques.desc: You let the swell carry you off his line and come back with it.

techniques.name: Down the Gangway
techniques.desc: Rizzo's own way onto an enemy deck: first, loud, and swinging.

maneuver.name: Galley Ramming
maneuver.desc: The rowers sprint the last two hundred paces and drive the beak into the enemy's side, and the marines are over the bow while his deck is still on its back.

ST04-04.name: Take Her Whole
ST04-04.origin: On New Year's Day 1044, when Lucerna and Ostra seized 38 Tessarian ships in their harbors, the shipmaster Bruno Dandin led the boarding party that took the largest of them without a death, and the Great Council gave his family the Lagoon Marines. The Dandin way is his: over the rail before the crew can arm, and take the ship whole, because a dead crew is a lawsuit in the Harbor Court and a burned cargo is a loss.
ST04-04.philosophy: Be over the rail before they are on their feet, and take the ship and its men alive: cargo is worth more than glory.
ST04-04.strengths: Speed and surprise, disarming, taking men alive.
ST04-04.weakness: It wants prizes, not kills: against a man who will fight to the death, or one already armed and waiting, the merciful hand is a slow one.

techniques.name: Grapnel and Go
techniques.desc: The hook bites, the line goes taut, and you are already climbing.

techniques.name: Shoot the Helmsman
techniques.desc: One bolt at the man on the steering oar, and the ship is yours to steer.

techniques.name: Before They Stand
techniques.desc: On deck while they are still reaching for their weapons, and the first man goes flat.

techniques.name: Strike the Hand
techniques.desc: The axe's back across his knuckles; a man without a weapon is a prisoner, not a corpse.

techniques.name: Knee in the Captain's Back
techniques.desc: Bruno Dandin's prize: the captain on his own deck with your knee in his back, and nobody dead.

ST04-05.name: Quiet Waters
ST04-05.origin: The Vannis planted figs and salted fish at Tibenza and knew its smuggling coves before Lucerna had a Night Watch, and since Vanni men began to lead it they have taught their sons the harbor police's trade: the patrol boat, the boathook, the crossbow and the knife. Ser Marco Vanni joined the Watch at twenty and has been its Lord since 1094, and in Lucerna treason still ends the old way, with a quiet drowning in the lagoon at night.
ST04-05.philosophy: No lights, no noise: hook him from the boat, put him in the water, and let the lagoon finish the argument.
ST04-05.strengths: Night work on canals and boats; hooking, drowning and the knife; surprise.
ST04-05.weakness: It needs the dark and the water: in daylight on a dry street it is a boathook and a knife against a man who saw you coming.

techniques.name: Lantern Out
techniques.desc: The boat's lamp goes dark, and he is the only one who cannot see.

techniques.name: Bolt from the Patrol Boat
techniques.desc: From a dark boat under the bridge, at the man running along the quay.

techniques.name: Hook from the Boat
techniques.desc: The boathook takes him by the collar or the ankle from two paces of black water.

techniques.name: Quiet Waters
techniques.desc: The house's words: his head under the canal, your weight on his back, and no sound at all.

techniques.name: Knife in the Dark
techniques.desc: Under the arm or into the kidney, from a man he took for a boatman.

ST05-01.name: The Rolled Bow
ST05-01.origin: Aldred III the Bowman made the Butts Law in 894, and every free man of Ashmere has shot on Sunday afternoons since or paid an ember. The yeomen on the rolls of the Crown Vale, the Ashwater, the Stag Downs and the uplands, about 22,000 of them, learn the yew war bow from boyhood, and the Uplands Butts at Brightkeep, where the yew carts arrive, teach the stake, the volley and the mallet.
ST05-01.philosophy: Drive your stake, nock on the horn, and put twelve heavy arrows a minute into the air before the charge reaches the wood.
ST05-01.strengths: Weight of heavy arrows at 200 m; bodkins through mail at 60–100 m; stakes and a hillside make a fortress of a field.
ST05-01.weakness: Rain on the strings, night, horse on the flanks; once a man is inside the stakes the bowman has a falchion, a mallet and a sore back.

techniques.name: Nock on the Horn
techniques.desc: Arrow on the string when the horn blows, loose on the second blast: the first thing the village butts teach.

techniques.name: Drive the Stake
techniques.desc: Every bowman carries a stake and a mallet; plant it in front of you and let the horse find it.

techniques.name: Heavy Arrow at Sixty
techniques.desc: A bodkin from a 90 kg yew bow at sixty metres goes through mail; you wait until he is that close.

techniques.name: Mallet and Falchion
techniques.desc: When the knight is down among the stakes, the bowmen leave their bows and go out to him with mallets and falchions.

techniques.name: Twelve a Minute
techniques.desc: Arrow after arrow from the bag at your feet, twelve in a minute, until what is in front of you is no longer a charge.

maneuver.name: Longbow Volley
maneuver.desc: Bowmen behind stakes or on a slope loose together on a horn, 10–12 aimed arrows a minute at 200 m; a charge is emptied in two minutes.

ST05-02.name: The Hedge Spear
ST05-02.origin: Ashmere raises 10,000 Hedge Spears from its shire musters, and they are drilled for the country they fight in: sunken lanes, hedgerows and the far side of a crest, where the bowmen draw the enemy on and the spears rise thirty paces in front of him. Queen Elsbeth's night march to the Brightwash in May 1014 ended with Ashmere spearmen coming out of the dark at 8,000 sleeping Varennans.
ST05-02.philosophy: Lie still in the hedge until the horn, then stand up where he did not know a man could be.
ST05-02.strengths: Ambush and surprise; a set point against horse at close range; deadly in lanes and hedged fields.
ST05-02.weakness: It needs cover and a lure: on an open field by daylight against a formed enemy it is a levy spear, and scouts sent ahead ruin it.

techniques.name: Lie Still
techniques.desc: Flat in the hedge bottom with the spear along your body: patience is the first weapon of the shire musters.

techniques.name: Rise at Thirty Paces
techniques.desc: Stand up out of the ditch thirty paces in front of a man who thought the field was empty.

techniques.name: Set in the Lane
techniques.desc: In a sunken lane a horseman can only come one way, and that way ends on your point.

techniques.name: Spear through the Hedge
techniques.desc: Thrust through the thorn where he cannot see the point coming and cannot reach the man holding it.

techniques.name: The Brightwash Dawn
techniques.desc: Elsbeth's spearmen after the night march: out of the dark at first light, into men still rolling out of their blankets.

maneuver.name: Hidden Spear Line
maneuver.desc: Spearmen lie flat in a sunken lane or behind a crest while the bowmen draw the enemy on; at the horn they rise 30–50 m in front of the pursuers and set spears.

ST05-03.name: The Downhill Falchion
ST05-03.origin: Ashmere fights on a hillside, and its 6,000 Men-at-Arms of the Shires are the hinge between the bow blocks: falchion and buckler, mail over a padded jack, standing where the slope makes the enemy climb to them. The Lord Wardens teach it at Ashwell Tower on the oldest lesson of the hilltop stand, that a man climbing a steep slope in mail is spent twice as fast.
ST05-03.philosophy: Make him climb to you, let him arrive tired, and cut down onto him with the whole weight of the slope.
ST05-03.strengths: A heavy chopping cut from above; wears out climbers; holds the gap between bow blocks.
ST05-03.weakness: Downhill is its whole art: on flat ground the falchion is a short cleaver, and an enemy who will not climb leaves it standing on a hill with no water.

school.name: The Hill School of Ashwell Tower

techniques.name: Make Him Climb
techniques.desc: Stay above him on the slope and give ground uphill; every step he takes after you costs him twice.

techniques.name: Buckler in the Face
techniques.desc: Show him the falchion and punch him in the face with the buckler boss instead.

techniques.name: Cut from Above
techniques.desc: The falchion is a heavy cleaver; swung down from a step above him, it breaks a collarbone through mail.

techniques.name: The Hinge Holds
techniques.desc: You stand in the gap between two bow blocks; if you step back the bowmen die, so you do not, and you answer every blow.

techniques.name: Downhill Charge
techniques.desc: When the climbers are spent, the men-at-arms come down the hill on them with the whole slope behind every cut.

maneuver.name: Hilltop Stand
maneuver.desc: The foot hold the crest and make the enemy climb in mail; when he arrives spent, they come down on him.

ST05-04.name: The Silver Arrow
ST05-04.origin: Aldred III's Butts Law of 894 made the King's Butts below Ashmere Castle the kingdom's target, and Queen Elsbeth put the first 1,200 bowmen in royal red in 1021. Sir Hereward Ashdown taught the war bow there to Hugh Fletcher from the age of seven; Sir Hugh, Master of the King's Bowmen, holds the Butts now, and his best pupil, Perrin Hollowell, holds the Return Day silver arrow.
ST05-04.philosophy: Strength to draw 100 kg, eyes to judge range and wind, and one voice to tell twelve hundred men both.
ST05-04.strengths: Aimed shooting at 200 m, seven arrows in ten in a 30 m box; reads range and wind; bodkins through mail up close.
ST05-04.weakness: A master bowman with a sword is a big man who has never killed; in a hall, in rain or at night the art has nothing special left.

techniques.name: Judge the Wind
techniques.desc: Wet a finger, watch the grass and the flags: the Butts teach you to read the wind, and a man reads much the same.

techniques.name: Draw a Hundred Kilos
techniques.desc: Back, not arms: the full draw of a war bow that took you since the age of seven to learn to bend.

techniques.name: Bowman's Back
techniques.desc: A man who draws a war bow every Sunday has a back like a plough-ox; take hold of him and throw him.

techniques.name: Range and Wind
techniques.desc: Sir Hugh's one shout sets range and wind for a thousand bows; for one man, it tells you exactly where he will be.

techniques.name: The Return Day Shot
techniques.desc: Seven arrows in ten in a thirty-metre box at 220 metres, and this one in the eye of the man you chose.

maneuver.name: The Called Volley
maneuver.desc: One voice sets range and wind for 1,200 bowmen; seven arrows in ten fall in a 30 m box at 220 m.

ST05-05.name: The Cinderwell Gate
ST05-05.origin: Sir Tobin Cinderwell held the 3 m gate of Ashmere Castle from dawn to dusk against 2,000 Hawkmarch rebels in April 976 with a shield and twelve guards, seven of whom died. King Cedric made him Captain of the King's Guard and gave him Kingsdale, where his kin have taught the shield and the gap ever since; Lord Tobias Cinderwell, blind now, has trained every royal shield-bearer for forty years and judges the gate test by ear.
ST05-05.philosophy: Do not go to him; stand where he must come to you, and let the gap do your fighting.
ST05-05.strengths: Holds a doorway, stair or breach against many; rim and thrust; a front that changes before it tires.
ST05-05.weakness: Slow to turn and loath to step out: a man who goes round, or shoots from above, beats it.

techniques.name: Rim and Thrust
techniques.desc: Take the blow on the shield, and thrust past its rim at the man who made it.

techniques.name: Change the Front
techniques.desc: Every two minutes the front man steps back and the next steps up; alone in a doorway, you take the half-step back yourself and breathe.

techniques.name: The Gate Test
techniques.desc: The Yard's test is an hour in a doorway against a ram; after that, a man with a sword is a light thing to stand against.

techniques.name: Dawn to Dusk
techniques.desc: Tobin held from dawn to dusk because he never wasted a blow: read him, wait, and spend only the answer.

techniques.name: Tobin's Gate
techniques.desc: Three metres of gateway, a shield and twelve guards against two thousand: whoever comes into the gap is thrown back out of it.

maneuver.name: Gate Holding
maneuver.desc: A few heavy shield-men fill a gateway, stair or breach so that only two or three enemies can strike at once, changing the front every two minutes.

ST05-06.name: The Wakeful Bow
ST05-06.origin: Aldred Ashford, the first king, slept four hours a night and spent the rest riding between his rivals, and about half his line has carried the Wakeful blood since. Every Ashford child draws a bow at seven and every Ashford king shoots at the Butts on Return Day; the house's own art is the bow and sword of a family that is awake when its enemies are not, from Elsbeth's night march to the Brightwash to Rowena's command of the King's Bowmen.
ST05-06.philosophy: Be awake when he is not: march by night, strike at first light, and never let the tired man rest.
ST05-06.strengths: Tirelessness; the dawn strike; bow and sword turned on a fighter who has not slept.
ST05-06.weakness: The Wakeful bold fit: it chases too far and rides through sleet, and the black mood afterwards leaves an Ashford slow and careless.

techniques.name: Four Hours' Sleep
techniques.desc: Aldred the Founder slept four hours a night; his blood fights its third hour as fresh as its first.

techniques.name: Return Day Shot
techniques.desc: Every Ashford king shoots at the Butts on Return Day, and every Ashford child has shot there since the age of seven.

techniques.name: First Light
techniques.desc: Come at him in the grey hour when he has not slept and you have; you see his mistake before he makes it.

techniques.name: The Bold Fit
techniques.desc: The Wakeful blood's bold mood: ride at him with no thought of the cost, as Elsbeth chased too far at the Brightwash.

techniques.name: The Night March
techniques.desc: Elsbeth's march of 1014: all night without lights or talk, and at dawn you are already among them.

maneuver.name: The Night March
maneuver.desc: The army marches by night without lights or talk and falls on the enemy at first light, when he is asleep, cold and unarmed.

ST05-07.name: The Long Stand
ST05-07.origin: Tobin Cinderwell was the first of his yeoman family with the oak tendons, a stiff, slow boy who carried a plough-ox yoke at fourteen. The Shield Yard teaches the gate to any guard, but the blood is taught its own way at home: in 1087 a Hawkmarch retainer challenged Sir Owain, who stood still until the man tired and then broke his arm.
ST05-07.philosophy: Hold the shield up longer than he can hold his sword up, then take his arm.
ST05-07.strengths: Endless stamina under the shield; a strapped shield that cannot be torn away; a crushing hold at the end.
ST05-07.weakness: Stiff joints and slow to turn; a torn tendon never heals right, and anyone quick enough to go round it is never caught.

techniques.name: The Ox Yoke
techniques.desc: Tobin carried an ox yoke on his shoulders at fourteen; the children of the blood carry the shield the same way, all day.

techniques.name: Stand Until He Tires
techniques.desc: Sir Owain's answer to the Hawkmarch challenger: stand still behind the shield and let him wear himself out on it.

techniques.name: Strap and Grip
techniques.desc: The shield is strapped to the forearm and will not be torn away; when he hooks it he has hooked an oak, and his own blade comes loose.

techniques.name: Break the Arm
techniques.desc: When he is spent, take his sword arm in both hands and break it; the fight is over and nobody has to die.

ST05-08.name: The Ashdown Hound-Spear
ST05-08.origin: Wat Ashdown came up from the southern downs under the Ashwater Charter in 798, and his family has kept the rule that is still its motto: one child to the hall, one to the bow. Their bow-children became sergeants of the King's Bowmen, and Sir Godwin Ashdown hunted Ashen cultists and Hael Hounds in the Stag Downs for twenty years with a boar spear, a bow and a long knife.
ST05-08.philosophy: Shoot the lead hound, brace for the pack, and hum the hall-song under your breath so your hands stay still.
ST05-08.strengths: Steady against beasts and rushes; bow, then spear, then knife in one unbroken sequence; calm.
ST05-08.weakness: A hunter's art, not a duelist's: against a swordsman who feints and will not charge, the braced spear waits for a rush that never comes.

techniques.name: Shoot the Lead Hound
techniques.desc: The pack follows the lead hound; drop it with the first arrow and the rest come on in disorder.

techniques.name: Brace for the Pack
techniques.desc: Kneel, brace the boar spear and let the rush come onto the bar; hound or cultist, it is the same lesson.

techniques.name: Hall-Song Breath
techniques.desc: One child to the hall: the bow-children learn the hall-songs too, and hum one under their breath to keep their hands still.

techniques.name: Knife Under the Jaw
techniques.desc: When the beast or the man is on top of you, the long knife goes up under the jaw.

ST05-09.name: The Galefall Ride
ST05-09.origin: During the Varennan siege of Stagley in 1013 a shepherd's son named Ingram rode through the siege lines four times with messages and was knighted for it. His heirs captain the 1,000 Downs Riders and have hunted the Stag Downs since for smugglers, Ashen cultists and Hael Hounds, and in 1102 they rode with Princess Rowena against the Ashen rioters.
ST05-09.philosophy: The horse is the weapon: ride through, never stop, cut once in passing and be gone before he turns.
ST05-09.strengths: Speed; slipping through lines; a cut or a shot in passing; running men down on open downs.
ST05-09.weakness: Light horse on small downs ponies: it cannot stand against heavy horse or a set spear, and dismounted it is a light sword and an impetuous temper.

techniques.name: Through the Lines
techniques.desc: Lie flat on the pony's neck and go through the gap between two fires; you are not there to fight them, only to pass.

techniques.name: Cut in Passing
techniques.desc: One cut at a gallop, low and backhand, and ride on; never stop to see whether it landed.

techniques.name: Saddle Shot
techniques.desc: A light bow loosed from the saddle at a running man or a Hael Hound, before it reaches the horse's legs.

techniques.name: Four Times Through
techniques.desc: Sir Ingram rode through the siege lines four times: read where they expect you, and be somewhere else.

techniques.name: Ride Him Down
techniques.desc: On the open downs no man on foot outruns a Downs Rider: ride him down from behind and over.

maneuver.name: Downs Sweep
maneuver.desc: Light riders sweep the open downs behind a broken enemy and catch his men before they reach a wood or a wall.

ST06-01.name: The Grove Bow
ST06-01.origin: The bow every grove teaches its children, drawn from the Grove Wardens of the Heartwood and the Rangers of the Edge who held the Oak Line through the War of the Forest Edge. It was shaped by elven bodies: a light yew bow of 35 to 50 kg, eyes that see two and a half times as far as a man's, and a people that cannot afford to lose anyone. On the Lost March of 1079 it killed about 400 Aldmark men and left no elven body behind.
ST06-01.philosophy: See first, shoot once at the face or the bow hand, move twenty paces, and never be where the answer lands.
ST06-01.strengths: Range and the first shot; accuracy at faces and hands; vanishing between shots.
ST06-01.weakness: A light bow on a light frame: a shield wall that keeps walking, a man in mail who closes, or a club in the trees ends it.

techniques.name: Loose from Cover
techniques.desc: The arrow leaves a trunk he never looked at, before he knows the trees are watching.

techniques.name: Twenty Paces Aside
techniques.desc: Shoot, then slip twenty paces sideways; his answer goes into the place you were.

techniques.name: The Bow Hand
techniques.desc: At a hundred meters an elf picks the hand on his bow or his spear and spoils it for the day.

techniques.name: Knife at the Trunk
techniques.desc: If he reaches the tree, the trunk takes his blow and the long knife answers from behind it.

techniques.name: Under the Brim
techniques.desc: Over the shield rim and under the helmet brim, into the hand's breadth that mail does not cover.

techniques.name: The Third Warning
techniques.desc: The first two arrows went into the bark beside his head. The third does not.

maneuver.name: The Silent Line
maneuver.desc: Archers shoot from cover by hand signal, move twenty or thirty meters after each shot and never show the enemy a line to charge.

ST06-02.name: The Silara Point
ST06-02.origin: The thrusting sword of the grove-wardens of Mirlas, taught on the shore of Lake Silara since before the War of the Forest Edge and carried to the bout-court of Evenglade every Leaf Fall. It was built for elven nerves and elven bones: a thin blade, a long step and a touch on the first exchange, never a trade of blows. Lirien Duskwater learned it at Mirlas before she left the forest, and the sellswords of the Free Marches still talk about the two centimeters she keeps outside their reach.
ST06-02.philosophy: Learn his longest reach in two passes, stand a finger beyond it, and touch the arm as it straightens.
ST06-02.strengths: Distance and speed of hand; the first clean touch; reading another swordsman's reach.
ST06-02.weakness: It hates walls, doorways and crowds that fix the distance; a spear outreaches it and a grapple or a mace breaks the bones behind it.

techniques.name: The Measuring Pass
techniques.desc: A pass that only asks a question: how far he reaches, and which way he steps when the point comes at his eyes.

techniques.name: A Full Step Back
techniques.desc: When it goes wrong, give a full step, not a half, and read him again.

techniques.name: Two Centimeters
techniques.desc: Stand a finger beyond his longest reach; he falls short, and the point is waiting where his arm ends.

techniques.name: The Arm as It Straightens
techniques.desc: His thrust is all the way out and yours is already coming home along it.

techniques.name: Under the Arm
techniques.desc: The thrust into the armpit, where mail gapes when a man lifts his blade.

techniques.name: Leaf Fall Touch
techniques.desc: The bout-court's oldest lesson: one exchange, one touch, and the leaves are still falling.

ST06-03.name: The Warden's Spear
ST06-03.origin: The Grove Wardens carry the spear in the Heartwood as their mothers did against the boar, the bear and the black aurochs, and it is taught at Lirthil, where the forest meets the grass of the orc clans and the Tusk Hills Watch has stood since 430. It is a hunter's spear more than a soldier's: long in the haft, used from behind a trunk to keep a heavier thing away until the archers finish it. Prince Caelan died on an aurochs' horns near Lirthil in 1036 because he rode into the bull's valley without one.
ST06-03.philosophy: Keep the beast or the man at the end of the haft, let the trunk take his rush, and wait for the arrows.
ST06-03.strengths: Reach against a heavier foe; holding a charge from behind a tree; beasts.
ST06-03.weakness: Light arms: it holds, it does not push, and once a shield is inside the point the elf behind it is in trouble.

techniques.name: Set Against the Root
techniques.desc: Butt against a root, point low: whatever charges runs onto it.

techniques.name: The Long Haft
techniques.desc: Hold the butt end and make him cross two meters of ash to reach you.

techniques.name: Turn the Bull
techniques.desc: Step round the trunk as the horns come, and the point goes into the shoulder from the side.

techniques.name: Hold Him for the Bows
techniques.desc: A thrust low into the leg that slows him for the archers in the branches.

techniques.name: Laewen's Spear
techniques.desc: The thrust the songs give the old king on the holy hills: all of the haft and none of the elf behind it.

ST06-04.name: The Starlight Shot
ST06-04.origin: When the Mistwalkers left Sylvaran in 340 they took the night eyes with them, and the Starlight Range of Lirith was founded to teach ordinary elven eyes to do by craft what Nimrael's kin did by birth. Faenor Nightbow taught it to Aelar the Silent from 880 to 960, and Aelar has trained every one of the 200 Silent and taught Prince Caelan the bow. On the Lost March of 1079 sixty of the Silent shot the Aldmark pickets every night for eleven nights.
ST06-04.philosophy: Never speak, never shoot at what you cannot see, breathe out and loose in the stillness between heartbeats.
ST06-04.strengths: Shooting by starlight at 80 to 150 m; silence; the first shot that nobody hears.
ST06-04.weakness: Full cloud and no stars blind it like any elf, and by day in the open an Ashmere war bow outranges it.

techniques.name: Between Heartbeats
techniques.desc: Breathe out, wait for the stillness between two beats of the heart, and let go.

techniques.name: Shoot and Slip
techniques.desc: Each shot, then twenty or thirty meters sideways by hand signal; he looses at a tree that is empty now.

techniques.name: Blackened Head
techniques.desc: Grey goose fletching and a head blackened in the fire, so nothing glints by starlight.

techniques.name: The Listening Stand
techniques.desc: Lie still on the stand and hear him: an elf catches a breath at thirty paces.

techniques.name: The Arrow Already There
techniques.desc: Aelar says the arrow is already there before the string is quiet, and the man beside the mark hears nothing.

maneuver.name: The Silent Night
maneuver.desc: Archers shoot by starlight at 50 to 100 m, where men see nothing beyond twenty, by hand signal only, and move after every shot.

ST06-05.name: The Oakborn Watching
