ST06-05.origin: Queen Ithrien learned from her father King Caerion's masters, the Heartwood swordsman Thandor Greyhand and the Lirith archer Orome Ashbow, and then watched Sethril the Unwounded for 350 years without once asking him for a lesson. What she built is no chain: it is centuries of watching breath, weight and eyes, made possible by the Deep Years that let an Oakborn keep her body while others lose theirs. The line is down to two carriers, and the Heartwood cousins learn what of it can be told.
ST06-05.philosophy: Read the whole body, move a fifth of a second before the blade does, and be somewhere else when it arrives.
ST06-05.strengths: Reading intent; moving early; point and dagger at the middle distance; a memory of every trick.
ST06-05.weakness: It needs centuries to work and young hands only half-learn it; long fights, maces, grapples and shield-shoves break it like any elf, and the queen's left hand is no longer to be trusted.

techniques.name: Watch the Breath
techniques.desc: The breath drawn before the lunge, the weight on the back foot: he tells you before he moves.

techniques.name: Already Gone
techniques.desc: She does not wait like Vaelor; she moves early, and his cut arrives where she has stopped being.

techniques.name: Point and Left Hand
techniques.desc: The point at his eyes, the dagger low in the other hand, small steps at the middle distance.

techniques.name: The Fifth of a Second
techniques.desc: The answer starts before his blade does. It looks like foresight; it is watching.

techniques.name: Six Hundred Years
techniques.desc: Nothing he can do has not been done in front of her, in some century, by someone now dead.

ST06-06.name: The Before-Thought
ST06-06.origin: Sethril the Unwounded, the first carrier of the Quickened blood, killed Sir Marcus Ravel at the Oak Line in four passes in 527 and went unbeaten for 400 years. He taught his grandson Vaelor from 740 until he died after a torchlit bout in 877; Vaelor taught Veyla, who has run the School of the Quickened at Evenglade since 1000 and taught every Quickened blade alive. The School tests the line's children first with a falling rod, and its first lesson is how Sethril died.
ST06-06.philosophy: Do not block and then strike: the parry and the answer are one movement, begun on the breath before his cut.
ST06-06.strengths: Answering a committed attack faster than anything on two legs; one exchange, one touch.
ST06-06.weakness: Against a fighter who feints and waits it has few answers; it never closes or grapples; and a carrier fights only by daylight or steady lamp, because a flicker brings the fit.

techniques.name: The Falling Rod
techniques.desc: The hand that catches the rod before it lands is the hand that parries; the line tests every child with it.

techniques.name: The Offered Target
techniques.desc: A target a hand's breadth too far, offered so that he commits to it.

techniques.name: Parry Into the Cut
techniques.desc: The blade meets his attack and goes on into him in one line.

techniques.name: Low Guard, Point to the Eyes
techniques.desc: Vaelor has stood three minutes without moving. Let him be the one who tires of waiting.

techniques.name: The Before-Thought Cut
techniques.desc: The answer that begins before the question: the point is in the throat a quarter second after his guard breaks.

ST06-07.name: The Falling Leaf
ST06-07.origin: Faelas Leafstep, born at Rinael in 380 with bones a fifth lighter than other elves', ran the canopy 160 km to Evenglade in a day and a half in 501 to warn of the Aeravel fire, and King Caerion made his kin the realm's couriers. His line became the Lightfoot Scouts and the rangers of the Eastern Edge, and his great-grandson Calithil, Ranger-Captain since 1003, dropped out of the trees onto three logging camps in one night in 1078. The family teaches its own blood to fight from the branches and hides from every enemy how many carriers single blows have crippled.
ST06-07.philosophy: From above and from behind, never from in front: the first second is a fall, and when it goes wrong, go up.
ST06-07.strengths: Running the canopy; shooting down over shields; drops and rolls; vanishing where mail cannot follow.
ST06-07.weakness: Light bones: a club, a mace, a thrown axe or a bad fall breaks a Lightfoot where it would bruise another elf, and open ground by day against horsemen is death.

techniques.name: Down Over the Rim
techniques.desc: From twelve meters up, a shield covers nothing that matters.

techniques.name: Up the Trunk
techniques.desc: When it goes wrong, go up; nobody in mail follows.

techniques.name: The Drop
techniques.desc: Eight meters from a branch onto his shoulders, landing rolling; the fall is the blow.

techniques.name: Loose Before Standing
techniques.desc: Calithil lands rolling and is shooting before he is on his feet.

ST06-08.name: The Firebreak Axe
ST06-08.origin: After the Aeravel fire of 501 King Caerion gave Ilareth Stillwood, who had led the cutters of the 6 km break that saved the southern groves, a standing company of fire-cutters, and the Stillwoods have led the Fire Wardens since. They are the only elves allowed to carry a felling axe into the Heartwood, and in 1105 they are cutting the 40 km firebreak the Eldest Keeper marked around Evenglade. What their children learn on the break they also learn for the day an axe must cut a man.
ST06-08.philosophy: Cut where the mark is and nowhere else: short, exact strokes that save the arm for the next hundred.
ST06-08.strengths: Endurance with the axe; exact cuts at limbs and hafts; keeping a cool head in smoke and heat.
ST06-08.weakness: An elf's arms behind a woodsman's axe: it does not break shields or bones as a dwarf's does, and the Stillwoods are cursed in every grove their break passes.

techniques.name: Mark and Cut
techniques.desc: Look at the mark, then cut it; never swing at the whole tree.

techniques.name: Limb the Branch
techniques.desc: The stroke that takes a branch clean off the trunk takes the haft out of his hands.

techniques.name: Breath in the Smoke
techniques.desc: Fire Wardens breathe low and slow when the air goes grey; the man who panics is the one who dies.

techniques.name: The Break-Line
techniques.desc: Low and across, the way a firebreak is cut: through the shins first, then the rest.

ST07-01.name: The Keel-Blade
ST07-01.origin: Eldergrove fights at sea, and when the archers' work is done and a raider's boat comes alongside, the fight is two steps of wet deck, a rail and a blade. The Ithira Fjord Watch, raised after the noon raid of 611, teaches the light sword and the long knife together for that fight. Its captain Loren Seabright, a half-elf trained at the Dusk School, is called the best blade in Eldergrove.
ST07-01.philosophy: Feet first, then blade: keep your balance when he loses his, and use the knife where the sword has no room.
ST07-01.strengths: Fighting on a moving deck; sword and knife together; close quarters at a rail or a hatch.
ST07-01.weakness: Light blades and light bones: a heavy man in mail who keeps his feet, or a boarding axe that hooks the blade, wins the shove.

school.name: The Fjord Watch Yard of Ithira

techniques.name: Sea Legs
techniques.desc: Knees soft, weight low; the deck rolls and he falls, not you.

techniques.name: Knife Under the Blade
techniques.desc: His sword is tied up with yours; the knife in the other hand goes under both.

techniques.name: On the Roll
techniques.desc: Strike as the ship rolls toward him; he is fighting the deck and you at once.

techniques.name: Hatch and Rail
techniques.desc: Hold the narrow place a boarder must cross, and meet him as he crosses it.

techniques.name: Sword High, Knife Low
techniques.desc: Both blades at once, one at the eyes and one under the ribs; he can only parry one.

ST07-02.name: Rope, Hook and Rail
ST07-02.origin: Since Queen Serewen built the first ships every child of the Elder Coast has learned the boat before the bow: the boat-hook, the rope, the net and how to put a man over the side. The ship-houses of Nimion, where the Brightkeels have built cogs since 560, teach it to every crew, elf, half-elf and human alike, and the marines who land with the Sea-Archers fight with it in the surf and on the rails.
ST07-02.philosophy: The sea is the third fighter on every deck: let it throw him, hook him while he staggers, and put him in the water.
ST07-02.strengths: The reach of the boat-hook; rope and net tricks; using the roll of a ship; putting heavy men overboard.
ST07-02.weakness: Little use on firm open ground: a steady man with a shield and good boots wins on land what he loses on a deck.

techniques.name: Boat-Hook
techniques.desc: The hook takes him by the collar or the ankle from two meters off.

techniques.name: Net Over the Rail
techniques.desc: A wet fishing net over head and sword arm; nets that hold seals hold men.

techniques.name: Let the Ship Throw Him
techniques.desc: Give ground on the down-roll; he comes after you and the deck comes up under him.

techniques.name: Over the Side
techniques.desc: A heavy man in mail who goes into the sea is a drowning problem, not a fighting one.

techniques.name: Down From the Yard
techniques.desc: Down a rope from the yard onto his deck, hook first, before his bowmen look up.

ST07-03.name: The Dusk Bow
ST07-03.origin: Nimrael the Grey Veil captained Sylvaran's night rangers in the War of the Forest Edge and won the Clarora Mist in 296; when she founded Silverbough in 340 her kin brought the night eyes and the night war with them. The Dusk School trains the 800 Night Rangers of the Veil, carriers and non-carriers alike, under Ilvara Mistwalker, Heir of the Veil since 1060. It teaches the hour when elven eyes still see and human eyes do not.
ST07-03.philosophy: Choose the hour: come at dusk, shoot while the light fails, and be gone before anyone can strike a light.
ST07-03.strengths: Dusk and night scouting; shooting in failing light; silent movement on forest roads.
ST07-03.weakness: Noon: the carriers are half-blind in sunlight and the school's tricks need the dark, so lamps, fires and dogs undo it.

techniques.name: The Failing Light
techniques.desc: Loose in the last of the light, when he can still see the sky and not the archer under it.

techniques.name: Count the Fires
techniques.desc: Find his fires, count them, and know where he sleeps and where he will look.

techniques.name: Kick Out the Lamp
techniques.desc: The lamp goes over and the knife comes in while his eyes are still full of the flame.

techniques.name: Dusk Volley
techniques.desc: Close as the sun goes, sweep him at 150 m and pull away before he has formed or found a torch.

maneuver.name: Dusk Volley
maneuver.desc: Archers close as the light fails, sweep the enemy at 150 m while his eyes still adjust, and pull away before he can form or strike lights.

ST07-04.name: The Nimthil Deck-Bow
ST07-04.origin: From Tarael Greywave's Forty Ships of 350 the archers of Nimthil have shot from pitching fir decks, and the chain runs from the ship-archer Mirthil Saltbow to Taeron Windward, who taught Elandor the Steady from 1000 to 1030. Elandor now trains all 2,400 Sea-Archers at the Yard, forty crews of sixty. They learn to lead a moving man at 200 m and to judge a wind that has not arrived yet by the spray and the gulls.
ST07-04.philosophy: Read the man and the wind, not the mark: shoot where he will be when the arrow comes down.
ST07-04.strengths: Long range in wind; shooting from a moving deck; leading a moving target; steady crew volleys.
ST07-04.weakness: Inside thirty meters it is an archer with a knife; it needs room or water between, and a man who walks up behind a shield closes it.

techniques.name: Top of the Roll
techniques.desc: Loose at the top of the roll, when the deck stands still for one heartbeat.

techniques.name: Read the Gulls
techniques.desc: Spray and gulls tell the wind before it comes; the same eyes tell you what he will do.

techniques.name: The Lead
techniques.desc: A lead most archers would call a miss; the arrow and the man arrive at the same place.

techniques.name: Helmsman First
techniques.desc: Taeron shot the helmsman of three raiding boats at 150 m before they reached the sheds: take the one who steers.

maneuver.name: Longship Sweep
maneuver.desc: Longships close to 150 or 200 m, the crews loose on the captain's call at the top of the roll, and the oars pull them off before anyone can board.

ST07-05.name: The Grey Veil
ST07-05.origin: Nimrael the Grey Veil was born about 200 BR at Mirlas with eyes that shone in lamplight, and her line carries True Night Sight: carriers see in near-total dark and are half-blind at noon. Every carrier wears the grey veil from dawn to dusk, and the lamp raised at a child's naming decides who may ever be named heir. What the queens' kin teach their own is the fight in no light at all, the fight the noon raid of 611 taught them they cannot have in the sun.
ST07-05.philosophy: Put out the light and the fight is yours: close, quiet and short.
ST07-05.strengths: Fighting in darkness; close knife work; reading men who cannot see.
ST07-05.weakness: Sunlight half-blinds the carriers; a lit hall, a torch thrust at the face or a noon ambush turns the line's great edge into its worst.

techniques.name: Douse the Lamp
techniques.desc: First the light, then the man: in the dark he is the blind one.

techniques.name: Eyes That Shine
techniques.desc: You see his weight shift in the black; he sees nothing at all.

techniques.name: The Quiet Knife
techniques.desc: Under the arm or over the collar, without a sound for the men a step away.

techniques.name: Under the Veil
techniques.desc: The veil hides the eyes; he never sees which way the answer will come.

ST07-06.name: The Grey Gull's Rail
ST07-06.origin: When Tarael Greywave launched the Forty Ships in 350 the ninth was given to Faelor Longwake and his sixty archers, and a Longwake has captained that crew ever since, through eleven hulls all called the Grey Gull, their keels cut from the graves of its captains. The crew fought the noon raiders off Ithira in 611 and shot pirates off the West Strand in 1031. The Yard teaches long shots in a wind; the Longwakes teach their own blood the last thirty meters, when boarders are at the rail.
ST07-06.philosophy: The last arrows are the ones that count: point-blank over the rail, then the knife, and the Gull comes home.
ST07-06.strengths: Fast close shooting; holding a rail; a crew that does not break under boarding.
ST07-06.weakness: No long game, and a crew that fights for its dead ship more than for sense; on land they are a long way from home.

techniques.name: Point-Blank Over the Rail
techniques.desc: At ten meters the arrow goes through what the long shots only scratch.

techniques.name: Two Arrows Nocked
techniques.desc: A second arrow held along the grip and loosed before the first has landed.

techniques.name: Knife at the Rail
techniques.desc: When the boarder's hand finds the rail, the knife finds the hand.

techniques.name: The Gull Comes Home
techniques.desc: The crew's oath from the October gale of 1089: bail, row, hold on, and bring her home.

ST08-01.name: The Ebb Raid
ST08-01.origin: Bjorn I the Shipwright made the Ship Levy in 856, and every coast district of Northreach owes the king a longship and its crew. The levy learns to row with muffled oars on the night ebb, run bow-first onto a beach and jump into knee-deep water with axe and shield; on the ebb of 4 August 1092 Kettil Frost took eight longships out of Wolfhaven and burned two Greyhaven galleys.
ST08-01.philosophy: Come on the tide, in the dark, over the side, and be rowing home before the alarm is rung.
ST08-01.strengths: Night landings and boardings; sure footing on wet decks and shingle; throwing spears at men still waking.
ST08-01.weakness: Light mail or none, because men in mail drown; caught on the beach at dawn by formed foot or horse, the crew has only its boat to run to.

techniques.name: Muffled Oars
techniques.desc: Rags round the oars and no word spoken: you are alongside him before he knows there is a boat on the water.

techniques.name: Bow-First Jump
techniques.desc: Off the bow into knee-deep water and straight up the shingle at the first man you see, shield in front.

techniques.name: Spear Before the Clash
techniques.desc: A throwing spear from the gunwale at the man on the quay, before either of you has a foot on the same ground.

techniques.name: Sea Legs
techniques.desc: On weed and wet planks the landsman slips when he swings; you do not, and he goes down in front of you.

techniques.name: Burn and Row
techniques.desc: The raid's last minute: cut down whoever stands between you and the boat, fire behind you, and the ebb carries you out.

maneuver.name: Night Tide Attack
maneuver.desc: Longships ride the ebb at night with muffled oars into or out of a harbor, and the crews are over the side before a lantern is lit.

ST08-02.name: The Fog-Hunt
ST08-02.origin: The forest men of the Stagflow hunt elk and boar in river fog, and on 26 May 1091 they hunted Aldmark: the Stone-Watch saw the 12,000 coming, and the hunters struck the strung-out column at the fords at 20–50 m, where it could not see its own flanks. The 800 Stagflow Hunters of the standing army teach the fog bow and the hand-axe at Saltbridge to any lad of the forest districts.
ST08-02.philosophy: Know the ground blind; shoot at a shape at twenty paces, move, and shoot again before he finds the sound.
ST08-02.strengths: Ambush in fog and forest; quick close shooting; hand-axe work among trees; felling a road shut.
ST08-02.weakness: A light hunting bow and no armor: in clear air on open ground, against mail and a formed line, it has neither the range nor the weight.

techniques.name: Shape in the Fog
techniques.desc: At twenty paces in the fog a man is a grey shape; you have shot at grey shapes since you could draw.

techniques.name: Shoot and Move
techniques.desc: Never loose twice from the same tree: he swings at where the sound was, and you are watching him from somewhere else.

techniques.name: Hand-Axe among the Trees
techniques.desc: Among trunks a long sword catches and a short axe does not: one chop at the arm or the neck, and step behind the next tree.

techniques.name: Felled Tree
techniques.desc: Put a fallen trunk between you and him; he has to climb it to reach you, and the axe meets him on top of it.

techniques.name: The Stagflow Fords
techniques.desc: What the hunters did to the Aldmark column in 1091: you know exactly where he must step out of the water, and you are waiting there.

maneuver.name: Fog Ambush
maneuver.desc: Men who know the ground strike a column in river or sea fog at 20–50 m, when it cannot see its own flanks or signals.

ST08-03.name: The Hird Wall
ST08-03.origin: The King's Hird has stood in the front rank since Eirik the Ice-Walker's 340 crossed the frozen bay in 812, and its hall at Wolfhaven teaches the shield, the axe and the front rank. Orm Half-Ear was Hirdmaster to Bjorn III from 1063 to 1090 and took in Kettil Frost at fourteen; Kettil holds the hall now and has taught the hird, Prince Bjorn and the shield drill of the Ice Walkers.
ST08-03.philosophy: Shield first, always: take the blow on the boss, hook his rim down with the beard of the axe, and keep your shoulder against the man beside you.
ST08-03.strengths: The shield wall by night, in fog, on ice and on a deck; hooking shields; stepping back so the next man steps up.
ST08-03.weakness: Short and close: reach beats it, open ground and anything mounted beat it, and a hooked shield on a strap drags the arm down with it.

techniques.name: Boss, Not Face
techniques.desc: Take the first blow on the iron boss, never on the face or the rim, and answer before he draws back.

techniques.name: The Bearded Hook
techniques.desc: The beard of a Northreach axe is ground to hook a rim: catch his shield and haul it down.

techniques.name: Over the Rim
techniques.desc: With his shield hooked down, the axe comes over your own rim into his neck.

techniques.name: Step Back One Pace
techniques.desc: The hird drills nothing harder: when it goes wrong, step back one pace and let the next man up; alone, the step draws him onto your axe.

techniques.name: The Shingle at Coldhaven
techniques.desc: Three hundred of the hird met two hundred landed men on the shingle in 1093: shield into shield, axe over the rim, and drive them into the sea.

maneuver.name: Shield Wall
maneuver.desc: Shields overlapped, shoulder to shoulder, axes working over the rims; the front rank steps back and the next steps up, and nobody runs.

ST08-04.name: The Ice Walk
ST08-04.origin: Orm Longski founded the Ski Yard of Saltbridge and taught Svala Snowstride from 1080; she holds it now with the 1,600 Ice Walkers on its rolls. She reads ice within 2 cm by its color and the ring of a pole, and on 19 January 1092 led the Winter Crossing over the frozen Glenwash to burn the Brightmoor barns; sixty raiders drowned on the way home through a crack she had passed as sound.
ST08-04.philosophy: Move where horses founder and men sink: strike the stores, not the soldiers, and be forty kilometres away by morning.
ST08-04.strengths: Speed over snow and ice; reading ice; raids by night; a quick spear on skis.
ST08-04.weakness: Summer and dry ground take it all away; no mail and little weight, and one misread crack drowns a column.

techniques.name: Pole and Point
techniques.desc: The spear you pole with is the spear you fight with: one push off the snow and the point is already in him.

techniques.name: Read the Ice
techniques.desc: Color and the ring of a pole tell you where the ice will hold; the set of his feet tells you where he will step.

techniques.name: Glide Past
techniques.desc: Slide past him on the skis and cut low at the back of the knee as you go; a man on foot in deep snow does not turn in time.

techniques.name: Seax in the Snow
techniques.desc: Drop him in the drift and finish it with the seax; a man floundering to the waist cannot fight.

techniques.name: The Winter Crossing
techniques.desc: Forty kilometres over the ice in a night, the stores burned at dawn, and you are fresher than the men who slept beside them.

maneuver.name: Ski Raid
maneuver.desc: Raiders on skis cover 40–60 km a day over snow where horses founder, burn the enemy's stores and are gone.

ST08-05.name: The Winter Road
ST08-05.origin: Eirik Winterborn was born in a sealers' camp on the sea ice in 784 and lived through the night in a snow-hole; in January 812 he led 340 men across the frozen bay and took Wolfhaven. The frost blood keeps the Winterborns warm in frost that kills others, and the house teaches its children to fight on ice in a shirt, bare-handed on cold iron, while their enemies fumble in mittens.
ST08-05.philosophy: Choose the coldest hour and the worst footing and fight there, because there you are the only one still whole.
ST08-05.strengths: Bare hands on cold iron; a sure grip and steady breath in frost; patience in a winter fight.
ST08-05.weakness: It is built for the cold: in a warm hall or a southern summer it is plain axe-work, and a Winterborn who chooses the wrong ground has no second trick.

techniques.name: Bare Hands
techniques.desc: No mittens: in hard frost your grip on the haft is sure while his slips in wet wool.

techniques.name: Snow-Hole Night
techniques.desc: Eirik's first night was spent in a snow-hole; the blood rests in the cold the way other men rest by a fire.

techniques.name: Across the Bay
techniques.desc: The crossing of 812: come at him over the ice he thought nobody could walk, and hit him while he is still staring.

techniques.name: Lantern Night
techniques.desc: On the longest night the Winterborns are crowned; in the dark and the cold you are patient, and he is not.

techniques.name: Frost-Handed
techniques.desc: The blow of a king who fights in a shirt on the ice: full strength, full reach, in cold that has already taken half of his.

maneuver.name: Winter Campaign
maneuver.desc: The king fights in the season nobody fights: frozen rivers carry his men, the enemy's hay burns and his horses starve.

ST08-06.name: The Stagflow Rush
ST08-06.origin: The Staggs hold Saltbridge on the road from Aldmark and have always been the first to meet an army from the south. On 26 May 1091 their house held the ambush line at the Stagflow fords in fog, and Jarl Halvard's sons Rane and Geir died leading the first rush into the Aldmark column; the house teaches its children that rush, and does not forget.
ST08-06.philosophy: When the arrows stop, go: the first rush into a column that cannot see decides everything, and the jarl's blood goes first.
ST08-06.strengths: A fearsome first charge out of cover; spear and axe at a stumbling enemy; a grudge that keeps it on its feet.
ST08-06.weakness: It leads from the front and pays for it: the men who start the rush die in it, and a column that holds its nerve for one minute breaks the rushers instead.

techniques.name: Out of the Fog
techniques.desc: The hunters' arrows stop and you come out of the grey at a run, the first man he sees and the last.

techniques.name: Stag's Leap
techniques.desc: Leap the bank of the ford with the spear levelled, and your whole weight lands on the point.

techniques.name: We Do Not Forget
techniques.desc: The house's words keep a Stagg on his feet when the wound says lie down; there is a debt still owed.

techniques.name: Rane and Geir
techniques.desc: The rush Halvard's sons led at the Stagflow: everything in the first minute, and no thought of the second.

maneuver.name: The First Rush
maneuver.desc: When the hunters' arrows stop, the jarl's house leads the rush out of the fog into the stumbling column.

ST08-07.name: Behind the King
ST08-07.origin: Orm Axeholm crossed the frozen bay with Eirik in 812 and was among the first through Wolfhaven's gate; every generation since has given the King's Hird a crew-leader, and Axeholm women have nursed Winterborn babies through the long winters. Three Axeholms stood behind Bjorn III at the Kingsmere feast of 1090 and could not save him, and the family has drilled the guarding of one man in a crowded hall harder ever since.
ST08-07.philosophy: Your body belongs between the king and the blade: watch hands, not faces, and strike the man who moves first.
ST08-07.strengths: Stepping between; short axe work in crowded halls; reading the hand that goes to a knife.
ST08-07.weakness: It waits to be attacked and guards someone else: drawn away from the man it protects, or made to chase, it is an ordinary hirdman.

techniques.name: Watch the Hands
techniques.desc: Faces lie at a feast; hands do not. You watch for the one that goes to a belt.

techniques.name: Step Between
techniques.desc: Your shield goes where the blade is going, whoever it was meant for, and the axe answers from behind it.

techniques.name: Short Haft in the Hall
techniques.desc: Between benches and pillars there is no room to swing: choke up on the haft and chop short.

techniques.name: Three at the Feast
techniques.desc: Three Axeholms stood behind a king who died anyway; their sons see the danger before it is poured, and kill it before it is drunk.

maneuver.name: Behind the King
maneuver.desc: The king's crews close round him so tightly that the enemy must kill them all to reach him, and they know it.

ST09-01.name: The Hall Trunk
ST09-01.origin: A giant swings a maul or a whole trunk that no shield stops, and every hall of Frostholm teaches its young the trunk before the maul: a spruce stripped of its branches, swung low and wide to clear a beach. It is older than the pairs, from the halls of the Long Walk North. At Ragvik in July 797 the Helstad giants swept the Cold Coast thanes' shield wall into the surf with it.
ST09-01.philosophy: Sweep wide and low, clear the ground in front of you, and never let the swing carry you round.
ST09-01.strengths: Enormous reach; sweeping several men off their feet; breaking shield walls from beyond spear range.
ST09-01.weakness: A giant takes three seconds to turn: after a full swing he is open, and the man who ducks it is inside, at the knee.

techniques.name: Low Sweep
techniques.desc: Knee-high and wide; three men go down where one stood.

techniques.name: Out of Reach
techniques.desc: Hold the trunk out level; no human weapon reaches the giant behind it.

techniques.name: Clear the Beach
techniques.desc: Walk forward swinging, and the ground in front of you is empty.

techniques.name: Half Swing
techniques.desc: Stop the swing halfway round; the man who ducked inside finds the trunk coming back.

techniques.name: The Spruce of Ragvik
techniques.desc: A whole stripped spruce swung once along a shield wall, as on the beach in 797.

ST09-02.name: Stamp and Sweep
ST09-02.origin: What kills a giant is a man with a long knife who gets behind it in the snow, and the halls teach their young from childhood to keep small men away from their knees. Hroa of Torvik, who has not bent her right knee since a walrus crushed it in 1047, is the proof that it can be done: when it goes wrong she sits, and a giant on the ground with a maul still covers four meters. The giants call it the low guard; humans who have seen it call it stamping.
ST09-02.philosophy: Guard the knees: stamp, sweep, sit if you must, but never let him behind you.
ST09-02.strengths: Defending against small, quick men; stamps and hand-sweeps that knock down; fighting from the ground.
ST09-02.weakness: It answers threats and makes none of its own; a crossbow at sixty meters or a warm day undoes it.

techniques.name: The Stamp
techniques.desc: A foot the size of a man's chest, set down where he was about to be.

techniques.name: Hand-Sweep
techniques.desc: An open hand swept along the snow takes the legs from anything near the knees.

techniques.name: Knee Shut
techniques.desc: The knee closes on the knife hand, and the other foot comes down.

techniques.name: Sit Down
techniques.desc: When it goes wrong, sit with your back to a rock: nothing gets behind a sitting giant, and the arms still reach four meters.

techniques.name: Heel of the Hall
techniques.desc: Fourteen hundred kilograms set down on purpose.

ST09-03.name: Back to Back
ST09-03.origin: Giants fight in pairs, back to back, because a giant needs three seconds to turn, and the Pair-Yard of Skarfell teaches every pair of the halls to fight as one body with two faces. Thrand the Broad of Helstad, who learned beside Ormhamar giants, has mastered it since 1090 and teaches by moving his pupils' feet with his own hands. Since his wife and pair-partner Gerd died of fever in 1099 he fights alone, and he wants every hall pair drilled to turn together before the Thing of 1106.
ST09-03.philosophy: Your back is your partner's: turn together, grip together, and the maul falls where the other cannot see.
ST09-03.strengths: No back to attack; wrestling holds at giant strength; a maul that breaks shield and arm together.
ST09-03.weakness: A pair is two giants or none: alone, a pair-fighter has no back, and heat and a long chase kill any giant.

techniques.name: Back to Back
techniques.desc: Your partner sees what is behind you, and nobody takes you from the back.

techniques.name: The Giant's Grip
techniques.desc: A hand that closes round a man's whole chest, and the ground comes up to meet him.

techniques.name: Turn Together
techniques.desc: The pair turns as one, and the man who thought he was behind them is in front.

techniques.name: Maul Over the Shoulder
techniques.desc: Your partner's shoulder hides the swing until it is coming down.

maneuver.name: Back-to-Back Pairs
maneuver.desc: Giants fight in pairs, back to back, breaking gates, boats and shield walls with nobody able to get behind them.

ST09-04.name: The Cape Stone
ST09-04.origin: On the northern capes of Torvik the hall's young throw 50 kg sea-rounded stones for its honor, and the Stone Ring teaches the throw and the harpoon at giant strength. Gunnhild of Torvik taught Hroa the throw from 1000 and the maul from 1010, and Hroa, the oldest giant alive, has run the Ring since 1045 and taught every Torvik thrower now living, Vermund Farcast among them. At the Thing of 1064 she threw 50 kg 34 m across the Thingvold, a mark no giant has matched.
ST09-04.philosophy: Nobody comes inside ten meters: stones at thirty, the harpoon at ten, and the Mountain Breaker for whatever is left.
ST09-04.strengths: Stones that break boats and men at 25 to 30 m; the harpoon; the overhead maul blow.
ST09-04.weakness: Slow to turn and slow to throw again; heat, soft snow and being circled undo it, and a crossbow outranges it.

techniques.name: Cape Stone
techniques.desc: Fifty kilograms of sea-rounded stone; it does not need to hit square.

techniques.name: The Half-Turn Throw
techniques.desc: From the hips and the left leg, because the right knee will not take a step.

techniques.name: Walrus Harpoon
techniques.desc: Thrown at ten meters with the strength of five men, it goes through a walrus hide.

techniques.name: The Mountain Breaker
techniques.desc: The maul falls overhead and breaks the shield and the arm under it together.

maneuver.name: Stone Volley
maneuver.desc: Giants on a cape or an ice edge throw 50 kg stones at 25 to 30 m; boats break and shield walls open before anyone can reach them.

ST09-05.name: The Runner's Hand
ST09-05.origin: Skarvi the Small, born at Skarfell Hall in 870, was the first small giant the chant records: 310 cm, and able to run and turn as no ordinary giant can. His line has given Frostholm its chieftains since 903 and its Skarfell Runners, small giants who scout, hunt and carry word between the halls. The big halls call them a lesser people; the Skarfells teach their own to fight as no other giant can, on the move.
ST09-05.philosophy: A giant who can turn is a giant nobody gets behind: keep moving, and strike where the big ones cannot.
ST09-05.strengths: Speed and turning for a giant; running men down; striking and being gone.
ST09-05.weakness: Smaller than the halls' champions: a Skarfell loses a wrestling match to a Torvik, and a small giant is still a giant on a warm day.

techniques.name: The Turn
techniques.desc: What a big giant needs three seconds for, a Skarfell does in one.

techniques.name: Run Him Down
techniques.desc: Men expect to outrun a giant. Not this one.

techniques.name: Stone on the Run
techniques.desc: Thrown at a jog, without stopping to plant the feet, as no other hall can.

techniques.name: Behind the Big One
techniques.desc: The man going for the big giant's knee finds a small one already behind him.

ST09-06.name: The Ragvik Pair
ST09-06.origin: On Ragvik beach in July 797 two pairs of Helstad giants broke the Cold Coast thanes' shield wall and sank two ships with thrown stones, and both pairs came from the household that farms the Ormhamar stead below Helstad Hall. The household has given the halls fighting pairs ever since, partners matched young and bound for life, and many of the Pair-Yard's champions. Frostholm has had no war since 797, so Ormhamar fights at the fair, against walrus and bear, and in the Pair-Yard's matches.
ST09-06.philosophy: Walk the pair into the wall together: what the first giant breaks, the second clears.
ST09-06.strengths: Breaking shield walls; a pair that attacks instead of waiting; stones at ships.
ST09-06.weakness: It is made for two, so an Ormhamar without a partner is half a style, and its pride rests on a fight three centuries old.

techniques.name: Stone at the Ship
techniques.desc: A stone meant for a hull goes through a shield on the way.

techniques.name: Walk Into the Wall
techniques.desc: Two giants step into the shield wall together, and it is not a wall any more.

techniques.name: The Second Giant
techniques.desc: The first giant breaks the rim; the second is already swinging at whatever stood behind it.

techniques.name: Bound for Life
techniques.desc: Partners matched as children: when one tires, the other's back holds them both up.

ST09-07.name: The Knee-Guard
ST09-07.origin: Since the Thanes' Raid the Spearwicks of Koldal, tin-diggers by birth, have led the human spearmen Skarfell Hall sets at its giants' flanks, because what kills a giant is a man with a knife at the back of the knee. They stood at Thrand the Broad's flanks when drunk Northreach sailors rioted at the fair in 1088, and a Spearwick took a knife meant for his partner Gerd. It is a small human art made for the shadow of a large one.
ST09-07.philosophy: Stand at the giant's knee, set the spear, and let nobody small reach what the giant cannot see.
ST09-07.strengths: Guarding a flank; short spear and shield; catching the knifeman who goes low.
ST09-07.weakness: Ordinary men with ordinary spears: without the giant beside them the Spearwicks are tin-diggers in a shield line.

techniques.name: Set at the Knee
techniques.desc: Your place is beside the giant's knee, point out, and you do not leave it.

techniques.name: Catch the Knife
techniques.desc: The man ducking under the giant's swing comes up into your shield rim and your point.

techniques.name: Low Thrust
techniques.desc: What he meant to do to the giant, do to him first.

techniques.name: The Knife Meant for Her
techniques.desc: The fair of 1088: step in front of the blade meant for the giant, and answer it.

ST10-01.name: The Hold Pick
ST10-01.origin: Irondeep is built around breastplates and war-picks in the gate, and every dwarf of the hold learns the pick in the Hold Guard before thirty. It is a miner's tool made a weapon in the galleries of the fourteen halls Korrin Deepeye united in 610: a long spike that opens helmets and finds the gap at a breastplate's edge, on a haft short enough to work in a passage two meters wide. The Duskdelves have carried it beside the royal iron trains by night since 790.
ST10-01.philosophy: Let the shield take the blow, then the pick goes over the rim into the helmet.
ST10-01.strengths: Piercing mail and plate; close work in passages; dwarven strength and wind behind a narrow point.
ST10-01.weakness: Short reach and short legs: in the open a spear, a horse or a faster man keeps it at a distance it cannot cross.

school.name: The Pick-Gallery of the Deep Halls

techniques.name: Over the Rim
techniques.desc: The spike comes over the shield rim and down into the helmet.

techniques.name: Hook the Shield
techniques.desc: The back of the pick takes his rim and drags it down for the dwarf beside you.

techniques.name: The Breastplate's Edge
techniques.desc: Smiths know where a breastplate ends; the pick goes in there.

techniques.name: The Shield Takes It
techniques.desc: Take his blow on the boss, square and patient, and answer while his arm is still coming back.

techniques.name: Thirty Years in the Gate
techniques.desc: The blow a gate sergeant has rehearsed for thirty years: his shield shoved high, the pick into the helmet under it.

ST10-02.name: The Iron Hedge
ST10-02.origin: The pike came to the Iron Mountains from Stonehold's Toll War of the 600s, and Irondeep drills it for the day a human army stands on the Ore Shelf instead of in the gate. An eight-rank hedge of four-meter pikes with five points out in front stops horse from the front, and the hold can turn out 6,000 at full levy within hours. The hold-wards of the old halls, Vardal first among them, still muster their own blocks.
ST10-02.philosophy: Stand still, keep the points level, and let them come onto the iron.
ST10-02.strengths: Stopping horse and charges; holding a front; reach far beyond a dwarf's arm.
ST10-02.weakness: Slow to turn and helpless on the flank; alone, a pike is a long pole in the hands of a short dwarf.

techniques.name: Points Level
techniques.desc: The point stays at his chest, wherever he goes, and he has four meters of iron to cross.

techniques.name: Butt to the Boot
techniques.desc: Against a rider: butt against your boot, point at the horse's chest, and the charge spits itself.

techniques.name: Thrust From the Second Rank
techniques.desc: Past the shoulder of the dwarf in front, into the man busy with him.

techniques.name: Push of Pike
techniques.desc: The whole hedge leans in at once and walks him backward off his ground.

techniques.name: The Hedge-Master's Count
techniques.desc: The master counts the charge in, stride by stride, and every point goes forward on the count.

maneuver.name: The Iron Hedge
maneuver.desc: An eight-rank block of pikes, five points out, plants itself across the road; nothing on horseback comes through the front.

ST10-03.name: The Gallery Shield
ST10-03.origin: Hauk Stonejaw speared the cave bear of 612 and Korrin gave his clan the Deep Gate; the Shield Gallery has been the Stonejaws' since 640, and no human army has passed the gate in 490 years. Asdis Stonejaw taught her grandson Harrek from 990 to 1020, and he has mastered the Gallery since 1060 and taught every Deep Gate Warden since. Its dark test puts a warden in a sealed gallery with no light against ten spearmen in turn, and a master blocks nine thrusts in ten.
ST10-03.philosophy: Stand square, shield planted, and listen: the breath, the scrape of a sole, the moment his weight lands.
ST10-03.strengths: Holding a gate or a tunnel; fighting in total darkness by ear; tall shield and gate spear together.
ST10-03.weakness: Light and open ground undo it: by lamplight its masters are good, not famous, and in the open a gate shield is a door with nothing to fill.

techniques.name: Plant the Shield
techniques.desc: Rim to the floor, boot behind it; the shield covers you from boot to eye and does not move.

techniques.name: Hear the Weight Land
techniques.desc: In the dark the scrape of a sole tells you when he commits.

techniques.name: The Gate Spear
techniques.desc: Spear low behind the shield; the thrust meets his chest at the moment his weight lands.

techniques.name: Nine in Ten
techniques.desc: The dark test: ten spearmen in turn, and a master turns nine of them.

maneuver.name: Gate Holding
maneuver.desc: A few heavy wardens fill a gate or gallery two to four meters wide so only two or three enemies can strike at once, and the front rank changes every two minutes.

ST10-04.name: The Dunheim Sap
ST10-04.origin: Grim Coalbrow cut the lower hold of Dunheim in 760, and his clan's mine-masters learned to bake coal into coke and to pump the deep workings dry with waterwheels. The Sapper Hall of Dunheim trains the Tunnel Crews in mining and counter-mining, and Vigdis Coalbrow, Sapper-Master since 1079, teaches water as a weapon: in 1066 she flooded a thieves' tunnel dug from the carters' camp.
ST10-04.philosophy: Hear him digging, dig to meet him, and let the water or the smoke go in first.
ST10-04.strengths: Fighting in tunnels; smoke, flood and collapse; short picks and knives in the dark.
ST10-04.weakness: Nothing it knows works under the open sky; in a straight fight a sapper is a short dwarf with a short pick.

techniques.name: Water in the Bowl
techniques.desc: A bowl of water on the gallery floor ripples when he digs; the same stillness tells you when he moves.

techniques.name: Smoke the Shaft
techniques.desc: Fire the shaft and let him breathe it before you go in.

techniques.name: Knife in the Breakthrough
techniques.desc: The wall gives, and you are through it with the knife before the dust settles.

techniques.name: Open the Sluice
techniques.desc: The pump water goes into his gallery faster than a man in mail can climb out of it.

maneuver.name: Flood the Mine
maneuver.desc: Sappers listen for the enemy mine, dig to meet it and turn the pump water or smoke into it; the attackers lose their tunnel and their nerve.

ST10-05.name: Nothing Passes
ST10-05.origin: In February 612 miners broke into a cave bear's winter den, and when the bear had killed five of them Hauk Stonejaw drove a boar-spear into its chest; its skull still hangs above the Deep Gate. The Gallery teaches every warden, but the clan keeps for its own blood the bear-spear, the underhand thrust Harrek has used since a club broke his jaw and a knife took his arm in 1041, and the last answer of the gate: drop the spear, take the pick and make the gap narrower with your own body.
ST10-05.philosophy: Brace for the rush as Hauk did, thrust underhand, and if the spear is gone, be the gate.
ST10-05.strengths: Bracing against a charge or a beast; the underhand thrust; refusing to give a step.
ST10-05.weakness: It knows one place to fight, a gate, and will not leave it; light, open ground and a crossbow from above kill its masters.

techniques.name: Bear-Spear
techniques.desc: The crossbar stops the rush a spear's length away; whatever comes on, comes onto the point.

techniques.name: The Underhand Thrust
techniques.desc: From the hip, under the shield, because the arm will not lift above the ear any more.

techniques.name: The Skull Above the Gate
techniques.desc: Men who have heard of the bear come on slower. Let them look up at it.

techniques.name: Be the Gate
techniques.desc: The spear goes down, the pick comes up, and his own body fills what is left of the gap.

ST10-06.name: Bolt and Windlass
ST10-06.origin: Thurid Slatebrow shot wolves off the iron trains for forty years before King Arnulf gave her the middle fort of the Iron Road at Storgrund in 951, and her clan has held its stone tower over the road since with 140 crossbows. Every Slatebrow child learns the windlass before the runes. They have fought road thieves and Pinewild outlaws, and a Slatebrow cousin died beside Harrek Stonejaw at the upper fort in 1094.
ST10-06.philosophy: Wind it, wait for the shot that cannot miss, and take the legs from whatever runs at the train.
ST10-06.strengths: Heavy bolts from a wall or a wagon; shooting at things that move, wolves and men alike.
ST10-06.weakness: One shot a minute: once the bolt is gone there is a dwarf with a knife and a windlass, and a fast rush catches him spanning.

techniques.name: Wolf-Shot
techniques.desc: Low, at the running legs; a wolf or a thief that cannot run is finished.

techniques.name: From the Tower
techniques.desc: Shooting down from a stone tower, where his shield faces the wrong way.

techniques.name: The Spanning Knife
techniques.desc: Caught winding, the windlass drops and the knife comes up; the clan drills it as hard as the shot.

techniques.name: Through Mail at Sixty
techniques.desc: A steel bow, a full windlass and a man in mail at sixty meters: the bolt does not stop at the rings.

ST11-01.name: The Two-Minute Wave
ST11-01.origin: Orc war has been fought in relays for as long as orcs have been blown after ten minutes, and the Horde made it a craft: Gorath beat three clans that way at Vrakoth in July 1028 and split his best riders into three waves when he founded the Horde in 1041. Every clan's war-captains teach it, and the Wave Ground outside Urgol takes any orc of thirteen who can sit a horse to the drum.
ST11-01.philosophy: Two minutes of everything you have, thirty heartbeats of breath behind the next wave, and back in before the enemy has found his feet.
ST11-01.strengths: the first two minutes; the lance at the shock and the axe after it; fast recovery between bursts
ST11-01.weakness: spent after ten minutes; stakes, wagons and crossbows; a hot afternoon

techniques.name: On the First Beat
techniques.desc: The drum sounds once and the whole weight of an orc's burst goes into one blow.

techniques.name: Fall Back on the Changed Beat
techniques.desc: Pull back a hundred paces and breathe for thirty heartbeats; an orc's arms come back full while the man who chased you is still panting.

techniques.name: Lance at the Shock
techniques.desc: The lance goes in at the first shock and is let go; the horse and the burst do the rest.

techniques.name: Axe After
techniques.desc: Once the lance is gone the bearded axe comes off the saddle, hooks the shield rim down and opens what is behind it.

techniques.name: The Next Wave
techniques.desc: You come in fresh on a man who has just fought the wave before yours and has not breathed since.

techniques.name: The Third Drum
techniques.desc: Every wave has struck and his line is bent; on the third drum the whole band goes in at once and spends the last of its wind in one ride.

maneuver.name: Relay Charge
maneuver.desc: Waves of 100 to 300 strike for about two minutes and pull back to breathe while the next wave strikes, timed by the drums; six to ten waves keep up the pressure for a quarter of an hour, and then the band is spent.

ST11-02.name: The Grass Sea Bow
ST11-02.origin: The orcs learned the horse bow from the men who beat them with it: at Goroth in August 874 the Wind riders shot the relays for hours until they tired, and the Long Flight clans that fled west in 876 brought the lesson home. The Goroth clans teach it among the remount herds, and the Wellkeepers of Krugak keep the shooting ground at the wells where the eastern relays water.
ST11-02.philosophy: Shoot close and heavy until the line wavers, then sling the bow and ride in behind your own arrows.
ST11-02.strengths: heavy arrows from an orc's draw at short range; the herd screen; turns into a charge at once
ST11-02.weakness: short range and few arrows beside the Wind riders; loses a long shooting match; the bow is only the start of the fight

school.name: The Shooting Ground of the Krugak Wells

techniques.name: Heavy Shaft
techniques.desc: An orc's arm draws a bow no Rider could pull; the arrow does not go far, but it goes through.

techniques.name: Behind the Herd
techniques.desc: Loose horses run ahead in the dust; he braces for the herd and the rider behind it is already on him.

techniques.name: Three at the Gallop
techniques.desc: Three arrows in the last hundred paces of the run-in, each one closer than the last.

techniques.name: Sling the Bow
techniques.desc: The bow goes over the shoulder and the axe comes out at the gallop, while he is still covering his face from the arrows.

techniques.name: Shoot the Horse's Face
techniques.desc: Not the man: the horse, in the face. A horse with an arrow by the eye throws its rider into your wave.

techniques.name: Grass Fire
techniques.desc: Pitch-wrapped arrows into the dry grass upwind of him in late summer; the steppe itself goes for his horse.

maneuver.name: Herd Screen
maneuver.desc: Loose horses are driven ahead of the attacking riders to hide their numbers in the dust and break the enemy's front with their weight; the bows shoot from behind the herd and the relays follow 200 to 300 m back.

ST11-03.name: Great Ride Wrestling
ST11-03.origin: The wrestling of the Great Ride is as old as the Ride itself, fought every 21 June at the Drum Stones while the clans count their votes. Durk Ironarms of Gorath's blood won it four times from 1092 to 1100, and the Hearth Guard wrestles every evening in the ring at Urgol where he teaches.
ST11-03.philosophy: Close, lift and break: an orc's burst is strongest in the first grip, so the first grip must be the last.
ST11-03.strengths: the lift and the slam; mass and burst at arm's length; needs no weapon
ST11-03.weakness: anything that keeps him outside his arms; blown after a few minutes of hard grappling; a quick wrestler who gives ground

techniques.name: Belt Grip
techniques.desc: Both hands in his belt and your weight on him; every breath he takes is now harder than yours.

techniques.name: Brow to the Nose
techniques.desc: A short, hard butt with the brow under his guard. Tusks are for showing; the skull is for breaking noses.

techniques.name: Lift and Slam
techniques.desc: Under the arms, up off his feet, and down on his back with all of you on top of him.

techniques.name: Break the Arm
techniques.desc: Trap the wrist under your arm and lean; whatever he was holding, he holds it worse now.

techniques.name: The Ride Throw
techniques.desc: The throw that wins at the Drum Stones: hip in, his feet over his head, and the ground does the hitting.

techniques.name: Crushing Hold
techniques.desc: An orc's burst against a man's ribs: nobody breathes again until you let go.

ST11-04.name: The Three Beats
ST11-04.origin: The Drum Lodge keeps the drums at the Drum Stones, where the clans came back under Old Mother Shagra in 923 and where Gorath was named war-chief in 1024. It teaches the three beats every wave obeys, one for the strike, a changed beat to recall the wave after about two minutes and another to send the next, and its 400 drummers stand at the Stones and at Urgol. Harkun the Drum-Master, head of the Drum Council, taught Skarn Redhand his drum speech.
ST11-04.philosophy: Listen for the beat under the noise: a fight has a rhythm, and whoever keeps time decides when the other side breathes.
ST11-04.strengths: timing the waves; reading a fight's rhythm; frightening untrained horses; holding men together
ST11-04.weakness: little for a lone fighter with a blade; useless when the drums are silenced or the wind takes the sound; drummers go deaf

techniques.name: Keep Time
techniques.desc: Breathe on the beat you hear in your head; you tire slower, and you hear where his rhythm is going.

techniques.name: The Changed Beat
techniques.desc: Break your own rhythm the way the drums change to call a wave back; he moves on the beat that never comes, and you answer.

techniques.name: Thunder Horse
techniques.desc: The drum-masters' roar and stamp, like the Thunder Horse that ran past the Stones when Gorath was named; a man's nerve goes before his arm does.

techniques.name: Every Drum at Once
techniques.desc: A drum-master hears a fight the way a fight hears four hundred drums: all of it at once, and the one beat that is wrong.

maneuver.name: The Three Beats
maneuver.desc: The drum-master stands beside the war-chief and times every wave: strike, recall after two minutes, send the next. No wave stays in too long and no gap opens between them.

ST11-05.name: The Long Wind Run
ST11-05.origin: Orrak the Walker, born at Gashmar in 961, could walk a horse to death and still stand, and his grandson Tukar ran 300 km in three days in 1046 to warn the summer camps; Gorath made the Gashmar runners a band of their own. Tukar ran 80 km through Aldmark patrols at the Gashmar Fords in 1070 and died bringing up the reserve. His son Brak Longwind keeps the Runners' Camp, 600 runners and a chain of runner posts to the Drum Stones.
ST11-05.philosophy: Never be where the fight wants you; run until he is blown, then let him find out an orc can still be standing.
ST11-05.strengths: endurance; scouting, maps and the ground; outlasting other orcs; slipping away
ST11-05.weakness: no burst: a Longwind hits about as hard as a strong human; little for the shock of a charge

techniques.name: Second Breath
techniques.desc: Slow the feet, not the mind; a runner's breath comes back while he is still moving.

techniques.name: Run Him Out
techniques.desc: Give ground, and give it again; make him chase until his ten minutes are gone and yours have not started.

techniques.name: The Map in the Feet
techniques.desc: A runner knows every gully and ford; draw him onto the bad ground before the fight begins.

techniques.name: Give Way and Strike
techniques.desc: Word before blood: give way and give way, and when he lunges at a man who will not stand, step off the line and strike once.

techniques.name: Eighty Kilometers
techniques.desc: What Tukar Longwind did at the Gashmar Fords: keep going through the wound when any other orc would be lying down.

maneuver.name: Runner Relays
maneuver.desc: Runners hand word on every 15 to 20 km and carry it 100 km a day on foot through hill and ford, so the war-chief's orders arrive before the enemy knows they were sent.

ST11-06.name: The Storm in the Blood
ST11-06.origin: In August 1012 Gorath, 14, rode bare-armed into the feud of the Krugak wells, killed three riders and then fell shaking and white; the Urgol hide shows 'the boy with the storm in him'. His carriers lead the first wave of the Hearth Guard, and his son Durgash broke Gunnar Harrow's ring at the Gordush Bend in 1049 and was named Blood-Fist. The line teaches its children of the blood to aim the fury rather than be ridden by it, which is the most any of them has managed.
ST11-06.philosophy: When the storm comes, aim it: three to five minutes without fear or pain, and every blow in them must count before the grey lips and the faint.
ST11-06.strengths: three to five minutes without fear or pain; harder and faster blows; breaks a ring or a shield line
ST11-06.weakness: faints afterwards with grey lips; cannot stop once it starts and strikes friends; hearts burst young; hold him for five minutes and he is lying down

techniques.name: The Storm Comes
techniques.desc: The heart hammers, the pain goes and the fear with it. You do not choose when it ends.

techniques.name: Bare-Armed
techniques.desc: As Gorath went into the Krugak feud at fourteen: no shield, no coat, nothing between the blow and the man.

techniques.name: Break the Ring
techniques.desc: The Gordush Bend: drive straight into the shields where they are thickest, because the blood does not count them.

techniques.name: Feel Nothing
techniques.desc: The cut is there. You will feel it tomorrow, if there is a tomorrow.

techniques.name: Blood-Fist
techniques.desc: What Hrakka the Red died doing at the Gashmar Fords and his father Durgash lived to be named for.

maneuver.name: Blood Fury Charge
maneuver.desc: Carriers of Gorath's blood lead the first relay wave; for three to five minutes they feel no fear and strike faster and harder, and then they faint grey-lipped behind the horse lines.

ST11-07.name: The Magak Hand
ST11-07.origin: Urzag Redhand killed a bear with a knife at thirteen and came home with red arms, and the Magak staff has passed from uncle to sister's son since 440. The Redhands ride the richest herds of the Horde, about 180,000 horses, and teach their heirs to read a horse before they can ride one. At the Old Lokshal Ring in July 1091 Skarn Redhand watched 300 Nine Winds horses bunch and toss their heads and sent the wave while their riders were still shouting.
ST11-07.philosophy: Watch the horses, not the men: ears flat, heads up, the back rank stepping backward; when the horses know, send the wave.
ST11-07.strengths: sees a line break before the men in it know; the best horses of the Horde; a left-handed axe that surprises
ST11-07.weakness: avoids foot fights, stakes and crossbows; blown after eight minutes; never charges on alone

techniques.name: Bear Knife
techniques.desc: Urzag's way at thirteen: inside the claws, the knife under the ribs, and do not let go until the arms are red.

techniques.name: Ears Flat
techniques.desc: His horse tells you before he does: ears back, head up, a half step behind. Go when the horse flinches.

techniques.name: The Left-Hand Axe
techniques.desc: Skarn learned the axe left-handed after a Goroth arrow went through his palm in 1084; the Horde thinks it a style, and so does the man who guarded the wrong side.

techniques.name: Send the Wave
techniques.desc: A minute before his line knows it is breaking, the Magak lances are already moving.

maneuver.name: Read the Horses
maneuver.desc: The captain watches the enemy's horses, not the men, and sends the wave the moment they bunch and toss their heads, about a minute before the riders know the line is breaking.

ST11-08.name: The Ford-Keepers' Spear
ST11-08.origin: Hagar Stonehoof broke a grey stallion whose hooves never went lame and led the Gashmar kin back to the Gordush in 923, and his line has fought for the fords ever since. Ushkar the Grey led the Gashmar wave across at the Gordush Bend in 1049; at the Gashmar Fords in 1070 Conrad's heavy horse broke the line and Garnak, 18, ran, and won his name back on the ladders at Graknak two years later. The Stonehoofs teach their sons to meet men in the water and never to be pulled from a horse, as Mogdur was by Gunnar Harrow in 1033.
ST11-08.philosophy: Fight where the water is to his waist and to your knees: a man wading at a kilometer an hour is a man who cannot dodge.
ST11-08.strengths: fighting in fords and on river banks; spear and hide shield against men coming up out of the water; night crossings
ST11-08.weakness: open ground and heavy horse that does not have to wade; the line still carries the day of the Gashmar Fords

techniques.name: First Out of the Water
techniques.desc: Meet the first man as he climbs the bank, while his feet are still in the mud.

techniques.name: Hide Shield in the Current
techniques.desc: Brace the shield with the current behind it; his blow skids off and your spear comes under it.

techniques.name: Never Pulled Down
techniques.desc: Mogdur was dragged from his saddle at a border meeting and never rode well again; every Stonehoof since is taught to turn a grab into a fall for the man who grabs.

techniques.name: Night Crossing
techniques.desc: Cross where he is not watching, on a moonless night, and come at his fires from the water side.

techniques.name: Hold the Ford
techniques.desc: The line's words: one spear, one bank, and every man who wades at you has to come up the mud alone.

ST11-09.name: The Copper-Tusk Finish
ST11-09.origin: When Gorath founded the Horde in 1041 he split his best riders into three relay waves and gave the third to Ugrash, who had ridden beside him at Vrakoth. The Thirdwaves have finished Gorath's charges at the Gordush Bend, the Gashmar Fords and the Shagnak wells, and every son caps his tusks with copper at sixteen and rides in the Hearth Guard. They have never held the first wave, and they resent it in silence.
ST11-09.philosophy: Wait while braver riders spend themselves; come in fresh when the enemy thinks he has won, and finish it.
ST11-09.strengths: patience rare among orcs; fresh against a tired enemy; the finishing blow and the pursuit
ST11-09.weakness: does nothing in the first minutes; if the first waves fail there is nothing left to finish

techniques.name: Watch the First Two
techniques.desc: Sit the horse behind the line while the first waves strike; you learn him while he tires.

techniques.name: Fresh on the Tired
techniques.desc: Your horse has not galloped and your arms have not swung; his have done nothing else for four minutes.

techniques.name: He Thinks He Has Won
techniques.desc: The waves pull back and he steps after them; the third wave is already in the gap he opened.

techniques.name: The Third Wave Finishes It
techniques.desc: The line's words, and its only boast: the last blow of the charge is copper-tusked.

maneuver.name: The Third Wave
maneuver.desc: The last wave is held back until the enemy has fought two; it comes in fresh on a line that thinks it has won, and rides down whatever runs.

ST12-01.name: The Hundred's Bow
ST12-01.origin: Every herder of the Nine Winds is a rider and an archer, and each tribe's hundreds drill the same way on their own grass: sixty arrows a rider, three to five led horses, six to ten shots a minute at 30 to 80 m and then wheel away. It is the bow that shot the orc relays for hours at Goroth in 874 until they tired. The khan's yard for it is on the reed flats outside Kultau, where any herder's child may come.
ST12-01.philosophy: Never close: shoot, wheel and shoot again, until the man who wants to fight you has nothing left to fight with.
ST12-01.strengths: the long shooting fight; many arrows and fresh horses; wearing down a heavier enemy
ST12-01.weakness: crossbows behind wagons that kill horses; poor once caught at arm's length; must stay near water and grass

school.name: The Reed Flats Butts of Kultau

techniques.name: Loose at Eighty
techniques.desc: The first arrow at eighty paces, before he can do anything about it.

techniques.name: Wheel Away
techniques.desc: Shoot and turn before he reaches you; the horse carries you out of his reach and you breathe.

techniques.name: Sixty Arrows
techniques.desc: Shoot and keep shooting, not to kill but to keep him moving, ducking and sweating under his mail.

techniques.name: Shoot the Horse
techniques.desc: A man in mail is hard to kill and his horse is not; a man on foot on the open steppe is already lost.

techniques.name: Change Horses
techniques.desc: Swing onto the led horse at the canter; a fresh horse is a Rider's second wind.

techniques.name: Ten Shots a Minute
techniques.desc: The quiver empties at the gallop faster than he can raise the shield, and one of them finds the gap.

maneuver.name: Shoot and Wheel
maneuver.desc: The hundreds ride past the enemy at 30 to 80 m, shoot, wheel away and come again on fresh horses; they do not close until he breaks.

ST12-02.name: The Ring Lance
ST12-02.origin: The Riders close only when the enemy is broken, and then they close fast; the light lance and the long knife are for that moment. It was the work of the last hour at the Dry Wells in August 1077, when Ozbek Kharsan closed 6,000 riders around 400 Horde raiders and left none alive, and a lance opened his own jaw from ear to chin. The khan's sweep riders teach it at the yam of Agbay.
ST12-02.philosophy: Do not close until he breaks; when he breaks, be the first one on him.
ST12-02.strengths: the sweep and the pursuit; lance and long knife from the saddle at speed; catching a running man
ST12-02.weakness: a formed line that holds; heavy horse met head-on; no shock against a wall of spears

techniques.name: Run Him Down
techniques.desc: A running man looks back; the lance takes him while he looks.

techniques.name: Long Knife from the Saddle
techniques.desc: Lean out of the saddle as you pass and draw the knife along him; you are gone before he turns.

techniques.name: Through the Gap
techniques.desc: Show the point high and put it low, through the gap between shield and saddle.

techniques.name: The Sweep
techniques.desc: When a line breaks the horsemen sweep the open ground and catch men before they reach the camp; this kills more than the fight did.

techniques.name: No Gap Left
techniques.desc: The last hour at the Dry Wells: every way out is a rider, and every rider is already moving.

maneuver.name: Cavalry Sweep
maneuver.desc: When the enemy's line breaks, the lances are loosed across the open ground to catch his men before they reach a camp, a gate or a wood.

ST12-03.name: The Herder's Rope
ST12-03.origin: A Rider's child is given a rope before a bow: about 1.5 million horses graze the Salt Steppe, and every one that is gelded, broken or sold west is caught first with a horsehair loop. In war the same cast takes a man from the saddle, and Jarak of the Red Wind carries a horsehair rope beside his bow. The Blue Wind's horse-breeders of Otbash, who drive their strings to the channel fairs, keep the catching ring where it is taught.
ST12-03.philosophy: Catch, don't kill: a man pulled from his horse on the open steppe is a prisoner, a ransom or a dead man, as you please.
ST12-03.strengths: unhorsing riders; taking men alive; a hold at a rope's length
ST12-03.weakness: useless in a press or a passage; a man on foot who cuts the rope; armored foot with no horse to pull from

techniques.name: Rope the Arm
techniques.desc: The loop goes over the sword arm and tightens; he can still swing, but not well.

techniques.name: Off the Saddle
techniques.desc: The loop over his shoulders, the horse turned away, and he leaves the saddle backward.

techniques.name: Hobble
techniques.desc: A low cast round his ankle or his horse's foreleg, and a pull; nobody runs far hobbled.

techniques.name: Drag Behind the Horse
techniques.desc: Take a turn of the rope round the saddle horn and ride; a man dragged across stony ground stops fighting quickly.

techniques.name: Bring Him In Alive
techniques.desc: Arms bound to his sides before he knows the second loop is on him; a live prisoner is worth more than a dead one.

ST12-04.name: Toghan's Gallop Bow
ST12-04.origin: Khan Toghan Swift-Arrow rode the legions' mounted-archery course three times on one mare at Torkul in 431 and shot 27 of 27, nine of them backward, and every Rider since learns the backward shot in his memory. The bowmaster Qutlugh taught Ozbek Kharsan at the Arrow Field from about 1053; Dorin Swiftarrow, a half-orc of 40, is the best of the line alive and leads its 400 Swift Arrows. The test is three passes at the gallop, hitting a mark ahead, to the side and behind.
ST12-04.philosophy: Shoot where the horse is going and where it has been: forward on the gallop, sideways on the turn, and backward over the rump at the man who thinks you are running.
ST12-04.strengths: the backward shot; shooting at full gallop in any direction; turning a pursuit into a killing ground
ST12-04.weakness: pursuers with crossbows, or who simply stop; hemmed in, a light rider with a short knife; needs open ground and a good horse

techniques.name: Ahead, Side, Behind
techniques.desc: The Arrow Field's first test: three marks on one pass, and the horse never slows.

techniques.name: The Backward Shot
techniques.desc: Run and let him chase; at full gallop turn in the saddle and shoot back over the horse's rump, and he rides into it.

techniques.name: Feigned Flight
techniques.desc: Flee in honest-looking disorder until his line strings out, then turn on the first man to arrive.

techniques.name: Nine Backward
techniques.desc: Shoot backward as if you were facing him, and watch over your shoulder where his shield goes.

techniques.name: Twenty-Seven of Twenty-Seven
techniques.desc: Torkul, 431: three passes on one mare, twenty-seven shots, nine of them backward, every one in the mark.

maneuver.name: Feigned Flight and Backward Shot
maneuver.desc: The riders break and run in apparent rout; the pursuit strings out across the grass and rides into arrows shot backward at the gallop, and then the riders turn.

ST12-05.name: The Closing Ring
ST12-05.origin: The winter ring hunt of Kyztai is older than the Compact of 925: thousands of Grey Wind riders form a ring tens of kilometers across and close it on the game by flag and horn, and in 952 Kyran of the Grey Wind made the code of seven flags and twelve horn-calls it still uses. Ozbek Kharsan closed a 40 km ring in an hour at the Horse Feast hunt of 1083 with no gap over 200 m, and taught Serik, who leads the hunt now. In war the same ring closes on an army, as at the Wells of Torkul in 871.
ST12-05.philosophy: Do not fight the man in front of you; fight the space around him, and close it until he has nowhere left to stand.
ST12-05.strengths: moving many riders as one; cutting off every retreat; patience; reading dust, ground and distance
ST12-05.weakness: a man who breaks out at one point before it closes; little for a lone duel with no riders behind you; a ring needs time

techniques.name: Close the Gap
techniques.desc: Step where he wanted to go before he goes there; every step he takes is a step further inside your ring.

techniques.name: Dust and the Drum of the Ground
techniques.desc: Ozbek knew where ten thousand riders were without seeing them; one man's weight and footing tell you where he is going.

techniques.name: No Gap over Two Hundred
techniques.desc: He looks for the way out and finds you already standing in it.

techniques.name: The Ring Closes
techniques.desc: Days of patience end in an hour: the ring is shut, the game is inside, and now it is only killing.

maneuver.name: Ring Hunt Drill
maneuver.desc: Thousands of riders keep their places by flag and horn and close a ring around the enemy army; when it shuts, nothing inside it gets home.

ST12-06.name: The Lean Wolf
ST12-06.origin: Kharsa the Thin walked his family's last 40 sheep through the killing winter of 788 on a strip of dried meat a day and came out lean and strong while his brothers died, and his blood still lets a Kharsan live for months on half rations. His great-grandson Ulagan grew up an exile in the salt marshes and built the Wind Empire, and Khatun Saran hid her husband's death for forty days. In the khan's tent the house teaches its children what the Arrow Field does not: patience, hunger, and never letting an enemy see what anything costs.
ST12-06.philosophy: Outlast him: eat less, wait longer, show nothing, and strike when he has used up what you never needed.
ST12-06.strengths: endurance on half rations; patience; hiding a wound or a weakness; the bow at close range
ST12-06.weakness: the lean blood turns to sugar sickness in plenty, with failing eyes and numb feet; slow to finish a fight it could have ended early

techniques.name: Half Rations
techniques.desc: The house's body wastes nothing; what would have tired another man has barely started on you.

techniques.name: Forty Silent Days
techniques.desc: Show him nothing. Saran hid a dead khan for forty days; you can hide a cut, a limp or a blind eye for one fight.

techniques.name: Shoot at the Voice
techniques.desc: Ozbek shoots at the shape a voice gives him at twenty meters. The eyes are not the only way to aim.

techniques.name: The Hungry Outlast
techniques.desc: The house's words: you can wait longer than he can eat.

techniques.name: Wolf in the Snow
techniques.desc: The lean wolf does not chase the herd; it waits for the one that falls behind, and takes the throat.

ST12-07.name: The Red Cord
ST12-07.origin: The Red Wind prides itself on fighting in the old way and on never serving in the khan's guard, and its old way is standing steppe wrestling on the salt flats of Torkul, with no ground work. Temuge the Salt-Wrestler, three times champion of the Horse Feast in the 1040s, taught Jarak of the Red Wind there from about 1070, and Jarak won the Horse Feast five times and has taught the tribe's young riders since 1096. Its champions braid red cord in their hair.
ST12-07.philosophy: Let him commit, then step inside the swing, chest to chest; take the wrist and the haft, turn the hip, and finish with his own weapon.
ST12-07.strengths: taking an attacker's weapon in the first half second; standing throws; fighting inside a long weapon's reach
ST12-07.weakness: anything that reaches from outside the arms: a lance at three meters, a spearman who backs away, a bow at fifty; a patient man who will not attack first

techniques.name: Hold the Jacket
techniques.desc: One hand in his collar, one at his belt, and pull him off his feet the way the salt-wrestlers do.

techniques.name: Inside the Swing
techniques.desc: Step into the blow, under the point or inside the arc, chest to chest before the stroke is finished.

techniques.name: Knife in the Boot
techniques.desc: No sword, ever; a short knife from the boot when the wrestling has brought you close enough to use it.

techniques.name: Over the Right Hip
techniques.desc: Hip in, turn, and he goes over and down on the hard salt. Jarak throws only to the right since 1085, and few know why.

techniques.name: His Own Blade
techniques.desc: At Shagnak in 1096 Jarak took an orc's axe out of its hands and killed two with it: one hand on the wrist, one on the haft, and the weapon changes sides.

ST12-08.name: The Tablet-Bearer's Ride
ST12-08.origin: When Berek made the Tent Law in 926 he chose 500 Blue Wind riders to guard his tent, each with a silver tablet that commands any yam, and Burkit was among the first; his line has held two hundreds of the Silver Tablet Guard ever since. Its sons are raised at the Arrow Field and taught at home how to keep a khan alive. At the Salt Shore in 1041, when two tribes stood still, they lost 60 riders bringing Khan Tulgar's body home to Kharsa.
ST12-08.philosophy: The khan first, the horse second, yourself last: ride between him and the blow, and never be caught on a tired horse.
ST12-08.strengths: guarding another; fighting retreats; a fresh horse at every yam; seeing who comes to the tent
ST12-08.weakness: tied to the man it guards; slow to press an attack; a guard who sees everything and says nothing can be blamed for anything

techniques.name: Any Yam, Any Hour
techniques.desc: The tablet commands a fresh horse at every station; a Tablet-Bearer is never on a tired one.

techniques.name: Between Him and the Blow
techniques.desc: Put your horse across the blow meant for the man you guard, and answer it.

techniques.name: Who Goes In
techniques.desc: Two hundreds at the tent door see who goes in and who comes out; watch his hands, not his face.

techniques.name: Bring the Khan Home
techniques.desc: The Salt Shore, 1041: a fighting ride home with the khan's body across a saddle, and nobody who reached it came back.

maneuver.name: The Tablet Guard Closes
maneuver.desc: The guard rides in a moving ring around its commander; the line may bend and give ground, but the khan's tent does not fall.

ST12-09.name: The Burning Pot
ST12-09.origin: When Khan Toghrul founded the Keepers of the Seeps in 1052 he took a Grey Wind potter named Askar who knew how to seal fire-oil in clay so it would burst and burn, and Askar's line has made and thrown the pots since. Three of them died when the old jar store at Kyzai burned in 1081, and in 1085 they were the first to swear the Keepers' death oath never to speak of the place. They throw the pots in war from saddle or boat, as the Riders burned the Solen barges at Kyzai in 425.
ST12-09.philosophy: Throw and be gone: thirty meters, a burning rag, and a horse already turning before the pot breaks.
ST12-09.strengths: fire at 20 to 30 m from saddle or boat; burning tents, hay and barges; terror
ST12-09.weakness: anyone inside ten meters; their own jars; wet hides, sand and rain; no mail, because of the fire

techniques.name: Rag and Pot
techniques.desc: Light the rag, throw, and the clay bursts on his shield; the fire sticks where it lands.

techniques.name: Throw and Turn
techniques.desc: The pot leaves your hand as the horse turns away; you are out of reach before it breaks.

techniques.name: Fire That Floats
techniques.desc: The oil burns on water and on wet ground; he cannot put it out, only run from it.

techniques.name: Smoke Before Fire
techniques.desc: The first pot is only stink and smoke; he turns his face from it, and the second is fire.

maneuver.name: Night Fire Raid
maneuver.desc: Riders or boats carry fire-oil pots to barges, hay and tents by night, throw and leave; one raid can burn a summer's grain.

ST13-01.name: The Flightfolk Hedge
ST13-01.origin: Alda the Pike-Mother's 4,000 highlanders stood behind stakes at Amberhurst on 4 July 471 and outlasted six relay waves of the Old Horde. When the Upland Flight brought 30,000 lowlanders to the League's mines in 719 their sons were put in the hedge, and the valley levies have drilled the eight-rank Flightfolk hedge every summer since.
ST13-01.philosophy: Five points in front of every man: the hedge does not fight, it stands, and whatever runs onto it dies.
ST13-01.strengths: No horse breaks it from the front; reach beyond any sword; a wall of points across a pass.
ST13-01.weakness: Slow and clumsy to turn; missiles and a flank attack ruin it, and alone out of the hedge a pikeman holds a 5 m pole with no room to use it.

techniques.name: Points Out
techniques.desc: Level the pike and keep the point at his face; a man who cannot reach you has to come round five metres of ash.

techniques.name: Brace the Butt
techniques.desc: Butt against the instep, both hands low: whatever comes at the point stops on it.

techniques.name: Push of Pike
techniques.desc: Eight ranks lean forward at once, and the front of the enemy is walked backwards off its feet.

techniques.name: Low Point at the Horse
techniques.desc: Drop the point to the horse's chest or the man's knee, where no shield is held.

techniques.name: Six Waves
techniques.desc: What the hedge did at Amberhurst: stand through one wave, and the next, and the next, until there are no more waves.

maneuver.name: Pike Hedge
