maneuver.desc: A block of long pikes eight ranks deep with the points of the first five out in front; no horse breaks it from the front.

ST13-02.name: The Herder's Sling
ST13-02.origin: Every highland herder carries a sling against wolves and eagles, and the League keeps 600 herders' slingers in its standing army. Slingers on the heights kept the Solen heads down while the ropes were cut in the Greycloak Gorge on 12 July 331, and a lead bullet from a highland sling still breaks bones through padding at 150 m.
ST13-02.philosophy: A penny's sling and ten years of practice: hit the face from the slope, then go up where he cannot follow.
ST13-02.strengths: Stuns through a helmet and breaks bones through padding; cheap, quick, and shoots from any rock.
ST13-02.weakness: Mail and shields stop most of it; at close quarters the slinger has a herding staff and no armor, and a man who closes fast finds him naked.

techniques.name: Wolf Stone
techniques.desc: One turn of the sling and a stone at the wolf's head: the first thing a herder's child is taught.

techniques.name: Staff and Crook
techniques.desc: Show him the staff's end and hook his ankle with the crook; the slope does the rest.

techniques.name: Lead to the Helmet
techniques.desc: A 40 g lead bullet on the helmet rings his head like a bell, and he is still swaying when you reach him.

techniques.name: Up the Scree
techniques.desc: Go up the loose stone where a man in mail slides back two steps for every three; let him follow if he wants.

techniques.name: Eagle Shot
techniques.desc: The shot that brings a Crown Eagle down off a lamb: at a moving head, from below, and it does not miss.

maneuver.name: Sling Volley
maneuver.desc: Slingers on the slopes hurl lead and clay at 100–200 m; bullets break bones through padding and stun through helmets.

ST13-03.name: The Companies' Count
ST13-03.origin: The Greycloaks learned the crossbow from the Solen legions and made Roseham its workshop; Asa Greycloak made the companies a League office between 952 and 968, and they held the stakes at Hartgate in 1051. Ulric Greycloak, taught by his uncle Odo from 1067, is Captain-General and master of the Highcastle Crossbow Yard, where the companies every realm hires learn their drill.
ST13-03.philosophy: Behind stakes, in ranks, two bolts a minute by the count, and never close: a company that keeps its contract keeps its distance.
ST13-03.strengths: Heavy 150 kg crossbows in ranks; pavise and stakes; a discipline that holds for whoever pays.
ST13-03.weakness: It never closes and is never meant to: a horseman inside 20 m finds a plain soldier with a short sword.

techniques.name: Pavise Down
techniques.desc: Prop the pavise, kneel behind it and span in its shadow; the first thing a company man learns is where to put his body.

techniques.name: Lever Span
techniques.desc: The lever does what a hurt shoulder cannot: a full 150 kg span, and a bolt that goes through a shield.

techniques.name: By the Count
techniques.desc: Ulric counts the drill aloud, and so do you: the man who rushes the pavise arrives exactly when the bolt is ready for him.

techniques.name: Roseham Steel
techniques.desc: A Roseham prod at full span from behind sharpened wood: at sixty metres no mail on Ardan stops it.

maneuver.name: Crossbow Volley
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen in two or three ranks behind pavises shoot in turn, one rank loosing while the others span.

ST13-04.name: The Ridge Run
ST13-04.origin: Hild Stonefoot climbed Mount Roktar in 702 and as First Speaker founded the Cliff Runners, scouts who run ridges and wall tops where no rider can follow. The Ridge School of Redford teaches their climbing, ridge running and mountain scouting to the League's young, and its rock-crews keep the Greycloak Gorge; Ada Stonefoot runs it and captains the 400 Cliff Runners.
ST13-04.philosophy: Stay above him: the ridge is a road only you can walk, so scout from it, strike from it and run along it.
ST13-04.strengths: Climbing and sure feet; scouting from the heights; striking from above and escaping where nobody can follow.
ST13-04.weakness: Light and unarmored: on a valley floor or a plain it has no advantage at all, and it hates water and swaying bridges.

techniques.name: Sure Feet
techniques.desc: Feel the rock through soft boots before you trust it; the man who trusts his eyes on scree is already falling.

techniques.name: From Above
techniques.desc: Drop on him from the ledge he walked under; the fall does half your work.

techniques.name: Stone from the Ledge
techniques.desc: A stone the size of a fist, thrown down from twenty metres above, before he has looked up.

techniques.name: Run the Ridge
techniques.desc: Run where he has to scramble: by the time he reaches the crest you have watched him the whole way up.

maneuver.name: Ridge Running Raid
maneuver.desc: Runners move along crests and wall tops where no rider can follow, scout a camp, strike it from above and run.

ST13-05.name: The Grey Cloak
ST13-05.origin: Bran Greycloak was a herder of Roseham who led 800 highlanders against the Solen weigh-house in 330 and trapped a Solen column in the gorge below Highcastle in 331, and his grey herding cloak became his house's name and its soldiers' coat. The Yard teaches the companies to stand off; the Greycloaks teach their own children what to do when the enemy arrives anyway: the cloak wrapped on the arm, the short sword, and the bolt kept for the last ten metres.
ST13-05.philosophy: Paid and true: keep the contract, keep your distance, and when distance fails, foul his blade in the cloak and finish it short.
ST13-05.strengths: Cloak work that fouls and traps a blade; the short sword up close; a last bolt at point-blank range.
ST13-05.weakness: A wet or slashed cloak is a rag and the short sword is short: a spear or a long blade that refuses to come close is never caught.

techniques.name: Cloak on the Arm
techniques.desc: Two turns of grey felt round the forearm stop a cut and catch a point; every Greycloak child learns it before the sword.

techniques.name: Foul the Blade
techniques.desc: Throw the cloak over his blade as it comes and twist; he spends the next breath getting his sword back.

techniques.name: The Last Ten Metres
techniques.desc: One bolt kept spanned for the man who reaches the pavise; at ten metres it goes through him and his shield.

techniques.name: The Gorge-Maker
techniques.desc: Bran's trick at the gorge in 331: give ground until he is somewhere narrow, then close the door behind him.

maneuver.name: Paid and True
maneuver.desc: Greycloak captains hold their companies to the contract when other hirelings would run; the line stands as long as the pay does.

ST13-06.name: The Stonefoot Stance
ST13-06.origin: Orm Stonefoot gathered eagle eggs from cliffs no one else would climb, and his blood gives the kin a balance the brain trusts over the eyes. The kin settle valley quarrels by the wall-run along the top of Highcastle's wall, where whoever falls loses the case, and their champions almost never lose; they teach their children to fight where others cannot stand.
ST13-06.philosophy: Stone does not sway: take the fight to the wall-top, the ice or the scree, and let the ground throw him for you.
ST13-06.strengths: Perfect balance on walls, ridges, ice and steep ground; shoves and trips that put men over edges.
ST13-06.weakness: On flat ground it is a herder with a staff; and a Stonefoot cannot cross a lake or a swaying bridge without collapsing.

techniques.name: Stone Does Not Sway
techniques.desc: The kin's words: on a wall a hand's breadth wide you stand as on a floor, and wait for him to wobble.

techniques.name: Staff to the Ankle
techniques.desc: Feint high with the iron-shod staff and sweep his ankle; on bad ground one lost step is a fall.

techniques.name: Over the Edge
techniques.desc: The wall-run's ending: a shoulder into his hip where the footing is worst, and he goes down hard.

techniques.name: The Wall-Run
techniques.desc: Run the wall-top at full pace while he edges along it; you watch his feet, and he is too busy watching them himself.

techniques.name: The Eagle's Ledge
techniques.desc: Helga Stonefoot climbed sixty metres of cliff to a Crown Eagle's ledge in 1063; at the edge you are home and he is not, and his own lunge throws him.

ST13-07.name: The Skardush Watch
ST13-07.origin: After the orc raid of 799 the Redfords raised a 22 m beacon tower over the valley road and gave its keeping to the Foxbys of Bearfold, herders who had caught the raiders in the pass on their way home. They have watched the Horde-held Skardush Pass for three centuries and lit the beacon eleven times, and no orc raid has surprised Redford since.
ST13-07.philosophy: See him first, light the fire, and kill him on his way home, when he is tired, loaded and looking back.
ST13-07.strengths: Watching and counting at long range; ambush on the return; the crossbow from a tower; patience.
ST13-07.weakness: A watcher's art that wants warning and a prepared place: a foe who comes straight on in daylight finds a tower guard with a crossbow and a spear.

techniques.name: Count the Riders
techniques.desc: Before anything else, count them and see how they ride; a Foxby knows the raider's business before he does.

techniques.name: Bolt from the Tower
techniques.desc: A bolt from the beacon platform, twenty-two metres up, at the rider who came too close to the road.

techniques.name: Catch Them Going Home
techniques.desc: The Foxbys' first deed in 799: let the raider go by full, and meet him in the pass on the way back, tired and loaded.

techniques.name: Eleven Fires
techniques.desc: Eleven times the beacon was lit and eleven times the tower held; keep the stair, and let him come up it to you.

maneuver.name: Catch Them Going Home
maneuver.desc: The watch lets raiders pass, lights the beacon, and falls on them in the pass on their way home, tired and laden.

ST13-08.name: Cut the Ropes
ST13-08.origin: On 12 July 331 about 1,500 highlanders cut the ropes holding back rocks stacked behind timber cribs above the gorge below Highcastle, and about 1,100 Solen soldiers died under them. The Screes built those cribs and cut the first rope; they have rebuilt them every generation since and teach their children the rope, the hatchet and the long patience of waiting above a road.
ST13-08.philosophy: Never fight the column: wait above it, cut once, and let the mountain do the killing.
ST13-08.strengths: Patience, ropes, hatchets and dropped stones; deadly from above to anyone in a narrow way.
ST13-08.weakness: Everything is set up beforehand: on open ground with no height and no cribs it is a carpenter with a hatchet, and rotten timber fails it.

techniques.name: Hatchet to the Rope
techniques.desc: One clean chop with the crib hatchet, the stroke you have practised on a thousand ropes.

techniques.name: Dropped Stone
techniques.desc: You do not throw the stone; you let it go from above and let the height throw it.

techniques.name: Wait Above the Road
techniques.desc: Lie on the cribs and watch the road for as long as it takes; the man below has to move, and you do not.

techniques.name: The Gorge Eats Them
techniques.desc: Cut the last rope and come down behind the rocks, hatchet in hand, onto whoever is still standing in the dust.

maneuver.name: Rockfall Ambush
maneuver.desc: Boulders stacked above a gorge road behind timber props are released by cutting the ropes; one fall closes the road and kills dozens.

ST14-01.name: The Rift Watch Spear
ST14-01.origin: King Godwin the Careful raised the Rift Watch in 830 to hold the Bellbridge and Falconhaven passes, after outlaw bands from the steppe edge crossed the Rift Heights and burned the farms below. The Scarrow sergeants of Bellbridge, whose first ancestor showed Godwin's captains the goat path round the narrows, made its barricade drill a school, and the Channel Spears of the shore districts now learn it in the yard at Briarhollow before they are sent to a pass or a beach.
ST14-01.philosophy: Find the narrowest place, put something solid in front of you, and kill whoever reaches it: one step forward to thrust, one step back to the post, and never a third.
ST14-01.strengths: Holding a gap, a stair or a barricade; long thrusts over cover; patient men who tire slowly.
ST14-01.weakness: Slow and rooted: in the open a single rank is flanked or ridden down, and in 275 years the drill has stopped bandits and raiders, never an army.

techniques.name: Thrust Over the Rail
techniques.desc: The long thrust that goes over the barricade rail into the first face that reaches it, and comes straight back.

techniques.name: Butt to the Stone
techniques.desc: Spear-butt jammed against the rock and the point at his chest: the man who rushes the pass does the killing for you.

techniques.name: Lean on the Post
techniques.desc: Rest the shield on the barricade post and let the timber take the weight; you breathe while he spends himself against it.

techniques.name: The Goat Path
techniques.desc: Wulf the Shepherd's lesson: know the way round before he does, and be waiting on it, low, with the point at his legs.

techniques.name: Not One Step
techniques.desc: The Scarrow words made into a stance: you give no ground at all, and the man who came for that ground goes down on it.

maneuver.name: The Bellbridge Barricade
maneuver.desc: A barricade at the narrowest point, spears behind it, crossbows on both slopes and a second line a mile back; nobody steps out to chase.

ST14-02.name: The Strand Charge
ST14-02.origin: Greyhaven's knights have ridden steppe horses since Edric II's Horse Road Compact of 925 began trading Redley grain to the Nine Winds, and they learned their trade on the beaches, riding down toll-runners and raiders as they came out of their boats. The 3,000 Tide Knights of Greyhaven and the Redley Plain are still broken to surf and shingle in the strand yard at Hawkcester, beside the paddocks where the Horse Road horses rest after the crossing.
ST14-02.philosophy: Catch them with their feet wet: charge along the hard sand of the ebb into men still coming out of the boats, and wheel away before the crossbows on the ships find you.
ST14-02.strengths: Quick, hardy steppe horses that turn on their own length; charging men who are not yet formed; riding on sand, shingle and surf.
ST14-02.weakness: Light horses and little real war, since a Tide Knight can go a lifetime without a charge: head-on against an Aldmark or Varenna destrier they lose the shock, and soft sand, a rising tide or a set spear line kills the charge.

techniques.name: Ride the Ebb
techniques.desc: Down the wet, hard sand at full gallop, where a steppe horse runs faster than it ever does on a road.

techniques.name: Wheel on the Shingle
techniques.desc: The steppe horse turns on its own length; the destrier opposite does not, and its rider is left facing the sea.

techniques.name: Knee-Deep
techniques.desc: The lance takes him knee-deep in the surf, where a man can neither brace nor step aside.

techniques.name: Through the Landing
techniques.desc: Into the crowd coming off a beached galley before it can form on the sand; the horse does half the killing and the panic does the rest.

techniques.name: The Turning Tide
techniques.desc: Ride away as if beaten, as the tide goes out, and come back with it: the man who follows you onto the open sand meets the point turning.

maneuver.name: The Waterline Charge
maneuver.desc: Tide Knights and Horse Road Riders wait behind the dunes until a landing is half ashore, then ride along the hard sand into its flank.

ST14-03.name: The Wrendale Fog Bow
ST14-03.origin: The Wrendale Bowmen are foresters' sons from the oak and chestnut woods that have built Greyhaven's galleys since Aelric Wren cut timber for King Aldred's fleet. Wulf Brackenridge led them home through the woods at the end of the War of the Channel, and his house, wardens of the Wren Foresters, still trains the crown's 3,000 bowmen to shoot where the channel kingdom fights: in sea fog and in thick forest.
ST14-03.philosophy: Shoot short and shoot first: in fog or among oaks the bowman who looses at a footstep thirty paces off lives, and the one who waits to see clearly does not.
ST14-03.strengths: Shooting by ear in fog and forest; ambush from cover; fast arrows at short range.
ST14-03.weakness: Light forest bows that will not drive through mail at long range: on an open field in clear weather a crossbow line outshoots them and a charge rides them down.

techniques.name: Loose at the Sound
techniques.desc: A cough, a footstep, the chink of mail in the grey: the arrow goes to the sound before the man is a shape.

techniques.name: Behind the Oak
techniques.desc: Put a trunk between you and him and make him come round it; the tree takes his first blow, not you.

techniques.name: Two Before One
techniques.desc: Nock, loose and nock again before the first arrow lands; in the fog it is the second one he never hears.

techniques.name: A Voice in the Fog
techniques.desc: Call out from where you are not; when he turns to the voice you are already behind him with the knife.

techniques.name: The Long Hold
techniques.desc: One arrow drawn to the ear on a rest of low bough and held until his breath goes out, then put through the gap under the arm.

maneuver.name: Fog Ambush
maneuver.desc: Bowmen who know the woods and the shore wait in sea fog or oak shade and shoot into a column at thirty paces, where it cannot see its own flanks or signals.

ST14-04.name: The Tide Divers' Knife
ST14-04.origin: Wenna Tidewell freed the sunken harbor chain from 30 m of water in 719, Osric the Diver cut the Khan's chain at Yarbek in 882, and the Diving School on the harbor steps has trained the Tide Divers ever since. Ness Tidewell, Prince Aldred's daughter, has been Diver-Master since 1099; off Wolfhaven in 1092 she and her divers cut the cables of the Northreach fire rafts under the keels.
ST14-04.philosophy: Go where he cannot follow and cannot see: under the keel, into black water, by touch, with a knife and as much breath as your blood allows.
ST14-04.strengths: Breath, cold and calm; cutting cables, straps and holds by feel; dragging a man into water where his mail drowns him.
ST14-04.weakness: No armor and half deaf by forty: on a dry quay in daylight a diver is a lightly armed man who cannot hear the one behind him.

techniques.name: The Slow Heart
techniques.desc: One deep breath in and none out: the diver's heart slows as it does on the harbor steps, and the fear of the fight drains out with it.

techniques.name: Saw the Cable
techniques.desc: The saw-backed knife dragged across whatever holds: a raft cable, a shield strap, the inside of a wrist.

techniques.name: Over the Side
techniques.desc: Arms round his waist and over the side together; in the water his mail and his fright fight on your side.

techniques.name: By Touch in Black Water
techniques.desc: Eyes shut, a hand on his arm: you feel the blow begin in his muscles before he knows he has started it.

techniques.name: Five Minutes Down
techniques.desc: The Diver-Master's own: take hold of him and hold your breath with him. He has one minute in him, and you have five.

maneuver.name: Under the Keels
maneuver.desc: Divers go down from the guard boats at dusk and cut the enemy's anchor cables and raft lines, so his line drifts apart before the fight begins.

ST14-05.name: The Brookhurst Gangway
ST14-05.origin: The Galley Yard trains crews beside the Brookhurst shipyards that Osric the Diver's silver built in the 880s, teaching galley ramming, rowing drill and boarding. Edwin Brook taught oar and gangway there from 1066; his pupil Rolf Brightwater, Admiral of the Channel, holds the Yard now and teaches both the Blackreef cog he took off Beaconstone in 1086 and the two galleys Kettil Frost burned off Wolfhaven in 1092.
ST14-05.philosophy: A galley fights as one body: the crossbow from the stern platform first, the ram if the helmsman can, then the whole crew down the gangway together, and never one man alone.
ST14-05.strengths: Sea legs on a pitching deck; the volley before the boarding; crew drill, timing and wind at the oar.
ST14-05.weakness: Without a crew around him a Yard man is a heavy sailor with an axe, slow on land; and men shed their mail before boarding, so a cut that mail would stop goes home.

techniques.name: Sea Legs
techniques.desc: Knees soft, feet wide, weight low: the deck rolls under the other man, not under you.

techniques.name: From the Stern Platform
techniques.desc: The windlass crossbow kept by the steering oar, loosed across the gap before the grapnels fly.

techniques.name: Down the Gangway
techniques.desc: Two hundred men behind you and one plank in front: you cannot stop, because they will not let you.

techniques.name: Back Water
techniques.desc: Back the oars hard and let his ram, or his rush, spend itself on the empty sea where you were; a Yard captain watches the other helmsman's hands, not his bow.

techniques.name: Never Alone
techniques.desc: The Admiral's rule: you hold and the man beside you strikes, so whoever comes at you meets two blades and an answer he did not see coming.

maneuver.name: Volley and Board
maneuver.desc: Crossbows sweep the enemy deck from the stern platform as the ram strikes, then the marines go down the gangway together before his crew can stand up.

ST14-06.name: Knife in the Teeth
ST14-06.origin: The Tidewells were chain-divers before they were kings, and their arms still show a silver diver with a knife in his teeth. From Cedric the Admiral, who swore himself king in the Oath Hall in 761, to Osric the Diver, who ruled twenty deaf years by the hand-signs his divers used under water, the royal house has taught its children to fight on a galley's stern with a sword in one hand and the diver's knife ready in the other, and to give orders without a word.
ST14-06.philosophy: Fight with your eyes, not your ears: watch his shoulders, sign to your guard, keep the knife back for the moment his blade is tied up, and never waste a breath.
ST14-06.strengths: Calm and wind in a long fight; the hidden second blade; silent orders by hand-sign to the men around them.
ST14-06.weakness: The diving takes their ears: no shouted warning reaches an older Tidewell, and the blow from behind is never heard.

techniques.name: Watch the Shoulders
techniques.desc: A deaf man learns to see a cut begin in the shoulder before it ever reaches the arm.

techniques.name: The Knife Comes Out
techniques.desc: While his blade is bound on your sword the second blade comes out of nowhere, as the diver on the arms carries it.

techniques.name: Two Fingers to the Guard
techniques.desc: Two fingers flicked at the guard beside you, and the answer comes from where he was not looking.

techniques.name: One Breath Down
techniques.desc: Everything on one held breath, as on the long way down to the ring: no flinch, no pause, no second thought until it is done.

techniques.name: Deep Water Keeps
techniques.desc: The house words in the body: when the fight goes loud and black for other men a Tidewell goes still, as at forty metres down, and waits for the light.

ST14-07.name: The Fanhope Banner-Guard
ST14-07.origin: On the night of 19 July 882, while Osric the Diver was under the Khan's chain at Yarbek, the marine Cuthbert Fanhope held the king's banner upright on the lead galley under the arrows until the chain came free, and Osric knighted him on the deck. A Fanhope has stood beside the Diver Banner on the king's stern in every sea fight since; Sir Oswy held it off Beaconstone in 1008 with an arrow through his thigh, and the family drills its children to stand, to cover and to endure.
ST14-07.philosophy: Your feet are nailed to the deck beside the banner and the king: cover, endure, strike only what comes within reach, and never step back.
ST14-07.strengths: Shield cover against arrows and bolts; fighting on through wounds; guarding another man's body.
ST14-07.weakness: A Fanhope will not leave his post: he can be shot at, worn down and walked around, and he never takes the fight to anyone.

techniques.name: Under the Arrows
techniques.desc: Shield high and tilted, chin down, the banner pole in the crook of your arm: let them empty their quivers into the lime-wood.

techniques.name: The Staff-Butt
techniques.desc: The iron-shod butt of the banner staff, driven into the face of the first man over the rail.

techniques.name: Break the Shaft
techniques.desc: Sir Oswy's lesson off Beaconstone: snap the arrow off, bind the thigh with the banner cord, and stand up again.

techniques.name: Cover the King
techniques.desc: Your shield goes across another man's body and your sword answers the blow it took; a Fanhope reads the hand-signs and knows where the king will step.

maneuver.name: The Diver Banner
maneuver.desc: While a Fanhope holds the silver diver upright on the king's stern the whole fleet steers by it, and no galley turns for home.

ST14-08.name: The Chainley Windlass Bar
ST14-08.origin: Edric Chainley forged the windlass gears for Prince Aldred's chain towers in 772 and raised the chain in a gale before a Velgradan raider could slip in, and the Chain-Maker knighted him for it. His children have worked the windlasses and served as sergeants of the Chain Guard ever since, and they fight as they work: with the oak bar of the windlass, forearms made huge by cranking, on the narrow stairs of the towers.
ST14-08.philosophy: Leverage beats strength: get the bar under his weapon, his arm or his heel, set your feet, and turn him like a windlass.
ST14-08.strengths: Grip and forearms like rope; levering, prying and breaking holds; holding a narrow tower stair.
ST14-08.weakness: A crude, slow weapon: a quick swordsman in the open is inside the bar before it moves, and a Chainley learns gears before footwork.

techniques.name: Greasy Hands
techniques.desc: Fingers black with gear-grease close on his wrist: his grip slides on your skin, and yours does not slide on his.

techniques.name: Under the Heel
techniques.desc: The bar goes low behind his heel and you turn it like a crank; he is on his back before he knows he was touched.

techniques.name: The Right-Hand Stair
techniques.desc: Tower stairs turn to the right: the man coming up has his sword arm against the wall and your bar against his ribs.

techniques.name: Raise It in a Gale
techniques.desc: Sir Edric's heave: back, legs and both arms behind one turn of the bar, and a shield or a man goes over the rail.

maneuver.name: Raise the Chain
maneuver.desc: The windlass crews raise the iron chain across the harbor mouth on its floats and the Chain Guard man both towers; no ship comes in until a Chainley lets it.

ST14-09.name: The Tarrant Drill
ST14-09.origin: Sewald Tarrant led the boarding party that took a Velgradan galley off Beaconstone in 1008, and in 1010 King Edmund made him a squire and a captain of the new Brookhurst Boarders. His family has taught the Boarders their axe-drill ever since and buries a man or two in every generation; Ivo Tarrant lost eighty boarders at Wolfhaven in 1092, and his son Ingram wants a fight with Sevany to win the name back.
ST14-09.philosophy: First over the rail and loudest on the deck: throw the hatchet as the hulls touch, jump before the grapnel lines are tight, and keep going until nobody is left in front of you.
ST14-09.strengths: The first rush of a boarding; short axe work in a crowd; throwing hatchets at close range; nerve.
ST14-09.weakness: Reckless: the first man over the rail is the first man the crossbows find, and a Tarrant held at the rail for a moment has no plan but to push harder.

techniques.name: Boots First
techniques.desc: Over the gap before the lines are tight, boots first into the nearest man, and up again before he is.

techniques.name: Hatchet Across the Gap
techniques.desc: A hand-axe thrown as the hulls touch, at the first face that shows above the enemy rail.

techniques.name: Over the Rail
techniques.desc: The family words shouted as you go: a boarding is won in the first ten heartbeats, and you mean to spend every one of them.

techniques.name: The Count of Three
techniques.desc: Boss to the face, axe to the shield edge, knee to the body: the drill every Boarder learns, three blows that land as one.

maneuver.name: The First Wave
maneuver.desc: The Boarders go over the bow in one wave behind a Tarrant, hatchets first and axes after, before the enemy crew can form at the rail.

ST15-01.name: The Coast Road Lance
ST15-01.origin: King Aurelio Falcone raised the Coast Road Knights in 1013 and named them for the victory of 896, when Roderic the Lionheart's knights broke Yargan the Hawk among the olive terraces of the coast road. They are drilled to wait behind terrace walls while crossbows shoot the enemy riders into a crowd, then to charge down the road in a column four to six wide.
ST15-01.philosophy: Wait behind the wall until the enemy bunches, then come down the road all at once.
ST15-01.strengths: timing, a narrow and heavy charge, fighting among walls, terraces and sunken roads
ST15-01.weakness: wasted on the open steppe against horse archers who will not bunch; a knight who charges too early is alone in a crowd

school.name: The Heights Yard of the Coast Road Knights

techniques.name: Behind the Terrace
techniques.desc: Sit the horse behind the olive wall and let the crossbows work; the knight who waits has a fresh horse when it matters.

techniques.name: Down the Road
techniques.desc: Out of the sunken lane at a gallop, knee to knee, into riders who have no room to turn.

techniques.name: Column of Four
techniques.desc: Four lances abreast on a road six metres wide: the point of the column hits first and the rest drive it through.

techniques.name: Into the Crowd
techniques.desc: The lance is gone in the first man; the sword comes out and cuts down on heads and shields packed too close to move.

techniques.name: Yargan's Bane
techniques.desc: The charge of 896: the whole banner out from behind the terraces at once, onto riders bunched by the walls and the bolts.

maneuver.name: Coast Road Charge
maneuver.desc: Knights wait behind terrace walls while crossbows bunch the enemy riders, then charge down the road four to six wide and spread into the crowd.

ST15-02.name: The Deep Wall Bolt
ST15-02.origin: Marius the Mason finished the Deep Walls in 806, twelve metres down and forty up, and crossbow sergeants have held them since; through the Khan's siege of 895 to 897 the Heights Garrison shot from the loopholes with two loaders to every master. A Mironi sergeant of the landward gate shot the Khan's engineer who first brought fire-oil pots against the harbor.
ST15-02.philosophy: A wall, a loophole and two loaders behind you: shoot the man who matters, then the next.
ST15-02.strengths: aimed shots through mail, patience, fighting from cover and in the dark
ST15-02.weakness: a slow weapon off the wall; once a man is on the wall-walk the crossbowman has a knife and very little room

school.name: The Landward Gate Yard of Morhaven

techniques.name: Bolt from the Loophole
techniques.desc: Rest the bow on the stone, wait for him to cross the gap between two merlons, and loose.

techniques.name: Span Under Cover
techniques.desc: Kneel behind the merlon while you span; the wall takes the arrows meant for you, and your breath comes back.

techniques.name: Visor Shot
techniques.desc: The bolt rings off the helm an inch from the slit; the Yard teaches you to aim for the slit, and even the miss leaves him reeling.

techniques.name: Wall-Walk Knife
techniques.desc: When the ladder tops the wall, drop the bow, step into the man's climb and knife him under the arm.

techniques.name: The Engineer's Bolt
techniques.desc: The shot that killed the Khan's fire-pot engineer: wait all day for the one man who matters, then do not miss.

maneuver.name: Wall Crossbow Relay
maneuver.desc: Each master shooter on the wall has two or three loaders who span and pass bows; one loophole keeps up four to six shots a minute.

ST15-03.name: The Hidden Spear of the Edicts
ST15-03.origin: The Edict Spearmen are the village levies of the Falcone Edicts, about 3,600 on duty at any time, and their trick is older than the Edicts: the Wind Riders who burned the Felano harvest in 693 and came again in 893 taught the coast farmers to hide. They lie flat in tall grass or a sunken lane while horsemen draw the raiders on, and rise at a horn call 30 to 50 metres in front of the pursuers with their spears set.
ST15-03.philosophy: Be where the horseman does not look, rise all at once, and let his own speed put him on the point.
ST15-03.strengths: ambush, setting the spear against a charge, numbers and nerve
ST15-03.weakness: farmers with spears: once they are found, or met on foot by a steady swordsman, the line has little to answer with

techniques.name: Down in the Grass
techniques.desc: Lie flat and still while he rides past; from the grass you see where he is looking, and it is never at you.

techniques.name: Rise on the Horn
techniques.desc: Up on the horn call with the point already level; the first he knows of you is the spearhead.

techniques.name: Set the Butt
techniques.desc: Kneel, put the butt against your heel and the point at the horse's chest: the charger spits himself on his own weight.

techniques.name: Hell Boar Stop
techniques.desc: The crossbar that stops a Castina hell boar on the point holds a man there too, long enough for a friend to come.

techniques.name: The Whole Village Rises
techniques.desc: Every man of the vale stands up out of the wheat at once, shouting, and the raider's horse rears before the spears even reach him.

maneuver.name: Hidden Spear Line
maneuver.desc: Spearmen lie flat in tall grass or a sunken road while horse draws the enemy on; at a horn call they rise in front of the pursuers and set spears.

ST15-04.name: The Far-Eye Watch
ST15-04.origin: Tancred the Steadfast's Tower Edict of 898 put a sworn lookout in a stone tower every 10 km along the coast and the steppe edge, and a charcoal-burner's boy who read flags at 3 km from the Castina tower founded House Falcone. The Tower of Far Eyes at Morhaven teaches the Watch its flags, fires and ciphers, and Dame Serena Falcone, who spotted the Redsail galleys 28 km off Felano in 1096, is its master.
ST15-04.philosophy: See first, say true, and let the man who knows where the enemy is choose where the fight will be.
ST15-04.strengths: seeing the blow coming, reading a line from afar, signals that move an army in time
ST15-04.weakness: watchers, not fighters: a lookout is no match for a swordsman at the foot of his stair, and glare, fog and night blind the best eyes

techniques.name: Read the Flag
techniques.desc: Before the hand moves the shoulder does; a lookout learns to see the flag before it is raised.

techniques.name: Sun at Your Back
techniques.desc: Step round until the sun is behind you: the Red Widow killed Prince Leone out of the setting sun, and the Tower never forgot it.

techniques.name: Signal Arrow
techniques.desc: The first shot marks the man the way a fire-arrow from the tower marks where the riders must ride.

techniques.name: Blind Before False
techniques.desc: The lookout's oath is to go blind rather than lie; a master sees the true blow behind the false one, and answers that.

maneuver.name: Far-Eye Signal
maneuver.desc: Towers and flag-riders pass the enemy's moves along the line in minutes, and every company is where it should be before the blow lands.

ST15-05.name: The Castina Counter-Mine
ST15-05.origin: Castina miners rebuilt Morhaven's landward walls with listening galleries 12 m under the ditch, and on the Night of the Mines in November 895 Arrigo Castor led them into Khan Ulagan's tunnel and fired it. House Castor opened the Mine Hall of Castina on its own ground in 898; Master Otto Deepgrave hears digging through 30 to 40 m of rock, and in 1098 killed two ore-thieves with the pick in a narrow heading.
ST15-05.philosophy: Hear him first, break in where he does not expect, and fight in the dark where his numbers count for nothing.
ST15-05.strengths: tunnels, doorways and the dark, listening, smoke and the short pick
ST15-05.weakness: slow feet and no armor; in daylight on open ground a miner is a strong man with a tool, and a target

techniques.name: Ear to the Stone
techniques.desc: A bowl of water on the gallery floor ripples before you hear the pick; feel his weight shift the same way.

techniques.name: Pick over the Rim
techniques.desc: The miner's pick hooks over a shield rim and comes down through the shoulder behind it.

techniques.name: Smoke Before Men
techniques.desc: Fire the brushwood and fan the smoke down the gallery; the men who come out coughing are the ones you fight.

techniques.name: Night of the Mines
techniques.desc: Break through the last hand of earth into his tunnel and be on him before his lamp has turned.

techniques.name: Fire the Props
techniques.desc: The counter-miner's last answer when the gallery is lost anyway: bring the roof down on him and crawl out the other way.

maneuver.name: Counter-Mining
maneuver.desc: Listeners in the galleries find every enemy mine, break into it, fire it or smoke it, and the walls above stay standing.

ST15-06.name: The Falcon's Stoop
ST15-06.origin: Piero the Falcon read the flags of the next tower at 3 km from the Castina tower in 935, and his grandson Aurelio saw 42 corsair sails at 30 km in 1011 and was crowned for it. The house teaches its children what to do with eyes that see a bow's draw at 150 m: shoot first, and in close, watch the blade's shoulder instead of its point.
ST15-06.philosophy: See it first and act on it first; the fight is decided before the other man knows it has begun.
ST15-06.strengths: first shots, seeing a feint for what it is, keeping the fight at a distance of the Falcone's choosing
ST15-06.weakness: light-built and never trained to the press; a Falcone without the eyes, like Prince Tancred, has the drill but not the edge, and fog or night takes it from the rest

techniques.name: We Saw It First
techniques.desc: The house words, in a fight: you saw his weight go onto the front foot before he decided to step.

techniques.name: A Range He Cannot Judge
techniques.desc: Shoot from further than the other man believes a shot can carry; he is still walking in when it lands.

techniques.name: The Shoulder, Not the Point
techniques.desc: Watch the shoulder, which moves first, and the point is never a surprise; let it pass and answer it.

techniques.name: The Stoop
techniques.desc: The falcon folds and drops: one cut, from the side the eyes chose three moves ago.

ST15-07.name: Felt Coat and Saddle Bow
ST15-07.origin: Baldo Sabine took 300 horses from steppe raiders in 823 and married a Wind Rider trader's daughter, and the Sabines have married steppe women every other generation since; they wear felt coats over mail and shoot from the saddle. Ottavio Sabine rode by night to burn the grass under the Khan's herds in 896, and Dame Oriana Sabine commands the 3,000 Santora Riders, though a Nine Winds archer beat her at her own Horse Fair in 1099.
ST15-07.philosophy: Half grass, half wall: shoot like the steppe, then close like a knight where the steppe would ride away.
ST15-07.strengths: shooting from the saddle and then closing in mail with the sword, which steppe riders will not do
ST15-07.weakness: good at both and the best at neither: the Nine Winds outshoot them and the Coast Road Knights outweigh them, and Sabine pride rides into ambushes

techniques.name: Loose at the Canter
techniques.desc: Shoot as the horse's feet leave the ground, the steppe way the Sabine brides brought to Santora.

techniques.name: Wheel Away
techniques.desc: Turn short before his reach and come round again; a heavy horse chasing a steppe mare tires first.

techniques.name: Close Like a Knight
techniques.desc: When the steppe rider expects you to wheel, do not: the mail under the felt goes straight in with the sword.

techniques.name: Shoot the Horse
techniques.desc: A rider on foot is half a rider; the house shoots the horse's legs and lets the man walk.

techniques.name: Santora Pride
techniques.desc: Straight at them without a look behind: it wins most days, and it lost 120 riders in the ambush beyond Santora in 1097.

maneuver.name: Felt-Coat Raid
maneuver.desc: The Santora Riders shoot the enemy's horse lines from the saddle, ride off before he forms, and run down whatever scatters.

ST15-08.name: The Pellegrane Sally
ST15-08.origin: Renzo Pellegrane, a sergeant who had ridden with the Sabine to the Nine Winds, got the keeping of the six small forts of the Horse Road from Tancred II after the compact of 930, and his descendants still hold them for the Marshal of the Steppe March. A fort of a hundred men survives raiders by the sally: out through the postern by night, strike the camp, and back before the grass riders have mounted.
ST15-08.philosophy: Never wait to be besieged: go out in the dark, hit hard, and be behind the gate again before dawn.
ST15-08.strengths: night fighting, short sharp sallies, shield work in a gateway
ST15-08.weakness: a sally caught outside the walls is lost; in a long open fight a Pellegrane runs out of tricks and breath

techniques.name: Through the Postern
techniques.desc: Come out of the little door low and to the side, where a man watching the gate does not look.

techniques.name: Shield in the Gateway
techniques.desc: One shield fills the gateway; whoever comes at it meets the rim and then the sword over it.

techniques.name: Among the Tents
techniques.desc: Cut ropes, cut men coming out of the tents half-dressed, and do not stop to fight anyone properly.

techniques.name: Back Before Dawn
techniques.desc: Break off, walk backward to the postern with the shield up, and count your men through the door.

maneuver.name: Night Sally
maneuver.desc: The garrison slips out at night to burn engines and tents and is back inside before the besiegers can form.

ST16-01.name: The Ward Bolt
ST16-01.origin: Ostra hires its walls, but since the Wind riders burned the villages around Sabena in 893 its citizens have drilled once a month in the Ward Bands, 11,000 of them now, with a crossbow for the window and a short blade for the stair. The banks pay for the bolts, and the butts below the West Gate teach the rest: shoot down a street, never across a square.
ST16-01.philosophy: Shoot from the window, the stair or the barricade, one good bolt at a time, and never stand in the open to do it.
ST16-01.strengths: Streets and walls; aimed bolts at short range; many hands, cheaply armed.
ST16-01.weakness: Citizens paid by the month: slow to span, no stomach for an open field, and gone the day the pay is late.

school.name: The Ward Butts of the West Gate

techniques.name: From the Window
techniques.desc: Shutter open, one bolt down into the street, shutter closed.

techniques.name: Behind the Barricade
techniques.desc: Carts, barrels and a counting-house door across the lane, and you behind them.

techniques.name: Down the Street
techniques.desc: The lane is narrow and straight; he has nowhere to step aside.

techniques.name: The Stair Blade
techniques.desc: He came up the stair while you were spanning; the short blade was waiting.

techniques.name: Paid on the First
techniques.desc: The pay came this morning in good silver, and a paid man holds his place.

techniques.name: The Ledger Shot
techniques.desc: One bolt, aimed as carefully as a banker adds a column, and just as final.

maneuver.name: Crossbow Volley
maneuver.desc: Ward crossbowmen shoot in turn from walls, windows and barricades, one rank loosing while the others span.

ST16-02.name: The Sea Wall Bill
ST16-02.origin: The earthquake of 697 threw down Ostra's harbor mole, and the Sea Walls raised after it, like Calora Castle on the Sun Road and the castle of Fort Barica on the coast, have been held ever since by hired men who learn one narrow trade. A bill to hook a man off a ladder, a shield to fill an embrasure, and a gate held while the chain goes up, as it did on New Year's Day 1044 when the Tessarian ships were trapped in port.
ST16-02.philosophy: A wall is a narrow place: hook, push, fill the gap and let the stone do the rest.
ST16-02.strengths: Walls, gates, ladders and embrasures; reach in narrow places; pulling men off their feet.
ST16-02.weakness: A wall art: in open ground the bill is slow and heavy, and an enemy who never comes to the wall leaves it nothing to do.

school.name: The Wall-Walk Yard of Fort Barica

techniques.name: Bill Down the Ladder
techniques.desc: The hook on the top rung or the top man, and a hard shove outward.

techniques.name: Fill the Embrasure
techniques.desc: The shield fills the gap in the parapet, and the bill comes out under it.

techniques.name: Hook and Pull
techniques.desc: The bill's hook goes behind his shield or his knee, and you pull.

techniques.name: Chain Up
techniques.desc: Hold the gate for as long as the windlass takes, and not a breath less.

techniques.name: The Stone Does the Rest
techniques.desc: Off the wall-walk with him; the fall finishes what the bill began.

maneuver.name: Gate Holding
maneuver.desc: Billmen and shields fill the gate and the wall-walk while the harbor chain is raised, and nobody follows a beaten attacker out.

ST16-03.name: The Calora Lance
ST16-03.origin: After the Wind riders burned Camina and the villages around Sabena in 893, Ilaria the Ledger decided the city needed horsemen of its own, and in 897 she hired Taddeo Cavaroni, a Morhaven horse-sergeant who had fought the Khan, to raise the Calora Lances. Cavaronis have led them since under contract, escorting Temple coin and Lunetti couriers on the Sun Road and chasing bandits in the Calora hills, and they have not fought a battle in two centuries and are proud of it.
ST16-03.philosophy: Escort, pursue, and never charge what you can ride around: the lance is for a fleeing bandit, not a formed line.
ST16-03.strengths: Escort and pursuit on roads; medium horse that can chase, turn and come back.
ST16-03.weakness: Untested in two centuries: medium horse that breaks on a set spear and loses a straight charge to real knights.

techniques.name: Courier's Escort
techniques.desc: Your horse between the courier's and the man in the road.

techniques.name: Lance at the Gallop
techniques.desc: A lighter lance than the knights carry, aimed at a man who is running.

techniques.name: Down the Sun Road
techniques.desc: A bandit on foot cannot outrun a horse for long, and you know every bend of the road.

techniques.name: Wheel Away
techniques.desc: You turn off before the clash and come back where he is not looking.

techniques.name: Remember Camina
techniques.desc: The day the Lances were raised for: raiders in the olive hills, and a full charge at last.

maneuver.name: Road Pursuit
maneuver.desc: Medium horse sweeps the Sun Road and the hills behind a beaten enemy and rides down everyone who runs.

ST16-04.name: The Ostran Buckler
ST16-04.origin: Buckler Hall stands on Buckler Lane by the West Gate among the fencing yards and the armorers, and teaches sword and buckler to merchants, guards and their sons for fighting in streets and on stairs; the buckler-men of the lane guarded the Exchange benches before the Temple's coin came to Ostra in 951. Master Rico Ambro, quick, joking and light on his feet, holds it now and captains the Exchange Guard besides.
ST16-04.philosophy: Keep the buckler out in front like a second hand, keep your feet moving on the cobbles, and hit the hand that holds the sword.
ST16-04.strengths: Quick close fighting on cobbles and stairs; punching with the buckler; footwork and cuts to the hand.
ST16-04.weakness: A small shield and a short reach: against a spear, a horse, a crossbow or a shield wall it has little, and it is a duelling art in a city that hires its soldiers.

techniques.name: Punch the Buckler
techniques.desc: The little iron boss straight into his face from a hand's length away.

techniques.name: The Cobble Step
techniques.desc: Half a step on the round stones, and he commits to where you were.

techniques.name: Hand Before Heart
techniques.desc: The Hall's first rule: cut the hand that holds the sword, and the heart can wait.

techniques.name: The Stair Fight
techniques.desc: Buckler high, blade low, a step above him, and every blow he throws comes back.

techniques.name: Ambro's Joke
techniques.desc: The master laughs, opens his guard, and you take the bait; then your sword is on the cobbles.

ST16-05.name: Paid, We Hold
ST16-05.origin: When the Twelve began the Sabena Citadel in 1084 after the dyers' riots, they wanted crossbowmen with no cousins in Sabena, and the Highland captain Rolf Brennock brought 400 men down from the valleys. His daughter Ulla has held the citadel since 1099, paid on the first of every month in good silver and never once mutinous, and the family teaches its children the Highland way: the heavy bow spanned with a lever behind a pavise, in ranks, by the count.
ST16-05.philosophy: Plant the pavise, span by the lever, and shoot only what the contract says to shoot.
ST16-05.strengths: Heavy bolts that go through mail and shield; pavise cover; discipline under pressure.
ST16-05.weakness: Slow: one heavy shot and a long span, and a man who closes before the lever turns meets only a sword behind a big board; it will not shoot into a crowd.

techniques.name: Plant the Pavise
techniques.desc: The tall board goes into the ground first, and everything else happens behind it.

techniques.name: The Lever Span
techniques.desc: A heavier bow than an arm can span, and a heavier bolt than a shield can stop.

techniques.name: Behind the Board
techniques.desc: He rounds the pavise expecting a crossbowman and finds a short sword.

techniques.name: Through Shield at Sixty
techniques.desc: The Highland bolt at sixty paces goes through the board and the arm behind it.

ST16-06.name: Behind Us, Gold
ST16-06.origin: On New Year's Day 951 the Temple's coin moved to the Lunetti vault, and the Lunettis chose the Scudieri, buckler-men of Buckler Lane who had guarded the Exchange benches, to stand at its door. A Scudieri has stood there since without once going inside; every Scudieri boy trains at Buckler Hall before he is ten, and the family adds its own lesson on top of Rico Ambro's: the door does not move.
ST16-06.philosophy: Plant your feet in the doorway and let them break on you; you do not follow, and you do not go in.
ST16-06.strengths: Holding a door, outlasting attackers, a guard that does not tire.
ST16-06.weakness: It never moves: give it no door to hold, or walk away and come back with crossbows, and it has nothing.

techniques.name: Feet Planted
techniques.desc: Heels on the threshold stone, and the buckler between you and everything.

techniques.name: Buckler in the Teeth
techniques.desc: He leans in to look past you, and meets the iron boss.

techniques.name: Let Them Break
techniques.desc: Every blow lands on the buckler and costs him more than it costs you.

techniques.name: The Door Does Not Move
techniques.desc: A hundred and fifty years of Scudieri have stood here; you will not be the one who stepped aside.

ST17-01.name: The Sea Keep Boarding Axe
ST17-01.origin: The Sea Keep, the old Solen harbor fort of Qadira that held out against the Wells from 590 to 604, is the naval arsenal of the sultans, and its school has drilled marines since the first fleet. Since the Night of Fire of 19 August 1024, when 19 Qadiri galleys burned under the towers of Sabra, it has taught the 2,400 Sea Keep Marines to board behind wet ox-hide shields with grapnel and boarding axe. Faris Bahri holds it in 1105 and drills endlessly for a fire he has never seen burn.
ST17-01.philosophy: Grapnel, volley, over the bow behind the wet hide, and take the deck before it takes fire.
ST17-01.strengths: Boarding, footing on a moving deck, swimming, fighting in smoke behind wet hides
ST17-01.weakness: Untested against real fire-oil, and wet hides only buy time; on dry land in the open a marine is a light man with an axe

techniques.name: Grapnel and Haul
techniques.desc: The iron hook over his rail or his shield rim, and a hard haul that brings him closer than he likes.

techniques.name: Hide Up
techniques.desc: The wet ox-hide shield up and forward; smoke, sparks and the first blow all slide off it.

techniques.name: Over the Bow
techniques.desc: The marines' rush down the gangway: shield first, axe behind, and nobody stops on the rail.

techniques.name: Axe-Beard Hook
techniques.desc: The beard of the boarding axe catches the shield rim or the wrist and pulls it out of the way.

techniques.name: Through the Smoke
techniques.desc: Breathe through the wet cloth, keep low where the air is clean, and come out of the smoke where he did not look.

techniques.name: Taking the Deck
techniques.desc: The last rush of a boarding: hides locked, axes over the top, and the enemy crew driven over their own far rail.

maneuver.name: Wet-Hide Boarding
maneuver.desc: Sea Keep Marines cross behind wet hides after a crossbow volley and take the enemy deck by the bow.

ST17-02.name: The Sunwall Sling
ST17-02.origin: The hill chiefs of the Sunwall fought the Solen beside Prince Idris from 258 to 262 and kept their slings when they submitted, and they slung beside Hazir's Riders in the Sabun Pass in 593. The sultans have left the Tabir valleys alone in return for their javelins, and the slinging terraces under Fort Tabir now train the 2,000 hill javelins and slingers of the Sunwall for the crown. A sling costs a penny and the skill takes years, and the hillmen say that is why coast men carry crossbows.
ST17-02.philosophy: Stay above him on the rocks, break bones at a hundred paces, and never be where his feet can reach.
ST17-02.strengths: Range, blows that stun through a helmet, sure feet on slopes, cheap kit
ST17-02.weakness: No armor and no reach up close; a man who closes fast through the stones finds a slinger with only a knife

techniques.name: Lead Bullet
techniques.desc: A lead bullet the size of a quail's egg at eighty paces; it does not need to find a gap.

techniques.name: Up the Scree
techniques.desc: Two goat-steps up the scree, and he must climb to reach you, blowing all the way.

techniques.name: Javelin Pair
techniques.desc: Two hill javelins at twenty paces, the first into the shield to drag it down, the second over it.

techniques.name: Skull-Stone
techniques.desc: A baked-clay bullet to the helmet: the iron holds, but the man inside it is somewhere else for a moment.

techniques.name: Knife on the Ledge
techniques.desc: When he finally reaches the ledge the slinger is not on it, and the knife comes from the rock beside him.

techniques.name: The Long Whirl
techniques.desc: The master's shot from high ground, whirled once at full arm: at 150 paces a bullet that breaks a collarbone through mail.

maneuver.name: Sling Volley from the Heights
maneuver.desc: Sunwall slingers line the slopes above a pass road and rain lead and clay on a column that cannot climb to them.

ST17-03.name: The Emirs' Wheel
ST17-03.origin: The emirs of Qadir have ridden as medium horse since Sultan Idris I took the Bahesh mouth in 848, and the 1,600 of the Emirs' Horse are their sons and riders, mounted from the studs of Hazifa. The riding ground there teaches the curved sword and the light lance from the saddle, and above all the wheel: ride at the enemy, cut, and turn away before the camel riders of Sabra can close. The Sabun Pass of 1022 hangs over the yard, and every rider is told never to go where he cannot see the heights.
ST17-03.philosophy: Charge to the cut, never to the stop: wheel, cut and wheel again.
ST17-03.strengths: The mounted sword, quick charges and wheels, pursuit on open ground
ST17-03.weakness: Horses shy at camels and die without water; it needs open ground and fails in passes and against a steady spear line

techniques.name: Passing Cut
techniques.desc: The curved blade drawn across him as the horse goes by, never stopping to fence.

techniques.name: Turn on the Haunches
techniques.desc: Sit back and turn the horse in its own length; his thrust meets air and the horse's quarters.

techniques.name: Light Lance
techniques.desc: A light lance at the gallop, aimed at the chest and let go before it can break the arm.

techniques.name: The Wheel
techniques.desc: Ride at him, swerve off before contact, and cut as he turns to follow.

techniques.name: Ride Him Down
techniques.desc: Lance couched for once, the whole horse behind it, into a man already off balance.

techniques.name: Stirrup Stroke
techniques.desc: Standing in the stirrups at the gallop, the curved sword brought down from the shoulder through mail and collarbone.

maneuver.name: Wheel and Cut
maneuver.desc: The Emirs' Horse charges in squadrons that cut and wheel away by turns, never stopping in the press.

ST17-04.name: The Pass Wardens
ST17-04.origin: Jalal II rode out of the Sabun Pass ambush of 1022 on half a water-skin while his men died of thirst, and he walled Mirad with royal silver in 1032–1036 so it would never happen again. Behind those walls the Wardens' Yard trains the 1,600 Wardens of the Sabun and the younger sons of House Tarsi in the spear and crossbow of a pass, and in climbing to the heights before an enemy can. Nabil Tarsi, who has held the Sabun Pass since 1096, is its master and speaks little.
ST17-04.philosophy: Hold the narrow place, own the heights, and make him pay for every step with bolts.
ST17-04.strengths: Holding passes, the crossbow from cover, climbing, patience
ST17-04.weakness: Built for a pass: on open ground it is slow, and a goat path round the side undoes the whole wall

techniques.name: Bolt from the Barricade
techniques.desc: Spanned behind the stones and loosed at sixty paces at the first man round the bend.

techniques.name: Barricade Point
techniques.desc: The spear laid over the barricade stones; he must climb into it.

techniques.name: Climb to the Heights
techniques.desc: Up the goat path first: whoever holds the slope sees every move made below.

techniques.name: The Pass Wall
techniques.desc: Spears in the gap, crossbows behind them: whoever comes through takes the point and then the bolt.

techniques.name: Warden's Patience
techniques.desc: Let him attack uphill in the heat for an hour while the Warden drinks from the walled cistern and waits.

techniques.name: The Sabun Volley
techniques.desc: Every bolt in the company at one shout, at forty paces, into a column with nowhere to go.

maneuver.name: Pass Holding
maneuver.desc: The Wardens hold the narrowest point of a pass with a barricade and crossbows on both slopes; a thousand supplied men stop ten thousand.

ST17-05.name: Of the Jar
ST17-05.origin: Zahir the Thirstless crossed the Burning Waste in January 790 with 600 camel riders and took Qadira without a battle. By the house law of 815 every Zahiri son rides two days in the Sabun heat on half a water-skin at fifteen, and those who come back strong are called 'of the Jar'. Jalal II rode out of the Sabun ambush of 1022 that way, and the house teaches its sons to fight as they ride: outlasting any man who must stop to drink.
ST17-05.philosophy: Outlast him: keep the blade moving and the breath slow, and win in the hour when he is begging for water.
ST17-05.strengths: Endurance in heat and thirst, the long fight, a sword arm that does not tire
ST17-05.weakness: The stones that come with the blood can fell a Zahiri mid-fight with pain no training reaches, and the style has little for the quick first exchange

techniques.name: Half a Water-Skin
techniques.desc: Slow breath, small movements and no wasted step: the Zahiri way of keeping strength in the heat.

techniques.name: The Long Hour
techniques.desc: Make him do the work: every parry small, every one of his cuts long, until his arm is lead.

techniques.name: Ride Clear
techniques.desc: What Jalal II did in the Sabun Pass: break off, ride clear on what water you have, and come back when they cannot.

techniques.name: Thirst-Cut
techniques.desc: The cut that comes when he licks his lips: hard, unhurried, at a man with nothing left to lift the shield.

techniques.name: Guardian of the Water
techniques.desc: The Sultan's own title as a guard: he cannot be worn down, and every attack on him costs the attacker water he does not have.

ST17-06.name: The Basir Oath
ST17-06.origin: For 177 years the Tarsi were the date lords of Basir, until in 1024 Sabran riders came through the gardens and Emir Anas Tarsi's eldest son died among the palms defending them. Anas led 3,000 people east to Mirad in 1025, and in 1060 his grandson Bashir swore at twelve never to sign any title but Emir of Basir. The house teaches its sons the fight of that last day in the gardens: curved sword and long knife together among trunks, ditches and walls where a camel cannot follow.
ST17-06.philosophy: Fight where the rider cannot come: between the trunks, over the ditch, close enough for the knife.
ST17-06.strengths: Fighting in close cover, two blades at once, killing riders who come in among the trees
ST17-06.weakness: On open sand it is two short blades against a lance, and the oath makes a Tarsi reckless against any Sabran

techniques.name: Sword High, Knife Low
techniques.desc: Sword high and knife low, both moving at once, so he cannot watch both.

techniques.name: Round the Trunk
techniques.desc: A step behind the palm trunk, and the knife comes round the other side of it.

techniques.name: Over the Ditch
techniques.desc: Jump the irrigation ditch into him knife first; he lands in the water and you do not.

techniques.name: The Rider's Leg
techniques.desc: A rider among the trees has his leg at your shoulder: cut the tendon of the man or the camel, and both come down.

techniques.name: Emir of Basir
techniques.desc: The oath sworn at twelve, said aloud, and both blades go in together.

ST17-07.name: The Jar Gate
ST17-07.origin: Saqr of the Crossing rode across the Burning Waste with Zahir the Thirstless in 790, and Zahir made him keeper of his door. A Saqri has commanded the Jar Gate company of the Guard of the Water Jar for fourteen sultans, and in 973 a Saqri captain refused Idris II's order to close the House of Water. The house trains its sons in mail with the sword and round shield for one place only: a doorway at night, where a guard must stand for hours and kill in a heartbeat.
ST17-07.philosophy: Stand in the door, trust no one who comes to it, and strike the instant the hand moves.
ST17-07.strengths: Doorways and corridors, the night watch, reading an attacker's hands, sudden counters
ST17-07.weakness: Made for the threshold: in the open, or against several men who need not come through the door, a Saqri is one man in heavy mail

techniques.name: Shield in the Door
techniques.desc: The round shield fills the lower half of the doorway, and nothing gets past it below the chest.

techniques.name: Watch the Hand
techniques.desc: Look at the hand, not the face: the instant it moves for the knife, the sword is already moving.

techniques.name: Night Draw
techniques.desc: From a standing doze at the door to a cut across the face in one motion.

techniques.name: Threshold Thrust
techniques.desc: Point low through the gap of the door into the belly of the man behind the first.

techniques.name: We Crossed With Him
techniques.desc: The house's words: the guard does not leave the door while the Sultan lives behind it, and whoever comes through pays.

ST18-01.name: The Two-Banks Spear
ST18-01.origin: The crown has drilled its soldier-farmers in the spear since the village spears of the Tamari Revolt of 981–989 drove the Tessarians out of the valley with no armor but linen. The javelin it learned from its enemies: Solen javelin men killed the teams of 300 Tamari chariots at Kadah in 207, and the valley never forgot. Every Field Spear and every Spear of the Two Banks learns two javelins and a 2.4 m ash spear in the yards of Akayn, between the harvest and the flood.
ST18-01.philosophy: Throw first, then keep the point between you and him, and trust the man beside you to do the same.
ST18-01.strengths: Reach, a javelin before the clash, cheap kit, steady in a line
ST18-01.weakness: Quilted linen and a hide buckler: no armor to speak of, and lost alone or against heavy horse in the open

school.name: The Spear Yards of the Two Banks

techniques.name: Two Javelins
techniques.desc: Two light javelins at fifteen paces, the second thrown before the first lands.

techniques.name: Point Between Us
techniques.desc: Keep the leaf head at his face and make him walk onto it.

techniques.name: Javelin in the Shield
techniques.desc: A javelin stuck in his shield drags it down, and the spear goes in over the top.

techniques.name: Second-Rank Thrust
techniques.desc: From behind the front man's shoulder, a thrust he never sees past his own shield.

techniques.name: Hold the Dyke Path
techniques.desc: On a dyke path one man wide, the spear waits, takes the rush on the point and thrusts again.

techniques.name: The Harvest Line
techniques.desc: The whole yard's drill in one step: point levelled, the count shouted, and the spear driven through him as a sickle goes through standing wheat.

maneuver.name: Javelin and Spear Line
maneuver.desc: The Field Spears throw two javelins on a horn and close with levelled spears before the enemy has his shields up again.

ST18-02.name: Low in the Water
ST18-02.origin: The Crocodile Boats were formed after Amenhar I's death in 1017 from the river men who had closed the water around Tamar in 987: long, low boats of twenty oars that hide in the reeds and strike at night. Their crews learned to come alongside a barge without a sound, cut it loose and fight on its deck with a short spear and a knife. Nakht the Oar keeps the boat stair at Talim where every crew of the 1,200 is made.
ST18-02.philosophy: Come in the dark and from below, cut the rope before the man, and be back in the water before the alarm.
ST18-02.strengths: Night, boarding, swimming, fighting on a pitching deck
ST18-02.weakness: No armor at all; on open ground, or against a high-sided ship whose archers are awake, a boat crew with knives

techniques.name: Over the Gunwale
techniques.desc: Up the side in one heave and into him before he has found his feet on the deck.

techniques.name: Cut the Rope
techniques.desc: The knife goes for the strap, the grip or the cord, never first for the man.

techniques.name: Under the Oars
techniques.desc: Hook him over the side and hold him in the brown water; the river does half the work.

techniques.name: Silent Stroke
techniques.desc: Muffled oars, a hand on the planking, and the first cut comes before anyone has seen the boat.

techniques.name: Deck Spear
techniques.desc: A short spear thrust up from the low boat under the barge rail, where the mail ends.

techniques.name: The Crocodile's Roll
techniques.desc: Seize, twist and go down together into the water, the knife working, and come up alone.

maneuver.name: Night Cutting-Out
maneuver.desc: Crocodile Boats slip into an enemy anchorage after moonset, cut the barges loose and fire what they cannot take.

ST18-03.name: The Rashira Javelin Ride
ST18-03.origin: Tamar lost its chariot horses to Solen javelins at Kadah in 207 and was a kingdom without horsemen for eight centuries. In 1036 Amenhar II gave the rift pastures above Rashira to breeders of desert mares crossed with Sandfolk stallions and asked for a royal cavalry, and the King's Horse rode out of those studs; in the Hungry Year of 1088 the army ordered the mares eaten, and the herd survived only because it was hidden in the hills. Its riders learn at the horse yard of Rashira to throw from the saddle and never to charge a formed line.
ST18-03.philosophy: Ride in, throw, wheel away, and come again from the side he is not watching.
ST18-03.strengths: Speed, javelins from the saddle, scouting, running down raiders
ST18-03.weakness: Few horses and light ones; against heavy horse or a steady spear line it can only run

techniques.name: Saddle Javelin
techniques.desc: Thrown from the trot at twenty paces, the horse already turning away.

techniques.name: Wheel Away
techniques.desc: Turn the horse off his point and let the distance do the parrying.

techniques.name: Side Pass
techniques.desc: Show him the right flank, ride the left, and watch where his shield goes.

techniques.name: Ride-Down
techniques.desc: Light spear underarm into a man who is already running; the horse's shoulder finishes it.

techniques.name: Hamstring Pass
techniques.desc: A low cut at the legs in passing; a man who cannot run cannot follow a horse.

techniques.name: The Rift Circle
techniques.desc: Ride a ring round him at javelin range, throwing on every pass, until his shield arm will not come up.

maneuver.name: Javelin Wheel
maneuver.desc: The King's Horse rides across the enemy front throwing javelins, wheels away out of reach, and rides down whatever breaks.

ST18-04.name: The Granary Staff
ST18-04.origin: In October of the Hungry Year of 1088 about 2,000 starving people came for the granaries of Tamar, and Intef the Shield held the granary gate all day without killing one of them. The Granary and Wall Watch learned then that a spear is the wrong tool against your own neighbors. Since that winter the Watch and the vizier's constables, who are paid in grain, have been drilled at the granary yard in the long staff and the bare hand: clear a gate, break a grip on a sack, and put a thief down alive.
ST18-04.philosophy: Clear the gate, break the hold, put the man on the ground, and never give the crowd a corpse.
ST18-04.strengths: Disarms, crowd work, taking men alive, cheap to learn
ST18-04.weakness: A staff against a steel blade and a man who means to kill: the Watch hesitates, and a killer does not

school.name: The Granary Yard of the Watch

techniques.name: Butt to the Belly
techniques.desc: The staff's end short and hard under the ribs; he folds and the crowd sees no blood.

techniques.name: Break the Grip
techniques.desc: Rap the knuckles, twist the wrist, and the knife or the sack falls.

techniques.name: Bar the Gate
techniques.desc: Staff held crosswise at chest height with the next man holding the other end, and the push comes back on the pusher.

techniques.name: Sweep the Legs
techniques.desc: Low along the ground behind his heels, then the staff across his chest.

techniques.name: Down and Held
techniques.desc: Knee on his back, staff across his neck, and two of the Watch kneeling on his arms.

techniques.name: The Hungry Year Gate
techniques.desc: What the Watch learned in 1088: take the whole rush on the staff, strip the weapon, put the leader down alive and hold the gate all day.

ST18-05.name: The Wall That Comes Back
ST18-05.origin: The House of the Shield at Tamar claims its chain from the spear walls of the Tamari Revolt of 981–989, and its tall shield of layered ox-hide roofs a column against arrows. Khnum the Tall held the House from 1060 to 1086 and took in a Monuti farmer's son of twelve named Intef, who won his name at the river below Talim in 1074 pulling broken men back into line. Since the granary gate of 1088 every Son of the Mother learns the three-breath drill: a 40-man front rebuilt on its center in under fifteen seconds.
ST18-05.philosophy: Fight the wall, not the man: plant the tall shield, call two names, and let the line close on you.
ST18-05.strengths: Rebuilding a broken front, the Shield Roof against arrows, endurance in the line, the overhand spear over the rim
ST18-05.weakness: Alone or flanked by horse it is a man behind a door; fire eats hide shields, and a short fast swordsman inside the spear is trouble

school.name: House of the Shield at Tamar

ranks: Master of the House of the Shield

techniques.name: Lock the Rims
techniques.desc: Tall shield locked to the shields beside it, knees bent, and nothing comes through the seam.

techniques.name: Overhand Over the Rim
techniques.desc: The ash spear comes down over the top of the shield into the face or the collarbone.

techniques.name: Shield Roof
techniques.desc: Kneel and roof: the hide takes the arrows and the stones while the arm counts the breaths.

techniques.name: Three Breaths
techniques.desc: The front breaks, you plant, shout two names, and on the third breath the wall is whole and the spear goes back in.

techniques.name: Kneel and Let It Pass
techniques.desc: When the wall goes for good, drop behind the tall shield, let the rush trip over you, and come up behind it with the spear.

techniques.name: Forty in Three Breaths
techniques.desc: The rebuilt front steps forward together on the master's call: rims into teeth, forty spears over the top, and the men who broke the wall find it in front of them again.

maneuver.name: The Three-Breath Wall
maneuver.desc: The Sons of the Mother rebuild a broken front on their center in three breaths, and men who thought they were through find the wall in front of them again.

ST18-06.name: The Ibis in the Reeds
ST18-06.origin: Delta bowmen shot from the reed banks when Queen Nefira's men threw the Solen landing back at Marira in 642, and 2,000 Tamari archers broke Maximus's line at Felano in 667. The Reed School of Marira teaches the delta's way: the short Tamari bow from a reed bed or a low boat at 30 to 80 m, and a way out through channels a stranger cannot follow. Hapu the Reed, trained by a Tashiri captain of the reed stations, holds it in 1105 and tells every class that a tall shield is only a target.
ST18-06.philosophy: Never be where the arrow came from: shoot from the reeds, move through the water, and shoot again.
ST18-06.strengths: Ambush shots, silent movement, the first arrow, marsh and river ground
ST18-06.weakness: In the open against a charge, or when the reeds are burned in the dry season, an archer with a short bow and a linen kilt; and the delta fever takes more of them than any enemy

techniques.name: From the Reeds
techniques.desc: A shot at forty paces from a reed bed nobody had looked at twice.

techniques.name: Wade and Vanish
techniques.desc: Down into the water to the chin and away along the channel, while he swings at reeds.

techniques.name: Boat Shot
techniques.desc: Kneeling in a low boat that does not rock, a narrow head at the gap below the helmet.

techniques.name: Reed Knife
techniques.desc: When he wades in after you, the reeds part on the wrong side and a knife goes for the back of his knee.

techniques.name: Arrow at First Light
techniques.desc: From the reeds at first light, as the delta captains say: the sun low behind you and his face turned into it.

techniques.name: The Ibis Stands Still
techniques.desc: Stand motionless in the reeds for an hour, as the ibis does, until the one man worth the arrow stands still too.

maneuver.name: Reed-Bank Archery
maneuver.desc: Ibis Archers hide in reed beds and small boats along the river, shoot barge crews and marching columns at close range, and vanish into the channels.

ST18-07.name: The Red Spear of Kadah
ST18-07.origin: House Kadari has led Tamar's soldiers since Kheti I gave it the Kadah nome in 670, and its captains led the archers who broke Maximus at Felano in 667. In April 985 Tessarian hired soldiers burned Kadah on a sealed imperial order; Wenamun Kadari was carried out of the fire at five and raised his son Rahotep, General of the River since 1086, on nothing but that story. The house teaches its blood the spear and bow of the Rift Guard on the natron road, and teaches them never to forgive.
ST18-07.philosophy: Fight as a man who remembers a fire: close fast, strike for blood, and do not stop while he is standing.
ST18-07.strengths: Ferocity, the first rush, spear and bow together, fighting on rift slopes and roads
ST18-07.weakness: Rage: a Kadari overcommits and chases, and anyone who insults Kadah can draw him into a trap

techniques.name: Kadah Remembers
techniques.desc: The house's words shouted, and the first thrust comes with the weight of a burned town behind it.

techniques.name: Rift Shoulder
techniques.desc: On the stony rift slopes, shoulder into him from above and let the hill throw him down.

techniques.name: Natron Road Shot
techniques.desc: The Rift Guard shoots raiders off the natron road from the posts above it before it ever closes.

techniques.name: Blood-Price
techniques.desc: The cut for the dead of 985: low, deep, and meant to bleed him while he watches.

techniques.name: The Burning Tower
techniques.desc: Through the man, over him, and on to the next before he has hit the ground.

maneuver.name: Kadah Remembers
maneuver.desc: The Kadari Rift Guard comes on shouting the house's words and does not stop to take prisoners.

ST18-08.name: The Wolf on the Border-Stone
ST18-08.origin: Pernakht, a captain of the Talim rising of 981, held the Fort of Talim after the Peace of 989, and since 1018 his line has given the Talim March its Warden six times in seven. A century of Tessarian raiders, deserters and hungry men crossing the Neck has taught the house one craft: let them reach the river, close the road behind them and run them down before the border-stone. Neferhor of Talim, the first woman to hold the March, was given it in 1090 because the soldiers would have no one else.
ST18-08.philosophy: Let the raider come to the river, close the road behind him, and hunt him down before he reaches the stone.
ST18-08.strengths: Ambush at fords, pursuit, reading a raider's next move, the spear on foot or horse
ST18-08.weakness: A hunter's craft: against a man who stands and fights in a formed line it has no special answer, and its riders are few

techniques.name: Horn at the Beacon
techniques.desc: Hear the horn and know the road: you are where he must cross before he knows you are there.

techniques.name: Ford Thrust
techniques.desc: A wading man has no feet to dodge with; the spear takes him in the thigh while the water holds him.

techniques.name: Close the Road
techniques.desc: Ride across his line of retreat and make him run the long way round in the heat.

techniques.name: Wolf's Pursuit
techniques.desc: Run him down from behind, the spear at his legs and then his back, as the house has done to raiders for a hundred years.

techniques.name: The Neck Road Ends Here
techniques.desc: The house's words as a stand: plant on the border-stone, read his last rush and answer it.

maneuver.name: Close the Neck
maneuver.desc: On a beacon signal the Wardens hold the fords and loose the March horse on raiders cut off from the border.

ST18-09.name: It Does Not Touch the Ground
ST18-09.origin: On Return Day, 21 June 989, a spearman named Seshen carried Amenhar I's sun-boat standard through the gate of Tamar ahead of the king, and the office has been hereditary since. The standard fell once, at the river below Talim in 1074, and a boy of the house lifted it out of the mud and carried it beside Intef the Shield. Every Sesheni son learns the tall shield at the House of the Shield, and at home learns what nobody else is taught: how to fight one-handed under the standard pole and never let it fall.
ST18-09.philosophy: The standard stays up: fight one-handed, give ground before you give the pole, and let the men see it.
ST18-09.strengths: Rallying a line, steadiness under pressure, using the standard pole as a bar and a club
ST18-09.weakness: One hand is always on the pole, so it has little attack of its own, and every archer on the field aims at the man under the standard

techniques.name: Pole Bar
techniques.desc: The pole held across the body turns a blow and keeps the cloth above the heads.

techniques.name: Bronze Butt
