techniques.desc: The bronze foot of the standard pole, driven back into the face of the man who reached for it.

techniques.name: Lift from the Mud
techniques.desc: What the boy did in 1074: get the standard up out of the mud first, and only then think of the wound.

techniques.name: Follow the Boat
techniques.desc: Step forward with the standard so the line must follow it, and put the shield rim into whoever stands in the way.

techniques.name: The Cloth Stays Up
techniques.desc: The pole upright, the shield over it, and the short sword answering anyone who comes for the cloth.

maneuver.name: Under the Sun-Boat
maneuver.desc: The Sesheni carry the king's standard into the front, and the Sons of the Mother give no ground while it stands.

ST18-10.name: The River Is Our Sword
ST18-10.origin: Wadjar the Dyke-Builder, a corvée foreman of Talim, broke the dykes at Lake Nubako in October 983 so that the late flood drowned the road, and 11,000 Tessarians fought in the mud and lost. His line has mastered the Dyke Corps since, and in the Hungry Year of 1088 Tjati Wadjari broke dykes again on Rahotep Kadari's order. The house teaches its sons to fight as it builds: with mattock, maul and spade, knee-deep in mud, where a man in mail cannot keep his feet.
ST18-10.philosophy: Choose the mud, break his footing, and fight him where the river has already half beaten him.
ST18-10.strengths: Fighting in mud and water, knocking men off their feet, endurance at heavy work
ST18-10.weakness: Engineers, not swordsmen: slow tools against a quick blade, and on hard dry ground the trick is gone

techniques.name: Mattock Swing
techniques.desc: A dyke-builder's mattock comes over hard and hooks whatever it lands on.

techniques.name: Into the Mud
techniques.desc: Step back onto the wet silt and pull him after you; mail sinks, and so does he.

techniques.name: Corvée Back
techniques.desc: A month of dyke work every year makes a back that does not tire: lean on the tool and breathe while he blows.

techniques.name: Break the Bank
techniques.desc: The maul goes into his shield as into a weak dyke, and the man behind it goes down with the earth.

techniques.name: Open the Sluice
techniques.desc: Lure him onto the low ground, then let the water in: knee-deep, cold and fast, and he cannot stand in it.

maneuver.name: Cut the Dykes
maneuver.desc: The Dyke Corps breaks the banks so the flood drowns roads and camps; the enemy must wade, and his horse cannot come on at all.

ST19-01.name: The Noon Lance
ST19-01.origin: Rashid Bahar the Far-Seer won the feud with Clan Talun on the plain of Sarad in 1000 with the first noon charge, when the glare blinds everyone but a Bahar, and founded the Noon Lances. The School of the Long Ride on the Camel Ground of Zarak teaches every captain of the clans the camel, the stars, thirst and that charge. Jabir Hazari, the finest camel lancer alive, has held it since 1085, and in 1101, after a bad year for his herds, he sold its Desert Night March to two Zanaran riders for 200 gold weights.
ST19-01.philosophy: One pass, sun behind you, lance underarm from a running camel, and gone before they form; never fight for ground.
ST19-01.strengths: The noon charge, the first pass, the camel lance, thirst and the night march
ST19-01.weakness: Afoot or at night it is a man with a curved sword; an enemy who refuses battle until evening never meets the charge at all

techniques.name: Underarm Lance
techniques.desc: The 3.5 m tamarisk lance held low under the arm, with the camel's whole run behind it.

techniques.name: Gone Before They Form
techniques.desc: Ride through and away; by the time he has turned there is nothing to fight but dust.

techniques.name: Star Road
techniques.desc: The Desert Night March: walk well to well by the stars, lie up in shade, and arrive fresh where he arrives thirsty.

techniques.name: Sun Behind
techniques.desc: Come out of the sun: he squints, lifts the shield against the glare, and the point comes in under it.

techniques.name: One Pass
techniques.desc: One run, one strike, no second look: the lance goes in at the gallop and the camel carries you past.

techniques.name: The Noon Charge
techniques.desc: Sarad again: at the hottest hour, the sun high behind, the whole line rides at men half spent and dazzled in their mail.

maneuver.name: Noon Charge
maneuver.desc: At midday in the desert summer, sun high behind them, the camel lances ride at an enemy dazzled and half spent by the heat.

ST19-02.name: The Marir Saddle-Bow
ST19-02.origin: The hill clans of the south-west came into the Riders from the Haliya Hills about 640, and Clan Marir's bowmen shot from camelback outside Mirah in 1060 while the Zanarans starved for water. The bow ground of Marir teaches the hill-camel bow to riders of all the southern clans: a short bow shot from the high saddle on the move, in hill country where camels pick their way and horsemen cannot follow.
ST19-02.philosophy: Shoot from the saddle, keep a hill between you, and let him chase until his water is gone.
ST19-02.strengths: Archery from the camel, hill ambush, wearing an enemy down at range
ST19-02.weakness: A short bow does little against mail at long range, and in a straight close fight the archer has only a knife

techniques.name: Down Over the Shield
techniques.desc: From two metres up on a walking camel, a shot down over the top of his shield.

techniques.name: Hill Between
techniques.desc: Put a ridge between you and his horse: he climbs, and you ride round.

techniques.name: Turning Shot
techniques.desc: Shoot at the trot, nock while the camel turns, and shoot again before he has closed.

techniques.name: Shoot the Water-Skins
techniques.desc: Arrows into the skins on his saddle, not into him; in the hills of Marir thirst kills slower, but surer.

techniques.name: Behind the Kneeling Camel
techniques.desc: If he reaches you, slide down behind the kneeling camel and come round its neck with the knife.

techniques.name: Arrow from the Ridge
techniques.desc: The master's shot from a ridge-top at a hundred paces into the one gap in his mail, as the Marir bows did outside Mirah.

maneuver.name: Ridge to Ridge
maneuver.desc: Camel bowmen shoot from the ridges, give ground, and shoot again from the next ridge until the enemy is out of water.

ST19-03.name: The Water-Skin Knife
ST19-03.origin: Camel theft between clans is almost a sport in the Waste, and a Janir boy's first raid is a camel stolen and returned the next day with a gift. In the Salt War of 1058–1063 the clans fought Zanara's columns at night with knives rather than lances, and Clan Nahuma's raiders cut water-skins rather than throats, because an army without water breaks within days. The night camp at Januma teaches the craft to riders of every clan: the approach by starlight, the cut and the slip away.
ST19-03.philosophy: Come at night, cut what he needs to live, and be a shadow among the camels before he wakes.
ST19-03.strengths: Night raiding, stealth, cutting gear and water, the knife at close quarters
ST19-03.weakness: A night craft: in daylight, against a man who is awake and armed, the raider has a short blade and no armor

techniques.name: Cut the Skin
techniques.desc: The knife goes into the water-skin at his hip, not into him; he will feel it within the hour.

techniques.name: Starlight Approach
techniques.desc: Low, slow and downwind of the camels, until you are close enough to hear him breathe.

techniques.name: Halter Knot
techniques.desc: Hook the arm, wrap it in a loop of halter rope and pull; the blade and the man both go down.

techniques.name: Shadow Among the Camels
techniques.desc: Step behind a kneeling camel and come out under its neck on the side he is not watching.

techniques.name: Hand Over the Mouth
techniques.desc: Hand over his mouth, blade in under the jaw: the raider's last resort when a cut skin is not enough.

techniques.name: Dry Camp
techniques.desc: The night camp's masterpiece: every skin cut, every halter slipped, and in the morning he must walk to water through the noon.

ST19-04.name: The Bare Eye
ST19-04.origin: Rashid Bahar, born in 960, was the first of his line with the sand-eyes: he could see riders' dust at 15 km over white sand at noon. He won the plain of Sarad in 1000 and was acclaimed Speaker in 1001, and four Bahar have held the Speakership since. The chief's kin go bare-eyed in the glare and teach their children to fight looking into it; but they are nearly blind on a moonless night, and Bakr Bahar died on the Hazir River in 1062 on just such a night.
ST19-04.philosophy: Fight looking into the sun he cannot face: see every move he makes and choose the moment.
ST19-04.strengths: Seeing through glare, reading the field and the man, timing the charge, sword, lance and bow alike
ST19-04.weakness: Nearly blind on moonless nights: a Bahar caught after dark outside the ring of sentries is helpless

techniques.name: Bare-Eyed
techniques.desc: Look straight into the glare where he hides his blade; for a Bahar there is nothing there to hide in.

techniques.name: Riders' Dust
techniques.desc: See him coming long before he sees you, and be already where he will have to turn.

techniques.name: Out of the White
techniques.desc: A shot loosed from the white sand at noon, from a place he cannot bear to look at.

techniques.name: We See the Noon
techniques.desc: The house's words: at noon a Bahar sees the cut begin while the other man sees only light.

techniques.name: The Far-Seer's Moment
techniques.desc: Rashid's gift at Sarad: wait, watching, until the line squints and wavers in the glare, then go at the one place it has opened.

maneuver.name: Sun at Back
maneuver.desc: A Bahar chooses the field and the hour so the sun is in the enemy's eyes, and sees through the glare what the enemy cannot.

ST19-05.name: The Well-Court Goad
ST19-05.origin: Hazir the Rider led eleven clans out of the towns' faith in 581, and since the Well Truce of 604 his clan has guarded the Well of Samar and its cisterns for 5,000 pilgrims. Within sight of the water no blade may be drawn and no blood shed, so the Riders of the Well learned to turn the lance around: the butt, the camel-goad and the bare hand stop men at the Well-court without killing them. Hazir's own saddle and lance hang there still and are carried round the Well each Well Day.
ST19-05.philosophy: No blood within sight of the water: turn the lance, stop the man, and kill only beyond the last cistern.
ST19-05.strengths: Stopping men without killing, pilgrim and crowd work, the lance butt and the goad, steadiness
ST19-05.weakness: It holds back, and against a killer who does not, the Well-guard gives away the first blow

techniques.name: Turned Lance
techniques.desc: The lance swung butt-first into his belly; at the Well-court the point stays toward the sky.

techniques.name: Camel-Goad
techniques.desc: The hooked goad catches his wrist and turns him like a stubborn camel.

techniques.name: The Ring Round the Well
techniques.desc: Riders in a ring with lances crossed; whoever pushes against it is pushed back the way he came.

techniques.name: No Blood at the Water
techniques.desc: Down off his feet, the lance shaft across his chest, and held for the elders' judgment.

techniques.name: Beyond the Last Cistern
techniques.desc: Out past the last cistern of the pilgrim road the lance turns round again, and the Riders of the Well kill like any other clan.

maneuver.name: Pilgrim Road Escort
maneuver.desc: The Riders of the Well ride ahead of and behind the pilgrim bands from cistern to cistern, and nobody touches a pilgrim on the Well road.

ST19-06.name: Mirah Stands
ST19-06.origin: Sayf the Hill-Rider brought the herders of the Southern Hills into the Riders about 600, and Fahd Sayf took the hill town of Mirah about 885. The Sayf are the one clan that lives behind walls, and from April 1060 Muhsin Sayf held Mirah for five months against 18,000 Zanarans and 30 elephants. The house fights its feuds with poetry at the Mirah market before anyone draws a blade, and teaches its sons the curved sword, the sling from the wall and the verse that comes first.
ST19-06.philosophy: Speak first, sling from the wall second, and draw the curved sword only when the gate is the last thing left.
ST19-06.strengths: Holding walls and gates, the sling from above, unsettling a man with words before the fight
ST19-06.weakness: A townsman's fight in a nomad's land: off the walls and on open sand the Sayf are slower riders than the clans they lead

techniques.name: Verse Before the Blade
techniques.desc: A poem at the market well about his mother and his camels; while he answers, watch how he stands.

techniques.name: Wall Sling
techniques.desc: From the hill towers of Mirah, a stone into the face of the man at the foot of the wall.

techniques.name: Through the Half-Open Gate
techniques.desc: The Sayf blade drawn and cutting in one stroke through the gap of the half-open gate.

techniques.name: Five Months
techniques.desc: Hold the gate as Mirah held it in 1060: patient and rested, answering every assault and never coming out to chase.

techniques.name: The Thirst of Mirah
techniques.desc: Let him besiege you in the heat: you have the cisterns and he has the sun, and every rush costs him water.

maneuver.name: The Walls of Mirah
maneuver.desc: The Sayf hold a walled town with slingers in the towers while the clans outside starve the besiegers of water.

ST19-07.name: The Red Thread
ST19-07.origin: Karam Bahad, Speaker from 962 to 979, raised the paid Salt Road Escort to guard the caravans between Zarak and Mirah and gave its captaincy to his brother's line. That tent-line has held it since, and its 4,000 riders know every well on the road. A Bahad rider braids a red thread into his camel's halter for every caravan guarded without loss, and the house teaches its sons the escort's way: a moving ring, raiders chased off, never followed out of sight.
ST19-07.philosophy: Guard the caravan, not your pride: drive the raider off and never chase him past sight of the camels.
ST19-07.strengths: Escort and screening, driving off raiders, the moving ring, staying power on long marches
ST19-07.weakness: Trained to drive men off rather than finish them, and paid from the chest: when the pay is late, so is the zeal
ranks: Captain of the Salt Road Escort

techniques.name: Turn Him Away
techniques.desc: Lance across his path, camel square to his horse: he goes round, and that is all the escort wants.

techniques.name: Warning Arrow
techniques.desc: The first arrow into the sand at his camel's feet; most raiders take the hint, and the second is for those who do not.

techniques.name: The Moving Ring
techniques.desc: Riders a kilometre out in a turning ring: wherever he strikes, someone is already riding at his flank.

techniques.name: Twentieth Day of the Road
techniques.desc: One more caravan through without loss: steady, patient and still in the saddle on the twentieth day of the road.

techniques.name: Not Past Sight
techniques.desc: One hard pass at the raider who will not take the hint, then back to the camels before his friends can draw you away.

maneuver.name: Caravan Screen
maneuver.desc: Escort riders guard a caravan in a moving ring a few kilometres out, chasing raiders off rather than fighting them.

ST20-01.name: The Horn Spear
ST20-01.origin: Mosi the Runner drilled his spearmen into the bull's horns, and at the Wamaya in November 905 his chest held while two horns of young runners closed on 18,000 Omamba spearmen. Every levy boy of the empire has learned the regiment's spear and long cowhide shield in the Horn Camps outside Zanara ever since. Since the Great Arming of 1104 the camps have doubled, and Zuberi Omamba, First Spear, drills 36,000 men and expects them to run as well as fight.
ST20-01.philosophy: Be one bead on a long string: hold when the drum says hold, run when it says run, and trust the man beside you to close the horn.
ST20-01.strengths: Drilled and steady; quick feet for a spearman; strong in a line and on open grass.
ST20-01.weakness: It fights to the drum: a lone man who keeps no beat finds it predictable, and it is poor on broken ground and against horse archers.

techniques.name: Cowhide Wall
techniques.desc: The long cowhide shield up, the spear resting on its rim; you hold, and you breathe.

techniques.name: The Horn Runs
techniques.desc: You run wide round his shield side as the horns run round a line, and he has to turn to find you.

techniques.name: Over the Rim
techniques.desc: Over the top of his shield and down into the collarbone, the stroke the chest has used since the Wamaya.

techniques.name: The Second Beat
techniques.desc: The drummers' trick: two beats where he expects one. He moves on the first, and your point is waiting on the second, low at his knee.

techniques.name: The Horns Close
techniques.desc: Everything the First Spear drills comes together at once: hold, run, turn and drive in from the side he stopped guarding.

maneuver.name: Bull's Horns
maneuver.desc: The chest closes with the enemy and holds him while two horns of young runners race round both flanks to meet behind him, steered by drums; the loins wait in reserve.

ST20-02.name: The Thousand-Arrow Arc
ST20-02.origin: Since Mosi's wars every governor has sent archers to the emperor by quota, and the Imperial Archers, 17,000 in 1105, shoot together on the drum at a high arc rather than man by man. The Archers' Ground of Anumba takes the herders' sons of the eastern plains and teaches them to loose on the beat with a thousand others. Few of their arrows kill through mail, and the drill knows it: it shoots to wound, to kill horses and to break nerve before the spears close.
ST20-02.philosophy: Shoot high, shoot many, shoot on the beat, and let the sky find the men.
ST20-02.strengths: First shots before contact; wearing a line down; cheap to learn and cheap to arm.
ST20-02.weakness: Its arrows rarely go through mail, and once the enemy is close an archer has a knife and a cotton coat.

techniques.name: Loose on the Drum
techniques.desc: One arrow on the beat, before he is close enough to matter.

techniques.name: Behind the Spears
techniques.desc: An archer lives by stepping back behind the shields and getting his breath while other men take the blow.

techniques.name: Arrow in the Fist
techniques.desc: When he is too close to shoot, the arrow is still a steel point: you drive it into the gap under his arm by hand.

techniques.name: Give Ground
techniques.desc: You back away the way the arc-callers teach, watching his feet, and he shows you what he means to do before he does it.

techniques.name: The Thousand
techniques.desc: Every arrow on your string as fast as the drum can beat: the shooting of a master who learned among thousands and now shoots like them alone.

maneuver.name: Arc Storm
maneuver.desc: Two thousand archers loose together on the drum at a high arc, fifteen thousand arrows a minute into the enemy before his line can close.

ST20-03.name: The Three Javelins of Owana
ST20-03.origin: The Javelin Men are the empire's skirmish screen, 10,000 light men with three javelins, a long knife and a small hide shield who run ahead of the horns and fall back through the gaps. Their field at Owana trains the boys of the governors' dry-season musters, the largest levy on the plains. They learn the throw that sticks in a shield and drags it down, and the run that keeps a thrower out of reach.
ST20-03.philosophy: Throw, run, throw again; close only when his shield is heavy with your iron.
ST20-03.strengths: Shield-breaking throws, hit and run, harrying slow armored foot.
ST20-03.weakness: Three javelins and then a knife: armor, archers who outrange it and horse in the open all beat it.

techniques.name: First Shaft
techniques.desc: The first javelin at twenty paces, thrown while he is still deciding whether you are worth chasing.

techniques.name: Iron in the Shield
techniques.desc: A javelin into his shield at five paces; while he wrestles the dragging weight, the knife comes in over it.

techniques.name: Run Out of Reach
techniques.desc: You turn and run as if beaten, and stop when he is blown and you are not.

techniques.name: The Long Knife Inside
techniques.desc: Inside his spear with the long knife, low and across, the cut the screen uses when the lines have met.

techniques.name: Three in the Air
techniques.desc: Three javelins thrown before the first one lands: one for the shield, one for the legs, one for the man.

maneuver.name: Javelin Screen
maneuver.desc: The screen throws two or three javelins a man at twenty paces just before the horns close, then runs back through the gaps in the spears.

ST20-04.name: The Runner's Pace
ST20-04.origin: Mosi the Runner's Law of the Runners of 933 made running a royal art and the House of Runners, kept by the Runner kin of House Kanemba, the one relay of the empire. Sefu the Runner, taken in at ten by the seventh master Kwasi Kanemba, is the eighth master in a line from Mosi's own runner-captains and the first since Mosi to run a horseman down in a day and kill him. In 1088 he ran a Sand Clan horse thief for three days until the horse foundered near Sawandi, and killed the man beside it.
ST20-04.philosophy: Start slow, drink at every water, and do not close until his horse stands with its head down.
ST20-04.strengths: Endurance, wearing the enemy out, the javelin at twenty metres, fighting after a day's run.
ST20-04.weakness: It gives away the first minute; cold months, woods and remounts beat it, and a runner wears no armor.

techniques.name: Keep the Pace
techniques.desc: You do not answer his hurry. Breathe through the nose, stay sideways, and let him spend himself.

techniques.name: Let Him Blow His Horse
techniques.desc: You give ground and make him chase, because a frightened man spends his wind by mid-morning.

techniques.name: Javelin at Twenty Paces
techniques.desc: The javelin goes into the horse if the man is still mounted, and into the legs if he is not.

techniques.name: The Short Spear When He Stands
techniques.desc: When he finally stands with his hands on his knees, you close and the stabbing spear goes in once.

techniques.name: A Day of Heat
techniques.desc: Sefu's whole art in one long breath: by now he is spent and you are not, and you can see every move he has left.

maneuver.name: The Day-Long Chase
maneuver.desc: The Runner Guard and the relay men hunt a beaten enemy over a day of heat, javelins at every water, until the horses founder and the men sit down.

ST20-05.name: The Tandi Close Spear
ST20-05.origin: This is the spear of the Tedana kings' men, who beat Mosi in the rains at Nuzeko in 916 and held Tandi for seven months in 921. It is taught at the Spear School of Tandi by the Spear School line of House Tedani. Baraka Tedani, nephew of King Kato, teaches the close spear and the horned attack; he taught Crown Prince Tano in 1100 and 1101, and since 1102 he has drilled the Tedana spears by night.
ST20-05.philosophy: Run in under the long points, shield to shield, and put the short spear where his shield is not.
ST20-05.strengths: Closing fast, hooking shields, bloody work at arm's length.
ST20-05.weakness: It must close to fight: a long spear backing away, a pike block or a horseman keeps it at the end of a pole.

techniques.name: Shield to Shield
techniques.desc: You run the last steps and hit his shield with yours, boss first, before his point is set.

techniques.name: Hook the Rim
techniques.desc: Your shield rim catches his and pulls it a hand's breadth aside, and that is all the room a short spear needs.

techniques.name: Under the Arm
techniques.desc: The short spear goes in under his raised arm, where the quilting is thin, and comes out red.

techniques.name: The Night Drill
techniques.desc: Taught in the dark at Tandi, where you fight by the sound of a man's feet and strike back at the noise of his blow.

techniques.name: Nuzeko in the Rain
techniques.desc: Sefu the Stubborn's day: catch him strung out and off balance, and go through him before he can set his feet.

maneuver.name: Running Spear Wall
maneuver.desc: The Tedana spears run the last hundred paces shield to shield and hit the enemy line before it has set its points.

ST20-06.name: The Kisara Gate
ST20-06.origin: Mosi the Runner, the best runner at the Tedana court, took the crown in May 903 with 3,000 spearmen behind him, and in April 910 he ran 600 men 100 km in a night to seize the gate of Kisara before the Tandi army came. The imperial line teaches its sons that gate: arrive before the news, strike before the gate shuts, and keep enough breath for the long fight on the Runner's Blood. Every emperor must run the Runner's Round at his crowning; Mosi II, who lacked the blood, stopped twice.
ST20-06.philosophy: Be there before he knows you are coming, and still be fresh when he is not.
ST20-06.strengths: Surprise, a fast first rush, wind for a long fight.
ST20-06.weakness: The thick blood: a Kanemba who strains all-out risks the stroke that killed five emperors, and a style built to arrive first has little for a man who waits behind a shield.

techniques.name: The Word Arrives
techniques.desc: The house words, taught with a spear: the blow lands before the news that you were coming.

techniques.name: Before the Gate Shuts
techniques.desc: You run straight through the gap while he is still turning to close it.

techniques.name: The Runner's Blood
techniques.desc: Your wind comes back when other men's does not. The Kanemba know what the blood gives and what it costs.

techniques.name: Kisara at Dawn
techniques.desc: After a night's run, the gate guard is still rubbing his eyes when the spear takes him.

techniques.name: The Runner Takes the Crown
techniques.desc: Mosi's way in May 903: all of it at once, before anyone can choose otherwise. The blood pounds in the temples, as it did for five emperors.

maneuver.name: Seizing the Gate
maneuver.desc: Runners cover a night's march no enemy believes possible and take the gate at dawn before it can be shut.

ST20-07.name: The Chest That Holds
ST20-07.origin: When Dembe Kanemba ran into Anumba in March 851, Captain Oduya Jiamari beat the drum and led the spearmen out, and under Mosi the Runner the Jiamari drilled the chest, the center of the bull that holds while the horns run. At the Wamaya in 905 their line did not move for two hours. Hereditary colonels of the Anumba Horn since 931, they lost half the regiment at the Matazi Ford in 1016 and a quarter before Mirah in 1060.
ST20-07.philosophy: Do not go to him; be the thing he cannot get past until the horns arrive.
ST20-07.weakness: It never wins quickly: the chest waits for horns a lone duelist does not have, and a patient enemy or an archer who will not come picks it apart.

techniques.name: The Chest Holds
techniques.desc: The house words, said with the shield: feet planted, rim to your chin, nothing past you.

techniques.name: Point Over the Rim
techniques.desc: His blow lands on cowhide, and your point is already coming back over the top of it.

techniques.name: Two Hours at the Wamaya
techniques.desc: The longest stand in the family's songs: you settle behind the shield as if you mean to stay all day.

techniques.name: Shove and Hold
techniques.desc: Shield into shield, your weight low, and you push until his feet slide and his arms burn.

techniques.name: The Chest Does Not Move
techniques.desc: He throws everything at a wall that will not step back, and the wall answers once, rim and point together.

maneuver.name: The Chest
maneuver.desc: The Anumba Horn locks shields at the center of the bull and does not take a step, forward or back, until the horns close.

ST20-08.name: The Gold Tail
ST20-08.origin: When the slaves of the Kabale shafts rose in 1049, Nduma Ngomani carried the Gold Tail standard at the front of the Golden Horse to relieve Lady Nala Kabale, and Mosi II made the standard hereditary in his family. In 1062 his son led the charge that caught 400 clan riders at a watering place on the Hazir River. The house breeds remounts at Seduna Walls and raises the Golden Horse's officers, though since 1100 the captaincy has gone to Kamau Sawandi.
ST20-08.philosophy: Ride where the tail flies, at the front, and catch them while they water.
ST20-08.strengths: The charge, catching riders unready, the lance and sword from the saddle.
ST20-08.weakness: Northern horses die of fly sickness and the charge needs open ground; on foot a Ngomani is a man in a quilted coat with a sword, and pride puts him first into everything.

techniques.name: Follow the Tail
techniques.desc: Knee to knee behind the standard at the trot, lance point steady at his chest.

techniques.name: At the Watering Place
techniques.desc: The Hazir River lesson: hit them while their horses drink and their hands are on the reins.

techniques.name: Wheel and Return
techniques.desc: You ride past him, wheel the horse in its own length, and come back on the side he did not watch.

techniques.name: The Tail Flies
techniques.desc: The standard goes in first and the family goes in after it, shouting, with no thought of the way back.

maneuver.name: Gold Tail Charge
maneuver.desc: The Golden Horse rides at the trot behind the Gold Tail and goes to the gallop at a hundred paces, into the flank of whatever has stopped to water or to fight.

ST20-09.name: The Left Line
ST20-09.origin: In 1008 Juma Mahundi, a woodsman who had raised an orphaned calf, brought 30 elephants alive out of the Mosawa woods for Kofi the Lion and became the first head-driver of the Elephant Corps. At the Matazi Ford in 1016 the beasts would not cross under Abari javelins and his son died trying to drive his into the water; at Mirah in 1060 the drivers gave the elephants their own water. The family drives the Left Line under Tafari the Horn and trains every new driver.
ST20-09.philosophy: Be calm enough that five tonnes trusts one hand, and shoot down at men who are not.
ST20-09.strengths: Calm under noise and fear, shooting from height, the hook of the goad.
ST20-09.weakness: A driver is a handler, not a swordsman: on foot he is ordinary, and when the beast panics the whole art fails, as it did at the Matazi Ford.

techniques.name: One Calm Hand
techniques.desc: Shouting does not reach you. You learned as a child that the beast feels your heart through your hand.

techniques.name: Shot From the Howdah
techniques.desc: Down over his shield from above, the shot the howdah archers use to pick out officers.

techniques.name: The Goad's Hook
techniques.desc: The iron hook that turns an elephant's ear catches a man behind the ankle just as well.

techniques.name: The Beast Trusts One Hand
techniques.desc: You read his fear as you read a bull elephant's ears, and you answer it before it turns into a blow.

maneuver.name: Elephant Screen
maneuver.desc: The Left Line's elephants stand at intervals before the foot; horses will not close with them, and the howdah archers shoot over the spears.

ST21-01.name: The Red Vine Shield
ST21-01.origin: The Pepper Guard keeps the Prince's house and the Pepper Hall, where one part in ten of every spice cargo is taken at the scales: 1,000 heavy foot with tall painted shields, spears and crossbows. Asha Redvine, its captain, paints a red vine on her shield and drills the Guard on Pepper Hall Hill, where the Hall's roof is climbed at Harvest Home and its doors must never be forced. In 1105 the Guard stands between the Prince and the Mistress of the Pepper Hall, who is withholding his fees.
ST21-01.philosophy: Hold the door, shoot the man on the stair, and never chase past the scales.
ST21-01.strengths: Doorways, stairs and narrow lanes; spear and crossbow together; steady nerves.
ST21-01.weakness: It is a guard, not a field soldier: slow in the open, and trained to stand where it is told, so a climber who comes over the roof gets behind it.

school.name: The Guardhouse of the Pepper Hall

techniques.name: Bolt on the Stair
techniques.desc: One bolt down the stair at the first man up it, spanned and waiting since the bell rang.

techniques.name: Door Shut
techniques.desc: The tall shield fills the doorway and your shoulder is behind it. Nobody gets in to the scales.

techniques.name: Spear Through the Gap
techniques.desc: His blow hits the painted vine, and your spear comes out past the shield's edge into whatever he left open.

techniques.name: Weigh Him First
techniques.desc: The Guard learns from the weighers: watch the hand, not the face, and the hand tells you what he will do with the blade.

techniques.name: Bolt at Three Paces
techniques.desc: You wait until he is almost on you, and at three paces the bolt goes through shield and quilting both.

maneuver.name: Stair and Door
maneuver.desc: Spears hold the stairs and doors while crossbows shoot from the windows above; a mob or a landing party must come one man at a time.

ST21-02.name: The Green Ambush
ST21-02.origin: The hill levies of the pepper gardens serve only in defense, and they fight from the forest: pit traps, poisoned bamboo stakes, an arrow out of the green and then nothing. The Kioya Vine Watch, 2,400 scouts and archers under Wema Kioyani, keeps the Kioya Hill Fort over the gardens and the landing at Kioya Water, where the Amber fleet burned 22 Kioyani ships in 1068. The League's own doctrine is to fight ashore from the forest and let the fevers do the rest.
ST21-02.philosophy: Let the forest and the fever fight for you: shoot once, move, and be gone before he finds the tree.
ST21-02.strengths: Ambush, first shots, stakes and traps, wearing an invader down.
ST21-02.weakness: Out of the trees it has nothing to stand on: on a beach at noon or in the open it is a light archer in a wet shirt, and an enemy who will not follow into the forest gives it no target.

school.name: The Vine Watch Fort of Kioya

techniques.name: Arrow From the Green
techniques.desc: A shot from the leaves before he knows which tree you are in.

techniques.name: Bamboo Stake
techniques.desc: You give ground over the brushwood, and the stake you set there last night goes into his foot.

techniques.name: Gone Before He Turns
techniques.desc: One step behind a trunk and you are somewhere else, watching him look for you.

techniques.name: The Fever Does the Rest
techniques.desc: You keep him moving in the wet heat in his mail, and the coast does to him what it does to every invader.

techniques.name: Bush Knife From Behind
techniques.desc: When he finally stops to listen, the garden knife comes out of the green behind him.

maneuver.name: Forest Ambush
maneuver.desc: The Watch lets a column string out on a garden track two abreast, then strikes both sides at close range where it cannot form.

ST21-03.name: The Black Water Knife
ST21-03.origin: The 400 Night Swimmers of Kesh swim through guarded harbors at night to cut cables and booms and to fire ships, and the League's whole navy is built to fight by night. Their captain Neema Nightwater, taught the water by her pearl-diver mother and the knife by Tumaini the Rope, cut a Tekook galley's anchor cable in the Madamo roads in 1093 and let the tide put it on the bar. Her boathouse under the Harbor Towers takes the diving boys and girls of Stilt Town and teaches them three minutes under and a blackened knife.
ST21-03.philosophy: Come out of the black water where he is not looking, cut, and go back over the side.
ST21-03.strengths: Stealth, the first cut, wet and dark places, slipping away.
ST21-03.weakness: On a quay at noon a swimmer is a small person with a knife and no armor, and would rather go over the side than stand.

techniques.name: Up From Under
techniques.desc: You come up under his reach the way you come up under a hull, knife first.

techniques.name: Blackened Blade
techniques.desc: A soot-black knife does not flash. He watches your shoulder and never sees the blade.

techniques.name: Three Minutes Under
techniques.desc: The diver's breath: slow the heart, wait, and come back up calm while he is still gasping.

techniques.name: Cut the Cable
techniques.desc: The saw-backed blade made for anchor cables finds the cords behind his knee.

techniques.name: Over the Side
techniques.desc: You take him over the rail or off the quay into the water, where you are at home and he is drowning in his own coat.

maneuver.name: Cable Cutting
maneuver.desc: Night swimmers cut an anchored fleet's cables so its ships drift onto the rocks or foul each other before the fire ships come in.

ST21-04.name: The Rope and the Roof
ST21-04.origin: Pili Keshari won the Harvest Home climb on the Pepper Hall roof in 985 by wedging his hands where no one else could, slipped the harbor stocks that winter, and founded the Rope Hall of Kesh in 1004 to teach climbing, rope-walking and slipping bonds. Its masters have been Keshari or Keshari-trained ever since. Tumaini the Rope held the rope below the Amber harbor-house window for Nuru the Boneless in 1068, at twelve, and now teaches 400 boarding climbers who cross Kesh by roof and rope.
ST21-04.philosophy: Never fight on the flat: go up in the first second, fight from above, and make him fall rather than cut him.
ST21-04.strengths: Height, falls, the weighted rope end, pulling men off their feet, escape.
ST21-04.weakness: The flat: an open deck, a shield wall, a spear on a ladder or a bowman who looks up; and every climber's grip and knees fail in the end.

techniques.name: Up in the First Second
techniques.desc: Before he has drawn, you are on the cart, the wall, the rail: anywhere above him.

techniques.name: The Weighted End
techniques.desc: The rope's weighted end swings from your off hand and cracks against his temple.

techniques.name: By the Ankle
techniques.desc: From the ridge you reach down, take his ankle, and let the roof do the rest.

techniques.name: Fall on Purpose
techniques.desc: When it goes wrong you jump. You know where you will land and he does not, and you come up beside him.

techniques.name: Down the Rigging
techniques.desc: Up his own rigging and down onto his deck behind the line, knife first, the way Tumaini boarded off Tekook in 1070.

maneuver.name: Boarding From Above
maneuver.desc: Climbers go up the enemy's rigging and come down on his deck behind the line his marines are holding.

ST21-05.name: The Night Galley
ST21-05.origin: Chande Monuri the Galley-Maker built the League's first twelve war galleys in his own yards and founded the Sea School of Monuro in 925 to train crews in ramming, boarding and night sailing. Its lesson has never changed: never meet a bigger fleet by daylight. Admiral Jabari Tide, whose father fought at Tekook in 1070, holds the School in 1105 and commands the League's 45 fighting ships.
ST21-05.philosophy: Come on the night tide with muffled oars, strike, burn and be gone before the sun shows him how few you are.
ST21-05.strengths: Night fighting, the ram's shock, footing on a moving deck, fire.
ST21-05.weakness: By daylight in open water against a bigger, steadier fleet it has no answer but to run, and ashore its men are sailors with knives.

techniques.name: Sea Legs
techniques.desc: Knees loose, weight low: the deck pitches and you do not.

techniques.name: Muffled Oars
techniques.desc: Rags on the oars and no lights: you are beside him before he knows there is a boat.

techniques.name: Fire Pot
techniques.desc: A clay pot of burning pitch thrown across the gap before the boarding, and he is fighting the fire before he fights you.

techniques.name: Ram Shock
techniques.desc: The beak goes into his oar bank and every man on his deck is thrown down; you are the one who braced for it.

techniques.name: The Night Tide
techniques.desc: You ride the ebb into his anchorage in the dark, and everything he does is a move against a ship that is not where he thinks.

maneuver.name: Night Tide Ramming
maneuver.desc: Galleys ride the night ebb into the enemy anchorage with rag-muffled oars, sprint the last 200 m and drive their beaks into hulls that never saw them come.

ST21-06.name: No Knot Holds
ST21-06.origin: Sauti Keshari folded her thumb flat against her wrist at fairs for coppers; her son Pili slipped his wrists out of the harbor stocks in 985; her great-grandson Nuru the Boneless put his own shoulder out of joint to get through a window 20 cm wide into the Amber harbor-house in 1068, and escaped capture at Amberport through a drain in 1069. The princely house teaches its children what their loose joints allow: no hold keeps them, and the knife is out while the other man still thinks he has them. Faraji Keshari, Keeper of Keys, is its best living hand.
ST21-06.philosophy: Let him take hold of you; then there is nothing there to hold, and your knife is already out.
ST21-06.strengths: Slipping holds and pins, close knife work, very hard to keep down.
ST21-06.weakness: Joints that dislocate when they should not, so a Keshari can win a hold and lose a shoulder, and knees that go early; against a man who does not grab but cuts from reach it has little.

techniques.name: Slip the Hold
techniques.desc: He grabs your wrist; it folds out of his hand, and the heel of it comes straight back into his face.

techniques.name: The Shoulder Goes Out
techniques.desc: You put your own shoulder out of joint to slip the lock and come round behind him. It will hurt tomorrow.

techniques.name: The Knife Already Out
techniques.desc: He thinks he has your arms. One of them was never where he thought, and it has a knife in it.

techniques.name: Through the Window
techniques.desc: Nuru's twenty centimeters: you fold through a gap no grown man should fit, and answer from the other side.

techniques.name: Boneless
techniques.desc: You wrap him the way he tried to wrap you, joints bending where his do not, until the weapon drops from his hand.

ST21-07.name: First on the Enemy Deck
ST21-07.origin: When Chande Monuri founded the Sea School of Monuro in 925, a dock-fighter named Chane Jahazi was its first master of boarders, and his heirs have led the Monuro Marines onto every enemy deck since. At Tekook in 1070 three Jahazi brothers led the boarding of an Amber galley, and one came home. Captain Mwanahawa Jahazi leads the 3,000 Monuro Marines in 1105 and serves House Monuri first and the League second.
ST21-07.philosophy: A volley across the gap, then over the bow before the smoke clears: first on the deck, or nobody follows.
ST21-07.strengths: Boarding, the crossbow-then-sword rush, fighting on a crowded, moving deck.
ST21-07.weakness: Everything goes into the first rush: held at the rail, or met by a steady shield line on a high-sided cog, a Jahazi has already spent his best.

techniques.name: Volley Across the Gap
techniques.desc: The bolt goes across the narrowing water while the grapnels are still in the air.

techniques.name: Over the Bow
techniques.desc: You go over first, shouting the family's name, because a Jahazi who waits is not a Jahazi.

techniques.name: Deck Cut
techniques.desc: A short, flat cut across the thigh, made for a deck where there is no room to swing.

techniques.name: Tekook
techniques.desc: The deck of the Amber galley where three brothers went over and one came back: shield into his chest, and through.

maneuver.name: Boarding Action
maneuver.desc: Grapnels thrown, a crossbow volley across the gap, then the Monuro Marines over the bow behind a Jahazi.

ST22-01.name: The Terrace Spear
ST22-01.origin: The highland kingdom has always fought on chosen ground: a spear of Nusalo ash, a tall hide shield, and a terrace wall at your back, so that the enemy must climb. The Northern and Southern Spears of both hosts, 22,600 men in 1105, learn it in every valley. Eleni Sabara, captain of the Blue Twin Guard, learned it from Kebede the Pike and teaches it on the terraces of Nusalo; at the Mazezi bread riot of 1103 she held the Guard steady and killed no one.
ST22-01.philosophy: Make him climb: shield high, point at his face, one step forward with every thrust, and the hill does the rest.
ST22-01.strengths: Uphill and terrace fighting, rank work, steady pressure.
ST22-01.weakness: It fights the same way alone as in a rank, one step and one thrust, so a lone horseman or a knife in the dark finds it slow and easy to read.

techniques.name: Make Him Climb
techniques.desc: You keep the higher step and let him come up to you, which costs him twice what it costs you.

techniques.name: A Step With Every Thrust
techniques.desc: Thrust, step, thrust, step, the rhythm of a whole rank coming down a terrace.

techniques.name: Point at the Face
techniques.desc: The point stays at his eyes, and when he steps in to beat it aside he steps onto it.

techniques.name: Hilltop Ring
techniques.desc: Surrounded, the shields close into a ring on the crest; alone, you turn your back to the slope and wait for him to come up.

techniques.name: Down the Terrace
techniques.desc: When he is spent from climbing, you come down onto him from the wall with all your weight behind the point.

maneuver.name: Hilltop Stand
maneuver.desc: The spears take the crest and make the enemy climb in mail, spent twice as fast; if surrounded, the shields form a ring around the top.

ST22-02.name: The Matazi Javelin
ST22-02.origin: At the Matazi Ford in March 1016 the twin kings' javelin men stood in the shallows and threw until Kofi the Lion's elephants would not cross, and a Zanari driver's son died trying to force his beast into the water. The Highland Javelins and Archers of both hosts, 13,000 in 1105, learn the throw in the yards of Yandi: four shafts, a short spear and a round shield. It is the weapon Abara turns on horses and beasts.
ST22-02.philosophy: Throw at what is coming and aim for the soft places, the eye, the horse's chest, the shield arm, then step back behind the spears.
ST22-02.strengths: Stopping charges, horses and beasts; pinning shields; quick feet.
ST22-02.weakness: Four javelins and then a short spear: an armored man who walks through the throws, or archers who outrange them, leave it little.

techniques.name: Shaft at the Horse
techniques.desc: The first javelin goes at whatever carries him, horse or legs, because a slow man is half beaten.

techniques.name: Pin the Shield
techniques.desc: You throw to hit the shield, not the man; the shaft hangs in it, and his guard sags with the weight.

techniques.name: Step Behind the Spears
techniques.desc: You fall back a pace and watch him come, as the throwers fall back behind the rank at the ford.

techniques.name: Into the Eye
techniques.desc: The Matazi lesson: a shaft at the eye stops five tonnes of elephant, and it stops a man too.

techniques.name: The Ford Does Not Cross
techniques.desc: He comes at you through the water; the last javelin, held short as a spear, meets him in the chest and he goes back the way he came.

maneuver.name: The Matazi Throw
maneuver.desc: Javelin men stand in the shallows behind the spears and throw into the beasts and horses as they wade; at the Matazi the elephants would not cross.

ST22-03.name: The Terrace Bow
ST22-03.origin: Behind the dry-stone terraces of the Highveld, a bowman can shoot at a column that must climb from wall to wall, and the walls stop horsemen from wheeling. The Highveld Archers of the Blue Host learn it at Selomba, shooting downhill from cover at Monundi raiders and anyone else who comes up the valley. It is the kingdom's defense of its own fields, and it has never been taught to stand in the open.
ST22-03.philosophy: Never stand in the open: shoot from behind the wall, downhill, and let the hill tire him before your arrow does.
ST22-03.strengths: Cover, shooting downhill, patience, picking off climbers.
ST22-03.weakness: Without its wall it is a light bowman in a cotton coat; a foe who goes round, or comes over the wall with fire, catches it standing still.

techniques.name: Shoot From the Wall
techniques.desc: Your shoulder against the stones, one arrow down the slope while he is still in the open.

techniques.name: Duck the Wall
techniques.desc: Down behind the stones as his blow or his arrow comes, and up again somewhere else along the terrace.

techniques.name: Pick the Climber
techniques.desc: You let him think you have stopped shooting, then put a shaft into his leg as he climbs the next wall.

techniques.name: Let the Hill Tire Him
techniques.desc: You fall back one terrace at a time and make him climb every one of them, watching how his legs go.

techniques.name: The Arrow for the Captain
techniques.desc: Downhill, from cover, at the one man who matters, with the heavy-headed arrow you kept for him.

maneuver.name: Terrace Wall Defense
maneuver.desc: Archers shoot from behind dry-stone terrace walls every 20 to 40 m while the spears wait; horsemen cannot wheel and every wall must be climbed under arrows.

ST22-04.name: The Tsega Pike Hedge
ST22-04.origin: House Tsega founded the Spear Yard of Zutati in 790 to drill the northern levies in the pike hedge, the defense of the terraces that has turned back every raider from the south; a Feresi grandfather first made the hedge stand. At Zutati in February 1051 Abebe Tsega's pikes broke Kiros's center and turned the Mandari charge. Kebede the Pike, whom Abebe took into the Yard at fourteen, drills the 12,000 Tsega Pikes in 1105, and he is the man who let Prince Tekle ride past in the dark in 1090.
ST22-04.philosophy: Five meters of ash held level and a line that does not move: the horse turns, and that is the whole of war.
ST22-04.strengths: Reach, stopping horses and charges, holding a line, iron discipline.
ST22-04.weakness: Alone a pike is a pole: slow to turn, helpless inside its own point, and lost on broken ground, under missiles or against a flank.

techniques.name: Point Level
techniques.desc: The first thing Kebede teaches: the point at a man's chest, level, and held there whatever comes at it.

techniques.name: The Horse Turns
techniques.desc: He comes straight at the points; you do not flinch, and he takes the iron before he can reach you.

techniques.name: Five Points Out
techniques.desc: A short, hard thrust from behind the point he was watching, as if the second rank had reached past you.

techniques.name: Stand Still
techniques.desc: The drill that makes farmers stand still in front of a charge. You stop thinking about running and only hold.

techniques.name: The Hedge at Zutati
techniques.desc: February 1051: the hedge steps forward together, every point at once, and Kiros's center breaks on it.

maneuver.name: Pike Hedge
maneuver.desc: A block of five-metre pikes eight ranks deep with five points out in front: no horse breaks it from the front and elephants stop on it, but it moves slowly and turns badly.

ST22-05.name: The Monundi Seat
ST22-05.origin: The Monundi valleys bred best the horses Asrat the Horse-Buyer brought to the Highveld, and the Mandari have taught riding, the javelin and horse-breaking at Mandi since they swore to Kasa II in 712. The Horse School still teaches the lesson of Zutati in 1051, where Tesfaye Mandari's charge broke on the Tsega pikes: never ride into set points. Yohannes Mandari has held it since 1096 and keeps 300 picked riders ready at the Monundi fords.
ST22-05.philosophy: Down a terrace, across a ford, a javelin from the gallop, and wheel away before you reach his points.
ST22-05.strengths: Highland riding over bad ground, javelins from the saddle, raiding, wheeling away.
ST22-05.weakness: Against set pikes or spears the horse gives it nothing, because the School teaches its riders to turn away rather than break through; on foot a Mandi rider is a raider with a short spear.

techniques.name: Over the Terrace Lip
techniques.desc: You take the horse down a drop he would not ride, and come at him from where he did not think a horse could be.

techniques.name: Javelin From the Gallop
techniques.desc: Loose rein, knees tight, and the javelin goes as the horse's forefeet come down.

techniques.name: Wheel Away
techniques.desc: The lesson of 1051: you turn short of his points, circle, and look again at what he has set against you.

techniques.name: Ride Him Down at the Ford
techniques.desc: Catch him waist-deep where he cannot turn, and ride over him with the short spear low.

techniques.name: Kiros's Raid
techniques.desc: At Zutati Kiros's horse looted Kaleb's camp while his center broke: you go where he is not, and hurt what he cannot spare.

maneuver.name: Monundi Raid
maneuver.desc: Riders of the Monundi go deep by the fords for days, driving off herds and burning stores and avoiding battle, or a wing rides round to loot the enemy camp.

ST22-06.name: Two Voices, One Song
ST22-06.origin: The twin kings Asfar and Asmar beat Emperor Kofi of Zanara at the Matazi Ford in 1016, one holding the spears in the water and the other leading the horse on the bank. House Asfari teaches its children to fight the way twins rule, one voice answering the other: shield, then spear, then shield. Dawit the Door, captain of Kiros's Blue Guard, taught it to Prince Tekle, who now holds any gap of three meters against nearly anyone alive.
ST22-06.philosophy: Never the same twice: when he expects the shield the spear answers, and when he expects the spear, the shield.
ST22-06.strengths: Alternating guard and attack, holding gaps and doors, reading a rhythm.
ST22-06.weakness: It is built for two: alone in the open, with no gap and no twin, it is a good spear and nothing more, and three men at once break the song.
ranks: Guard of the Green and Blue

techniques.name: The Answering Voice
techniques.desc: The shield takes his blow and the spear answers it, as one twin answers the other.

techniques.name: Turn the Banner
techniques.desc: As the banner turns at dawn on New Year's Day: you show him one half, then the other.

techniques.name: Hold the Ford
techniques.desc: King Asfar's half of the Matazi: you stand in the water and every man who comes out of it meets your point.

techniques.name: The Door
techniques.desc: Dawit the Door's lesson: choose a gap no wider than three meters, plant the shield, point at face height, and do not go forward.

techniques.name: Two Voices, One Song
techniques.desc: Shield and spear strike in one breath, the way the twin kings fought the Matazi as one man with two minds.

maneuver.name: The Twin Kings' Ford
maneuver.desc: Spears meet the first men out of the water while the horse waits on the bank to fall on the baggage, as the twin kings did at the Matazi in 1016.

ST22-07.name: The Hall Spear of Tsega
ST22-07.origin: In 786 Tsega the Spear led 600 spearmen of Zutati into the royal hall at Abara, killed Hawaz the Red, who had murdered King Seyum II, and set the dead king's son on the throne. The lords of Zutati teach their own sons the short spear of that day, the weapon for halls, doors and stairs and for the one blow that ends a usurper, and leave the pike hedge to the Yard and the farmers. Gebre Tsega, Marshal of the Northern Host, learned it from his father Abebe.
ST22-07.philosophy: The hill does not move, but in a hall the spear does: one step, one thrust, through the man who should not be standing there.
ST22-07.strengths: Close quarters, decisive thrusts, killing the leader, cold nerve.
ST22-07.weakness: Everything rides on the one thrust: a man who keeps his distance in the open, or a rider, gives it nothing to close on, and the house leaves its holding to its pikes.

techniques.name: Into the Hall
techniques.desc: Through the doorway shield first, before the men inside have stood up from the benches.

techniques.name: The Throat Above the Rim
techniques.desc: Short and straight, over his shield into the throat: there is no room in a hall for anything longer.

techniques.name: The Hill Does Not Move
techniques.desc: The house words: you plant yourself in the doorway, and he comes onto the spear or not at all.

techniques.name: Kill the Usurper
techniques.desc: Tsega the Spear's blow of 786: past the guards, through the mail, into the one man the whole fight is about.

ST22-08.name: Ride for the True King
ST22-08.origin: Mandar the Horse-Lord swore to Kasa II the Rider at Mandi in 712 on condition of keeping his horse fairs and his own judges, and his house has been the kingdom's heavy horse ever since. Tesfaye Mandari led the southern horse for Kiros in the Twin War; at Zutati in 1051 his charge broke on the Tsega pikes, and in 1052 his riders starved before the walls of Abara. In 1105 Lord Mesfin Mandari is raising 6,000 Horsemen of the Monundi for Prince Tekle.
ST22-08.philosophy: Choose your king, then ride straight at whoever stands in front of him.
ST22-08.strengths: The lance charge, the second pass, loyalty that does not break.
ST22-08.weakness: The house charges where the Horse School would wheel away, and set pikes break it as they broke Tesfaye at Zutati; on foot it is a horseman far from his horse.

techniques.name: Couch the Lance
techniques.desc: The lance under the arm and the horse doing the work, as every Mandari son learns before he can read.

techniques.name: For the True King
techniques.desc: The family cry of the Twin War, and the charge that goes with it, with no thought of the way back.

techniques.name: The Second Pass
techniques.desc: You ride past, let him think it is over, and come back with the sword while he is still turning.

techniques.name: Through the Front Rank
techniques.desc: Full gallop into the first man; the lance takes him and the horse takes the one behind.

maneuver.name: Charge of Kiros's Men
maneuver.desc: The Horsemen of the Monundi wait on a wing until the enemy line is fully engaged, then ride into its side; against set pikes it breaks, as at Zutati in 1051.

ST22-09.name: Lie Low, Rise Last
ST22-09.origin: The Lamari are the oldest lords of the north, given the Jimba valley in 493 for restoring Ayele I's son after the royal cousin Gashaw murdered his father. Their javelin men learned to lie flat in the tall grass and rise at a horn call, and the Northern Host still drills the hidden spear line the Lamari way. In 1090 Lord Tadesse Lamari's eldest son rode out with Prince Tekle, and the Tsega have watched the house ever since.
ST22-09.philosophy: Lie flat until he has passed you, and rise thirty paces in front of him with your point already set.
ST22-09.strengths: Ambush, surprise, the first moment, patience.
ST22-09.weakness: Once seen it is a light spearman in a cotton cloak; scouts on the crest, or a pursuer who wheels away instead of riding on, waste the whole art.

techniques.name: Flat in the Grass
techniques.desc: You make yourself small and still and let him decide you are not there.

techniques.name: Rise at the Horn
techniques.desc: Up out of the grass on the call, the point already moving, before he can rein in.

techniques.name: Points Set
techniques.desc: Thirty paces in front of the pursuit, the butt in the earth and the point at the horse's chest.

techniques.name: Rise Last
techniques.desc: The house words: everyone else has moved and shown their hand, and only then do you come up, behind him.

maneuver.name: Hidden Spear Line
maneuver.desc: Javelin men lie flat in tall grass while the horse draws the enemy on; at a horn call they rise 30 to 50 m in front of the pursuers and set their spears.

ST23-01.name: The Ice Edge
ST23-01.origin: On the White Coast boats and sledges must land at the edge of the sea ice or the shore ice, and the giants of Hrimfell have always waited for them there. The halls teach every young giant to stand at the edge with stones at their feet and a club in hand and to break whatever comes in before it can unload. Its masters say it is not war but weather: the giants fight in the cold, rarely, and only where the ice makes the enemy come to them.
ST23-01.philosophy: Let the ice bring him to you, break the boat before the men are out of it, and never step onto the thin ice yourself.
ST23-01.strengths: Ambush at a landing; stones at boats and sledges; clubbing men who must come ashore.
ST23-01.weakness: A defender's art for one kind of ground: land somewhere else, or come on a warm day, and it has nothing to wait for.

techniques.name: Stone at the Boat
techniques.desc: Before the bow touches the ice, a stone goes through its planks.

techniques.name: Wait for the Landing
techniques.desc: Stand still at the edge; he has to come to you, and you see every step he takes on the way.

techniques.name: Club at the Waterline
techniques.desc: The man stepping out of the boat has one foot on the ice and none on the ground.

techniques.name: Break the Floe
techniques.desc: Strike the ice, not the man; when the floe tips, he is in the sea.

techniques.name: The Sledge-Breaker
techniques.desc: A stone the size of a seal, thrown at a sledge and the men behind it.

maneuver.name: Ice Edge Ambush
maneuver.desc: Giants and their harpooners wait where boats and sledges must land and break them with stones and clubs as they come in.

ST23-02.name: The Floe-Walk
ST23-02.origin: The hall of Ulfdal hunted the far ice where the sea froze thickest, and its giants were called ice-walkers. When the Warm Winters of 762 to 768 failed the ice, the Thing raised Thorgrim Icewalker as war-king and he kept the halls alive for seven winters on long hunts, until a floe broke under him and his partner in 769. The last of Ulfdal came into Jotunhall by 790 and brought the hunt with them, and every young giant of Hrimfell still learns from it to walk the sea ice with a harpoon-spear and to know which floe will hold.
ST23-02.philosophy: Test the ice before you trust it, and fight where every step he takes is a guess.
ST23-02.strengths: Footing on ice; reading treacherous ground; the heavy harpoon-spear against seal, walrus and men.
ST23-02.weakness: Patient to a fault and heavy on thin ice: when the floe breaks under a giant, as it did under Thorgrim, nothing saves him.

techniques.name: Test the Ice
techniques.desc: The butt of the spear on the ice before every step; listen to what it says, and to what he does.

techniques.name: Harpoon Thrust
techniques.desc: A seal-hunter's thrust with a giant's arm behind it.

techniques.name: Where the Floe Tips
techniques.desc: Draw him onto the ice you know is bad; your weight tips it, his feet go.

techniques.name: Hold the Walrus
techniques.desc: Haft braced and your weight on it, until the beast or the man tires on the end of it.

techniques.name: Thorgrim's Winter
techniques.desc: Seven winters on the far ice: what the cold does to him, it does not do to you.

ST23-03.name: The Valdgard Pair
ST23-03.origin: Valdgard, the youngest of the great halls, was founded in 834 by Sigvald the Woodwright and has always kept close to Jotunhall, and its Pair Hall is where every young giant of Hrimfell learns to fight: back to back, with human harpooners at the knees, with the maul and the thrown stone. Ragna of Valdgard, who fought through the Hrimfell Raids and lost an ear at Yarov, has mastered it since 1099; Ulfar of Jotunhall trained beside her from 1093.
ST23-03.philosophy: Trust your partner's back completely, throw before they close, and keep the harpooners at your knees.
ST23-03.strengths: Pairs that fight with human flank-guards; stones from a sling; the maul in the cold.
ST23-03.weakness: The pair is the weakness: break from your partner to chase one man and your partner dies alone, as Hallgerd did at the Torholm shore in 1096.

techniques.name: Sling-Stone
techniques.desc: A walrus-leather sling and a stone a man could not lift, loosed before he closes.

techniques.name: Trust the Back
techniques.desc: Do not look round. Your partner is there; look at the man in front of you.

techniques.name: Harpooners at the Knee
techniques.desc: The man who goes low meets the harpoons; the man who stands meets you.

techniques.name: Maul in the Cold
techniques.desc: In the deep cold a giant is at full strength, and the maul comes down with all of it.

maneuver.name: Pairs and Harpooners
maneuver.desc: Giant pairs fight back to back with human harpooners guarding their knees; whoever goes low meets the harpoons, whoever stands meets the maul.

ST23-04.name: The Mountain's Weight
ST23-04.origin: Grom the Mountain, born in 950, grew to 460 cm, larger than any giant in any chant; in the Famine Winter he dragged a frozen whale 20 km across the ice to feed three halls, and the Thing of 993 made him king. His size runs in the Jotunhall line through its Mothers, and so does its price: Grom ruled from a seat of whale vertebrae, Hrolf the Heavy died of a fall on the ice, Hraldr commands from a sledge and Ulfar walks on crutches. The line teaches its giants to use what no other giant has, sheer weight, and to fear the ground.
ST23-04.philosophy: Lean on him with eighteen hundred kilograms and let him find out what that means; and never fall.
ST23-04.strengths: Mass beyond any other living thing on two legs: grapples, crushing presses, the reach of the largest giants alive.
ST23-04.weakness: Hips and knees that break under the weight; a fall can kill, a long walk cripples, and one giant of the line eats more than a household.

techniques.name: Lean
techniques.desc: Put a hand on him and let the weight settle; he holds up a hall-roof until he cannot.

techniques.name: The Whale-Drag
techniques.desc: Grom dragged a frozen whale twenty kilometers; a man in mail is a short pull.

techniques.name: Arm of the Mountain
techniques.desc: An arm longer than a man is tall, coming down from higher than any giant's.

techniques.name: Never Fall
techniques.desc: The line's first lesson: feet wide, weight low, and never give the ground a chance at your hips.

ST23-05.name: The Gate Breaks
ST23-05.origin: The Haugnes household has given Torholm its shore pairs since the Hunters' Rising of 412, when its giants fought beside Bolverk the Hard on the ice. In July 1096 a Haugnes pair carried Hakki of Torholm's body home from the Drevnan crossbows on the shore, and in August 1097 three Haugnes pairs broke Dobin's harbor gate beside Torvald and Brodd and burned the whaling boats. The household spoke against the Truce of Dobin and trains its young every winter on the shore, facing Dobin's lights across Whale Sound.
ST23-05.philosophy: Shoulder, maul, shoulder: the gate breaks, and then whatever stood behind it.
ST23-05.strengths: Breaking gates, palisades and shield walls; the charge into a held door.
ST23-05.weakness: Gate-breakers are easy marks: crossbows at the knees on a warm day killed two giants at the Torholm shore, and the household's grudges make it reckless.

techniques.name: Shoulder to the Door
techniques.desc: A thousand kilograms behind one shoulder; doors and shields both give.

techniques.name: Maul on the Bar
techniques.desc: Strike where the bar holds the gate, or where the arm holds the shield.

techniques.name: Through and Over
techniques.desc: Once the gate goes, the pair does not stop at it.

techniques.name: Dobin's Gate
techniques.desc: August 1097: the harbor gate of Dobin in three blows, and the boats burning behind it.

ST23-06.name: The Hookwater Harpoon
ST23-06.origin: Grom the Mountain could neither run nor turn, so he put human harpooners on his flanks and taught the pairs to fight beside them, and the first harpooner he chose was a Hookwater. The family has led Jotunhall's sixty harpooners since, hunters with iron-barbed harpoons who guard the giants' knees. At Dobin in August 1097 Hookwater harpooners held the flanks while the pairs broke the gate, and two of them died there.
ST23-06.philosophy: Throw, haul and keep the line tight: a man on the end of your harpoon cannot reach the giant's knee.
ST23-06.strengths: Barbed harpoons thrown and hauled; holding a man or a seal at a line's length; guarding a flank.
ST23-06.weakness: Hunters, not soldiers: no armor worth the name, and once the harpoon is thrown and the line cut, they have a knife.

techniques.name: Barbed Throw
techniques.desc: An iron barb on a sealskin line; it does not come out the way it went in.

techniques.name: Haul the Line
techniques.desc: The harpoon is in; haul, and he comes off his feet toward you.

techniques.name: At the Giant's Knee
techniques.desc: Stand where Grom told the first Hookwater to stand, and meet whatever comes for the knee.

techniques.name: Seal-Hunter's Thrust
techniques.desc: The thrust that finds a seal's heart through blubber finds a man's through a padded coat.

ST24-01.name: The Black Tower Crossbow
ST24-01.origin: The harbor towers of Sabra are still black from the Night of Fire, 19 August 1024, when the Qadiri galleys anchored beneath them and burned. Emir Farid ordered them never to be whitewashed and filled them with crossbowmen and engines, and the 3,000 harbor troops learn at the tower yard to shoot down from height onto decks and boats and to hold the stair with a short spear if anyone climbs it. Sabra's whole plan of war is to let a fleet come to the towers, and the towers must hold until the fire-boats are lit.
ST24-01.philosophy: Shoot down from height, keep the enemy on the water, and hold the stair if he ever reaches it.
ST24-01.strengths: Plunging shots from walls and towers, bolts through mail, holding a narrow stair
ST24-01.weakness: Slow to span, two bolts a minute; in the open a crossbowman caught by horse or a fast man is nearly helpless

techniques.name: Down from the Tower
techniques.desc: A bolt from above into a deck or a boat, where the shields all face the wrong way.

techniques.name: Stair Spear
techniques.desc: A short spear held down the tower stair; whoever climbs must climb onto it.

techniques.name: Merlon Span
techniques.desc: Kneel behind the merlon, span with a foot in the stirrup, and let his arrows break on the stone.

techniques.name: Through the Mail
techniques.desc: At thirty paces a bolt goes through mail and the man in it, and the tower yard teaches how to wait for thirty paces.

techniques.name: Stock to the Face
techniques.desc: When he reaches the top of the stair before the bolt is spanned, the crossbow's stock goes into his face.

techniques.name: Shoot the Steersman
techniques.desc: As the towers did in 1024: wait in the dark until the galley is lit by its own burning, then shoot the man at the steering oar.

maneuver.name: Tower Fire
maneuver.desc: The harbor towers sweep the anchorage with bolts and engine stones while the fire-boats are lit beneath them.

ST24-02.name: The Long Breath
ST24-02.origin: The pearl banks of Azara are worked by about 400 boats, by free divers of the gulf and by slave divers brought from the Veld, and a diver who reaches twelve fathoms is a famous man. In the knife fights on the banks, in the boats and in the water, the divers made their own way of fighting: the short hooked oyster-knife, a long breath and a body that does not tire. The diving stones of Azara teach it to anyone who can hold a breath, and the Pearl Banks watch is drawn from its students.
ST24-02.philosophy: Breathe slow, close in, and take him somewhere he cannot breathe.
ST24-02.strengths: Fighting in water and on boats, grappling, long breath and endurance, small blades
ST24-02.weakness: A diver's knife and bare skin: no reach and no armor, and on land against a spear or a sword the diver must get inside or die

techniques.name: Oyster-Knife
techniques.desc: The short hooked blade that opens a shell opens a wrist just as well.

techniques.name: Long Breath
techniques.desc: The diver's breath, slow and deep, between exchanges; he tires later than anyone on the beach.

techniques.name: Under the Arm
techniques.desc: Duck under the blade and come up inside it, knife to the armpit where the mail opens.

techniques.name: Pull Him Down
techniques.desc: Into the water together: the diver has two minutes of air and the other man has none.

techniques.name: Coral-Cutter
techniques.desc: Show the knife high and cut low at the back of the ankle, as the coral cuts a careless diver.

techniques.name: Twelve Fathoms
techniques.desc: The deepest dive of the banks made into a fight: a hold that does not let go, taken down until he stops struggling.

ST24-03.name: The Oil Yard Throw
ST24-03.origin: About 958 Wafiq Nafari found that the thin oil boiled off the seep pitch of Zariya burns on water, and on 19 August 1024 boats smeared with it burned 19 Qadiri galleys under the towers of Sabra. The Oil Yard of Zariya trains the 1,200 Fire-Boat Crews to throw the clay pots, drift the rafts on the tide and live through it, and it teaches only Sabrans. Saad the Burnt, whose face and arms are shiny with old fire, holds it in 1105 and bitterly resents that House Nafari will not let him boil his own oil.
ST24-03.philosophy: Light it, throw it and be gone before it reaches you; never fight a fleet, burn it.
ST24-03.strengths: Fire that sticks, floats and burns on water; terror; striking ships and camps from range
ST24-03.weakness: Anyone inside ten paces, a wind from the wrong quarter, sand and wet hides, and the jars themselves: the Oil Yard buries its own

techniques.name: Fire-Pot
techniques.desc: A clay pot of oil with a burning rag, thrown at twenty paces; the fire sticks wherever it breaks.

techniques.name: Sand and Roll
techniques.desc: The first thing the yard teaches: when it catches you, down in the sand and roll, and live to throw again.

techniques.name: Black Smoke
techniques.desc: A smoking pot thrown short: black smoke between you, and he coughs and squints while you move.

techniques.name: Burning Water
techniques.desc: Pots thrown onto the water around him, not at him; the oil floats and burns, and there is nowhere left to stand.

techniques.name: Fire-Raft
techniques.desc: A burning raft let go on the tide into his boat or his line: he must jump or burn, and either way he is off his feet.

techniques.name: The Master's Jar
techniques.desc: The heavy jar the masters keep for one throw: it bursts across shield and man, and the burning runs into every gap.

maneuver.name: Fire-Boats on the Ebb
maneuver.desc: Small boats with oil pots drift into an anchored fleet at night; the crews light them at a hundred paces and swim back.

ST24-04.name: The Camel Screen of Hazim
ST24-04.origin: The Hazimi have been camel lords of the uplands since the 880s, and in the Sabun Pass in 1022 they learned both how a column dies of thirst and how camels break horse. When Emir Farid raised the Camel Guard of the Emir in 1036, the Camel School of Hazim was made to train it: lance and bow from the camel, and fighting through the midday heat of August when mailed men fall from their saddles. Nuri Hazimi, master since 1100, trains the 2,000 of the Guard and waits on the Sabun road to see which way the war turns.
ST24-04.philosophy: Hold the road at noon: let the heat fight him first, kneel the camels into a wall, and lance what is left.
ST24-04.strengths: Camel lance and bow, the camel screen, horses that shy from camels, fighting through the noon heat
ST24-04.weakness: Camels start and turn slowly; a steady line of foot or a night attack undoes it, and away from water and shade its tricks run out

techniques.name: Camel Smell
techniques.desc: Ride the camel straight at his horse; a horse that has never smelled a camel shies, and its rider with it.

techniques.name: High Saddle Shot
techniques.desc: From the camel's high saddle, a shot down over his shield at forty paces.

techniques.name: Kneel the Camels
techniques.desc: The camel kneels into a wall of hide and saddle, and the bow shoots over it at whatever comes.

techniques.name: Noon Heat
techniques.desc: Keep him moving in the sun at noon: the quilted Sabran shirt breathes, and his mail cooks him.

techniques.name: Camel Lance
techniques.desc: The long lance from two metres up, coming down at an angle no horseman is used to parrying.

techniques.name: Charge of the Guard
techniques.desc: At the hottest hour the Camel Guard rides into men half spent by the sun: lances down, camels roaring, horses bolting.

maneuver.name: Camel Screen
maneuver.desc: The camels kneel in a line with riders shooting from behind them: a wall against horse and a store of water at once.

ST24-05.name: The Dry Emir's Way
ST24-05.origin: Bakr Sabrani was the first of the house with the Salt-skin, and his grandson Farid the Dry burned the Qadiri fleet in 1024 and fought at noon in August while his enemies fell from the heat, a servant always riding beside him with salted water. By Farid's house law of 1035 every Sabrani child grows up in the Emir's household at Sabra, and the sons are drilled at noon in the curved sword and the oil-pot, the way Farid fought. Tahir, the heir and Captain of the Fire-Boats, has his great-grandfather's taste for noon drills.
ST24-05.philosophy: Fight at the hottest hour: sweat while he burns, and press him until the sun finishes what the sword began.
ST24-05.strengths: Fighting in the midday heat, pressing a tiring enemy, the curved sword and the oil-pot together
ST24-05.weakness: The Salt-skin's price: without salt and water a Sabrani cramps and collapses in a long action, and the servant with the cup is a target

techniques.name: Noon Drill
techniques.desc: Cut, cut, step in, at the hour when the sand burns through sandals: the drill every Sabrani child learns.

techniques.name: The Salted Cup
techniques.desc: A mouthful of salted water from the servant at your shoulder, and the cramp that was coming does not.

techniques.name: Pot and Blade
techniques.desc: An oil-pot broken at his feet to open the fight, and the sword in the hand before it has finished burning.

techniques.name: We Sweat, They Burn
techniques.desc: The house's words: come on hardest when the sun is highest, while the man in mail boils inside it.

techniques.name: Farid's Cut
techniques.desc: The Dry Emir's blow from the saddle at noon, never seen to drink: one unhurried cut into a man too spent to raise his guard.

maneuver.name: The Hottest Hour
maneuver.desc: The Emir waits until noon in August to give battle, and his men fight in quilted cotton with salted water carried behind every rank.

ST24-06.name: The Rope
ST24-06.origin: Jafar Zarani, a caravan captain, was made Lord of the South March in 1041 to hold the frontier toward the Western Veld. From 1062 the house raided the Veld for young divers to sell to the pearl boats, and its 600 slave-riders learned to take people alive: the noose from the saddle, the weighted net and the club behind the ear. The free divers of Azara call the house 'the Rope', and Musa Zarani has ridden on its raids since he was seventeen.
ST24-06.philosophy: Take him alive: rope him, drag him, club him quiet, and count him as silver.
ST24-06.strengths: Captures, bringing men down from a distance, ropework from the saddle, fighting the frightened and the scattered
ST24-06.weakness: A slaver's craft made for villagers: against a formed line, a man in mail who does not run, or a cut rope it has little, and every Sandfolk clan would kill a Zarani on sight

techniques.name: Saddle Noose
techniques.desc: A thrown loop from the trotting horse, and he is on the ground before he knows he was caught.

techniques.name: Club Behind the Ear
techniques.desc: A short club, not a blade: a captive with a cracked head can still dive.

techniques.name: Weighted Net
techniques.desc: The net with lead weights thrown over sword arm and shoulder, and every move tangles him worse.

techniques.name: The Drag
techniques.desc: Rope him and ride: twenty paces over stones takes the fight out of anyone.

techniques.name: Counted as Silver
techniques.desc: Down, bound and alive: the Zarani way of ending a fight, because a dead man fetches nothing at Zaran.

ST25-01.name: The War-Hearth Spear
