ST25-01.origin: Velgrad's war-hearths send their spearmen to the rota, 14,000 of them with a quarter on duty at any time, and most are forest farmers and trappers who learned the boar spear before the war spear. The crown yard at Belovo teaches both: the shield wall that held the neck of land at Lake Ostec in 957, when the Tessarians broke against Radoslav's line, and the cross-barred spear that stops a bear, a boar or a rider a hand deep.
ST25-01.philosophy: Stand in the wall with your neighbors, let the beast or the rider come, and stop him on the crossbar a hand deep so the next man can finish him.
ST25-01.strengths: Shield-wall drill; cross-barred spears against charges, beasts and big men; steady farmers who do not run.
ST25-01.weakness: Plain levy men on a quarter rota: little skill alone, slow in the open, and a crossbow volley or an axe that hooks shields opens the wall.

techniques.name: Rim Over Rim
techniques.desc: Your rim over your neighbor's rim, feet planted: the wall holds you up as much as you hold it.

techniques.name: On the Crossbar
techniques.desc: The bar behind the blade stops the point a hand deep; the boar, or the man, is held off his feet and the next spear finishes him.

techniques.name: Second-Rank Thrust
techniques.desc: From behind your neighbor's shoulder, low under the rim, while the man in front is busy with the wall.

techniques.name: The Neck of Land
techniques.desc: Radoslav's day at Lake Ostec made a lesson: marsh on one side, water on the other, and the enemy breaking himself on a wall that does not move.

techniques.name: The Bear Hunt
techniques.desc: Every hearth's oldest lesson: when the big one comes, three of you go in together, low, and the spear goes under the ribs while he is still deciding whom to kill.

maneuver.name: The Hearth Wall
maneuver.desc: The war-hearth spearmen lock shields three deep with cross-barred spears in the second rank, and riders and charging foot stop on the bars.

ST25-02.name: The Pass-Gate Crossbow
ST25-02.origin: Velgrad lives behind its passes, the Mirovo and the Ostmir Gate, both walled by Solen engineers, and the Ostmir walled again by King Lubomir against the Wind riders. When the regent Anka Tolmir founded the crown bolt-yard at Mirgrad in 1036 she gave it to Zbynek Strelnik, who had learned the crossbow as a prisoner of the Drevnans, and the Strelnik loading drill is now taught to every crown crossbowman who will stand on a pass wall.
ST25-02.philosophy: Shoot down: from the pass wall or the slope above the road into men who must climb to reach you, and span again while they climb.
ST25-02.strengths: Shooting from height into a column or a breach; the Strelnik loading drill; pass walls and ambush slopes.
ST25-02.weakness: A gatekeeper's art: on the flat a crossbowman spans two bolts a minute while a rider crosses the whole field, and in rain the strings go slack.

techniques.name: Wind Up, Let Fly
techniques.desc: The Strelnik count, foot in the stirrup, hook to the string, back straight: every crown crossbowman says it under his breath.

techniques.name: Down the Slope
techniques.desc: Shot from above into the top of the shoulder, where the mail is thin and a man climbing cannot lift his shield.

techniques.name: Span Behind the Stone
techniques.desc: Step back behind the stone to span while the man beside you shoots; the wall takes what was meant for you.

techniques.name: Shoot the Last Man
techniques.desc: Let the column into the narrows and shoot the last man first: the front cannot go back, the rear cannot go on, and you know where every one of them must step.

techniques.name: The Gate-Tower Bow
techniques.desc: The lever-spanned bow that lives on the gate tower: one shot in a fight, and it goes through a shield, the mail behind it and most of the man.

maneuver.name: Pass Ambush
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen on both slopes of a pass wait for the column to string out, then shoot its head, its tail and its baggage from above.

ST25-03.name: The Dawn Ride
ST25-03.origin: The knights of the Lords' Bench serve the king by rota from their castles, and since Borislav Sevrin was crowned at dawn in sight of Redcrown's glow they have kept the custom of fighting at first light: march by night, pray at the grey hour, and strike in the first quarter-hour while the enemy is cold and half-armed. The knights' yard at Belina teaches the flanged mace from the saddle and the dismounted fight on a pass wall, because Velgrad's valleys rarely give a knight room to charge.
ST25-03.philosophy: Ride by night, strike at first light: the first quarter-hour of a dawn attack decides it, and a knight who has ridden all night must win before his horse remembers it is tired.
ST25-03.strengths: The dawn attack; the mace from the saddle against mail; fighting in narrow valleys and dismounted on a wall.
ST25-03.weakness: Everything is spent on the first rush: after a night march the horses are tired, and if the enemy stood to arms before dawn a Bench knight has no second plan.

techniques.name: Mace in Passing
techniques.desc: The flanged mace falls on the helmet as the horse goes by; mail turns a blade, and does nothing for the skull under it.

techniques.name: First Light
techniques.desc: Strike while he is still cold and half-armed, in the grey before sunrise, when a man's hands are slow to find his weapon.

techniques.name: Down From the Saddle
techniques.desc: The valley is too narrow for horses, so the knight steps down to the wall and fights there with the same mace, shield up.

techniques.name: Up in the Stirrups
techniques.desc: Standing in the stirrups with the whole horse behind one blow: the mace bends the helmet, and the man under it goes down with it.

techniques.name: The Night March
techniques.desc: Come from where he posted no picket, at the hour he did not expect, and let him spend himself turning to face you.

maneuver.name: Dawn Attack
maneuver.desc: The knights march by night and strike at first light, before the enemy has stood to arms; the first fifteen minutes decide it.

ST25-04.name: The North Woods Hatchet
ST25-04.origin: The North Woods around Solgrad yield sable and wax, and the trappers who work them in winter go on skis with a hand-axe in the belt and a hunting bow on the back. The crown raised the North Woods Ski-Runners from them, 1,200 strong, to scout and raid over snow where horses founder, and the Lisovik knights, whose children ski before they walk, teach the trappers' hatchet in a yard among the trap lines of Dobina.
ST25-04.philosophy: Never stand where he can reach you: throw from the run, close only when he is down or blown, and be gone across the snow before his friends arrive.
ST25-04.strengths: Throwing hand-axes; moving over snow; hit-and-run, ambush and the long chase.
ST25-04.weakness: Light men in fur coats: they cannot hold a line, a shield turns most of what they throw, and in summer mud or on open ground they are only hunters.

techniques.name: Hatchet From the Run
techniques.desc: Thrown overhand while you are still sliding, so the hatchet carries the speed of the skis with it.

techniques.name: Read the Tracks
techniques.desc: A trapper reads tracks: you read how he sets his feet in the snow, and where he will be next.

techniques.name: Hamstring the Elk
techniques.desc: The hand-axe low to the back of the knee, as you take an elk floundering in deep snow.

techniques.name: Run Him Down
techniques.desc: Let him flounder after you through the drifts until he is blown, then turn on him: a man in mail on snow is done in minutes.

techniques.name: Two Hatchets
techniques.desc: One hatchet from each hand, the second while the first is still turning in the air; he can lift his shield for only one.

maneuver.name: The Snow Road Raid
maneuver.desc: Ski-runners cover forty kilometres a day over snow where horses founder, burn the enemy's stores and are gone before his riders can find them.

ST25-05.name: The Bear's Hook
ST25-05.origin: Radoslav the Bear founded the Hall of the Bear with the Bear Guard after Lake Ostec, choosing the tallest men of the realm and teaching them the great-axe and the long-axe in mail. Bogdan Oak-Arm held the Hall from 1071 to 1090; Ruslan Hardhand, who hooked down four shields on the Feleria bridge in 1083 and finished the fight left-handed, holds it now and has taught King Stanislav since the prince passed 200 cm.
ST25-05.philosophy: Do not swing at the man: swing at the top of his shield, hook the beard over the rim, pull it down with your whole weight as you step in, and come back up through the gap.
ST25-05.strengths: Breaking shield walls, three shields in ten seconds; reach and weight in a line; big men in mail who do not flinch.
ST25-05.weakness: A spear line reaches him first, a quick blade gets inside the haft, and the swing lasts two minutes at full effort, not ten.

techniques.name: Beard Over the Rim
techniques.desc: The long beard of the axe goes over the top of his shield, and you pull it down toward your own knee.

techniques.name: Up Through the Gap
techniques.desc: The same swing coming back: the shield is down, and the axe rises through the gap into the face or the neck.

techniques.name: Short Grip
techniques.desc: When a quick man gets inside the head, slide your hands up the haft and fight him with the ash like a quarterstaff.

techniques.name: Three Shields in Ten Seconds
techniques.desc: Hook, pull, cut, step, and again: Ruslan's name, a wall of shields opened one by one faster than the men behind can close it.

techniques.name: All Day
techniques.desc: The Hall's oldest boast: breathe on the backswing and let the weight of the head do the work, and the axe goes on falling long after the arm should have quit.

maneuver.name: The Bear Guard's Hook
maneuver.desc: Great-axemen go into an enemy shield wall in a wedge, hooking the shields down so the spearmen behind can strike through the gaps.

ST25-06.name: The Sevany Oar-Beat
ST25-06.origin: The channel squadron at Sevany is older than the kingdom: its 22 galleys came over to Borislav Sevrin and the Dawn in 735, and since the War of the Channel the Volan Channel-Masters have built it to 38. Its Oar School teaches rowers, debt-rowers and the 1,600 Sevany Hooks to row, ram and board in the channel tides, and Dmitri Hale, who learned the long-axe in the Hall of the Bear and the oar from Pavle Strak, is its master and its voice in 1105.
ST25-06.philosophy: The voice first: stroke, ram, rush, everything on the beat, and the master goes over the bow before anyone, with the long-axe and no mail.
ST25-06.strengths: The oar-beat in the arms; the grapnel throw; long-axe and round shield on a deck; one voice that fifty benches obey.
ST25-06.weakness: No mail and no fleet battle in living memory: ashore, or with a diver under the keel, a Sevany man is a big ordinary man with an axe.

techniques.name: On the Beat
techniques.desc: Breathe on the stroke and strike on the stroke: fifty benches taught your body a rhythm it does not forget in a fight.

techniques.name: Throw the Hook
techniques.desc: The grapnel thrown over his rail, or his shoulder, and hauled: whatever it catches comes toward you.

techniques.name: The Voice
techniques.desc: A shout that carries over fifty oar-benches in a gale, let go a hand's breadth from his face: he flinches, and the axe does not.

techniques.name: Long-Axe From the Bow
techniques.desc: From the high bow down onto the lower deck, the long haft reaching over the rail before his sword can.

techniques.name: Stroke, Ram, Rush
techniques.desc: Dmitri Hale's three words, the whole school in one breath: the last stroke, the shock of the ram, and the master over the bow before anyone.

maneuver.name: Grapnels and Hooks
maneuver.desc: The Sevany Hooks throw their grapnels as the ram strikes and haul the enemy galley alongside, and the half-orc galley axemen go over before her crew can cut the lines.

ST25-07.name: The Standing Bear
ST25-07.origin: Borislav Sevrin stood 203 cm at eighteen and carried the black bear standard of the Eastern March before men who could see it across any field, and his house has taught its sons to fight as he did: upright, from above, and where they can be seen. Radoslav the Bear, 211 cm, held the neck of land at Lake Ostec this way and lived to 56; Miroslav, 208 cm, fought this way through the Lakeland War and was dead at 47. Every Sevrin boy is measured at the Bear Keep doorpost each Midwinter, and the tall ones are taught to spend their hearts carefully.
ST25-07.philosophy: Stand to your full height and fight downhill from it: be seen, strike from above, crush whatever comes close, and end it before the heart asks for its price.
ST25-07.strengths: Height, reach and weight in the bear-blood sons; downward blows and crushing holds; a presence that makes ordinary men hesitate.
ST25-07.weakness: The bear-blood heart: the tall Sevrins fade in a long fight and die young, and the headaches can blind a king for a breath in the middle of a bout.

techniques.name: Stand Tall
techniques.desc: Rise to your full height and let him look up at you; most men lose half a heartbeat working out where to cut.

techniques.name: From Above
techniques.desc: A downward cut from a height no other man's sword starts from, over the top of his guard.

techniques.name: The Bear's Embrace
techniques.desc: Let him come inside your reach, as the clever ones do, and then close your arms: the bear-blood crushes what it holds.

techniques.name: Radoslav's Neck
techniques.desc: Stand where the ground narrows, as the Bear stood at Lake Ostec, and let a giant's reach close the gap he must come through.

techniques.name: The Heart's Price
techniques.desc: Everything the bear-blood has, all at once, and the heart pays for it afterwards; the tall kings who did this twice in a day did not see fifty.

maneuver.name: The Bear Standard
maneuver.desc: A Sevrin in the front rank under the black bear and the red lamp: the men who can see him across the field follow him, and the men facing him look twice.

ST25-08.name: The Ostec Lance
ST25-08.origin: Ostoja Koren held the marsh flank of the neck of land at Lake Ostec in September 957, and Radoslav the Bear gave his family the Ostec March and the southern border. The Korens raised the Ostec Lances, the only Velgradan knights trained to fight in the open, and have led them into the Neck for Prince Andros since 1075; Lord Zoran Koren is Lord Marshal, and his son Anton led the storm of Doria in 1103.
ST25-08.philosophy: Hold the gate, then ride out of it: a Koren waits on the flank as Ostoja waited in the marsh, and charges only when the enemy's line is committed and his side is open.
ST25-08.strengths: The couched lance in the open; flank charges timed to the moment; marcher cunning and the Marchfolk speech of the border.
ST25-08.weakness: Marsh-and-gate patience makes them late: a Koren waits for the sure moment, and against an enemy who never commits, the moment never comes.

techniques.name: Wait on the Flank
techniques.desc: Hold your horse still at the edge of the marsh and watch which way his line leans.

techniques.name: The Couched Lance
techniques.desc: Knee to knee, lance under the arm: walk, trot, and only the last fifty paces at the gallop.

techniques.name: Into His Side
techniques.desc: The lance comes from where his shield is not: a flank charge in one man, timed to the moment he commits to the front.

techniques.name: We Hold the Gate
techniques.desc: The house words on foot: dismounted at the Ostmir Gate with the lance shortened, a Koren lets nothing past and answers everything that tries.

techniques.name: Ostoja's Marsh
techniques.desc: Draw him onto the soft ground where his horse sinks and yours does not, as the Tessarians were drawn in 957, and take him while he struggles.

maneuver.name: The Ostec Flank Charge
maneuver.desc: The Ostec Lances wait on a wing until the enemy line is fully engaged, then go round into its side at the gallop, knee to knee.

ST25-09.name: The Kamogda Ice-Pick
ST25-09.origin: Ctibor Zhelnik was a crossbow sergeant who lived through the winter siege of Brodava in 1035 and 1036 and walked home across the ice when it failed, and in 1038 the regent Anka Tolmir gave him Kamogda Kremlin to watch the new Drevnan border. His family keeps it and the Tolek river forts, searches every barge from the Lakeland to the plank, and has twice sent men across the frozen border at night to break Drevnan fish-weirs.
ST25-09.philosophy: Remember Brodava: trust no ice you have not tested, no barge you have not searched and no Drevnan you cannot see; then cross at night, strike once and walk home.
ST25-09.strengths: Fighting on river ice and frozen ground; the crossbow from a fort or a bank; a suspicion that finds the hidden blade.
ST25-09.weakness: Grim, slow and suspicious: a Zhelnik tests every step and every man, and a bolder enemy has struck twice while he is still deciding.

techniques.name: Test the Ice
techniques.desc: Tap before you trust: a Zhelnik feels for the weak place in the ice, and in a man's guard, before he puts his weight on either.

techniques.name: Plank by Plank
techniques.desc: Search everything, even the man you are fighting: the hidden knife meets the pick before it is out of the sleeve.

techniques.name: Bolt From the Bank
techniques.desc: Shot from the river fort's bank into a bargeman or a sled driver who has nowhere on the open ice to hide.

techniques.name: The Ice-Pick
techniques.desc: The short pick that tests the ice and holds you on it goes through mail just as easily: one blow, point first, where the rings are thinnest.

techniques.name: We Remember Brodava
techniques.desc: Across the frozen border at night, as the castellans have gone twice: cold that kills other men is home to you, and you strike out of it while he shivers.

maneuver.name: The Tolek Forts
maneuver.desc: The river forts close the Tolek with crossbows on both banks and search every barge; nothing moves on the river or its winter ice without a Zhelnik seeing it.

ST26-01.name: The Hearth Crossbow
ST26-01.origin: Women shot crossbows from the walls of Brodava through the winter of 1035, and Queen Ludmila let them keep their weapons and serve; the Radov crossbows held the burning line behind Kraina in 1034 while she pulled back, and since the Tusk War the law of 1066 has made every Steppe March farmer keep a crossbow at home. The crown yard at Radov teaches the hearth-roll crossbow to farmers, fishers and their daughters, and those bows are why the Lakeland's army can win by waiting.
ST26-01.philosophy: Never go to him: put water, a fence or a wall between you, let him come across it, and shoot him while he wades.
ST26-01.strengths: Shooting from behind water, fences and walls; men and women alike; patience; volleys by rank.
ST26-01.weakness: A defender's bow: slow to span and useless on the advance, and a quick rider inside twenty paces finds a farmer with a short knife.

techniques.name: While He Wades
techniques.desc: Shot while he crosses: a man waist-deep in a Lakeland stream cannot run, cannot dodge and cannot reach you.

techniques.name: Rank Behind Rank
techniques.desc: Step back to span while the next rank shoots, then step up again: no rank is ever empty-handed.

techniques.name: The Fence-Rail Rest
techniques.desc: The bow laid on a fence rail and held until he chooses his line; then the bolt goes where he is about to be.

techniques.name: Burn the Field
techniques.desc: Ludmila's lesson at Kraina: give ground, burn what he would eat, and let hunger and the long walk fight him before you do.

techniques.name: The Brodava Walls
techniques.desc: Zdenka of Brodava's shot in the starving winter: aimed down into the siege lines at the one man who mattered, with all the cold patience of the siege behind it.

maneuver.name: Crossbow Line Behind a Stream
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen stand behind a stream, a flooded ditch or a marsh edge and shoot the enemy as he wades, at thirty to sixty paces.

ST26-02.name: The Bearward's Spear
ST26-02.origin: Lakeland hunters have always taken bears on the spear, kneeling with the butt in the earth and letting the beast come onto the point, and the Lovchin bearwards of the Lubevo forest have taught it since King Lubor made the first Medved Lovchin bearward after the Black Cough. When the Tusk riders and the Hrimfell giants came, the crown made it the hearth-roll's war drill: a set spear line for riders on the Steppe March, and the low thrust at the knee that the spearmen used on the giants caught on the Torholm shore in 1096.
ST26-02.philosophy: Kneel, set the butt and let him come: horse, bear or giant spits itself on its own weight, and anything too tall to stop you go low and take its knees.
ST26-02.strengths: Stopping charges with a set spear; fighting beasts, riders and giants; low thrusts at knees and hamstrings.
ST26-02.weakness: Nerve is all it has: against a patient man who will not charge, a kneeling spearman is only a target, and a volley, or a rider who stops short and shoots, breaks the line.

techniques.name: Set the Butt
techniques.desc: Butt in the earth behind your heel, point at his chest, and kneel: whatever charges you pays for its own speed.

techniques.name: Low to the Knee
techniques.desc: Anything taller than you has knees: the thrust goes low, into the joint, and the big ones stop being big.

techniques.name: Let It Come
techniques.desc: The bearward's patience: not a hair's movement while it closes, until it is on the point and cannot stop.

techniques.name: Two Spears, One Bear
techniques.desc: One point in its face to hold its eyes while the other goes in under the arm: the hunters' way, and the soldier's against a man too strong to face.

techniques.name: The Giant's Knee
techniques.desc: Learned on the Torholm shore: under the swing, low, the point through the back of the knee, and a giant, or any big man, goes down and stays down.

maneuver.name: Set Spear Line
maneuver.desc: Spearmen kneel and set the butts of their spears in the ground, points at a horse's chest or a giant's knee, and the charge spits itself on its own weight.

ST26-03.name: The Lake Knight
ST26-03.origin: Drevna's crown and lake-lord knights are few, and they ride horses bought from the steppe. At Zorek in 1064 the orc war-drums broke their charge and both princes fell, and since then the knights' yard at Kraina has trained horses to the drum, riders to hand-signs, and whole companies to cross the frozen lakes on spiked shoes in winter, the season Drevna fights.
ST26-03.philosophy: Wait for winter and wait for the moment: a Lake Knight crosses the ice where nobody expects horse, charges only when the crossbows have broken the enemy, and does not hear the drums.
ST26-03.strengths: Charging over frozen lakes on spiked shoes; horses trained to drums; silent hand-sign orders; riding down an enemy already shaken.
ST26-03.weakness: Few, and taught to wait: they charge late or not at all, the thaw and the summer mud ground them, and a fresh enemy in good order is not their fight.

techniques.name: Spiked Shoes
techniques.desc: Iron spikes on the horse's shoes and on your own heels: on lake ice you stand and turn where other men slide.

techniques.name: Drum-Broken Horses
techniques.desc: A horse that has heard the war-drum every morning of its life does not shy; the noise that broke the charge at Zorek breaks nothing now.

techniques.name: Across the Ice
techniques.desc: Out of the snow-glare at a gallop over a lake nobody thought would bear a horse; he is still turning when the lance arrives.

techniques.name: After the Volley
techniques.desc: Charge only a beaten enemy: watch the bolts land, see who staggers, and ride at that man.

techniques.name: The Silent Charge
techniques.desc: No horn and no shout: the order is a raised fist, and the line is moving before the enemy's ears tell him anything has changed.

maneuver.name: The Winter Crossing
maneuver.desc: The knights cross a frozen lake on spiked shoes, five metres apart and never bunched, and strike the enemy from the side he thought the water guarded.

ST26-04.name: The Forearm in the Dark
ST26-04.origin: Queen Ludmila built the Still Hall after 1048, with the Listener's Guard, to train the night watch in silent movement and in fighting by hand-signs. Oleg Marsh, its second master, took in a Steppe March scout's orphan in 1065, and that boy, Lev Hollis, has been master since 1084 and has trained all 600 of the Still Watch; about thirty men are dead by his hands, and not one of them saw him first.
ST26-04.philosophy: A fair fight is a failure of planning: come from behind, walk on the outside of the foot, count his breaths, and put the forearm across his throat.
ST26-04.strengths: Silence, patience and the dark; the choke that leaves a man senseless in ten seconds; the knife under the ear when it must be seen.
ST26-04.weakness: Daylight and a fair fight: a man with his back to a wall, a lantern lit or a dog awake has little to fear from the Still Hall.

techniques.name: The Outside of the Foot
techniques.desc: Walk on the outer edge of the sole and count his breaths: you know where he is, and he has not yet learned that you exist.

techniques.name: Already Behind You
techniques.desc: There is no first second as other men know it; by the time he turns, the place he is looking at is empty.

techniques.name: Forearm Across the Throat
techniques.desc: The left arm, as Lev Hollis has used it since a spy's knife opened his right: across the throat from behind, and senseless in ten seconds.

techniques.name: Under the Ear
techniques.desc: When the queen wants it seen: the long knife under the ear, once, and away into the dark before he falls.

techniques.name: If He Turns, Leave
techniques.desc: The hardest lesson: the moment he sees you, the fight you planned is over; step back into the dark, breathe, and choose the next one.

maneuver.name: Night Raid
maneuver.desc: The Still Watch go in by night in silence, kill the sentries, burn stores or take a man from his tent, and are gone before dawn.

ST26-05.name: The Zorin Steppe Bow
ST26-05.origin: The Zoracs have kept the Steppe March with crossbows and wagon forts since Ratko Zorac was made warden at Zorin in 887, and the yard behind the town's stone walls trained the bows that turned back 5,000 Tusk riders in the spring of 1063. Mara Zorac, the Lord Marshal's daughter, has been its master since 1096 and commands the 3,000 Zorin Crossbows; she learned her loading drill from the Samostrel women, who still serve as its sergeants.
ST26-05.philosophy: Kill the horse, not the rider: from behind stakes and wagons, shoot the beast that carries the orc to you, and let him come the last thirty paces on foot into the next volley.
ST26-05.strengths: Aimed shooting at riders and horse archers; stakes, ditches and wagon forts; the fastest loading drill in the Lakeland.
ST26-05.weakness: It needs its works: caught without stakes, wagons or walls, a Zorin crossbowman has one bolt and a short spear against a relay of riders.

techniques.name: The Samostrel Count
techniques.desc: The loading drill the Samostrel women pass from mother to daughter: foot, hook, string, bolt, breathe, and not one movement wasted.

techniques.name: Shoot the Horse
techniques.desc: Aim at the horse's chest, not the man: a rider who falls with his horse gets up slowly, if at all.

techniques.name: Behind the Stakes
techniques.desc: Sharpened stakes at forty-five degrees in front of you: the man who comes through them comes slowly, and meets the short spear.

techniques.name: The Second Volley
techniques.desc: Shoot as he comes, span while he closes, and shoot again at thirty paces: the second bolt finds him on foot and close, where mail is no help.

techniques.name: Shoot the Drummer
techniques.desc: The Yard's answer to Zorek: find the drummer behind the first wave and put a bolt in him, and the relay loses its count.

maneuver.name: Stake Line
maneuver.desc: Each crossbowman plants a stake sharpened at both ends, in staggered rows a pace apart; horses refuse it and orc relays break on it while the volleys go in.

ST26-06.name: The Listener's Blade
ST26-06.origin: Queen Ludmila heard two men whispering behind the wall on the night after her crowning in 1010 and lived; every Dravic since descends from her, and those with her ears are taught to fight by them. Since the princes Radim and Svetozar fell to the orc drums at Zorek, the house also teaches its heirs to fight deaf, with wax in their ears, and Lev Hollis has trained Princess Ludmila so since 1102.
ST26-06.philosophy: We hear before we strike: listen to his breath and his feet, let him tell you the blow by its sound, and when the drums come, stop your ears and fight with your eyes.
ST26-06.strengths: Hearing a step, a breath or a blade leaving the sheath before anyone sees it; ambushes behind walls and in the dark; answers that come early.
ST26-06.weakness: Drums: a war-drum's rhythm overwhelms a Dravic skull and can fell them where they stand, and with the wax in they lose the gift that made them dangerous.

techniques.name: Hear the Breath
techniques.desc: A man breathes in before he cuts; a Dravic hears it from across the room.

techniques.name: Whisper Behind the Wall
techniques.desc: Ludmila's night in the Tower: you heard him coming before he moved, so the blow meets a blade already waiting for it.

techniques.name: Wax in the Ears
techniques.desc: Stop the ears and fight on the eyes alone, as the Listener's Guard do: deaf, the drums cannot touch you, and neither can a feint made by sound.

techniques.name: First to Hear
techniques.desc: You heard his blade clear the scabbard and yours was already moving; the first cut belongs to whoever heard it first.

techniques.name: We Hear Before We Strike
techniques.desc: The house words: every shift of his weight and catch of his breath has told you his next three moves, and you answer all of them before he makes the first.

maneuver.name: Hand-Signs and Wax
maneuver.desc: The Listener's Guard fight by hand-signs with wax in their ears; drums, horns and shouting cannot break an order that is never heard.

ST26-07.name: The Zorin Wall-Walk
ST26-07.origin: Ratko Zorac was made warden of the steppe edge at Zorin in 887, and his family walled the town in stone over the next thirty years and has kept the Steppe March from its walls since. In the spring of 1063 Zorin turned back about 5,000 orcs of the Tusk Clans after three weeks; a year later, out on the open field at Zorek, the orc drums broke the Drevnan charge and killed both princes, the Zoracs' own cousins, and the house has trusted stone over horses ever since.
ST26-07.philosophy: The wall does not ride: let the steppe come to the stone, fight it at the top of the ladder with shield and axe, and never follow it back out onto the grass.
ST26-07.strengths: Wall-top fighting; throwing down ladders and the men on them; endurance through a long siege.
ST26-07.weakness: A Zorac will not leave the wall: he never pursues and never takes the field, and off the stone, in the open, the house fights like men who remember Zorek.

techniques.name: Ladder Top
techniques.desc: The man at the top of a ladder has one hand on the rungs and no footing; hit him then, and the ladder does the rest.

techniques.name: Merlon and Shield
techniques.desc: Half your body behind the stone and the other half behind the shield: there is very little of a Zorac on the wall to hit.

techniques.name: Push the Ladder
techniques.desc: The forked pole set under the top rung and the whole wall-walk shoving: the ladder goes back, and the men on it come down with it.

techniques.name: Three Weeks on the Wall
techniques.desc: The siege of 1063 taught the house to last: eat, sleep and fight in turns on the wall-walk, and still be standing when the riders give up.

techniques.name: The Wall Does Not Ride
techniques.desc: The house words: you will not go to him, ever. He must come up to you, and every time he does it costs him more than it costs you.

maneuver.name: Hold the Stone
maneuver.desc: The garrison fights from the wall-walk and the gate towers and never sallies; ladders are thrown down and the steppe is left to break itself on the stone.

ST26-08.name: The Brodar Ice-Staff
ST26-08.origin: In the winter of 1035 Vasil Brodar, sled master of Brodava, drove about 600 sleds across the frozen lake by night with food for the besieged town while Velgradan sentries froze on the bank, and Queen Ludmila rode on the first run herself. The Sled Riders were raised from his drivers and a Brodar has commanded them since; the house teaches its children the Ice Crossing, sleds thirty paces apart and a man with an ice-staff walking ahead of the first team.
ST26-08.philosophy: The ice will hold if you know it: walk ahead with the staff, listen for the groan, keep thirty paces apart, and come off the lake where nobody posted a sentry.
ST26-08.strengths: Footing and fighting on ice; the iron-shod ice-staff; night raids by sled with crossbows; knowing where the ice is weak and luring men onto it.
ST26-08.weakness: A winter house: from the thaw to the first hard freeze the Brodar way is half a style, and an enemy who stays off the ice has little to fear from it.

techniques.name: Tap the Ankle
techniques.desc: The iron-shod staff that tests the ice ahead of the first team taps a man's ankle just as well, and on ice he goes down.

techniques.name: Thirty Paces Apart
techniques.desc: Never bunch: keep your distance, and he can never catch two of you, or close on you before you see him coming.

techniques.name: Bolt From the Sled
techniques.desc: Shot from a sled at the gallop across the ice, the driver holding the team steady for one breath.

techniques.name: Where the Ice Groans
techniques.desc: You know where the ice is thin and he does not: give ground toward it, let him follow, and the lake takes his feet.

techniques.name: The Night Run
techniques.desc: Vasil Brodar's winter: across the frozen lake in the dark, past men who never believed the ice would bear a sled, and on them before they know which shore you came from.

maneuver.name: Winter Sled Raid
maneuver.desc: Sled Riders cross the frozen lakes by night at forty to sixty kilometres a day, shoot or burn what they find, and are gone across the ice before dawn.

ST26-09.name: Behind the Wagons
ST26-09.origin: In the spring of 1063, while 5,000 orcs besieged Zorin, a Zorac captain named Bojan Ugavin held the half-built fort at Ugava for eleven days with 300 crossbows behind a ring of farm wagons. His line was given the fort, made stone after the war, and keeps the wagon-fort drill; but the Ugavins keep for their own children the worst job in it, the fight from under the wagon beds when the riders reach the ring.
ST26-09.philosophy: Make a fort of whatever you have: chain the wheels, shoot between the spokes, and when the riders reach the wagons, be under the bed with a long knife for the horse's legs.
ST26-09.strengths: Fighting from cover and from below; crippling horses and riders; making a stand anywhere, with anything.
ST26-09.weakness: Nothing to offer in the open: an Ugavin without a wagon, a wall or a ditch is a careful man with a crossbow, and fire or engines break the ring.

techniques.name: Between the Spokes
techniques.desc: The wheel is your shield and the spokes your loophole: shoot through them, and pull back before he finds the gap.

techniques.name: Under the Bed
techniques.desc: Flat on your back under the wagon as the riders come up to it, and the long knife goes across the horse's legs from below.

techniques.name: Chain the Wheels
techniques.desc: Ring closed, wheels chained, gaps stopped with pavises: whatever he does, he does it to oak and iron first.

techniques.name: The Gap in the Ring
techniques.desc: Leave one gap in the ring on purpose and wait beside it with the spear; the bravest rider takes it, and the bravest rider is the one you wanted.

maneuver.name: Wagon Fort
maneuver.desc: Wagons chained wheel to wheel in a ring, the gaps closed with pavises and stakes; crossbows shoot between the wheels and spearmen fight from under the beds.

ST26-10.name: The Kolin Harpoon
ST26-10.origin: Stepan Kolin led about 300 burned-out families of the Steppe March north to Dobin in 1064, and when Queen Milena turned the kingdom to the Whale Coast his whalers learned the harpoon on Whale Sound. Giants of Hrimfell burned the station at Yarov in 1095 and killed Stepan with 40 whalers, and his son Ivo fought at Dobin's harbor gate when the giants broke it in 1097; the house teaches its harpoon for whales, and for the things that come for whales.
ST26-10.philosophy: Strike from a few paces and hold on: the iron goes in, the line goes taut, and whatever is on the other end, whale or giant or man, spends itself against you.
ST26-10.strengths: The thrown harpoon at close range; the line that holds and drags; nerve against things far bigger than a man.
ST26-10.weakness: A whaler's weapon: one heavy throw, then a man with a line and a lance, slow to recover; and the grievance makes Kolins pick fights they cannot finish.

techniques.name: The Iron Goes In
techniques.desc: The harpoon thrown from the bow at a few paces, its barbed iron head made to stay where it lands.

techniques.name: Make the Line Fast
techniques.desc: Turn the line round the post and let it run: whatever you struck pulls against the boat until it has nothing left to pull with.

techniques.name: The Whale-Lance
techniques.desc: The long lance for the kill once the beast is tired, driven deep between the ribs where the life is.

techniques.name: The Harbor Gate
techniques.desc: Dobin in August 1097: when the giants broke the gate the whalers met them with lances in the gateway, and the first one through came onto the iron.

techniques.name: Yarov Remembered
techniques.desc: The throw every Kolin practises for the day it is owed: the whole body behind the iron, at the biggest thing on the shore.

ST27-01.name: The Stair Guard Staff
ST27-01.origin: Abbot Yeshe raised the Stair Guard in 722, paid in butter and barley, to keep the White Stair and the pilgrim roads, and since its men killed three Moonstair robbers in 767 the Guard has sworn never to kill. Its 2,400 lay guards carry iron-shod staves, slings and yak-hair ropes. Tsering Snowborn, Captain of the Stair Guard and a student of Nima of the Still Hands, drills them in the yard below the seven flights, and must now decide what to do with the Chanari blades the Steward has bought.
ST27-01.philosophy: Three staves on one man: pin the arms, pin the legs, bind him, and let the thin air do the rest.
ST27-01.strengths: Disarming, knocking down and binding; fighting in pairs and threes; the thin air.
ST27-01.weakness: Sworn not to kill, it gives the edge to a man who would rather die than be held, or to a crossbow at 60 m; and alone, a staff is a long stick.

school.name: The Guard Yard of the White Stair

techniques.name: Iron Shoe to the Wrist
techniques.desc: The shod end of the staff cracks across his sword hand, and his grip is never quite the same.

techniques.name: Staff Across the Chest
techniques.desc: Both hands on the staff, held crosswise, and you drive him back off his feet with it.

techniques.name: A Stone Before the Staff
techniques.desc: A sling stone off his helmet as he comes up the stair, so that he arrives at your staff with his ears ringing.

techniques.name: Pin the Arms
techniques.desc: The staff goes across his elbows and pins them to his body; whatever he held is on the ground.

techniques.name: Bound in Yak Hair
techniques.desc: Down, a knee on him, the rope around his wrists: another armed man walked down the Stair alive and bound.

maneuver.name: Staff Binding
maneuver.desc: Guards in threes pin an armed man's arms and legs with iron-shod staves and bind him with yak-hair rope; whole files take a band of raiders without a death.

ST27-02.name: The Roof Sling
ST27-02.origin: Every herder child on the Roof learns the sling with the yaks, and in danger every herder family sends a man with sling and staff to the levy. Dorje Stonesling, captain of the Bluewater circuit wardens, learned his sling from Nima of the Still Hands and teaches it at Starspire to the wardens who keep the 280 km pilgrim circuit. A stone of 30 to 60 grams breaks bones through padding and stuns through a helmet, and every warden knows how thin the line is between stopping a man and killing him.
ST27-02.philosophy: Stop him at a hundred paces with a stone, and he never reaches your staff.
ST27-02.strengths: Range, stunning, ridges and ledges, the rope snare.
ST27-02.weakness: Mail and shields shrug off stones and a man who closes fast finds a herder with a stick; and it is the one art of the Roof in which a stone thrown too well kills.

techniques.name: Stone at the Herd's Edge
techniques.desc: The same cast that turns a straying yak, aimed at a man instead.

techniques.name: Rope Across the Ledge
techniques.desc: The yak-hair rope you laid across the path comes taut at his shins as he steps onto the ledge.

techniques.name: The Loaded Sling Close In
techniques.desc: Too close to cast, you swing the loaded pouch like a flail into the side of his head.

techniques.name: Above Him on the Ridge
techniques.desc: You keep the higher ground on the scree, and every step he takes up toward you is answered.

techniques.name: The Stone That Stops
techniques.desc: A river stone at a hundred paces, thrown to drop him and not to kill him; only a master can be sure which it will be.

maneuver.name: Sling Volley
maneuver.desc: Slingers on the ridge hurl stones and baked-clay bullets at 100 to 200 m into a column in a narrow valley; bones break through padding and men drop stunned.

ST27-03.name: The Still Hands
ST27-03.origin: Abbot Sherab founded the Hall of Still Hands in 768, the year after the Stair Guard killed three Moonstair robbers, to give the Guard a way to stop a man without killing him. Twelve masters refined the staff, the throw and the hold; the twelfth, Brother Dawa the Quiet, took Nima in at twelve in 1061 and taught him for 25 years. Nima, the thirteenth, has disarmed about 400 armed men and killed none, and on the Bluespire road in 1094 he bound six robbers one after another, the last two with one good hand.
ST27-03.philosophy: Stand still, let him move first, take the wrist and not the weapon: the weapon falls on its own.
ST27-03.strengths: Calm, disarming, throws and holds, ending a fight without a death.
ST27-03.weakness: It never kills: a man who would rather die than be held, a crossbow at 60 m, or three spears at once are problems it has not solved.

techniques.name: Let Him Move First
techniques.desc: Staff low, breath slow. You are the only person in the room who is not frightened, so you see him decide.

techniques.name: Take the Wrist
techniques.desc: The staff takes the wrist, not the weapon. The weapon falls on its own.

techniques.name: The Throw
techniques.desc: Inside the arc of his weapon, hip against hip, and he goes over onto the stones.

techniques.name: Go Down With Him
techniques.desc: When it goes wrong you take him to the ground and hold, because the man always tires before you do.

techniques.name: Knee on the Shoulder
techniques.desc: Your knee settles on his shoulder joint and all the fight goes out of the arm beneath it.

techniques.name: Rope Around the Thumbs
techniques.desc: Nima's fifteen seconds: the throw, the knee, the yak-hair loop round both thumbs, and an armed man lies bound and alive.

maneuver.name: Rope Snare
maneuver.desc: Yak-hair ropes laid across a ledge are pulled taut to trip men and horses, and the brothers bind whoever falls; nobody dies, and nobody passes.

ST27-04.name: Where Others Gasp
ST27-04.origin: In January 650 Abbot Norden, a son of the household, led twelve monks over the Zardeep Pass in deep winter and brought 46 people out of a snowbound caravan, and his brother Dondrub's household took the name Snowborn the next year. For four centuries they have sent their boys to the highest camps at eight and hired them out as guides to pilgrims, salt caravans and dwarven prospectors. In 1105 Tsering Snowborn captains the Stair Guard, Jigme the Snowborn Guides, and the elder Pasang once carried a Drevnan merchant down from 5,400 m on his back.
ST27-04.philosophy: Never fight him where he can breathe: climb, wait, and let the height take his legs before you take his footing.
ST27-04.strengths: Thin air, endurance, footing on ice and scree, wearing out lowlanders.
ST27-04.weakness: The art is the mountain: below the snow line, on a warm plain, a Snowborn is a short herder with a staff, and the family trades on a story of special lungs that is not true.

techniques.name: Climb, Then Wait
techniques.desc: You go up a little and stop, and make him come up after you into air that does not feed him.

techniques.name: Loose Stone Underfoot
techniques.desc: You know which stones on the path roll. You step aside, and he steps on one.

techniques.name: The Thin Air
techniques.desc: His head aches, his breath will not come, and every exchange costs him what it costs you on a valley floor.

techniques.name: The Guide's Rope
techniques.desc: The coil that ties a caravan together on a col goes round his legs, and you pull.

techniques.name: Norden's Crossing
techniques.desc: What brought twelve monks over the Zardeep in deep winter: you keep going, steady and warm, long after he has stopped.

maneuver.name: Thin-Air Retreat
maneuver.desc: The Guides fall back uphill above 3,000 m, where lowlanders sicken within a day or two, cut the supply road behind them and wait.

ST27-05.name: Bind, Do Not Break
ST27-05.origin: Dorje of the stone tents was among the first file-leaders of the Stair Guard in 722, and a Stonetent guard was one of those who killed the three Moonstair robbers in 767, the shame that made the Hall of Still Hands. Since then the household has trained there more faithfully than any other, and no Stonetent son carries a staff until he passes the Hall's test. In November 1104 its file-leader was told that his company will carry the Steward's Chanari blades.
ST27-05.philosophy: A Stonetent fights to bring the man home alive, and carries the rope for it.
ST27-05.strengths: Rope work, entangling and binding, leading a file, refusing to be provoked.
ST27-05.weakness: The rope needs room and time: a blade through the coil, a fast man in a narrow place or a fighter who will die before he is bound defeats it, and the family's vow now sits beside forty Chanari blades.

techniques.name: Coil in the Left Hand
techniques.desc: The thick coil of yak hair on your left forearm takes his first cut and holds the blade a moment too long.

techniques.name: The Weighted Cast
techniques.desc: The rope's stone-weighted end flies low and wraps his legs, and he fights the rest of the bout half-hobbled.

techniques.name: Three on One
techniques.desc: The file-leader's drill done alone: staff to the arm, rope to the leg, and your weight on the third thing he needs.

techniques.name: Bound Before He Knows
techniques.desc: One loop at the ankles, one at the wrists, pulled together while he is still trying to stand.

techniques.name: The Blade Not Drawn
techniques.desc: The Stonetent answer to the forty Chanari blades: win it without drawing one, and bring him home alive.

ST28-01.name: The Living Wall
ST28-01.origin: The Gate Wardens of Kelfast have taught the Living Wall since the hold was opened about 100 BR: one dwarf, one shield, one passage, for as long as it takes. Eyvind Graywall learned it from Shield Elder Audun Flatshield and held a broken gallery alone for a quarter of an hour at the siege of Kelfast in 1002 while the sappers flooded the mine behind him. As Shield Elder he has taught every one of the 2,400 Gate Wardens of the last sixty years, Crown Prince Hrodgar among them.
ST28-01.philosophy: In the first second do nothing but set your feet; strike only when his weight is on your shield.
ST28-01.strengths: Holding a passage two meters wide against anyone alive; outlasting a column; the pick over the rim.
ST28-01.weakness: Open ground, horse archers, a crossbow on the wall above and water: off its passage a Gate Warden is a slow dwarf with a shield.

school.name: The Gate Wardens' Hall of Kelfast

techniques.name: Set the Feet
techniques.desc: The first second belongs to the feet; the shield covers knee to eyes and nothing else moves.

techniques.name: Weight on the Shield
techniques.desc: Strike only when he has leaned on the shield; then the pick comes over the rim.

techniques.name: One Knee for the Second Shield
techniques.desc: When the shield lifts, go to one knee and let the warden behind you come over the top.

techniques.name: Pick Over the Rim
techniques.desc: His shield is busy with yours; the war-pick goes over both rims into his helmet.

techniques.name: A Quarter of an Hour
techniques.desc: Kelfast, 1002: one shield in a broken gallery until the water came. He tires before you do.

maneuver.name: The Living Wall
maneuver.desc: One warden, one shield, one passage: the wardens hold a gallery or gap two meters wide and swap the front shield before it tires.

ST28-02.name: Hook and Pull
ST28-02.origin: The axe of the Mormund gate teaches hooking before cutting: the beard of the axe takes a shield rim or an ankle and the cut comes on the pull. Skeggi Rockcleaver taught it to his son Torvald, who stepped aside from five Ranpuri war elephants at Tiravi in 1083 and cut the cord above each heel, and in 1086 raised the Axe Hall of Mormund from the axemen who had lived through that day. Every adult of the hold trains with the axe; the Axe Hall's 600 train with nothing else.
ST28-02.philosophy: Go low and to the right, hook the rim or the ankle, and cut on the pull; keep moving, as a Gate Warden does not.
ST28-02.strengths: Hooking shields and ankles; laming horses and beasts; broken ground; an axe swung for an hour.
ST28-02.weakness: Flat open ground against horse, and a hot temper: it commits, and a lance or a crossbow on the far slope punishes that.

techniques.name: Hook the Rim
techniques.desc: The beard of the axe takes his shield rim and pulls it out of the way.

techniques.name: Cut on the Pull
techniques.desc: Hook first, then draw the edge back toward you; the pull does the cutting.

techniques.name: Low and to the Right
techniques.desc: Go under his shield side, take the ankle with the beard, and keep moving.

techniques.name: The Heel Cord
techniques.desc: Stand still for the last two strides, step to the side the driver cannot see, and the leg folds.

techniques.name: Five Elephants
techniques.desc: Five at Tiravi in one morning:the beard takes the cord, the leg folds, and the next is already coming.

maneuver.name: Heel-Cutters
maneuver.desc: Axemen wait among pits and stones, let beasts and riders come to the last strides, then step aside and cut legs.

ST28-03.name: The Listening Stone
ST28-03.origin: Stonehold has dug against every mine laid under its walls since Thargard in 611, and the Hall of Counter-Mines at Kelfast teaches listening through stone. Gisla Deepdelve ran it at the siege of 1002, when two Tessarian tunnels were flooded, and taught her son Ulf, who knifed Tessarian miners in a broken gallery that year and lost his left ear and the third race under the Dwarf's Gate in 1084. Ulf hears a pick through 60 m of rock.
ST28-03.philosophy: Hear him first, drive your gallery to within two meters of his, then break in: smoke first, knives after.
ST28-03.strengths: Hearing through rock; fighting in galleries a meter wide; smoke and the knife in the dark.
ST28-03.weakness: It strikes no blows in the open; under the sun a counter-miner is a short, slow dwarf with a knife.

techniques.name: Peas on the Drumskin
techniques.desc: Dry peas jump on a drumskin when a pick strikes far off; learn to feel the floor the same way.

techniques.name: The Hooded Lamp
techniques.desc: Open the hood in his face and shut it again; he is blind for the one breath that matters.

techniques.name: Break In
techniques.desc: The last hand's breadth of rock goes, the smoke goes in, and the knives follow it.

techniques.name: Within Two Meters
techniques.desc: Drive your gallery to within a body's length of his and wait for him to break into yours.

maneuver.name: Counter-Mining
maneuver.desc: Listeners find the enemy mine by rippling water and jumping peas, dig to meet it and break in with smoke and knives.

ST28-04.name: The Mormund Block
ST28-04.origin: The Pike Hall of Mormund goes back to the Worldspine Toll War of the 600s, when Stonehold won the Zardeep tolls, and it teaches the pike block in a pass. Brenna Ironbrow, sister of the Toll-Warden Kettil, led a block at Tiravi in 1083, where sixty war elephants stopped on pits, caltrops and pikes, and has mastered the Hall since 1087. She counts the cadence aloud and has no patience for slow feet.
ST28-04.philosophy: Fill the pass from wall to wall, count the step aloud, and let nothing with legs reach the second rank.
ST28-04.strengths: Stopping horse and elephants in a pass; cadence and drill; a block that moves as one.
ST28-04.weakness: It needs walls on both sides: on a plain it can be ridden around, and it turns badly.

techniques.name: On the Count
techniques.desc: Step when the count says step, and not before; tired feet are slow feet.

techniques.name: Points at the Knee
techniques.desc: Points low at the elephant's knee and the horse's chest; the charge does the work.

techniques.name: Step and Thrust
techniques.desc: One step and one thrust, the whole block together, on the master's shout.

techniques.name: The Tiravi Block
techniques.desc: What stopped sixty elephants: the block holds, the points go in, and the beast in front stops the beasts behind.

maneuver.name: Pike Block in the Pass
maneuver.desc: A pike block fills the pass wall to wall on the master's count; horse and elephants stop on the points or turn back into their own column.

ST28-05.name: The Crown Shelf
ST28-05.origin: Brom Bardun climbed above every other dwarf to the Crown Shelf at about 7,000 m, and every Bardun heir since has carried an ingot up to it before the Eldest Carver cuts the new name. The line's Summit Breath lets carriers work and fight where other dwarves gasp, and the eighty Bardun cousins and guides of the Crown Shelf Guard fight on the ice above 6,000 m. They teach their own blood the pick on ice, the rope, and the thin air as a weapon.
ST28-05.philosophy: Fight uphill and higher than he can breathe; let the mountain tire him, then the pick.
ST28-05.strengths: Fighting on ice and steep ground; breath that never fails at height; outlasting lowlanders.
ST28-05.weakness: A Bardun sickens below 1,000 m within weeks, so low, hot or flat country takes the edge away, and the climb itself has killed heirs.

techniques.name: Thin Air
techniques.desc: Draw him upward; at height the lowlander's own breath fights on your side.

techniques.name: Ice-Pick
techniques.desc: The pick that bites blue ice bites a boot and a shin as easily.

techniques.name: Never Out of Breath
techniques.desc: A Bardun does not gasp below the snow line; stand, breathe, and watch him gasp.

techniques.name: From Above
techniques.desc: Every fight on the mountain is won by the one standing higher.

ST28-06.name: The Dust Gallery
ST28-06.origin: Old Hald Stonelung cut rock in the dustiest headings for a century and never coughed, and he could smell almost nothing; in 812 his partner died in a pocket of bad air Hald walked through without noticing. His clan carries the Dust-Proof Lungs and heads the mine-masters of Stonehold and Emberdeep. Grimbald Stonelung, war leader of the Hall Council, stopped Ranpur's elephants at Tiravi by spending a week digging the valley first, and the clan teaches its blood to fight in dust that chokes other dwarves and on ground it has shaped itself.
ST28-06.philosophy: Choose the ground a week before the fight, raise the dust, and fight where only you can breathe.
ST28-06.strengths: Fighting in dust and broken galleries; prepared ground; pike and pick from the second rank.
ST28-06.weakness: They cannot smell gas: a caged finch and a partner's nose go with them, and gas has killed 31 kin; on a plain they are slow old dwarves.

techniques.name: Raise the Dust
techniques.desc: A kicked spoil-heap fills the gallery; he coughs and you do not.

techniques.name: From the Second Rank
techniques.desc: Grimbald fights in the second rank, the pike over a shoulder, where he can see the ground.

techniques.name: Dug a Week Before
techniques.desc: Every pit and stake is where you put it; he is fighting your ground and does not know it yet.

techniques.name: Through the Cloud
techniques.desc: Out of the dust he cannot see through, the pick that he never saw coming.

ST28-07.name: The Dragon Windlass
ST28-07.origin: The Boltcarvers made the first heavy windlass crossbows of Stonehold about 600, and King Orm III put a Boltcarver over the crossbow galleries above the First Hall's gate; the clan has held them since with 400 crossbows that put a bolt through a breastplate at 150 m. Two of the clan's sons marched with Ostra's gold expedition of 1097 and tore the Red Widow's wing on the upper Tirana, and one came home. The clan believes a big enough bolt can kill a dragon, and it has been building one.
ST28-07.philosophy: Wind it, aim it, wait: the shot you take late is the one that goes through.
ST28-07.strengths: The heaviest bolts in the world; breastplates at 150 m; patience on a wall.
ST28-07.weakness: The slowest shot of all: a minute to wind, and anything that closes while the windlass turns has the dwarf.
ranks: Captain of the First Hall Crossbows

techniques.name: Aim and Wait
techniques.desc: The clan's words: wind it, aim it, wait. Most men shoot too soon.

techniques.name: Behind the Loophole
techniques.desc: The stone takes his answer while you are already turning the crank.

techniques.name: A Hundred and Fifty Meters
techniques.desc: The distance at which a First Hall bolt still goes through a breastplate.

techniques.name: The Wing-Tearer
techniques.desc: A bolt built for the Red Widow, heavier than one dwarf can wind; what it does not kill, it knocks down.

ST28-08.name: The Horn-File
ST28-08.origin: The Gate Wardens fight in passages too dark and too loud for shouted orders, and since the siege of Thargard in 611 the Hornhelms have carried their horns: one blast to brace, two to swap shields, three to give ground, and the long note that shuts a door. A Hornhelm stands in every company of the line. In August 1084 Hrefna Hornhelm sounded the long note that shut the inner door of the Dwarf's Gate on the last forty of the rear guard, and she has not blown a horn since.
ST28-08.philosophy: The horn thinks for the line: brace on one, swap on two, give ground on three, and on the long note the door shuts, whoever is behind it.
ST28-08.strengths: Timing, rotation and discipline in the dark; keeping a line fresh; knowing when to give ground.
ST28-08.weakness: A signaller, not a champion: alone, with no line to answer the horn, a Hornhelm is a soldier with a shield and a heavy conscience.

techniques.name: One Blast: Brace
techniques.desc: Every warden in the line sets his feet on the same note.

techniques.name: Two Blasts: Swap
techniques.desc: The tired shield steps back and a fresh one steps in, without a gap and without a word.

techniques.name: Three Blasts: Give Ground
techniques.desc: The line steps back together; he comes on alone into the points.

techniques.name: The Long Note
techniques.desc: The note that shuts a door: everything forward of it is shoved out, and the door closes.

maneuver.name: Horn Signals
maneuver.desc: Horn-bearers call brace, swap and give ground in the dark; the line rotates fresh shields to the front without a word shouted.

ST29-01.name: The Tharmund Turn
ST29-01.origin: Dagna cut Tharmund Gate about 430 at 2,673 m on the one road up from the Gundgard valleys, and since Forge-Queen Ragna's day every dwarf of Emberdeep serves five-year turns in the 1,600 Gate Shields. The turns are drilled by the Granitejaw sergeants, who have stood in the gate longest and have shouted the shield-wall into every thane, smith and carver now living, the Forge-Princess among them. Water from the hot springs is piped to the gate to pour on anyone below it.
ST29-01.philosophy: Five years, one wall: lock rims, give the dwarf beside you your shield's edge, and let the hot water do the rest.
ST29-01.strengths: Shield-wall drill; holding the road and the gate; a steadiness every dwarf of the hold has learned in turn.
ST29-01.weakness: A conscript's art: solid rather than brilliant, built to stand in one gate and not to march.

techniques.name: Lock Rims
techniques.desc: Your rim over his, his over the next; one shield is a board, sixty are a wall.

techniques.name: Shove
techniques.desc: Boss forward, shoulder behind it, and the whole file moves one step on the sergeant's word.

techniques.name: Spear Over the Wall
techniques.desc: The second rank thrusts over the first rank's rims while he is busy with the shields.

techniques.name: The Sergeant's Voice
techniques.desc: Every dwarf of Emberdeep remembers being shouted at by a Granitejaw, and in a fight the voice still holds the feet.

techniques.name: Water From the Hoardings
techniques.desc: Give one step back under the murder holes, and let the spring water fall on whoever follows.

maneuver.name: Scalding Gate
maneuver.desc: The Gate Shields lock rims in the gateway while hot spring water and sand pour from the hoardings onto anyone pressing them.

ST29-02.name: The Hot Gallery
ST29-02.origin: Emberdeep lives inside a hot mountain and fights its tunnel war in galleries already too warm for anyone else: shield-files three wide, drop-stones every 50 m, and air shafts closed or fired to smoke the attacker. Since the steam burst of February 1050 killed Forge-Queen Ragna and 23 smiths, every young dwarf of the Breath Halls also learns to read the sweat on the walls. The works guard under Vigga Blackpick teaches the short pick and the short spear for that heat.
ST29-02.philosophy: Fight where it is hot and close: the heat tires him first, and the shaft you shut chokes him second.
ST29-02.strengths: Tunnel fighting in heat and smoke; short weapons; endurance where others wilt.
ST29-02.weakness: Out of its galleries it has no special answer, and the heat it uses may one day be the thing that kills the hold.

school.name: The Stair Yard of the Breath Halls

techniques.name: Short Pick
techniques.desc: A haft no longer than a forearm, for a gallery where nothing longer swings.

techniques.name: Shut the Shaft
techniques.desc: Close the air shaft behind him; in that heat, he will be gasping in a minute.

techniques.name: Drop-Stone
techniques.desc: Every fifty meters a stone hangs over the gallery; pull the pin as he passes under it.

techniques.name: Sweat on the Walls
techniques.desc: Read the rock as the Stair Watch does, and the man in front of you is easier to read.

techniques.name: Three Wide
techniques.desc: A shield-file of three blocks the gallery while picks and short spears strike past it.

maneuver.name: Tunnel Holding
maneuver.desc: A shield-file of three blocks a hot gallery while picks and spears strike past it, with drop-stones and closed shafts behind; nobody takes a tunnel the hold means to keep.

ST29-03.name: The Breath Hall Hammer
ST29-03.origin: The Hall of the Hammer teaches the great hammer and the war-pick to the 400 of the Hammer Guard, who stand in the Breath Halls around the Forge Crown, and its chain runs back to the smiths who walked the exile road with Dagna in 398. Its master Rolf Hammerhand, the Forge-Queen's nephew, has the full hammer arms of his clan and won the Guard's champion's place in 1088 by breaking an iron-bound door with three blows. He teaches tunnel fighting with pick and hammer as if every problem could be hammered flat.
ST29-03.philosophy: Break what is in front of you: the shield, then the arm, then the door behind them.
ST29-03.strengths: Breaking shields and doors; picks that go through plate; raw power in a tunnel.
ST29-03.weakness: Heavy, slow and hungry: it spends its strength fast, and its own master's heart has already stumbled twice.

techniques.name: Shield-Breaker
techniques.desc: The hammer goes at the shield itself, until there is no shield.

techniques.name: Pick Through the Plate
techniques.desc: The war-pick is a hammer with one idea: a hole in the breastplate.

techniques.name: Haft Check
techniques.desc: The long haft stops his blow near the hands, and the head comes round behind it.

techniques.name: Three Blows
techniques.desc: Rolf broke an iron-bound door in three; a shield does not last that long.

maneuver.name: Hammer Guard Assault
maneuver.desc: The Hammer Guard goes into a gallery or a breach behind its champions, breaking shields and doors before the files behind them follow.

ST29-04.name: The Dragon Watch Crossbow
ST29-04.origin: After Durek Hammerhand's party stole two dragon eggs in 612 and died on the Gundgard road, Forge-King Harl founded the Kardeep Dragon Watch, and its crossbows have been aimed at the sky above the gold mines at 4,773 m ever since. The Bolt Yard teaches the steel crossbow spanned with a lever and the heavy engines on the heights. Its master Inga Crag drove the Ash Dragon off an ore train in 1074 and captains the 300 of the Watch.
ST29-04.philosophy: Wind, angle, wait: talk about the wind, not the beast, and put the bolt where the wing will be.
ST29-04.strengths: The steel crossbow through a shield; long shots upward and in wind; engines on a height.
ST29-04.weakness: One bolt a minute and a long time spanning; close up, or caught on the road, it has nothing.

techniques.name: Lever and Steel
techniques.desc: A steel bow spanned with a lever: slow, and it goes through what it hits.

techniques.name: Read the Wind
techniques.desc: At 4,773 m the wind decides every shot; learn it, and you learn where things are going.

techniques.name: Through the Shield
techniques.desc: The dwarven steel crossbow does not care what the shield is made of.

techniques.name: Where the Wing Will Be
techniques.desc: The shot the Watch drills for its whole life and does not speak of loosing.

maneuver.name: Dragon Watch Engines
maneuver.desc: Steel crossbows and engines on the heights shoot down into the road and up into the sky; whatever comes in range comes under bolts that go through shields.

ST29-05.name: Dagna's Blow
ST29-05.origin: Dagna Hammerhand, born in 340 with the full hammer arms, struck the mine-master Thrand Bardun once with a forge hammer in 398, meaning to break his arm, and broke his skull; the Carvers exiled her whole clan, and she founded Emberdeep. No child of the line inherits who cannot lift her 90 kg anvil above the head at the Kindling, and the clan marries carriers to keep the arms. It teaches its own a way of fighting built on one blow that ends things, and on knowing what that blow once cost.
ST29-05.philosophy: One blow, and mean it: lift it or leave it.
ST29-05.strengths: Shoulders and arms half again a dwarf's: crushing single blows, broken arms and shields, a man lifted off his feet.
ST29-05.weakness: Short legs that cannot keep up on a march, and the clan's heart: Dagna died of it, and Rolf's has stumbled twice.

techniques.name: The Lift
techniques.desc: Arms that raise a 90 kg anvil overhead raise a man off the floor.

techniques.name: Break the Arm
techniques.desc: Dagna meant only to break Thrand's arm. The clan still teaches the blow, and what it cost.

techniques.name: The Anvil Stroke
techniques.desc: The forge blow, from over the head, with everything the shoulders have.

techniques.name: Wait for the Heart
techniques.desc: Stop, breathe, let the heart settle: the clan has buried twenty-two who would not.

ST29-06.name: The Barbed Head
ST29-06.origin: The first bolt-sergeant Forge-King Harl named to the Dragon Watch was a Skybolt who had seen Durek's party fall from the gorge road, and the clan has crewed the Watch's heavy crossbows above Kardeep ever since. Its bolt yard forges the barbed heads that tear a wing membrane, and a Skybolt crew wound the bow Inga Crag shot in 1074. The clan is proud of the most dangerous post in the hold, and since November 1104 it has slept badly.
ST29-06.philosophy: Aim for the wing: whatever cannot fly or run can be finished with the axe.
ST29-06.strengths: Barbed bolts that tear and bleed; fast crew loading; finishing whatever falls.
ST29-06.weakness: Stiff necks from a life of watching the sky, and a crew art: one Skybolt alone shoots as slowly as anyone.

techniques.name: Barbed Bolt
techniques.desc: A head forged to tear going in and tear worse coming out.

techniques.name: Loader's Hand
techniques.desc: The crew passes up a wound bow; the shooter never takes his eyes off the sky.

techniques.name: Aim for the Wing
techniques.desc: Not the heart or the head: the thing it moves with. Dragon or man, it comes down.

techniques.name: When It Lands
techniques.desc: The hand-axe for whatever the bolt brought down and did not kill.

ST30-01.name: The Paddy Spear
ST30-01.origin: Every delta village has sent spearmen to the Raja's dry-season wars since the Mitra rajas, and after the Sagar raised the dykes again in 588 the drill was built around the dyke-top, where the enemy must wade to reach you. The 28,000 Paddy Spears are soldier-farmers called after the rice harvest and never in the monsoon; thousands of them died on the Girvan terraces at Tiravi in 1083.
ST30-01.philosophy: Hold the bank, keep the point long and low, and let the enemy come up out of the mud to you.
ST30-01.strengths: reach, holding a dyke, ford or terrace, cheap and steady in numbers
ST30-01.weakness: stiff and slow off the dyke; a quick swordsman inside the point, or a man in good mail, finds the cotton coats and bamboo shields thin

techniques.name: Point from the Dyke
techniques.desc: From the high bank the spear reaches down; the man in the mud is hit before he can lift his feet.

techniques.name: Mud Step
techniques.desc: Give a step back along the dyke, let him slide into the soft edge, and put the point into his leg as he struggles.

techniques.name: Harvest Rush
techniques.desc: The whole file goes down the bank at a run, shouting, the way the village goes into the field when the rain is coming.

techniques.name: Ford Keeper
techniques.desc: Stand where the water is knee-deep in front of you and dry behind; every man who wades is met by the point first.

techniques.name: The Monsoon Thrust
techniques.desc: All the weight of a man who has carried rice sacks for twenty years, behind one point driven through a cotton coat and out the other side.

maneuver.name: Dyke-Top Line
maneuver.desc: Spearmen line a dyke or terrace wall three deep; horse and elephants must climb to them, and foot must wade.

ST30-02.name: The Lotus Bow
ST30-02.origin: Raja Jaidev Sagar gave the Lotus Banner to the archer Deepak Senapat in 590, and the royal archers who guard it grew into the Lotus Bows, 14,000 strong in 1105 and the largest bow corps of the east. They shoot cane bows in massed volleys on the conch, high and together, to break a line before the elephants go in.
ST30-02.philosophy: Shoot many, shoot together and shoot first, and let the Raja's elephants finish what the arrows began.
ST30-02.strengths: the first exchange, volleys, wounding and tiring a foe before he closes
ST30-02.weakness: light cane bows that slacken in wet weather and seldom go through good mail; little left once the enemy is close

techniques.name: Rain of Reeds
techniques.desc: The first arrows go up high, like the first drops of the monsoon, while the enemy is still far off.

techniques.name: Keep the Distance
techniques.desc: An archer does not stand to be hit: give ground across the open paddy and make him pay for every step he chases you.

techniques.name: Katar from the Sash
techniques.desc: When the enemy is through the arrows the bow drops, and the punch-dagger comes out of the sash low and fast.

techniques.name: The Lotus Opens
techniques.desc: Five arrows loosed in a breath from the fingers, a fan like the opening flower, the way the whole corps opens its volley.

techniques.name: The Mahout's Eye
techniques.desc: One arrow drawn to the ear and held for the gap in a helmet or the eye of an enemy driver: the shot the old bearers teach last.

maneuver.name: The Monsoon Volley
maneuver.desc: Thousands of cane bows loose together on the conch, high and dense, before the elephants and spears go in.

ST30-03.name: Khanda and Dhal
ST30-03.origin: The straight, heavy khanda and the round dhal came down from the hill lords whom Aditya the Hill-Taker brought under the crown in 338, when Chanari held out five months behind its walls. Their sons became the Lords' Shields, 6,000 heavy foot who stand in the Raja's second line; the Tirwala Shields have stood there in every dry-season war since the Sagar rajas.
ST30-03.philosophy: Shield up, chop down: the khanda breaks what the dhal has stopped.
ST30-03.strengths: solid in a line, heavy cuts that break shields and forearms, steady against spears that come one at a time
ST30-03.weakness: heavy and slow; a light quick blade or a good feint pulls the dhal wide, and the Shields tire fast in the heat

techniques.name: Dhal Punch
techniques.desc: The round shield is a fist: take his cut on the boss and drive the boss into his face.

techniques.name: The Falling Khanda
techniques.desc: A straight blade with its weight at the tip, brought down from above the head onto whatever he holds up.

techniques.name: Under the Rim
techniques.desc: Show the khanda high, then cut low under your own rim at the knee he forgot to cover.

techniques.name: Second Line Holds
techniques.desc: Stand in the second rank, breathe while the first rank bleeds, and give back the blow that reaches you.

techniques.name: Splitting the Dhal
techniques.desc: Two hands on the basket hilt and the whole body under it: the cut that cleaves a shield and the arm behind it.

maneuver.name: Shields of the Second Line
maneuver.desc: The Lords' Shields stand behind the spears and close every gap the first line opens.

ST30-04.name: The Tiger Beat
ST30-04.origin: The Baghmar and the hill folk of Chanari have beaten tigers out of the grass for five centuries, and when the Forest Beaters were raised their drums and gongs became army drill. Since Tiravi in 1083 the beaters walk ahead of the elephants with long poles to find pits, and in 1098 old Kalu Baghmar beat the drive that brought the Striped Death, a man-eater of about 200 people, under the Raja's bow.
ST30-04.philosophy: Never meet the tiger alone: make noise, make it move, and put it where the spears are waiting.
ST30-04.strengths: reading ground and men, wearing a foe down, finding traps, the javelin from cover
ST30-04.weakness: a hunter's courage, not a soldier's: poor in a straight fight against a steady armored man, and nothing without room to move

techniques.name: Gong and Shout
techniques.desc: Bang the gong, yell, make him turn his head; a beast that has been turned is half beaten.

techniques.name: Pole for the Pit
techniques.desc: Feel the ground ahead with the long pole and watch the man, not his blade: you learn where he means to step.

techniques.name: Javelin from the Grass
techniques.desc: Rise out of the elephant grass, throw at the legs, and drop again before he knows where it came from.

techniques.name: Give the Tiger a Gap
techniques.desc: Open the line and let him run for the gap, then turn him with the drums onto the crossbar of your boar spear.

techniques.name: The Striped Death's End
techniques.desc: Wait for the spring, ground the butt, and let the tiger, or the man, come onto the point under the breastbone.

maneuver.name: The Tiger Beat Drive
maneuver.desc: Lines of beaters with drums and gongs drive scattered enemies out of grass and forest onto waiting elephants and archers.

ST30-05.name: Goad and Howdah
ST30-05.origin: Bala Mallik the Catcher brought Raja Aditya Pratap 40 trained elephants in 338, and his house has trained the kingdom's war elephants ever since; the junior line keeps the School in the Elephant Hills at Nagita. After the staked pits of Tiravi in 1083, Master Bala Mallik rebuilt its training around noise, fire and hidden ground.
ST30-05.philosophy: Patience breaks the wild: the beast does the fighting, and the rider's whole art is keeping it calm, pointed and sure of its feet.
ST30-05.strengths: weight and terror from the howdah, shooting down over shields, breaking horse that never trained with elephants
ST30-05.weakness: pits, caltrops, fire and noise drive the beast mad, and a maddened elephant tramples its own side; on foot a mahout is a small man with a goad

techniques.name: A Word to the Beast
techniques.desc: A touch of the ankus behind the ear and a word the calf learned at ten: the beast stands, and so does its rider's nerve.

techniques.name: Howdah Shot
techniques.desc: From three metres up the archer shoots down over the shield rims at whoever is giving orders.

techniques.name: Trunk and Tusk
techniques.desc: The bull is set at one man, and the tusks do what no lance can; whoever is not trampled is thrown.

techniques.name: Still in the Fire
techniques.desc: Bala's drill since Tiravi: torches, drums and shouting until the beast no longer starts, so when the enemy tries it the howdah answers instead.

techniques.name: The Wave of Tusks
techniques.desc: Four tonnes at a run with the guards' spears beside the legs: nothing on foot stands in front of it twice.

maneuver.name: Screen of Tusks
maneuver.desc: Elephants stand at intervals in front of the foot; horses that never trained with them will not close, and the howdah archers shoot over the line.

ST30-06.name: The Chanari Draw-Cut
ST30-06.origin: The smith Harish Rane founded the Blade Hall of Chanari in 1003 when he saw that a crucible blade keeps its edge through a mail ring, and built a school on one cut. Ranes have mastered it since, smiths and swordsmen both; Kavi Rane trains the Steel Guard, and in 1098 a Spice Coast sellsword who drew on him at the smiths' gate died of one cut through the collar before his own blade was level.
ST30-06.philosophy: The sword stays in the scabbard until the cut, and the draw is the cut.
ST30-06.strengths: the fastest first strike of any human school; Chanari steel through mail at the collar and the wrist
ST30-06.weakness: one cut: if it misses, a good swordsman and nothing more is left; spears, shields, horses and anyone who stays outside two steps

techniques.name: Hand on the Hilt
techniques.desc: Walk in talking with the hand resting on the hilt, and watch where his eyes go when he sees it.

techniques.name: Wrist from the Sheath
techniques.desc: The short draw that opens the sword hand before it has closed on the hilt.

techniques.name: The Draw
techniques.desc: From the scabbard to the neck in a third of a second; the blade is drawn and the cut is made in one movement.

techniques.name: Off the Line to the Point
techniques.desc: If the first cut misses, step off the line and go to the point; the Hall drills the second answer because its master knows the first can fail.

techniques.name: Crucible Edge
techniques.desc: The master's draw, inside two steps: crucible steel that does not stop at the rings of a mail collar.

ST30-07.name: The Unpoisoned Stand
ST30-07.origin: The Ranavir were hill captains of Devesh for the Sagar rajas before they were kings, and Devendra took the throne in 998 by holding the palace with 3,000 soldiers.
