Every child of the house drinks the arsenic cup from the age of five and is taught to stand where other men fall; Indrajit learned it before he won the Nagora Pass and shot the Striped Death from an elephant's back in 1098.
ST30-07.philosophy: Take what comes, stand, and strike back while the other man is still waiting for you to fall.
ST30-07.strengths: staying power, nerve, a sword arm trained by the best masters a crown can buy
ST30-07.weakness: pride: a Ranavir commits to the charge he has decided on, as Indrajit did into the pits at Tiravi, and a patient foe who refuses the fight wins

techniques.name: Drink and Stand
techniques.desc: Swallow the pain the way the house swallows the cup at the Festival of Lamps, and do not sit down.

techniques.name: Hill Captain's Cut
techniques.desc: A plain, heavy cut down the line, taught in Devesh when the house were captains and not kings.

techniques.name: From the Elephant's Back
techniques.desc: The shot that killed the Striped Death: wait until the beaters have done their work, then loose once and do not hurry it.

techniques.name: Hold the Palace
techniques.desc: Devendra held the palace in 998 with his back to the doors; the house teaches its sons to fight best with nowhere left to go.

techniques.name: Into the Pass
techniques.desc: Indrajit's way at Nagora: decide, then go in with everything. It won a pass, and at Tiravi it lost an army.

ST30-08.name: The Nagora Road Guard
ST30-08.origin: Raja Tej III Sagar gave Tirpur fort to Suresh Nagar in 971, after Tessarian surveyors mapped the Nagora mule road and marked its forts, and the Nagar have kept the road since. Vasu Nagar built the road forts and died at Tiravi; his son Rohan, Warden of the Nagora March, came out of the dust when the Dwarf's Gate tower fell in 1084 and learned from the dwarves that a crossbow behind a wall beats a brave man in front of one.
ST30-08.philosophy: Hold the gate, make them come up the road to you, and shoot the first man who does.
ST30-08.strengths: bolts that go through mail at close range, patient gate-keeping, fighting from behind a wall
ST30-08.weakness: slow to span and slower to chase; a road-fort soldier caught in the open without his wall is half a soldier

techniques.name: Bolt at the Gate
techniques.desc: Spanned and waiting on the gate tower: the first man up the road takes a bolt through his mail.

techniques.name: Shut the Gate
techniques.desc: Shield across the gap, spear over it; whoever pushes at the gate is pushing onto a point.

techniques.name: The Toll-Keeper's Eye
techniques.desc: Read the man at the gate like a carter's load: what he shows you, and what he has hidden under the sacks.

techniques.name: Breach of the Dwarf's Gate
techniques.desc: When the tower comes down, go into the dust and the broken stone at once and hit whatever is still standing.

ST30-09.name: Behind the Chair
ST30-09.origin: Raja Devraj raised the Steel Guard in 1046 with Chanari blades and gave its captaincy to Arun Sodhi, a hill soldier who had tasted his father's cup for twenty years. Every Sodhi son trains at the Blade Hall and then unlearns half of it behind the Raja's chair; Captain Veer Sodhi, who held the palace gate in the riots of 1104, has begun to take the first touch from Kavi Rane himself.
ST30-09.philosophy: The man behind the chair does not need to win, only to stand between the blade and the Raja until the blade is gone.
ST30-09.strengths: interposing, reading an assassin's hands, answering the draw-cut, steel that does not break
ST30-09.weakness: a guard does not chase or press; draw him away from his charge and he is torn in two, and a crowd of plain men wears him down

techniques.name: Taste the Cup
techniques.desc: Watch hands, not faces; a Sodhi learns the poisoner's shrug before he learns the sword.

techniques.name: Shield Across the Chair
techniques.desc: Step in front of the one you guard with the shield high, and cut past its edge at whoever struck.

techniques.name: Answer to the Draw
techniques.desc: Veer Sodhi's secret: let the draw-cut come, take it on the steel near your hilt, and cut the drawing wrist.

techniques.name: The Gate in the Riots
techniques.desc: Hold, breathe, cut whoever comes through, and never step out after the next one: the palace gate of 1104.

ST30-10.name: The Lotus Banner
ST30-10.origin: Raja Jaidev Sagar gave the Lotus Banner to the archer Deepak Senapat in 590, and his sons have carried it for three dynasties, lowering it only once, to Devendra Ranavir in the palace courtyard in 998. At Tiravi in 1083 the banner stood while the elephants broke around it, and Bhanu Senapat took it from his wounded father and walked it backward out of the rout.
ST30-10.philosophy: Wherever the banner stands is the front, and the bearer fights with the pole in one hand and never turns his back.
ST30-10.strengths: holding one spot, rallying the men around it, fighting while giving ground in good order
ST30-10.weakness: one hand on the pole: stiff, proud and easy to find, since every archer on the field aims at the banner

techniques.name: Pole Butt
techniques.desc: The bronze-shod foot of the banner pole, swung short into the shins of the man who reaches for the silk.

techniques.name: Walk It Backward
techniques.desc: Step back, face front, step back: Bhanu's walk out of Tiravi, giving ground without giving up the fight.

techniques.name: Bow Under the Banner
techniques.desc: The banner guard are archers first: they shoot the men who come for the silk before they arrive.

techniques.name: The Banner Does Not Fall
techniques.desc: The house words, in a fight: plant the pole, take the wound, and kill the man who gave it while the silk still flies.

maneuver.name: Rally on the Lotus
maneuver.desc: The banner stands and the Lotus Bows close around it; men who were running see it and stop.

ST30-11.name: The Catcher's Rope
ST30-11.origin: The Mallik caught wild elephants in the hills around Nagita long before those hills were Ranpur's, and their chief Bala the Catcher brought Raja Aditya Pratap 40 trained beasts in 338 and was made Master of Elephants. The senior line still takes about 60 wild elephants a year with ropes, pits and patience; Hari Mallik caught his first at 15 and rode a howdah at Tiravi.
ST30-11.philosophy: Patience breaks the wild: tire it, rope it and take it alive, because a dead elephant is worth nothing.
ST30-11.strengths: patience, rope work, taking a foe alive, nerve among big beasts and big men
ST30-11.weakness: a catcher's patience is slow; a man who is not afraid, does not tire and comes straight in with steel gives the rope no time

techniques.name: Patience Breaks the Wild
techniques.desc: Let him charge, step aside, let him charge again; the catchers walk a wild bull for a day before they touch him.

techniques.name: Leg Noose
techniques.desc: A loop of coir rope round the ankle and a turn round anything that will hold; the leg stops, and the rest must follow.

techniques.name: The Goad Behind the Ear
techniques.desc: The hooked ankus finds the soft place behind the ear that a mahout knows on every beast, and on every man.

techniques.name: Take It Alive
techniques.desc: When he is tired and roped, put him down and sit on him: the house has never sold a dead elephant, nor a dead prisoner.

ST31-01.name: The Breach Spear of Tessar
ST31-01.origin: The Crown Spearmen of Tessar learned their trade on the old walls: through the siege of 1064 and 1065 Sergeant Aldo Corradi held the North Gate breach for nine days until Silas Vane's engine smashed the prince's towers, and the queen made his post hereditary. The yard at the North Gate drills the set spear line and the breach, three points for every man who tries the gap.
ST31-01.philosophy: The wall is us: plant the butt, close the gap with shields and points, and let nobody through who has not paid for every step.
ST31-01.strengths: holding a breach or a gate, setting spears against horse, stubborn morale on home ground
ST31-01.weakness: hungry, ill-paid men who fight well only where they stand; on the march or in the open they are slow, and a crossbow volley before contact hurts them badly

school.name: The North Gate Yard of Tessar

techniques.name: Plant the Butt
techniques.desc: Heel against the butt, point up: the first thing a man meets in the gap is iron.

techniques.name: Rim to Rim
techniques.desc: Lock your rim to your neighbor's, take the blow on both, and thrust under the join.

techniques.name: Nine Days
techniques.desc: The breach was held nine days by men who slept standing: breathe behind the shield and be there again tomorrow.

techniques.name: Three Points to One Man
techniques.desc: The second and third ranks thrust past the first, so the man in the gap meets three spearheads before he reaches a shield.

techniques.name: The Wall Is Us
techniques.desc: The family words of the North Gate: take the charge on the planted spear, throw him back into the rubble, and step into his place.

maneuver.name: Set Spear Line
maneuver.desc: Spearmen kneel in the gap and set their butts in the ground, points at the horses' chests; the charge spits itself on its own weight.

ST31-02.name: The Calossa Bolt
ST31-02.origin: Crossbow sergeants have trained the north since Radoslav the Bear stopped Cassian Reed at Lake Ostec in 957 and the lords of Calossa were paid to guard the new border. The Tirabelli make the bows in a Feleria workshop and teach their sons to span them at ten, and the Calossa Crossbows are the only men Prince Andros pays in coin, struck at his own mint.
ST31-02.philosophy: Paid bolts fly straight: find a stream or a ditch, make them wade, and shoot them while they cannot answer.
ST31-02.strengths: volleys from behind water and ditches, killing knights in mail at 60 metres, discipline while the pay comes
ST31-02.weakness: two shots a minute and a soldier who fights for pay: caught in the open by horse, or left unpaid, the line comes apart

techniques.name: Wading Shot
techniques.desc: Shoot him in the stream, knee-deep and slow, where he can neither hurry nor answer.

techniques.name: Behind the Pavise
techniques.desc: The tall shield stands on its prop; the man who comes round it meets the short sword of a crossbowman who expected him.

techniques.name: Through the Lance-Coat
techniques.desc: A Feleria steel-and-horn bow at 60 metres goes through mail, padding and the man inside them.

techniques.name: Paid Men Hold
techniques.desc: Professionals do not hurry: span, wait, shoot on the word, and let the levies around you do the shouting.

techniques.name: Knight Off His Horse
techniques.desc: The captain's shot, held until the knight is close enough that the bolt takes him out of the saddle.

maneuver.name: Crossbow Line behind a Stream
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen stand behind a stream, a flooded ditch or a marsh edge, and shoot attackers slowed to a wade at 30 to 60 metres.

ST31-03.name: The Neck Road Ride
ST31-03.origin: The Imperial Post kept a relay station every 30 km on the Neck road, and its post-riders, the Tessarans and the Fennaro among them, could ride from Calora to Tessar in four days. Leo the Free turned the stations into small forts in 712; today both claimants keep Road Riders who live in the saddle between them, chasing raiders and collecting the same toll twice.
ST31-03.philosophy: Thirty kilometres and a fresh horse: strike, ride on, and let the next station finish it.
ST31-03.strengths: speed, endurance in the saddle, javelins on the move, never being where the enemy expects
ST31-03.weakness: light horse in leather with a short spear: against a set spear line or a knight's charge they can only run

school.name: The Post Station Yard of Tessar

techniques.name: Fresh Horse
techniques.desc: Change horses at the station and come back to the fight before the other man has caught his breath.

techniques.name: Javelin at the Gallop
techniques.desc: Two javelins thrown as you pass, the second while he is still ducking the first.

techniques.name: Ride Through the Toll
techniques.desc: Through the bandits' road-block at a gallop, the spear low for their legs, and gone before they turn.

techniques.name: Four Days from Calora
techniques.desc: Kallias Tessaran's ride of 621: keep moving until the other man's horse is blown and yours is not.

techniques.name: Every Thirty Kilometres
techniques.desc: The station captain's charge: one hard pass from a fresh horse into a man whose horse has run all day.

maneuver.name: Road Riders' Chase
maneuver.desc: Light horse change mounts at the road stations and ride down raiders, stragglers and supply carts along the whole Neck road.

ST31-04.name: The Counterweight Throw
ST31-04.origin: In 1063 Master Silas Vane hired the ship carpenter Bruno Morello to build an engine nobody had built before, and on 4 June 1065 it threw 90 kg stones 250 metres and smashed both of Prince Andros's siege towers before Tessar. The Engine Yard has trained the queen's Engine Corps since; Vane, 68, calls a throw within 10 metres at 250 and keeps the aiming tables in his head.
ST31-04.philosophy: War is a problem of angles and weights: measure twice, throw once, and never stand where the answer lands.
ST31-04.strengths: breaking towers, walls and formations from afar, measuring ground, fire
ST31-04.weakness: nothing up close: an engineer whose engine is reached is an old man with a measuring cord, and fire-oil burns its keepers as gladly as its targets

techniques.name: Measuring Cord
techniques.desc: Pace the ground and look at the man as you would at a wall: where he is weak, and how far away.

techniques.name: Fire-Pot
techniques.desc: A clay pot of fire-oil with a burning rag, thrown at 20 metres; the fire sticks and will not be beaten out.

techniques.name: Lever and Wedge
techniques.desc: A wright knows where a lever goes: under the knee, against the hip, and the heavy thing falls over.

techniques.name: The Called Throw
techniques.desc: Silas Vane's art in small: judge distance, weight and wind, and put the heavy thing exactly where the man will be standing.

maneuver.name: Counterweight Bombardment
maneuver.desc: Trebuchets drop tonnes of earth and throw 50 to 100 kg stones 150 to 300 metres, always to the same spot, breaking towers and the men massed behind them.

ST31-05.name: The Calossa Lance
ST31-05.origin: Calossa has been the base of the northern border since Radoslav the Bear's victory at Lake Ostec in 957, and its Lance Yard trains the heavy horse of the north, today the 1,200 Dawn Lances of Prince Nikos. Sir Petar Grell, a gruff grey knight with small white scars on the outer edge of each hand, teaches the Six-Finger Rein Grip of the old post-riders, though he cannot use it himself.
ST31-05.philosophy: Hold the reins as if you had six fingers: the horse goes where the lance points, and the lance goes through.
ST31-05.strengths: control of the horse at the moment of impact, unhorsing, turning for a second pass
ST31-05.weakness: a knight's art of open ground: woods, ditches, stakes and the queen's crossbows behind a stream have killed more Dawn Lances than any knight has

techniques.name: The Six-Finger Rein Grip
techniques.desc: The rein wrapped round the hand the post-rider way: the horse does not shy from the lance, and the rider does not lose his seat.

techniques.name: Couched and Level
techniques.desc: Lance tucked hard under the arm and held level to the last stride; the point arrives before his does.

techniques.name: Unhorse
techniques.desc: Take him high on the shield, not the body, and lift: he goes over the crupper and the lance does not break.

techniques.name: The Turn and Second Pass
techniques.desc: Wheel short after the first pass while he is still finding his reins, and come again on the side he has not covered.

techniques.name: Through the Shield
techniques.desc: The lance-master's pass: the whole weight of horse and man behind a point that goes through the linden and what is behind it.

maneuver.name: Dawn Lance Charge
maneuver.desc: Heavy horse knee to knee, walk, trot and canter, and only the last hundred metres at the gallop, into one point of the enemy line.

ST31-06.name: Six Fingers Hold
ST31-06.origin: Kallias Tessaran, post-rider of the Imperial Post, was born with a working sixth finger on each hand in 603, and the hand has been the house's sign since Leo the Free raised a six-fingered banner in 712. The blood gives a grip almost nobody can break and, in one carrier in three, a weak heart; Dame Helena Tessaran, captain of the Queen's Six-Fingers, closes, binds the blade and takes it, as she did to a Dawn Lance on the Doria road in 1103.
ST31-06.philosophy: Close, bind, take: the first cross of blades decides, so make it a hold instead of a cut.
ST31-06.strengths: binding and taking weapons, a grip that will not be disarmed, close sword work
ST31-06.weakness: the weak heart of the line: past the third minute a Tessaran fades, and a foe who keeps his distance and waits can outlast the hand

techniques.name: The Hand Holds
techniques.desc: Six fingers round the hilt: his beat does not move your blade, and his own wrist takes the shock.

techniques.name: Close and Bind
techniques.desc: Step in on the first cross, blade against blade near the hilts, and wind his sword down where it cannot cut.

techniques.name: Take the Blade
techniques.desc: What Helena did on the Doria road: the sixth finger hooks the crossguard, and his sword is in your other hand.

techniques.name: Breath Between Passes
techniques.desc: The house's quiet drill for its weak hearts: step out, lower the point, breathe slow, and do not let them see your lips grey.

techniques.name: The Crowned Hand
techniques.desc: Bind, take the blade aside with the hand, and thrust with your own in the same breath, before his heart or yours can fail.

ST31-07.name: We Hold the South
ST31-07.origin: Captain Justin Asterio led 3,000 unpaid imperial soldiers over to Leo the Free at Albina in 711, and his house has led the southern levies ever since, from the conquest of Tamar to the Nagpur gorge in 999. Lord Marshal Corvin Asterio defended Tessar through the siege of 1064 and 1065, brought the army home after Vitella, and held the line at Coreria in 1104; he taught the sword to his niece Helena.
ST31-07.philosophy: Hold the line you are given, keep your men alive, and know the moment when the other side is ready to come over.
ST31-07.strengths: patient defense, counters, keeping a line together, choosing the moment to change the fight
ST31-07.weakness: a tired house that fights not to lose: it seldom presses home, and a bold enemy who keeps attacking finds it giving ground

techniques.name: Copper Shield
techniques.desc: Shield square, feet wide, weight low: the southern levies are taught to be hard to move before they are taught to hit.

techniques.name: The Line You Are Given
techniques.desc: Do not step out to him; let him come again and again onto the rim, and answer each time he leaves himself open.

techniques.name: The Albina Turn
techniques.desc: Seem to give way, as Justin Asterio's cohort seemed to break at Albina, and come back on the side he thought was already his.

techniques.name: Bring the Army Home
techniques.desc: Corvin's art after Vitella in 1068: break off in good order, bind the wounds, and live to fight next year.

techniques.name: The Coreria Line
techniques.desc: The day the line should have broken and did not: stand in it yourself, take the worst blow on the copper rim, and kill the man who gave it.

maneuver.name: The South Holds
maneuver.desc: The Copper Hill Spears close up behind the Marshal's banner and give ground only a step at a time.

ST31-08.name: The Red Dawn Banner
ST31-08.origin: Dmitar Varisco, a hill knight's son, carried the first proclamation of Andros through the north in 1061, and the boy king gave him the new red dawn banner at Calossa in 1062. At Vitella in 1068 the color-blind Marcus Corvane took that red for the queen's gold and rode into it to his death; Andrei Varisco carried the banner through the queen's crossbow fire at Coreria in 1104 and has three bolt scars to prove it.
ST31-08.philosophy: The banner rides first and does not slow: whatever the enemy throws at it, the men behind it do not have to face.
ST31-08.strengths: courage under missiles, leading a charge, making the enemy look at the wrong thing
ST31-08.weakness: the banner draws every bolt on the field, and a bearer cannot turn aside or fight for himself without lowering it

techniques.name: Prayer Over the Silk
techniques.desc: The women of the house pray over every stitch of the red; the bearer says the same prayer before the trumpet, and his hands stop shaking.

techniques.name: Three Bolt Scars
techniques.desc: The bolts hit and the bearer keeps riding; the pain comes after the charge, when there is time for it.

techniques.name: Red Like Gold
techniques.desc: The lesson of Vitella: in dusk and dust a banner is mistaken for a friend's, and a bearer learns to ride where the mistake will be made.

techniques.name: The Dawn Goes First
techniques.desc: The house words: the red goes in ahead of the Dawn Lances, and the bearer's lance takes the first man of the line.

maneuver.name: Follow the Red
maneuver.desc: The Dawn Lances ride at the red banner wherever it goes, and the line that sees it coming knows who is behind it.

ST32-01.name: The Galley Bow
ST32-01.origin: Every war galley of the sultan carries archers in its bow and stern castles, 1,800 of them in 1105, and since forty Amber ships burned 22 Keshi pepper ships at Kioya in 1068 the fleet archers have drilled fire arrows as hard as plain ones. They learn to shoot from a deck that rolls under them, on the downroll, and to pick out the steersman and the drummer of an enemy galley.
ST32-01.philosophy: Shoot on the roll, kill the man who steers, and set the rest on fire.
ST32-01.strengths: shooting from moving decks, fire arrows, picking out officers
ST32-01.weakness: short island bows of bamboo and horn that do little against mail; out of the bow castle, the archer is light and lightly armed

school.name: The Bow Castle Yard of Amberport

techniques.name: Shoot on the Downroll
techniques.desc: Loose as the deck drops under you, never as it rises; the arrow goes where the bow was pointing.

techniques.name: Below the Rail
techniques.desc: When their arrows come the castle archer is behind the planking; when they stop, he is up again with the next shaft on the string.

techniques.name: Fire Arrow
techniques.desc: Pitch-wrapped tow on the head, lit from the pot at your feet: the man it hits beats at the flames instead of fighting.

techniques.name: Over the Rail
techniques.desc: When the boarders come over, the bow goes on its hook and the kris comes out at the man still straddling the rail.

techniques.name: The Burning of Kioya
techniques.desc: One shot through the oar-port into a pitch-soaked hold; by the time the man knows he is hit, his ship is burning under him.

maneuver.name: Bow Castle Volley
maneuver.desc: The archers of every galley in the line shoot together at the enemy's steersmen and rowers before the rams go in.

ST32-02.name: The Wave-Blade Kris
ST32-02.origin: The Pulau forged the first kris for Sultan Daud's court in 891, folding island iron with meteor nickel into the wavy blade that every Amber man of standing wears at his back. Spice-ship guards, marines and courtiers learn the same short, close art, and the yard at Paamu, where the old harbor chiefs swore to Bima Maruang in 859, still teaches it on a floor of ship's planking.
ST32-02.philosophy: Stay close, cut and slip away; the wavy blade does its work after you have stepped back.
ST32-02.strengths: close quarters on decks and in alleys, wounds that bleed, quick footwork
ST32-02.weakness: a short blade: a spear or a long sword keeps the kris-fighter out, and good mail turns its cuts

techniques.name: Draw from the Back
techniques.desc: The kris rides at the small of the back; it comes out reversed and cuts on the way round.

techniques.name: Slip the Spear
techniques.desc: Turn the body sideways, let the point go past your belly, and step in along the shaft to the man's thigh.

techniques.name: Seven Waves
techniques.desc: Seven bends in the blade, seven edges in the wound; it does not close, and he grows weaker every breath.

techniques.name: Deck-Step
techniques.desc: One small step on the planking, and his cut falls where you were; the kris goes in under the arm that made it.

techniques.name: Meteor Iron
techniques.desc: The master's thrust: the folded nickel point slides between the layers of quilted cotton, and the waves do the rest.

ST32-03.name: The Wyrm Spear
ST32-03.origin: After an Amber Wyrm killed the heir Prince Salim in 1022, Sultan Harun set a bounty on every head, and the stockade at Aming in the highlands of Great Amber became the school of the hunt. The Spear Yard teaches what Hasan Batu learned killing eleven wyrms: take the beast on a cold morning when it is slow, with heavy cross-barred spears, one man to take the charge and two to drive for the neck; Bakar the Wyrm-Killer has been its master since 1096.
ST32-03.philosophy: Never fight the wyrm's way: choose the cold hour, set the crossbar, and let three spears do what one man cannot.
ST32-03.strengths: stopping a rush on the point, tracking, patience, fighting beasts and big men
ST32-03.weakness: a heavy, slow spear made for beasts: a quick swordsman inside the crossbar, or a fight alone instead of in three, leaves the hunter exposed

techniques.name: The Cold Hour
techniques.desc: Choose when: at dawn, before the wyrm's blood is warm and before the man has eaten or stretched.

techniques.name: Crossbar Stop
techniques.desc: Take the rush on the point and let the crossbar stop it a spear's length away from your legs.

techniques.name: Two for the Neck
techniques.desc: While the charge-taker holds him, the second spear goes in behind the jaw where the scales are thin.

techniques.name: Follow the Scent
techniques.desc: The wyrm bites and follows its dying prey for hours; the hunter learns to follow the same way, patient, reading every stagger.

techniques.name: The Neck of the Dragon
techniques.desc: Bakar's thrust: two tonnes of lizard or one man in mail, the heavy blade goes in under the head and the weight behind it throws him over.

maneuver.name: Wyrm Spear Stand
maneuver.desc: Spearmen in threes with heavy cross-barred spears picket the forest edge: one takes the rush, two drive for the neck.

ST32-04.name: The Rowing Hall Stroke
ST32-04.origin: Sultan Idris founded the Rowing Hall when he built the naval yard at Tekook in 1031, and the Dayung drummers have set its stroke since. Master Fikri Laut teaches oar, sail and swimming with chants and drums, and in 1093 his Tekook rowers took three Keshi smuggling boats by night in the Madamo roads.
ST32-04.philosophy: On the beat: a crew that pulls as one, swims as one and goes over the rail as one beats a braver crew that does not.
ST32-04.strengths: endurance, swimming, fighting on decks and in the water, the strength of the oar
ST32-04.weakness: rowers, not swordsmen: crude with a blade, and their whole art depends on the beat, the crew and the boat

techniques.name: On the Beat
techniques.desc: Breathe on the drum, move on the drum; a rower who keeps the beat in his head does not blow in a fight.

techniques.name: Oar-Loom Shove
techniques.desc: The loom of an oar is a beam of hardwood; shove with the whole back, and men go over the side.

techniques.name: Over the Side
techniques.desc: Take him into the water with you: a Tekook rower can hold his breath, and a man in mail cannot.

techniques.name: Ramming Stroke
techniques.desc: The last two hundred metres at full stroke, the whole bench shouting, and the shock of the beak through the oars.

techniques.name: Six Hours on the Stroke
techniques.desc: A master holds the stroke for six hours; when the other man has nothing left, the rower is only halfway through his day.

maneuver.name: Galley Ramming
maneuver.desc: The rowers sprint the last 200 metres at the drum and drive the iron-shod beak across the enemy's oar bank.

ST32-05.name: The Bronze Ram
ST32-05.origin: The Rawang were harbor chiefs of Tekook until their fleet drowned in the Great Cyclone of 858, and for 170 years they were only captains, until Sultan Idris made Harith Rawang first sea lord of the new Tekook yard in 1031. Admiral Jaya Rawang was aboard his father's galley at ten in the battle off Tekook in 1070, when a fire ship took Prince Adil's galley, and the house teaches its sons the deck as he learned it that day.
ST32-05.philosophy: The sea remembers: keep your feet on a moving deck, keep the stern, and make the enemy fight the water as well as you.
ST32-05.strengths: footing on a pitching deck, boarding fights, fire and the grapnel, leading a crew
ST32-05.weakness: a deck fighter ashore is an ordinary one, and a captain who must keep the stern cannot chase the man who leaves it

techniques.name: Sea Legs
techniques.desc: Knees soft, feet wide, weight riding the swell: the landsman on the same deck is fighting his own feet.

techniques.name: Grapnel and Over
techniques.desc: Hook him by the rail, the belt or the shield rim and pull: on a rolling deck a man who is pulled goes down.

techniques.name: Hold the Stern
techniques.desc: The captain's place is by the steering oar; whoever comes up the deck for it meets a shield and a kris.

techniques.name: The Fire Ship
techniques.desc: What took Prince Adil in 1070: come at him wreathed in smoke and burning pitch, and let him choose between you and the fire.

ST32-06.name: From the Surf
ST32-06.origin: Ismail Ombak, a pearl diver's son who could swim in mail, raised the Sultan's Marines for Sultan Idris in 1031, and an Ombak has led them since. They boarded the Keshi pepper ships at Kioya in 1068 and lost a third of their men to the fire ship off Tekook in 1070, and in April 1105 Captain Hasyim Ombak means to take the first boats onto the Isle of Pearls.
ST32-06.philosophy: From the surf, up the beach: the worst moment is the knee-deep water, so get through it fastest and form on the sand before they can.
ST32-06.strengths: landing under missiles, swimming in mail, fighting with wet sand underfoot, a loud, fast assault
ST32-06.weakness: everything rides on the first rush: a beach held by a steady line with stakes, or a landing that stalls in the water, leaves them packed and helpless

techniques.name: Rope in the Teeth
techniques.desc: Swim ashore ahead of the boats with the line in your teeth; a marine who can do that is not tired by a fight on dry sand.

techniques.name: Out of the Knee-Deep
techniques.desc: Over the bow, through the water at a run and straight into the first man on the beach before he has set his feet.

techniques.name: Form on the Sand
techniques.desc: Shields locked at the tide line and spears over them; the boats behind are the only way out, so nobody steps back.

techniques.name: Up the Beach
techniques.desc: Loud, fast and all together: the marines' charge from the waterline, before the defenders have counted the boats.

maneuver.name: Beach Landing
maneuver.desc: Galleys run bow-first onto the beach; marines and archers jump into knee-deep water and form on the sand under the bow castles' arrows.

ST32-07.name: The Highland March Spear
ST32-07.origin: Hasan Batu, a tapper's son of Great Amber, killed eleven Amber Wyrms for the bounty and was given the new Highland March and the stockade at Aming in 1034. The house has fought the Cloudfolk clans every dry season since, in cloud forest where no column can form; Warden Hamzah Batu led his first spear patrol at 18, lived through three days of bleeding after a wyrm bite in 1084, and killed the Cloud Ridge chief in 1086.
ST32-07.philosophy: The forest pays the bold, but only the bold who see the ambush first: walk light, keep the spear low, and strike before the arrows.
ST32-07.strengths: patrols and ambush in thick forest, javelins at close range, spotting traps, living through wounds
ST32-07.weakness: light spearmen with no armor worth the name; in the open against a formed line or a horseman, the forest fighter has nothing to hide behind

techniques.name: See the Ambush First
techniques.desc: Birds that stop singing, a fern bent the wrong way: the patrol leader reads the forest, and then the man.

techniques.name: Javelin in the Trees
techniques.desc: A short bamboo javelin thrown at ten paces through the leaves, before he can lift his shield in the tangle.

techniques.name: Spear Low in the Fern
techniques.desc: Under the ferns, at the shin and the knee: a man who cannot walk out of the cloud forest does not leave it.

techniques.name: Three Days Bleeding
techniques.desc: Hamzah lived through a wyrm bite by refusing to lie down; the house teaches its sons to bind a wound tight and fight on.

maneuver.name: Forest Ambush
maneuver.desc: Highland Spears strike a column on a forest track from both sides at close range, where it cannot form.

ST33-01.name: The Reef Crossbow
ST33-01.origin: After the Peace of Ratrock in 1056 the Brotherhood needed fighters it could hire out when it could no longer raid, and a toll-boat crossbowman named Penn taught 30 men to shoot from a pitching deck and stand behind pavises ashore. His family, the Windlasses, has trained every crossbowman of the Brotherhood since, and the 800 Reef Crossbows under Brann Hollow held Queen Livia's line at Coreria on 26 October 1104. Any sworn hand who can crank a windlass may learn it in the harbor yard.
ST33-01.philosophy: Wind, loose, wind again: the deck moves, the pavise does not, and a bolt at sixty meters does not care who is braver.
ST33-01.strengths: kills a man in mail at 60 m; shooting from a pitching deck; standing behind pavises ashore; hired discipline
ST33-01.weakness: two bolts a minute; rain on the string; a fast charge before they span; unpaid, they walk

techniques.name: Wind and Loose
techniques.desc: Foot in the stirrup, crank the windlass, loose; a farmhand learns it in weeks and a knight dies of it all the same.

techniques.name: Behind the Pavise
techniques.desc: Span behind the big shield and shoot the man who comes round it.

techniques.name: Shoot on the Roll
techniques.desc: Loose at the top of the swell, when the deck hangs still for a heartbeat and everyone else is grabbing a rope.

techniques.name: Sixty Meters
techniques.desc: The distance at which a bolt goes through mail and the man inside it; wait for him to walk into it.

techniques.name: Hold the Line at Coreria
techniques.desc: Paid men who stay: the Reef Crossbows held a queen's line for a day and turned a battle into a draw.

techniques.name: The Close Bolt
techniques.desc: Hold the shot until he is ten paces off and certain he has you; at that range nothing he wears matters.

maneuver.name: Crossbow Volley
maneuver.desc: Crossbowmen behind pavises shoot in two or three ranks, one loosing while the others span; from a deck or a beach, they kill what comes at them in mail.

ST33-02.name: The Toll-Boat Gaff
ST33-02.origin: Since the Peace of Ratrock in 1056 the toll boats of Ratrock have stopped every ship in the Strait lane and taken one in forty, and a toll-boat hand's weapon is the boathook: a long gaff to hold a hull alongside, haul a man off a ladder or keep a boarder off your own gunwale. Aled Coyle's kin have run the toll boats since that year, and the 400 toll-boat fighters of Ratrock and Gull Isle all learn the gaff before the crossbow.
ST33-02.philosophy: Keep the hook between you and him: a gaff holds a boat, a ladder or a man exactly where you want him, which is out of reach.
ST33-02.strengths: reach from a small boat; hooking men off ladders and rails; holding a hull alongside; putting a man overboard
ST33-02.weakness: a clumsy weapon on a crowded deck; nothing against a man already inside the hook; toll boats are small and they burn

techniques.name: Hold Alongside
techniques.desc: Hook his rail, or his belt, and hold him at the length of the pole while he wonders what to do about it.

techniques.name: Hook the Ankle
techniques.desc: Show the point at his face and take the hook round behind his ankle.

techniques.name: Off the Ladder
techniques.desc: A man climbing has both hands busy; hook him under the arm and pull.

techniques.name: Over the Side
techniques.desc: Hook him at the belt and lean back; a man in mail who goes into the Strait does not come up arguing.

techniques.name: Butt and Blade
techniques.desc: When he gets inside the hook, the butt goes into his teeth and the knife comes out of your belt.

techniques.name: One in Forty
techniques.desc: The toll boat counts every ship; the toll-hand counts every move, and takes his share of the one that matters.

ST33-03.name: The Fire-Raft
ST33-03.origin: On the night of 12 July 1051 Mag Brine burned three Lucernan ships in the Strait and gave the Middle Sea its dragon, and the raft-builders of Ratrock towed the burning rafts into the current; in May 1053 their rafts burned 11 galleys at anchor off Gull Isle. The Raft Yard teaches pitch, smoke, fire-rafts and the sea in bad weather, and only the sworn learn what really burns on the water. Sten the Quiet, Oil-Keeper of Ratrock, keeps the yard, the oil caves and the Forty.
ST33-03.philosophy: Fire, smoke and weather do the fighting; a raft-man's art is to be somewhere else when they do.
ST33-03.strengths: fire and smoke; night and bad weather; terror; knowing the tide and the current
ST33-03.weakness: little for a fight hand to hand; its own fire; a wind that changes; a secret that must be kept

techniques.name: Smoke Pot
techniques.desc: Wet straw and tar in a pot, thrown upwind; he fights a shape in the smoke while you fight a man.

techniques.name: Pitch on the Water
techniques.desc: A pot of hot pitch and a torch after it; the fire clings to whatever it lands on.

techniques.name: Weather Eye
techniques.desc: Know the squall before it comes and the swell before it lifts; you are braced when he is thrown.

techniques.name: The Dragon Wakes
techniques.desc: Fire on the water in long streams, with horns and gongs: crews who see it believe in dragons, and a man who sees it at arm's length forgets his sword.

maneuver.name: Fire Rafts on the Tide
maneuver.desc: Log rafts heaped with pitch and brush, and something worse where it can be had, are set adrift on the tide into ships at anchor, with horns and gongs in the dark behind them.

ST33-04.name: Hook and Short Blade
ST33-04.origin: Harl Gannet taught the first captains of the Articles in 990 to fight a navy at night, in the shoals, and to win a ship by going over its side, and the boarding yard beside the Shrine of the Dice has taught it since, with dice thrown before every lesson that matters. Rafe Hookhand, 36, keeps it now with a boarding hook at each hip and climbs rigging for fun; he trains the boarders of the Redsails and the Copperhulls for the Lion Fleet expected after Sea Opening.
ST33-04.philosophy: Over the rail before he has drawn: hook, climb, and fight so close that his long sword is a stick.
ST33-04.strengths: climbing and boarding; fighting chest to chest on a deck; two hooks and a short blade; fists
ST33-04.weakness: open water with no hull to climb; marines in a formed line on a high-sided cog; reach

techniques.name: Over the Rail
techniques.desc: Grapnel, two pulls on the rope and you are over, landing on whoever was standing there.

techniques.name: Two Hooks
techniques.desc: One hook takes the shield rim, the other the man behind it.

techniques.name: Fist on the Deck
techniques.desc: Too close for a blade? A fist with a hook-handle in it does the same work.

techniques.name: Throw the Dice
techniques.desc: Once a fight, gamble: show him the opening you would never leave, and be inside it with the knife when he takes it.

techniques.name: From the Rigging
techniques.desc: Fight from above him: up the shrouds, a boot on his shoulder, and down behind him before he finds you.

techniques.name: First Over
techniques.desc: The first man over the rail takes the first share and the first blow; the Yard's masters are the ones who lived to take the share.

maneuver.name: Boarding Action
maneuver.desc: Grapnels thrown, a crossbow volley across the gap, then the boarders over the bow with hooks and short blades before the enemy's marines have formed.

ST33-05.name: The Still Deck
ST33-05.origin: Tamsin of Brinehole rowed the salt boats in any sea and was never sick, and her son Mag sailed to Sabra and back through the winter storms of 1049 to 1050 and was elected Captain-General for it. The Brines have the sea-steady blood: perfect footing on a pitching deck, and land that sways under them for days after. Every Brine child sails from six and learns to fight where other men cannot stand, as Nell Brine did.
ST33-05.philosophy: The deck pitches and you do not: fight on the roll, when he is holding the rail and you are holding a blade.
ST33-05.strengths: perfect footing on a pitching deck, wet rigging or in a storm; fighting in weather; balance
ST33-05.weakness: on land the ground sways for days after a voyage; trusts weather that drowns crews, as Rook Brine did off Wreck Isle

techniques.name: Feet of Brinehole
techniques.desc: Let him lunge as the deck drops; he goes where the sea takes him and you stay where you were.

techniques.name: Cut on the Roll
techniques.desc: Strike as the ship heels toward him, with the whole sea behind the blade.

techniques.name: Winter Run
techniques.desc: Mag Brine sailed to Sabra and back through storms no one sails in; the house has never yet been the first to tire of bad weather.

techniques.name: The Sea Stands Still for Us
techniques.desc: The house's words: wait for the wave that throws him, and be the only steady thing on the deck when it comes.

ST33-06.name: The Red Sail
ST33-06.origin: In 1031 Hob Redsail dyed every sail of his crew red with madder from a Lucernan prize, so that merchants would know whose ships they were before they could run. The Redsails have raided for three generations, sailed on Dragon Night, and hated the toll of 1056 that forbids them a ship that has paid; Cob Redsail raided Felano without leave in 1096 and died of a tower crossbow bolt. Ima Redsail leads nine galleys and the Old Articles now, and teaches her crews to win before the fight starts.
ST33-06.philosophy: Win before the fight: let him see the red sail and hear the crew and know what happens to crews that fight, and most will pay.
ST33-06.strengths: terror; the rush over the rail; cruelty that breaks a crew before it forms
ST33-06.weakness: a crew that does not frighten; tower crossbows; reckless captains who sail without leave

techniques.name: Show the Red Sail
techniques.desc: Let him see who you are; a frightened man's arms are heavy before the first blow.

techniques.name: Howl Over the Rail
techniques.desc: The whole crew over at once, screaming; nobody fights well the first time he sees that.

techniques.name: No Quarter for Fighters
techniques.desc: The crews that pay live and the crews that fight do not; make sure the first man who fights is seen to die.

techniques.name: Take It or Pay
techniques.desc: The house's words, said once with a blade at his throat; there is no second offer.

ST34-01.name: The Winter Wave
ST34-01.origin: The eastern clans learned what winter does to herds in the killing winters of the old songs, and what hay does in the Great Blizzard of February 1081, when the council's hay law saved the horses; since then they fight in the season nobody fights. Their relays are axe and hide shield, short waves to the drum with a fire behind the line, and the Gorak clans of the Northern Steppe, who fight best in snow, teach them at the Drukgar stockade on the forest edge.
ST34-01.philosophy: Fight when the enemy is cold and you are not: short waves of axe and shield in the snow, and back to the fire between them.
ST34-01.strengths: cold-weather fighting; axe and hide shield in relay; hooking shields; quick recovery between waves
ST34-01.weakness: summer and noon heat; ten minutes of hard fighting; crossbows behind stakes

techniques.name: Hook the Rim
techniques.desc: The beard of the axe over the shield rim, and a pull; the shield comes down and his face is there.

techniques.name: Hide Shield Shove
techniques.desc: Take the blow on the rhino-hide and shove with the whole burst behind it; on frozen ground he goes down.

techniques.name: Breath Smoke
techniques.desc: Back to the fire between waves; in the frost an orc cools and comes again, while the man who chased him freezes.

techniques.name: Snow-Blind Rush
techniques.desc: Come out of the blowing snow with the sun behind it, before he has seen there is anything to see.

techniques.name: Frozen Ford
techniques.desc: Draw him onto the ice of a ford or the crust of a drift; the man who breaks through is yours.

techniques.name: Blizzard Wave
techniques.desc: The whole band in one wave in the worst of the weather, when no horn can be heard and no Sunland horse will face the wind.

maneuver.name: Winter Wave
maneuver.desc: The clans strike in short relays in snow and frost, each wave going back to fires behind the line; the cold that numbs the enemy keeps orcs from overheating.

ST34-02.name: The Silk Road Screen
ST34-02.origin: When Grakka Ironhide made the Toll of Kraoth in June 1067 she raised the Toll Riders from the Kraoth clans to escort the silk caravans and run down any that dodged the toll; with a single toll guarded, the caravans grew from about 20 to about 40 a year. The 1,600 Toll Riders under Toruk Chainsilver are horse archers rather than charge riders, and they teach the screen at the Roktuk springs where every caravan from Kraoth must water.
ST34-02.philosophy: Ride the ring a kilometer out from the caravan; chase raiders off rather than fight them, and kill only the ones who will not go.
ST34-02.strengths: horse archery on the move; escort and pursuit; long rides between wells
ST34-02.weakness: not charge riders; a strike at a well or a ford where the caravan bunches; poor in the press

school.name: The Toll Riders' Ground at Roktuk

techniques.name: Warning Shaft
techniques.desc: The first arrow goes into the ground at his horse's feet. Most raiders understand.

techniques.name: Screen the Flank
techniques.desc: Ride between the raider and the camels, and shoot the one who tries to go round you.

techniques.name: Run Down the Toll-Dodger
techniques.desc: A caravan that slips the toll at night leaves tracks a child could follow; shoot the lead animal and the rest stop.

techniques.name: Where the Caravan Bunches
techniques.desc: Raiders strike at wells and fords, where the camels crowd; the screen is already watching there.

techniques.name: Arrow from the Dust
techniques.desc: Out of the caravan's own dust cloud, from the side he thought was camels.

techniques.name: Forty Caravans a Year
techniques.desc: The road pays because the road is safe; the man who makes it unsafe is shot until he is not.

maneuver.name: Caravan Screen
maneuver.desc: Riders escort a column in a moving ring one to three kilometers out, scouts ahead, bows on the flanks and a reserve behind; raiders are chased off before they reach it.

ST34-03.name: The Rhino Spear
ST34-03.origin: The Rhino Spear Lodge at Krarog grew out of the Turquoise Hills clans' spring trials, where youths face the woolly rhinos that den at the Grashmar Crag; every hill clan gives it one youth in five, and its 800 Rhino Spears are the best foot of the league. It teaches the cross-barred spear set against a charging beast or rider, hunting and tracking. Grel Rhinospear, born in the hills in 1060, has buried 31 students killed in the trials since 1092 and still sends every one of them to the rhino.
ST34-03.philosophy: Set the butt, lower the point and let the beast come: a rhino kills itself on a spear held still by someone who did not run.
ST34-03.strengths: bracing against a charge of beast or rider; tracking and reading an animal; the heavy thrust that goes through hide
ST34-03.weakness: missiles; riders who swerve and strike from the side; slow on open ground; the trials bury its students

techniques.name: Set the Butt
techniques.desc: Butt in the ground, foot on the butt, point at the chest; whatever charges you does the work.

techniques.name: The Cross-Bar
techniques.desc: The bar stops the point a hand deep, so the spear is not lost in him and the next man can strike.

techniques.name: Read the Track
techniques.desc: Hoof, dung and broken grass: a hunter knows which way the beast will turn before it turns.

techniques.name: Through the Hide
techniques.desc: A thrust with both arms and the whole body behind it, through hide that turns arrows.

techniques.name: Step from the Horn
techniques.desc: Wait for the horn to drop, step off the line at the last stride and put the point into the flank as it passes.

techniques.name: The Trial Kill
techniques.desc: One spear, on foot, into the chest of a charging woolly rhino: what every youth of the hills is sent to do, and what some of them do.

maneuver.name: Boar Spear Stand
maneuver.desc: A file braces cross-barred heavy spears against a charge of beasts or riders; the bar stops each point a hand deep so no spear is lost and the next man can strike.

ST34-04.name: Drum Speech of Grakmar
ST34-04.origin: At Zorek on 11 May 1064 Clan Harrak's drummers beat Grakka's charge, and both Dravic princes, whose ears cannot bear war-drums, fell from their saddles; the league has drilled its drummers on the Grakmar Drum Ground ever since. The 400 of the Drum Band set the pace of every relay and the turn of every wave. Bolg the Drummer, chief shaman and master of the ground, is nearly deaf and leans on Ashka Drumtongue to tell him what the drums are saying.
ST34-04.philosophy: The drum decides when the wave strikes and when it breathes, and an enemy who cannot hear his own horns cannot move.
ST34-04.strengths: timing the relays; drowning horn calls; frightening horses; the weakness of Drevna's princes
ST34-04.weakness: a lone fighter's art only at the edges; horses trained to drums, hand signals and wax in the ears; drummers go deaf

techniques.name: Count the Beats
techniques.desc: Fight in waves inside your own head: two minutes, a breath, two minutes; you never spend more than you have.

techniques.name: Drown the Horn
techniques.desc: A roar on the downbeat, right in his ear; it rings, and the next thing he hears is your blow.

techniques.name: Turn of the Wave
techniques.desc: On the changed beat the wave turns back; the man who follows it runs into the next one.

techniques.name: The Zorek Beat
techniques.desc: The rhythm that broke the Dravic princes: few drummers alive can still play it right, and Drevna would pay well to know how few.

maneuver.name: Drum Storm
maneuver.desc: Hundreds of war-drums beat together as the relay waves charge: untrained horses shy and bolt, horn calls drown, and at Zorek the Dravic princes fell from their saddles.

ST34-05.name: The Hide Wall
ST34-05.origin: In January 988 Uzma Ironhide, 17, took three knife cuts in a fight over a stolen mare that barely passed her skin, and killed both her attackers; when she became clan-mother the clan took her name and its thick-skinned riders rode at the front of every raid. Grakka formed the Ironhide Hearth Band in 1066 from carriers of every branch, and on 21 June 1062 she killed the year's rhino and 31 clans swore to her. Any child who shows the hide takes the Ironhide name at 13 and learns this way in the Hearth Band, where Garn Hornbreaker teaches the spear.
ST34-05.philosophy: Let the cut come: what opens another orc to the bone only scores an Ironhide, and the man who expected to see you fall is still looking when the spear comes back.
ST34-05.strengths: shrugging off cuts and claws; the front of the first wave; winter fighting; spear and hide together
ST34-05.weakness: crossbow bolts and spear thrusts still kill; overheats faster than any other orc, and no Ironhide fights at summer noon

techniques.name: Take the Cut
techniques.desc: Let the blade come across the hide, and answer while he is still looking for the blood.

techniques.name: Front of the First Wave
techniques.desc: The Hide Wall rides first behind the drums, because the arrows and the first cuts are meant for it.

techniques.name: Three Cuts at Seventeen
techniques.desc: Uzma's fight: take what he gives, and kill him before he understands he has not hurt you.

techniques.name: Frost Morning
techniques.desc: In the cold the hide does not burn; on a frost morning the band can fight a whole wave longer than in May.

techniques.name: Rhino-Taker
techniques.desc: Grakka's kill on the Great Ride of 1062, which made a league: one spear into the year's rhino, in front of 31 clans.

maneuver.name: Hide Wall Charge
maneuver.desc: The thick-skinned riders of Clan Ironhide form the front of the first wave behind the drums; cuts and claws barely mark them, though bolts still kill.

ST34-06.name: The White Horn
ST34-06.origin: About 790 Mother Tarsha killed a pale-horned woolly rhino on foot with one spear on the Tuknak grass and won her kin the valleys, and in the spring of 1083 Hrok, 15, did it again and took the name. The Whitehorns took the Otsai horse lines when they burned the Wind camp in 916 and fight with heavy spears and fast relays on those horses. Their youths face a rhino every spring until they kill one, and the clan sings the names of the dead.
ST34-06.philosophy: Be the first spear in: on the first grass, at the first rhino, in the first wave, and do not ask who follows.
ST34-06.strengths: the first two minutes of the first wave; a heavy spear from a fast horse; courage to the edge of madness
ST34-06.weakness: the long fight; reckless, burying more sons than any kin; a crossbow at sixty meters

techniques.name: Spring Trial
techniques.desc: Every spring until you kill one: walk at the rhino, point low, and do not stop.

techniques.name: Otsai Spear
techniques.desc: The heavy spear from a horse bred from the Wind camp's own lines; it reaches him before his sword does.

techniques.name: Sing the Dead
techniques.desc: Every name sung in the spring was someone who did not run; the song steadies the hands that hold the spear.

techniques.name: First Spear In
techniques.desc: First grass, first spear: be the point of the first wave, and let the rest of the clan follow the hole you make.

techniques.name: One Spear
techniques.desc: What Tarsha did and Hrok did again: one spear, one thrust, and nothing held back for a second.

ST34-07.name: Hear Us and Fall
ST34-07.origin: The Thunderskins were freed-thrall drummers of Clan Harrak when Grakka took them to war in 1062, and at Zorek their drums began the charge that dropped the elder Dravic prince from his saddle. Their captain has stood at Bolg the Drummer's side since the Drum Band was made and they teach every drummer in it, and when a wave breaks back on the drums the Thunderskins fight with their heavy mallets. They lead the league's drumming every 11 May.
ST34-07.philosophy: Fight on the beat: a drummer's arms never tire on the rhythm, and a heavy mallet that lands on the downbeat lands where the ear is.
ST34-07.strengths: tireless arms; blows that ring the skull; timing; standing over the drums
ST34-07.weakness: a little deaf, all of them, so a quiet feint or a step behind goes unheard; mallets are not blades against mail; tempers

techniques.name: Downbeat
techniques.desc: A drummer strikes on the beat without thinking; a heavy mallet across the helmet does the same thing to a man as to a drum.

techniques.name: Arms That Do Not Tire
techniques.desc: Arms that beat for an hour at the Great Ride can block for a few minutes more than his.

techniques.name: Ring the Skull
techniques.desc: A mallet across the ear on the beat; the Dravic heir still collapses at war-drums, and a man in a helmet finds out why.

techniques.name: Stand Over the Drums
techniques.desc: When the wave breaks back, the drums do not move; every man who reaches them meets a drummer who has not stopped keeping time.

ST34-08.name: The Iron Bit
ST34-08.origin: When Grakka raised the Toll Riders in June 1067 the Ironbits were among the first hundred, and their founder Urbash took the name when he ran down a caravan that tried to slip the toll and brought its lead camel back by an iron bit through the nose. The line has held the Roktuk springs and a hundred of the Toll Riders since. Under the Law of the Fire they feed every caravan master before the count, and under Grakka's law they kill anyone who robs a caravan that has paid.
ST34-08.philosophy: Paid, or caught: ride him down, take the bit, and bring him back to the toll fire alive to be counted.
ST34-08.strengths: running down and catching; taking prisoners; long chases on the silk road
ST34-08.weakness: a man who will fight to the death rather than be caught; poor in the line; the bow is someone else's art

techniques.name: Catch the Halter
techniques.desc: Lean across and take his reins or his wrist; a man who cannot steer cannot fight well either.

techniques.name: Ride Him Down
techniques.desc: Push your horse into his flank until his tires and stumbles; the chase ends when his horse does.

techniques.name: Bit Through the Nose
techniques.desc: What Urbash did to a camel, done to a man: a hook in the face and a short pull, and he goes where you lead.

techniques.name: Back to the Toll Fire
techniques.desc: Down off his horse, bound and across your saddle; the toll is counted, and so is he.
